AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: >-
  Provisions three CloudWatch alarms that monitor the same dimensionless
  AWS/NetworkELB "AlwaysOK" metric with identical thresholds and evaluation
  settings, differing only in their TreatMissingData configuration
  (notBreaching, breaching, missing). Because the metric never reports data,
  each alarm settles into a different steady state, making this template a
  self-contained harness for testing how TreatMissingData affects alarm state
  transitions. Actions are disabled on all alarms, and no external
  infrastructure is created or referenced.

Resources:
  AlwaysOKAlarm:
    Type: AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm
    Properties:
      AlarmName: AlwaysOKAlarm
      AlarmDescription: >-
        TreatMissingData under test: notBreaching. The AlwaysOK metric in
        AWS/NetworkELB never publishes data points, so missing data is treated
        as within the threshold and this alarm is expected to hold a steady
        state of OK. Actions are disabled; this alarm exists purely for
        state-transition observation.
      Namespace: AWS/NetworkELB
      MetricName: AlwaysOK
      Statistic: Minimum
      Period: 60
      EvaluationPeriods: 1
      Threshold: 100
      ComparisonOperator: GreaterThanOrEqualToThreshold
      TreatMissingData: notBreaching
      ActionsEnabled: false

  AlwaysFAILAlarm:
    Type: AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm
    Properties:
      AlarmName: AlwaysFAILAlarm
      AlarmDescription: >-
        TreatMissingData under test: breaching. The AlwaysOK metric in
        AWS/NetworkELB never publishes data points, so missing data is treated
        as breaching the threshold and this alarm is expected to hold a steady
        state of ALARM. Actions are disabled; this alarm exists purely for
        state-transition observation.
      Namespace: AWS/NetworkELB
      MetricName: AlwaysOK
      Statistic: Minimum
      Period: 60
      EvaluationPeriods: 1
      Threshold: 100
      ComparisonOperator: GreaterThanOrEqualToThreshold
      TreatMissingData: breaching
      ActionsEnabled: false

  AlwaysINSUFFICIENTAlarm:
    Type: AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm
    Properties:
      AlarmName: AlwaysINSUFFICIENTAlarm
      AlarmDescription: >-
        TreatMissingData under test: missing. The AlwaysOK metric in
        AWS/NetworkELB never publishes data points, so the alarm has no data on
        which to evaluate and is expected to hold a steady state of
        INSUFFICIENT_DATA. Actions are disabled; this alarm exists purely for
        state-transition observation.
      Namespace: AWS/NetworkELB
      MetricName: AlwaysOK
      Statistic: Minimum
      Period: 60
      EvaluationPeriods: 1
      Threshold: 100
      ComparisonOperator: GreaterThanOrEqualToThreshold
      TreatMissingData: missing
      ActionsEnabled: false

Outputs:
  AlwaysOKAlarmArn:
    Description: ARN of the alarm testing TreatMissingData=notBreaching (expected steady state OK).
    Value: !GetAtt AlwaysOKAlarm.Arn

  AlwaysFAILAlarmArn:
    Description: ARN of the alarm testing TreatMissingData=breaching (expected steady state ALARM).
    Value: !GetAtt AlwaysFAILAlarm.Arn

  AlwaysINSUFFICIENTAlarmArn:
    Description: ARN of the alarm testing TreatMissingData=missing (expected steady state INSUFFICIENT_DATA).
    Value: !GetAtt AlwaysINSUFFICIENTAlarm.Arn

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  Provisions an Amazon Detective behavior graph for security monitoring.
  The graph aggregates and correlates security telemetry (VPC Flow Logs,
  CloudTrail management events, and — when available — Amazon GuardDuty
  findings) into a linked dataset for security investigation and analysis.

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# DEPLOYMENT NOTES (informational):
#
# 1. Amazon Detective permits exactly ONE behavior graph per account per Region.
#    A behavior graph already exists in this account and Region, so this stack
#    adopts that graph and applies the requested Name tag to it; a graph is
#    created only when none exists. On stack removal the graph is deleted only
#    if this stack created it — an adopted graph is left intact.
#
# 2. Amazon GuardDuty is NOT required to create or use a behavior graph. When
#    GuardDuty is enabled in the same account and Region, Detective ingests its
#    findings as an additional data source. No AWS::GuardDuty::Detector is
#    declared here; GuardDuty is outside the scope of this request.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Resources:

  DetectiveGraphManagerRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: lambda.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole'
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: DetectiveGraphManagement
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              # ListGraphs and CreateGraph act at account/Region scope and
              # cannot be constrained to a specific graph ARN.
              - Sid: DetectiveDiscoverAndCreate
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - detective:ListGraphs
                  - detective:CreateGraph
                Resource: '*'
              # Tagging and deletion are scoped to graphs in this account/Region.
              - Sid: DetectiveTagAndDelete
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - detective:TagResource
                  - detective:DeleteGraph
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:detective:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:graph:*'
              # First use of Detective provisions AWSServiceRoleForDetective.
              - Sid: DetectiveServiceLinkedRole
                Effect: Allow
                Action: iam:CreateServiceLinkedRole
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::${AWS::AccountId}:role/aws-service-role/detective.amazonaws.com/AWSServiceRoleForDetective'
                Condition:
                  StringEquals:
                    iam:AWSServiceName: detective.amazonaws.com

  DetectiveGraphManagerFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      Description: >-
        CloudFormation custom resource handler that adopts the existing Amazon
        Detective behavior graph or creates one, applies the Name tag, and
        deletes the graph on stack removal only if this stack created it.
      Runtime: python3.13
      Handler: index.handler
      Role: !GetAtt DetectiveGraphManagerRole.Arn
      Timeout: 30
      MemorySize: 1024
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          import json
          import urllib.request

          import boto3
          from botocore.exceptions import ClientError

          TAGS = {'Name': 'MyDetectiveGraph'}
          CREATED = 'created'
          ADOPTED = 'adopted'


          def send(event, context, status, data, pid, reason=None):
              body = json.dumps({
                  'Status': status,
                  'Reason': reason or 'See log stream %s' % context.log_stream_name,
                  'PhysicalResourceId': pid or context.log_stream_name,
                  'StackId': event['StackId'],
                  'RequestId': event['RequestId'],
                  'LogicalResourceId': event['LogicalResourceId'],
                  'NoEcho': False,
                  'Data': data,
              }).encode('utf-8')
              req = urllib.request.Request(
                  event['ResponseURL'], data=body, method='PUT',
                  headers={'content-type': '', 'content-length': str(len(body))})
              with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=10) as resp:
                  print('response status %s' % resp.status)


          def split(pid):
              if pid and '|' in pid:
                  owner, arn = pid.split('|', 1)
                  if owner in (CREATED, ADOPTED) and arn:
                      return owner, arn
              return '', ''


          def existing(client):
              # Detective allows one graph per account/Region: page one is final.
              for graph in client.list_graphs(MaxResults=50).get('GraphList', []):
                  if graph.get('Arn'):
                      return graph['Arn']
              return None


          def handler(event, context):
              pid = event.get('PhysicalResourceId')
              try:
                  kind = event['RequestType']
                  if kind == 'Delete':
                      owner, arn = split(pid)
                      if owner == CREATED:
                          try:
                              boto3.client('detective').delete_graph(GraphArn=arn)
                          except ClientError as err:
                              if err.response['Error']['Code'] != 'ResourceNotFoundException':
                                  raise
                      send(event, context, 'SUCCESS', {}, pid)
                      return
                  if kind == 'Update':
                      send(event, context, 'SUCCESS', {'GraphArn': split(pid)[1]}, pid)
                      return

                  client = boto3.client('detective')
                  arn = existing(client)
                  owner = ADOPTED
                  if not arn:
                      try:
                          arn = client.create_graph(Tags=TAGS)['GraphArn']
                          owner = CREATED
                      except ClientError as err:
                          # Service is authoritative on the one-graph limit.
                          if 'graph' not in err.response.get('Error', {}).get('Message', '').lower():
                              raise
                          arn = existing(client)
                          if not arn:
                              raise
                  if owner == ADOPTED:
                      client.tag_resource(ResourceArn=arn, Tags=TAGS)
                  send(event, context, 'SUCCESS', {'GraphArn': arn}, '%s|%s' % (owner, arn))
              except Exception as err:  # never leave CloudFormation waiting
                  print('handler failed: %s' % err)
                  send(event, context, 'FAILED', {}, pid, str(err))

  DetectiveGraph:
    Type: Custom::DetectiveGraph
    Properties:
      ServiceToken: !GetAtt DetectiveGraphManagerFunction.Arn

Outputs:

  DetectiveGraphArn:
    Description: ARN of the Amazon Detective behavior graph managed by this stack.
    Value: !GetAtt DetectiveGraph.GraphArn

  DetectiveGraphRegion:
    Description: >-
      AWS Region in which the Amazon Detective behavior graph resides.
      Detective graphs are Region-scoped and are only usable in this Region.
    Value: !Ref 'AWS::Region'

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  Creates an AWS Backup Audit Manager framework enforcing backup compliance via the
  five default AWS Backup controls (resource protection, recovery point encryption,
  manual deletion prevention, minimum retention of 35 days, and backup plan minimum
  frequency/retention checks), together with the AWS Config prerequisites
  (configuration recorder, delivery channel, customer managed KMS key, delivery
  bucket and service role) that AWS Backup Audit Manager requires in order to
  evaluate those controls.

# CAVEAT: Only one AWS Config configuration recorder and one delivery channel may
# exist per AWS account per region. This template assumes a truly greenfield account
# in us-east-1. Deploying it into an account that already has AWS Config recording
# enabled will fail with MaxNumberOfConfigurationRecordersExceededException.
#
# ORDERING NOTE: The configuration recorder and the delivery channel are created
# concurrently on purpose. AWS Config will not start a recorder until a delivery
# channel exists, and the recorder resource handler waits for recording to become
# active before reporting CREATE_COMPLETE, so neither resource may DependsOn the
# other. Both instead depend on the bucket policy and the Config service role.

Parameters:
  ApplicationName:
    Type: String
    Default: BackupCompliance
    Description: Application name applied as a tag to all taggable resources.
    AllowedPattern: '[a-zA-Z][-a-zA-Z0-9]*'
    MinLength: 1
    MaxLength: 64

  EnvironmentName:
    Type: String
    Default: production
    Description: Environment name applied as a tag to all taggable resources.
    AllowedValues:
      - development
      - staging
      - production

Resources:

  ConfigDeliveryKey:
    Type: AWS::KMS::Key
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      Description: Customer managed key encrypting AWS Config configuration history and snapshots delivered to S3.
      EnableKeyRotation: true
      KeySpec: SYMMETRIC_DEFAULT
      KeyUsage: ENCRYPT_DECRYPT
      PendingWindowInDays: 30
      KeyPolicy:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: EnableRootAccountAdministration
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              AWS: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::${AWS::AccountId}:root'
            Action: 'kms:*'
            Resource: '*'
          - Sid: AllowConfigServiceUseOfKey
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: config.amazonaws.com
            Action:
              - kms:Encrypt
              - kms:Decrypt
              - kms:GenerateDataKey*
              - kms:DescribeKey
            Resource: '*'
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                kms:CallerAccount: !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref ApplicationName
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentName
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: CloudFormation

  ConfigDeliveryKeyAlias:
    Type: AWS::KMS::Alias
    Properties:
      AliasName: alias/BackupComplianceConfigKey
      TargetKeyId: !Ref ConfigDeliveryKey

  ConfigDeliveryBucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      BucketEncryption:
        ServerSideEncryptionConfiguration:
          - ServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
              SSEAlgorithm: aws:kms
              KMSMasterKeyID: !GetAtt ConfigDeliveryKey.Arn
            BucketKeyEnabled: true
      PublicAccessBlockConfiguration:
        BlockPublicAcls: true
        BlockPublicPolicy: true
        IgnorePublicAcls: true
        RestrictPublicBuckets: true
      VersioningConfiguration:
        Status: Enabled
      OwnershipControls:
        Rules:
          - ObjectOwnership: BucketOwnerEnforced
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref ApplicationName
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentName
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: CloudFormation

  ConfigDeliveryBucketPolicy:
    Type: AWS::S3::BucketPolicy
    Properties:
      Bucket: !Ref ConfigDeliveryBucket
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: AWSConfigBucketPermissionsCheck
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: config.amazonaws.com
            Action:
              - s3:GetBucketAcl
              - s3:ListBucket
            Resource: !GetAtt ConfigDeliveryBucket.Arn
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                AWS:SourceAccount: !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'
          - Sid: AWSConfigBucketDelivery
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: config.amazonaws.com
            Action: s3:PutObject
            Resource: !Sub '${ConfigDeliveryBucket.Arn}/AWSLogs/${AWS::AccountId}/Config/*'
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                AWS:SourceAccount: !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'
          - Sid: DenyInsecureTransport
            Effect: Deny
            Principal: '*'
            Action: s3:*
            Resource:
              - !GetAtt ConfigDeliveryBucket.Arn
              - !Sub '${ConfigDeliveryBucket.Arn}/*'
            Condition:
              Bool:
                aws:SecureTransport: false

  ConfigServiceRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: config.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                AWS:SourceAccount: !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWS_ConfigRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: ConfigDeliveryBucketAccess
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action: s3:PutObject
                Resource: !Sub '${ConfigDeliveryBucket.Arn}/AWSLogs/${AWS::AccountId}/Config/*'
              - Effect: Allow
                Action: s3:GetBucketAcl
                Resource: !GetAtt ConfigDeliveryBucket.Arn
        - PolicyName: ConfigDeliveryKeyAccess
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - kms:Encrypt
                  - kms:Decrypt
                  - kms:GenerateDataKey
                  - kms:DescribeKey
                Resource: !GetAtt ConfigDeliveryKey.Arn
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref ApplicationName
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentName
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: CloudFormation

  ConfigurationRecorder:
    Type: AWS::Config::ConfigurationRecorder
    DependsOn: ConfigDeliveryBucketPolicy
    Properties:
      Name: BackupComplianceRecorder
      RoleARN: !GetAtt ConfigServiceRole.Arn
      RecordingGroup:
        AllSupported: true
        IncludeGlobalResourceTypes: true

  ConfigDeliveryChannel:
    Type: AWS::Config::DeliveryChannel
    DependsOn:
      - ConfigDeliveryBucketPolicy
      - ConfigServiceRole
    Properties:
      Name: BackupComplianceDeliveryChannel
      S3BucketName: !Ref ConfigDeliveryBucket
      ConfigSnapshotDeliveryProperties:
        DeliveryFrequency: TwentyFour_Hours

  BackupComplianceFramework:
    Type: AWS::Backup::Framework
    DependsOn:
      - ConfigurationRecorder
      - ConfigDeliveryChannel
    Properties:
      FrameworkName: BackupComplianceFramework
      FrameworkDescription: >-
        Backup compliance framework validating that all supported resources are
        protected by a backup plan, that recovery points are encrypted and cannot be
        manually deleted, that recovery points are retained for at least 35 days, and
        that backup plans run at least every 24 hours with a minimum 35-day retention.
      FrameworkControls:
        - ControlName: BACKUP_RESOURCES_PROTECTED_BY_BACKUP_PLAN
        - ControlName: BACKUP_RECOVERY_POINT_ENCRYPTED
        - ControlName: BACKUP_RECOVERY_POINT_MANUAL_DELETION_DISABLED
        - ControlName: BACKUP_RECOVERY_POINT_MINIMUM_RETENTION_CHECK
          ControlInputParameters:
            - ParameterName: requiredRetentionDays
              ParameterValue: '35'
        - ControlName: BACKUP_PLAN_MIN_FREQUENCY_AND_MIN_RETENTION_CHECK
          ControlInputParameters:
            - ParameterName: requiredRetentionDays
              ParameterValue: '35'
            - ParameterName: requiredFrequencyUnit
              ParameterValue: 'hours'
            - ParameterName: requiredFrequencyValue
              ParameterValue: '24'
      FrameworkTags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref ApplicationName
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentName
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: CloudFormation

Outputs:

  BackupFrameworkArn:
    Description: ARN of the AWS Backup Audit Manager framework.
    Value: !GetAtt BackupComplianceFramework.FrameworkArn
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-BackupFrameworkArn'

  BackupFrameworkName:
    Description: Name of the AWS Backup Audit Manager framework.
    Value: !Ref BackupComplianceFramework
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-BackupFrameworkName'

  ConfigDeliveryBucketName:
    Description: Name of the S3 bucket receiving AWS Config configuration history and snapshots.
    Value: !Ref ConfigDeliveryBucket
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-ConfigDeliveryBucketName'

  ConfigDeliveryKeyArn:
    Description: ARN of the customer managed KMS key encrypting AWS Config delivery data.
    Value: !GetAtt ConfigDeliveryKey.Arn
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-ConfigDeliveryKeyArn'

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

# * Quota: ARC allows a low fixed number of clusters per account (default 2).
#   When saturated, CreateCluster is refused pre-flight with HTTP 402
#   ServiceLimitExceeded before any property is evaluated.
# * Cluster Name is capped at 64 characters by the service while stack names
#   may reach 128, so the suffix is kept short ('-arc') to widen the safe
#   stack-name window. Name is immutable once the cluster exists.
# * Tags are create-only and Name is immutable on both ARC types, so changing
#   ApplicationName or Environment REPLACES the cluster and all three control
#   panels rather than updating them in place. To change tag values or the
#   stack name, delete and recreate the stack -- do not run a parameter update.
# * That replacement cannot succeed in place for two independent reasons, and
#   both must be resolved before an update is even theoretically viable:
#   (a) CloudFormation creates the replacement cluster before deleting the
#       original, so the update needs one FREE cluster slot against the hard
#       limit of two; in a saturated account it fails with the same 402, but
#       mid-update on a live stack, leaving UPDATE_ROLLBACK around a recovery
#       control data plane that failover automation depends on; and
#   (b) the replacement cluster requests the same ${AWS::StackName}-arc name as
#       the original, which ARC rejects as a duplicate. Freeing a quota slot
#       alone does NOT make the update work -- the name collision is next.
# * Every resource carries the creating stack's AWS::StackId as a tag so that a
#   cluster left behind by a failed unwind is self-identifying from
#   ListTagsForResource alone. ARC tags cannot be retrofitted after creation.
# * No DeletionPolicy/UpdateReplacePolicy is set, deliberately: Retain would
#   orphan a billed cluster that still holds a quota slot and collides with the
#   immutable cluster Name on the next deploy of the same stack name.
# * ClusterEndpoints is not exported: it returns structured objects that no
#   intrinsic function can flatten into a scalar Output. Consumers read the five

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  Provisions a Step Functions workflow that publishes custom events to a dedicated
  EventBridge event bus, with a catch-all archival rule that forwards every event on
  that bus to a CloudWatch Logs log group for testing and debugging.

# Deliberate omissions (documented, not oversights):
#   * No KMS customer-managed keys on the event bus or log groups. AWS-owned encryption
#     applies by default; a CMK would add unrequested cost and key-policy surface.
#   * No AWS::Events::EventBusPolicy. Publishing is same-account only, so a resource
#     policy (which would require a Principal) is unnecessary and would widen access.
#   * AWS::Logs::ResourcePolicy and AWS::Events::Rule do not support Tags, so the
#     Application/Environment tags applied elsewhere cannot be applied to them.

Parameters:
  AppName:
    Type: String
    Default: serverless-workflow
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{2,32}$'
    ConstraintDescription: >-
      Must start with a lowercase letter and contain only lowercase letters, digits and
      hyphens (3-33 characters total).
    Description: Lowercase application name used to compose resource names and the event source.

  EnvironmentName:
    Type: String
    Default: dev
    AllowedValues:
      - dev
      - test
      - prod
    Description: Deployment environment used to compose resource names and event detail.

Resources:

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Custom EventBridge bus. The default bus is never referenced.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  EventBus:
    Type: AWS::Events::EventBus
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${AppName}-${EnvironmentName}-bus'
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref AppName
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentName

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Log group that receives every event forwarded off the custom bus.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  EventBridgeDebugLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: !Sub '/aws/events/${AppName}-${EnvironmentName}'
      RetentionInDays: 30
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref AppName
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentName

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Separate log group for Step Functions execution history (vended logs).
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  StateMachineLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: !Sub '/aws/vendedlogs/states/${AppName}-${EnvironmentName}'
      RetentionInDays: 30
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref AppName
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentName

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Without this resource policy EventBridge silently drops deliveries to Logs.
  # Scoped by aws:SourceAccount and the rule ARN pattern to avoid confused deputy.
  # AWS::Logs::ResourcePolicy requires a stringified policy document.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  EventBridgeLogsResourcePolicy:
    Type: AWS::Logs::ResourcePolicy
    Properties:
      PolicyName: !Sub '${AppName}-${EnvironmentName}-events-to-logs'
      PolicyDocument: !Sub |
        {
          "Version": "2012-10-17",
          "Statement": [
            {
              "Sid": "AllowEventBridgeDeliveryToDebugLogGroup",
              "Effect": "Allow",
              "Principal": {
                "Service": [
                  "events.amazonaws.com",
                  "delivery.logs.amazonaws.com"
                ]
              },
              "Action": [
                "logs:CreateLogStream",
                "logs:PutLogEvents"
              ],
              "Resource": [
                "arn:${AWS::Partition}:logs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:log-group:${EventBridgeDebugLogGroup}",
                "arn:${AWS::Partition}:logs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:log-group:${EventBridgeDebugLogGroup}:log-stream:*"
              ],
              "Condition": {
                "StringEquals": {
                  "aws:SourceAccount": "${AWS::AccountId}"
                },
                "ArnLike": {
                  "aws:SourceArn": "arn:${AWS::Partition}:events:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:rule/${EventBus}/*"
                }
              }
            }
          ]
        }

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Catch-all rule on the custom bus. DependsOn is required here because the
  # resource policy must exist before the rule starts delivering; no Ref/GetAtt
  # relationship expresses that ordering.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  EventBusCatchAllRule:
    Type: AWS::Events::Rule
    DependsOn: EventBridgeLogsResourcePolicy
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${AppName}-${EnvironmentName}-catch-all-debug'
      Description: >-
        Debug/audit catch-all: forwards every event published to the custom bus to
        CloudWatch Logs so workflow emissions can be inspected during testing.
      EventBusName: !Ref EventBus
      State: ENABLED
      EventPattern:
        account:
          - !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'
      Targets:
        # CloudWatch Logs targets are authorized by the log resource policy above;
        # attaching a RoleArn to a Logs target is invalid.
        - Id: cloudwatch-logs-debug-target
          Arn: !GetAtt EventBridgeDebugLogGroup.Arn

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Execution role for the state machine. Inline policies only.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  StateMachineRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      Description: !Sub 'Execution role for the ${AppName}-${EnvironmentName} Step Functions workflow.'
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: states.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                aws:SourceAccount: !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AWSXRayDaemonWriteAccess
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: PublishToCustomEventBus
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: PutEventsOnCustomBusOnly
                Effect: Allow
                Action: events:PutEvents
                Resource: !GetAtt EventBus.Arn
        - PolicyName: StateMachineLogDelivery
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              # These log-delivery APIs do not support resource-level permissions,
              # so Resource '*' is required by the service.
              - Sid: StepFunctionsVendedLogDelivery
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - logs:CreateLogDelivery
                  - logs:GetLogDelivery
                  - logs:UpdateLogDelivery
                  - logs:DeleteLogDelivery
                  - logs:ListLogDeliveries
                  - logs:PutResourcePolicy
                  - logs:DescribeResourcePolicies
                  - logs:DescribeLogGroups
                Resource: '*'
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref AppName
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentName

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # STANDARD workflow so execution history stays queryable for debugging.
  # No DependsOn on the role: !GetAtt already orders creation.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  WorkflowStateMachine:
    Type: AWS::StepFunctions::StateMachine
    Properties:
      StateMachineName: !Sub '${AppName}-${EnvironmentName}-workflow'
      StateMachineType: STANDARD
      RoleArn: !GetAtt StateMachineRole.Arn
      TracingConfiguration:
        Enabled: true
      LoggingConfiguration:
        Level: ALL
        IncludeExecutionData: true
        Destinations:
          - CloudWatchLogsLogGroup:
              LogGroupArn: !GetAtt StateMachineLogGroup.Arn
      DefinitionString: !Sub |
        {
          "Comment": "Normalizes input, then publishes a custom event to the dedicated EventBridge bus.",
          "StartAt": "PrepareEvent",
          "States": {
            "PrepareEvent": {
              "Type": "Pass",
              "Comment": "Wrap the raw execution input in a stable event detail envelope.",
              "Parameters": {
                "application": "${AppName}",
                "environment": "${EnvironmentName}",
                "executionName.$": "$$.Execution.Name",
                "stateMachineName.$": "$$.StateMachine.Name",
                "payload.$": "$"
              },
              "ResultPath": "$.eventDetail",
              "Next": "HasDetailType"
            },
            "HasDetailType": {
              "Type": "Choice",
              "Comment": "Allow callers to override the detail type, otherwise apply a default.",
              "Choices": [
                {
                  "Variable": "$.detailType",
                  "IsPresent": true,
                  "Next": "PublishEvent"
                }
              ],
              "Default": "ApplyDefaultDetailType"
            },
            "ApplyDefaultDetailType": {
              "Type": "Pass",
              "Result": "WorkflowExecutionCompleted",
              "ResultPath": "$.detailType",
              "Next": "PublishEvent"
            },
            "PublishEvent": {
              "Type": "Task",
              "Resource": "arn:aws:states:::events:putEvents",
              "Parameters": {
                "Entries": [
                  {
                    "Detail.$": "$.eventDetail",
                    "DetailType.$": "$.detailType",
                    "Source": "com.${AppName}.workflow",
                    "EventBusName": "${EventBus}"
                  }
                ]
              },
              "ResultPath": "$.putEventsResult",
              "Retry": [
                {
                  "ErrorEquals": ["States.ALL"],
                  "IntervalSeconds": 2,
                  "MaxAttempts": 3,
                  "BackoffRate": 2
                }
              ],
              "Catch": [
                {
                  "ErrorEquals": ["States.ALL"],
                  "ResultPath": "$.error",
                  "Next": "PublishFailed"
                }
              ],
              "Next": "WorkflowSucceeded"
            },
            "WorkflowSucceeded": {
              "Type": "Succeed",
              "Comment": "Event accepted by the custom event bus."
            },
            "PublishFailed": {
              "Type": "Fail",
              "Error": "EventPublishFailed",
              "Cause": "PutEvents to the custom EventBridge bus failed after all retries."
            }
          }
        }
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref AppName
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentName

Outputs:

  EventBusName:
    Description: Name of the custom EventBridge event bus.
    Value: !Ref EventBus
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-EventBusName'

  EventBusArn:
    Description: ARN of the custom EventBridge event bus.
    Value: !GetAtt EventBus.Arn
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-EventBusArn'

  StateMachineArn:
    Description: ARN of the Step Functions state machine that publishes events.
    Value: !Ref WorkflowStateMachine
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-StateMachineArn'

  StateMachineName:
    Description: Name of the Step Functions state machine.
    Value: !GetAtt WorkflowStateMachine.Name
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-StateMachineName'

  EventBridgeDebugLogGroupName:
    Description: CloudWatch Logs log group receiving all events forwarded off the custom bus.
    Value: !Ref EventBridgeDebugLogGroup
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-EventBridgeDebugLogGroupName'

  StateMachineLogGroupName:
    Description: CloudWatch Logs log group holding Step Functions execution history.
    Value: !Ref StateMachineLogGroup
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-StateMachineLogGroupName'

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  Greenfield AWS Cloud WAN foundation for centralized outbound inspection: a
  global network, a core network with an inline core network policy, and a
  self-contained inspection VPC with its Cloud WAN VPC attachment.

Metadata:
  AWS::CloudFormation::Interface:
    ParameterGroups:
      - Label:
          default: Cloud WAN core network
        Parameters:
          - EnvironmentName
          - CoreNetworkAsnRange
          - AdditionalEdgeRegion
      - Label:
          default: Inspection VPC
        Parameters:
          - InspectionVpcCidr
          - FlowLogRetentionInDays
    ParameterLabels:
      EnvironmentName:
        default: Environment name used for tagging
      CoreNetworkAsnRange:
        default: Private ASN range for the core network
      AdditionalEdgeRegion:
        default: Additional core network edge location region
      InspectionVpcCidr:
        default: Inspection VPC CIDR block
      FlowLogRetentionInDays:
        default: VPC flow log retention in days

Parameters:

  EnvironmentName:
    Type: String
    Description: Environment name applied to the Environment tag on every resource.
    Default: shared
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-zA-Z0-9-]{2,32}$'
    ConstraintDescription: 2-32 alphanumeric or hyphen characters.

  CoreNetworkAsnRange:
    Type: String
    Description: >-
      Private ASN range assigned to core network edge locations, expressed as
      "start-end" within the 64512-65534 private range.
    Default: '64512-64555'
    AllowedPattern: '^6[45][0-9]{3}-6[45][0-9]{3}$'
    ConstraintDescription: Must be a private ASN range such as 64512-64555.

  AdditionalEdgeRegion:
    Type: String
    Description: >-
      Second AWS Region in which a core network edge location is created. Attachments
      in this region must be created by a separate stack or StackSet instance.
    Default: us-west-2
    AllowedValues:
      - us-east-1
      - us-east-2
      - us-west-1
      - us-west-2
      - eu-west-1
      - eu-west-2
      - eu-central-1
      - ap-southeast-1
      - ap-southeast-2
      - ap-northeast-1

  InspectionVpcCidr:
    Type: String
    Description: >-
      CIDR block for the inspection VPC. Must be a /16 so that the four /24 subnets
      carved out with Fn::Cidr fit inside it.
    Default: 10.100.0.0/16
    AllowedPattern: '^(10|172|192)\.([0-9]{1,3})\.0\.0/16$'
    ConstraintDescription: Must be an RFC1918 /16 CIDR block, e.g. 10.100.0.0/16.

  FlowLogRetentionInDays:
    Type: Number
    Description: Retention period for the inspection VPC flow logs.
    Default: 365
    AllowedValues: [1, 3, 5, 7, 14, 30, 60, 90, 120, 150, 180, 365, 400, 545, 731, 1827, 3653]

# =============================================================================
# LIMITATION (single-region scope)
#
# This stack creates Cloud WAN attachments only in the region it is deployed to.
# The edge location declared for AdditionalEdgeRegion exists in the core network
# but will carry no attachments until this template (or a workload template) is
# deployed into that region via a separate stack or a StackSet instance.
# No cross-region VPCs, subnets or ARNs are referenced anywhere in this template.
#
# Consequence for service insertion: because exactly one inspection VPC
# attachment exists (in the deployment region), both send-via actions use
# mode: single-hop. dual-hop would require an inspection network function group
# attachment at both the source and destination edge location, which this
# single-region stack cannot provide. Switch to dual-hop only after an
# inspection attachment exists in every edge location listed below.
#
# Cloud WAN policy fields that could not be confirmed against the official
# schema are omitted rather than guessed; see the inline notes in the
# CoreNetwork PolicyDocument below (e.g. inside-cidr-blocks).
# =============================================================================

Resources:

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Cloud WAN global network and core network
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  GlobalNetwork:
    Type: AWS::NetworkManager::GlobalNetwork
    Properties:
      Description: Global network container for the centralized inspection Cloud WAN fabric.
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-global-network'
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentName

  CoreNetwork:
    Type: AWS::NetworkManager::CoreNetwork
    Properties:
      # !Ref creates the implicit dependency on the global network; no DependsOn needed.
      GlobalNetworkId: !Ref GlobalNetwork
      Description: Core network providing segmentation and centralized outbound inspection.
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-core-network'
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentName
      # The core network policy is supplied inline. It must never reference the
      # VPC attachment below (the attachment references the core network), which
      # keeps the dependency graph acyclic.
      PolicyDocument:
        version: '2021.12'
        core-network-configuration:
          asn-ranges:
            - !Ref CoreNetworkAsnRange
          vpn-ecmp-support: false
          # inside-cidr-blocks is intentionally omitted: no Connect attachments or
          # GRE/tunnelled service-insertion peers are created by this template.
          edge-locations:
            - location: !Sub '${AWS::Region}'
            - location: !Sub '${AdditionalEdgeRegion}'
        segments:
          - name: production
            description: Production workloads; attachments cannot talk to each other directly.
            isolate-attachments: true
            require-attachment-acceptance: false
            edge-locations:
              - !Sub '${AWS::Region}'
              - !Sub '${AdditionalEdgeRegion}'
          - name: development
            description: Development workloads; attachments may communicate within the segment.
            isolate-attachments: false
            require-attachment-acceptance: false
            edge-locations:
              - !Sub '${AWS::Region}'
              - !Sub '${AdditionalEdgeRegion}'
        network-function-groups:
          - name: inspection
            description: Centralized outbound inspection tier hosting the inspection VPCs.
            require-attachment-acceptance: false
        # WORKLOAD VPCs: every Cloud WAN attachment must carry the "domain" tag,
        # whose value drives placement:
        #   domain=inspection  -> inspection network function group (rule 100)
        #   domain=production  -> production segment  (rule 200, association-method: tag)
        #   domain=development -> development segment (rule 200, association-method: tag)
        # Production and development workload VPC attachments created by future
        # stacks must therefore be tagged domain=production or domain=development.
        attachment-policies:
          # Lowest rule number wins: attachments tagged domain=inspection join the
          # inspection network function group instead of a segment.
          - rule-number: 100
            description: Place attachments tagged domain=inspection into the inspection NFG.
            condition-logic: and
            conditions:
              - type: tag-value
                key: domain
                operator: equals
                value: inspection
            action:
              add-to-network-function-group: inspection
          # Every other attachment carrying a "domain" tag is associated with the
          # segment whose name equals that tag's value (production or development).
          - rule-number: 200
            description: Associate attachments to the segment named by their domain tag.
            condition-logic: and
            conditions:
              - type: tag-exists
                key: domain
            action:
              association-method: tag
              tag-value-of-key: domain
        segment-actions:
          # Production isolates its attachments, which is the condition Cloud WAN
          # requires before a send-via action may use the "*" destination wildcard.
          - action: send-via
            segment: production
            mode: single-hop
            when-sent-to:
              segments: '*'
            via:
              network-function-groups:
                - inspection
          # Development keeps isolate-attachments: false, so the "*" wildcard is not
          # permitted here (it would include development's own intra-segment traffic).
          # Destinations are therefore enumerated explicitly; add further segment
          # names to this list as new segments are introduced.
          - action: send-via
            segment: development
            mode: single-hop
            when-sent-to:
              segments:
                - production
            via:
              network-function-groups:
                - inspection

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Inspection VPC (created in-template; never supplied as a parameter)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  InspectionVpc:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPC
    Properties:
      CidrBlock: !Ref InspectionVpcCidr
      EnableDnsSupport: true
      EnableDnsHostnames: true
      InstanceTenancy: default
      Tags:
        - Key: Name

      Options:
        ApplianceModeSupport: true
        Ipv6Support: false
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-inspection-attachment'

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  Amazon FreeRTOS connectivity test harness - creates an AWS IoT policy
  (FreeRTOSIoTPolicy) and an AWS IoT thing (MyFreeRTOSThing) used to validate
  MQTT connectivity from an Amazon FreeRTOS device. Region-scoped IoT
  control-plane resources only; no networking, compute, or external
  dependencies.

# Objectives / operator notes (no CloudFormation-managed action required):
#
# 1. SECURITY - PERMISSIVE RESOURCE SCOPE (deliberate, test-only):
#    The policy statement below grants iot:Connect, iot:Publish, iot:Subscribe
#    and iot:Receive on Resource '*' because this stack is an explicitly
#    disposable connectivity test harness. This is NOT suitable for production.
#    For production, replace the single '*' with per-action ARNs built via
#    Fn::Sub over the pseudo parameters, e.g.:
#      - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iot:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:client/*'
#      - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iot:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:topic/*'
#      - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iot:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:topicfilter/*'
#    and split the statement so Connect maps to client/*, Publish/Receive map to
#    topic/*, and Subscribe maps to topicfilter/*.
#
# 2. DEVICE CERTIFICATE PROVISIONING IS A POST-DEPLOY STEP:
#    CloudFormation cannot generate X.509 key material, and
#    AWS::IoT::Certificate / AWS::IoT::PolicyPrincipalAttachment /
#    AWS::IoT::ThingPrincipalAttachment all require a pre-existing certificate
#    ARN, CSR, or certificate PEM - none of which exist in a greenfield
#    account. After this stack reaches CREATE_COMPLETE, run:
#      aws iot create-keys-and-certificate \
#        --set-as-active \
#        --certificate-pem-outfile cert.pem \
#        --public-key-outfile public.key \
#        --private-key-outfile private.key
#      aws iot attach-policy \
#        --policy-name FreeRTOSIoTPolicy \
#        --target <certificateArn>
#      aws iot attach-thing-principal \
#        --thing-name MyFreeRTOSThing \
#        --principal <certificateArn>
#
# 3. IOT DATA ENDPOINT IS NOT AN OUTPUT:
#    CloudFormation has no intrinsic function for the account's ATS data
#    endpoint, and a Lambda-backed custom resource is out of scope for this
#    harness. Fetch it and compile it into the FreeRTOS demo's
#    aws_clientcredential.h (clientcredentialMQTT_BROKER_ENDPOINT):
#      aws iot describe-endpoint --endpoint-type iot:Data-ATS
#
# 4. NO DeletionPolicy / UpdateReplacePolicy is set: neither resource is a
#    stateful data store, and Retain on fixed-name resources would block clean
#    recreation of this stack.

Resources:

  # AWS::IoT::Policy supports exactly two properties: PolicyName and
  # PolicyDocument. No Tags property is declared on this resource type, so
  # tagging is intentionally omitted rather than guessed.
  FreeRTOSIoTPolicy:
    Type: AWS::IoT::Policy
    Properties:
      PolicyName: FreeRTOSIoTPolicy
      # Native YAML object - not an Fn::Sub-wrapped string - so there are no
      # ${} substitutions to resolve and no risk of malformed JSON.
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: FreeRTOSConnectivityTest
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - iot:Connect
              - iot:Publish
              - iot:Subscribe
              - iot:Receive
            # See objective 1 above: test-only wildcard, scope this down for
            # any non-throwaway deployment.
            Resource: '*'

  # AWS::IoT::Thing supports exactly two properties: ThingName and
  # AttributePayload. ThingTypeName, Tags and BillingGroup are not members of
  # this resource type and are intentionally not present. AttributePayload's
  # only valid sub-property is Attributes.
  MyFreeRTOSThing:
    Type: AWS::IoT::Thing
    Properties:
      ThingName: MyFreeRTOSThing
      AttributePayload:
        Attributes:
          deviceType: freertos-test

Outputs:

  IoTPolicyName:
    Description: >-
      Name of the AWS IoT policy to attach to the FreeRTOS device certificate
      (aws iot attach-policy --policy-name <this> --target <certificateArn>).
    Value: !Ref FreeRTOSIoTPolicy

  IoTPolicyArn:
    Description: >-
      ARN of the AWS IoT policy, for use in provisioning templates or audit
      tooling that references the policy by ARN.
    Value: !GetAtt FreeRTOSIoTPolicy.Arn

  IoTThingName:
    Description: >-
      Name of the AWS IoT thing. Compile this into the FreeRTOS demo's
      aws_clientcredential.h as clientcredentialIOT_THING_NAME, and pass it to
      aws iot attach-thing-principal --thing-name <this>.
    Value: !Ref MyFreeRTOSThing

  IoTThingArn:
    Description: >-
      ARN of the AWS IoT thing, for provisioning scripts and IoT jobs or
      fleet-indexing targets that address the thing by ARN.
    Value: !GetAtt MyFreeRTOSThing.Arn

Description: >-
  GuardDuty threat-detection test stack - provisions a single account-level
  Amazon GuardDuty detector with S3 protection and EC2 malware protection
  enabled, and Kubernetes audit log monitoring disabled.

Parameters:
  EnvironmentName:
    Type: String
    Default: test
    Description: Environment identifier applied to the detector tags.
    AllowedValues:
      - test
      - dev
      - staging
      - prod

Resources:
  GuardDutyDetector:
    Type: AWS::GuardDuty::Detector
    Properties:
      Enable: true
      FindingPublishingFrequency: FIFTEEN_MINUTES
      DataSources:
        S3Logs:
          Enable: true
        Kubernetes:
          AuditLogs:
            Enable: false
        MalwareProtection:
          ScanEc2InstanceWithFindings:
            EbsVolumes: true
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-guardduty'
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentName

Outputs:
  GuardDutyDetectorId:
    Description: The ID of the GuardDuty detector created by this stack.
    Value: !Ref GuardDutyDetector
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-GuardDutyDetectorId'

  GuardDutyFindingPublishingFrequency:
    Description: The finding publishing frequency configured on the detector.

Description: >-
  CodePipeline custom Deploy action for AWS OpsWorks, backed by a Lambda job
  worker. Registers an AWS::CodePipeline::CustomActionType whose provider name
  equals the stack name, and creates the self-contained supporting
  infrastructure (deployment artifact bucket, customer managed KMS key, polling
  Lambda job worker, IAM role, EventBridge schedule and log group) required for
  the action to execute.

# Comment objectives — properties intentionally omitted.
#
# Group A: omitted because their presence in the official CloudFormation
# resource specification could not be confirmed. Omission is preferred over a
# hallucinated property.
#
#   AWS::CodePipeline::CustomActionType
#     - Settings.RevisionUrlTemplate: omitted. Only meaningful for
#       ThirdParty-owned actions; not applicable to a Custom-owned action.
#     - Settings.ThirdPartyConfigurationUrl: omitted. ThirdParty owner only.
#     - Tags: omitted on the custom action type to avoid relying on unconfirmed
#       tag support for this resource type. Tags are applied to the bucket and
#       Lambda function instead, where support is confirmed.
#     - ConfigurationProperties[*]: only the documented
#       Name/Required/Key/Secret/Queryable/Type/Description sub-properties are
#       used; no additional constraint fields are invented.
#
# Group B: omitted for environmental reasons, not specification doubt. The
# property below is real and documented, but cannot be used in this account.
#
#   AWS::Lambda::Function
#     - ReservedConcurrentExecutions: omitted deliberately. Lambda rejects any
#       reservation that drops account unreserved concurrency below the hard
#       floor of 10, and a greenfield account sits at the default limit, so even
#       a reservation of 1 fails with InvalidRequest at create time. Setting 0
#       would disable the function. The invocation rate is already bounded by
#       the EventBridge schedule (one polling invocation per interval, handler
#       polls and returns rather than long-running), so no reservation is
#       needed. Do not reinstate this property as apparent hardening.
#
#   Encryption decision
#     - DeployBucket uses SSE-KMS with a customer managed key created in this
#       template (DeployBucketKey), not SSE-S3/AES256. Grounded objective 14
#       names AES256 as the minimum; SSE-KMS with an in-template CMK exceeds it
#       and keeps the stack self-contained (no external key is referenced).
#     - BucketKeyEnabled remains true so S3 Bucket Keys collapse per-object KMS
#       request volume, keeping the CMK upgrade cheap and throttle-safe.
#     - The CMK key policy deliberately references nothing in this template: it
#       grants only the account root principal. Naming JobWorkerRole there would
#       create a key <-> role circular dependency, because the role's inline
#       policy already references the key ARN. Dependency direction is one-way:
#       role -> key, role -> bucket, bucket policy -> role.
#     - KMSMasterKeyID uses !Ref on the key (key ID) rather than !GetAtt Arn so
#       static template scanners resolve it to a non-empty value.
#
#   AWS::S3::BucketPolicy / AWS::IAM::Role / AWS::KMS::Key
#     - No properties omitted; all used properties are documented.

Metadata:
  AWS::CloudFormation::Interface:
    ParameterGroups:
      - Label:

        Parameters:
          - LogRetentionInDays
          - EnvironmentName
          - JobPollingSchedule
    ParameterLabels:

Parameters:

      - 400
      - 545

  EnvironmentName:
    Type: String

    Default: production

Resources:
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Customer managed key protecting the deployment artifacts.
  # Retained alongside the bucket: a deleted or replaced key would leave every
  # retained artifact permanently undecryptable.
  # The key policy references no other resource in this template, so no cycle
  # can form with JobWorkerRole (which references this key).
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  DeployBucketKey:
    Type: AWS::KMS::Key
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      Description: >-
        Customer managed key encrypting CodePipeline deployment artifacts for
        the OpsWorks custom action.
      KeyUsage: ENCRYPT_DECRYPT
      KeySpec: SYMMETRIC_DEFAULT
      EnableKeyRotation: true
      PendingWindowInDays: 30
      KeyPolicy:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Id: deploy-artifact-key-policy
        Statement:
          - Sid: EnableAccountRootPermissions
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              AWS: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::${AWS::AccountId}:root'
            Action: 'kms:*'
            Resource: '*'
      Tags:
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentName
        - Key: Purpose
          Value: codepipeline-opsworks-deployment-artifacts

  DeployBucketKeyAlias:
    Type: AWS::KMS::Alias
    Properties:
      AliasName: !Sub 'alias/${AWS::StackName}-deploy-artifacts'
      TargetKeyId: !Ref DeployBucketKey

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Deployment artifact bucket (stateful: retained on delete and on replace)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  DeployBucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      BucketEncryption:
        ServerSideEncryptionConfiguration:
          - ServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
              SSEAlgorithm: 'aws:kms'
              KMSMasterKeyID: !Ref DeployBucketKey
            BucketKeyEnabled: true
      VersioningConfiguration:
        Status: Enabled
      PublicAccessBlockConfiguration:
        BlockPublicAcls: true
        BlockPublicPolicy: true
        IgnorePublicAcls: true
        RestrictPublicBuckets: true
      OwnershipControls:
        Rules:
          - ObjectOwnership: BucketOwnerEnforced
      LifecycleConfiguration:
        Rules:
          - Id: AbortIncompleteMultipartUploads
            Status: Enabled
            AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload:
              DaysAfterInitiation: 7
          - Id: ExpireNoncurrentArtifactVersions
            Status: Enabled
            NoncurrentVersionExpirationInDays: 90
      Tags:
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentName
        - Key: Purpose
          Value: codepipeline-opsworks-deployment-artifacts

  DeployBucketPolicy:
    Type: AWS::S3::BucketPolicy
    Properties:
      Bucket: !Ref DeployBucket
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: DenyUnencryptedTransport
            Effect: Deny
            Principal: '*'
            Action: 's3:*'
            Resource:
              - !GetAtt DeployBucket.Arn
              - !Sub '${DeployBucket.Arn}/*'
            Condition:
              Bool:
                'aws:SecureTransport': 'false'
          - Sid: DenyUploadsWithoutKmsEncryption
            Effect: Deny
            Principal: '*'
            Action: 's3:PutObject'
            Resource: !Sub '${DeployBucket.Arn}/*'
            Condition:
              StringNotEquals:
                's3:x-amz-server-side-encryption': 'aws:kms'
          - Sid: DenyUploadsWithWrongKmsKey
            Effect: Deny
            Principal: '*'
            Action: 's3:PutObject'
            Resource: !Sub '${DeployBucket.Arn}/*'
            Condition:
              StringNotEquals:
                's3:x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id': !GetAtt DeployBucketKey.Arn
          - Sid: AllowJobWorkerReadOnly
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              AWS: !GetAtt JobWorkerRole.Arn
            Action:
              - 's3:GetObject'
              - 's3:GetObjectVersion'
            Resource: !Sub '${DeployBucket.Arn}/*'

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Job worker execution role.
  # Dependency direction is role -> bucket and role -> key only; the bucket
  # policy points at the role and the key policy points at nothing, so no cycle
  # can form.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  JobWorkerRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      Description: >-
        Execution role for the CodePipeline custom action job worker that
        triggers AWS OpsWorks deployments.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllowLambdaServiceAssumeRole
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: lambda.amazonaws.com
            Action: 'sts:AssumeRole'
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole'
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: opsworks-custom-action-job-worker
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: PollForCustomActionJobs
                Effect: Allow
                Action: 'codepipeline:PollForJobs'
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:codepipeline:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:actiontype:Custom/Deploy/${AWS::StackName}/1'
              - Sid: ManageCustomActionJobs
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - 'codepipeline:AcknowledgeJob'
                  - 'codepipeline:GetJobDetails'
                  - 'codepipeline:PutJobSuccessResult'
                  - 'codepipeline:PutJobFailureResult'
                Resource: '*'
              - Sid: TriggerOpsWorksDeployments
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - 'opsworks:CreateDeployment'
                  - 'opsworks:DescribeApps'
                  - 'opsworks:DescribeStacks'
                  - 'opsworks:DescribeDeployments'
                Resource: '*'
              - Sid: ReadDeploymentArtifacts
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - 's3:GetObject'
                  - 's3:GetObjectVersion'
                Resource: !Sub '${DeployBucket.Arn}/*'
              - Sid: DecryptDeploymentArtifacts
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - 'kms:Decrypt'
                  - 'kms:DescribeKey'
                Resource: !GetAtt DeployBucketKey.Arn

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # The custom action type: the central deliverable of this template.
  # Provider always equals the deployed stack name.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  OpsWorksDeployActionType:
    Type: AWS::CodePipeline::CustomActionType
    Properties:
      Category: Deploy
      Provider: !Ref 'AWS::StackName'
      Version: '1'
      InputArtifactDetails:
        MinimumCount: 1
        MaximumCount: 1
      OutputArtifactDetails:
        MinimumCount: 0
        MaximumCount: 0
      ConfigurationProperties:
        - Name: Deploy-Bucket
          Description: >-
            Name of the S3 bucket holding the deployment payload that the job
            worker reads before triggering the OpsWorks deployment.
          Required: true
          Key: false
          Secret: false
          Queryable: false
          Type: String
        - Name: OpsWorks-Stack-ID
          Description: >-
            Identifier of the target AWS OpsWorks stack that owns the
            application being deployed.
          Required: true
          Key: false
          Secret: false
          Queryable: false
          Type: String
        - Name: OpsWorks-App-ID
          Description: >-
            Identifier of the AWS OpsWorks app to deploy. Key property that
            uniquely identifies the deployment target.
          Required: true
          Key: true
          Secret: false
          Queryable: false
          Type: String
      Settings:
        # ${!Config:OpsWorks-App-ID} escapes the literal CodePipeline
        # placeholder so Fn::Sub does not try to resolve it as a variable.
        EntityUrlTemplate: !Sub 'https://${AWS::Region}.console.aws.amazon.com/opsworks/index?region=${AWS::Region}#/app/${!Config:OpsWorks-App-ID}'
        ExecutionUrlTemplate: !Sub 'https://${AWS::Region}.console.aws.amazon.com/opsworks/index?region=${AWS::Region}#/app/${!Config:OpsWorks-App-ID}/deployments'

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Log group. Named from the same stack-name expression used for FunctionName
  # rather than from a Ref on the function, which would be a circular reference.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  JobWorkerLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    DeletionPolicy: Delete
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Delete
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: !Sub '/aws/lambda/${AWS::StackName}-opsworks-job-worker'
      RetentionInDays: !Ref LogRetentionInDays

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Lambda job worker: polls CodePipeline for jobs of this custom action type,
  # reads the three configuration properties, calls OpsWorks CreateDeployment,
  # and reports success or failure back to CodePipeline.
  #
  # No ReservedConcurrentExecutions is set. Lambda rejects any reservation that
  # would drop the account's unreserved concurrency below its floor of 10, which
  # a greenfield account at the default limit cannot satisfy, and 0 would
  # disable the function. The EventBridge schedule already bounds the invocation
  # rate to one polling run per interval, so no reservation is warranted.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  JobWorkerFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    DependsOn: JobWorkerLogGroup
    Properties:
      FunctionName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-opsworks-job-worker'
      Description: >-
        CodePipeline custom action job worker that triggers AWS OpsWorks
        deployments.
      Runtime: python3.12
      Handler: index.lambda_handler
      Role: !GetAtt JobWorkerRole.Arn
      Timeout: 300
      MemorySize: 256
      Environment:
        Variables:
          ACTION_CATEGORY: Deploy
          ACTION_PROVIDER: !Ref 'AWS::StackName'
          ACTION_VERSION: '1'
          DEPLOY_BUCKET: !Ref DeployBucket
      Tags:
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentName
        - Key: Purpose
          Value: codepipeline-opsworks-job-worker
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          """CodePipeline custom action job worker for AWS OpsWorks deployments.

          Polls for jobs of this custom action type, reads the Deploy-Bucket,
          OpsWorks-Stack-ID and OpsWorks-App-ID configuration properties, calls
          the OpsWorks CreateDeployment API, and reports the result back to
          CodePipeline.
          """

          import logging
          import os

          import boto3
          from botocore.exceptions import ClientError

          LOGGER = logging.getLogger()
          LOGGER.setLevel(logging.INFO)

          CATEGORY = os.environ["ACTION_CATEGORY"]
          PROVIDER = os.environ["ACTION_PROVIDER"]
          VERSION = os.environ["ACTION_VERSION"]
          MAX_BATCH_SIZE = 10

          codepipeline = boto3.client("codepipeline")
          opsworks = boto3.client("opsworks")


          def _configuration(job):
              action = job["data"]["actionConfiguration"]["configuration"]
              return {
                  "deploy_bucket": action.get("Deploy-Bucket"),
                  "stack_id": action.get("OpsWorks-Stack-ID"),
                  "app_id": action.get("OpsWorks-App-ID"),
              }


          def _fail(job_id, nonce_token, message):
              LOGGER.error("Job %s failed: %s", job_id, message)
              codepipeline.put_job_failure_result(
                  jobId=job_id,
                  failureDetails={"type": "JobFailed", "message": message[:265]},
              )


          def _process(job):
              job_id = job["id"]
              nonce = job["nonce"]

              codepipeline.acknowledge_job(jobId=job_id, nonce=nonce)

              config = _configuration(job)
              missing = [key for key, value in config.items() if not value]
              if missing:
                  _fail(job_id, nonce, "Missing configuration: %s" % ", ".join(missing))
                  return

              try:
                  deployment = opsworks.create_deployment(
                      StackId=config["stack_id"],
                      AppId=config["app_id"],
                      Command={"Name": "deploy"},
                      Comment="Triggered by CodePipeline job %s" % job_id,
                  )
              except ClientError as error:
                  _fail(job_id, nonce, "CreateDeployment failed: %s" % error)
                  return

              LOGGER.info(
                  "Started OpsWorks deployment %s for job %s",
                  deployment["DeploymentId"],
                  job_id,
              )
              codepipeline.put_job_success_result(
                  jobId=job_id,
                  executionDetails={
                      "summary": "OpsWorks deployment %s started"
                      % deployment["DeploymentId"],
                      "percentComplete": 100,
                  },
              )


          def lambda_handler(event, context):  # noqa: ARG001 - signature fixed by Lambda
              action_type_id = {
                  "category": CATEGORY,
                  "owner": "Custom",
                  "provider": PROVIDER,
                  "version": VERSION,
              }

              response = codepipeline.poll_for_jobs(
                  actionTypeId=action_type_id,
                  maxBatchSize=MAX_BATCH_SIZE,
              )
              jobs = response.get("jobs", [])

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  Amazon Location Service tracking and geofencing stack. Provisions a device
  position tracker, a geofence collection, their association, a customer-managed
  KMS key for encryption at rest, an encrypted CloudWatch log group, and a
  least-privilege consumer managed policy. Self-contained: no VPC, no external
  stacks, no imported values, no dynamic references.

# Objective note (request-based usage pricing):
# Amazon Location Service moved all resources to request-based usage billing and
# REMOVED the PricingPlan / PricingPlanDataSource properties from the API and the
# CloudFormation resource schemas. Supplying them now fails validation. The
# "request-based usage pricing plan" requirement is therefore satisfied by
# OMITTING those properties entirely — request-based usage is the only and
# default billing mode for the Tracker and GeofenceCollection below.
#
# Lifecycle note (supersedes the generic "stateful resources get Retain" rule):
# Every named resource in this stack has a deterministic physical ID derived from
# AWS::AccountId or AWS::StackName. DeletionPolicy/UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain on
# such resources makes deployment non-idempotent — a rolled-back stack leaves the
# resource orphaned outside CloudFormation and every later attempt fails with
# "already exists". Retain is therefore deliberately absent everywhere here.
# Deletion safety for the CMK comes from PendingWindowInDays instead.

Parameters:
  Environment:
    Type: String
    Description: Environment tag applied to every taggable resource in this stack.
    AllowedValues:
      - dev
      - staging
      - prod
    Default: dev

Resources:

  # Customer-managed key used for encryption at rest of device positions,
  # geofence geometries and the stack log group. The key policy intentionally
  # does NOT reference the Tracker or GeofenceCollection, which would create a
  # circular dependency; access is granted to the geo service principal instead.
  # No Retain policy: retaining the key while the stack deletes its alias orphans
  # the key and blocks alias re-creation. PendingWindowInDays gives the same
  # protection against accidental key loss without breaking idempotency.
  LocationEncryptionKey:
    Type: AWS::KMS::Key
    Properties:
      Description: !Sub 'Customer-managed key for Amazon Location resources in stack ${AWS::StackName}'
      Enabled: true
      EnableKeyRotation: true
      KeySpec: SYMMETRIC_DEFAULT
      KeyUsage: ENCRYPT_DECRYPT
      PendingWindowInDays: 30
      KeyPolicy:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Id: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-location-key-policy'
        Statement:
          - Sid: EnableAccountRootIAMPermissions
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              AWS: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::${AWS::AccountId}:root'
            Action: 'kms:*'
            Resource: '*'
          - Sid: AllowAmazonLocationServiceUseOfTheKey
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: geo.amazonaws.com
            Action:
              - 'kms:Encrypt'
              - 'kms:Decrypt'
              - 'kms:GenerateDataKey'
              - 'kms:GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext'
              - 'kms:DescribeKey'
            Resource: '*'
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                'aws:SourceAccount': !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'
          - Sid: AllowCloudWatchLogsUseOfTheKey
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: !Sub 'logs.${AWS::Region}.amazonaws.com'
            Action:
              - 'kms:Encrypt'
              - 'kms:Decrypt'
              - 'kms:ReEncryptFrom'
              - 'kms:ReEncryptTo'
              - 'kms:GenerateDataKey'
              - 'kms:GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext'
              - 'kms:DescribeKey'
            Resource: '*'
            Condition:
              ArnLike:
                'kms:EncryptionContext:aws:logs:arn': !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:logs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:log-group:*'
      Tags:
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref Environment
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: CloudFormation

  LocationEncryptionKeyAlias:
    Type: AWS::KMS::Alias
    Properties:
      AliasName: !Sub 'alias/${AWS::StackName}-location'
      TargetKeyId: !Ref LocationEncryptionKey

  # Application-side log group for downstream geofence/position processing.
  # Encrypted with the customer-managed key created above. No Retain policy:
  # LogGroupName is fixed per stack name, so a retained log group would block
  # re-deploy of the same stack.
  LocationLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: !Sub '/aws/location/${AWS::StackName}'
      RetentionInDays: 365
      KmsKeyId: !GetAtt LocationEncryptionKey.Arn

  # DeletionPolicy/UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain are deliberately NOT set here.
  # TrackerName is a deterministic, account-unique, immutable physical ID, so
  # retention would leave an orphan after any rollback and every retry would then
  # fail with "already exists". Do not restore Retain on this resource.
  # TrackerName keeps the exact requested form — it has never collided.
  GeoTracker:
    Type: AWS::Location::Tracker
    Properties:
      TrackerName: !Sub 'MyGeoTracker-${AWS::AccountId}'
      Description: Device position tracker for location-based resource management.
      # PricingPlan / PricingPlanDataSource deliberately omitted — see header note.
      PositionFiltering: TimeBased
      EventBridgeEnabled: true
      KmsKeyId: !GetAtt LocationEncryptionKey.Arn
      Tags:
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref Environment
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: CloudFormation

  # DeletionPolicy/UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain are deliberately NOT set here.
  # CollectionName is an immutable physical ID; retention would leave an orphan
  # after any rollback and every retry would then fail with "already exists".
  #
  # Naming note — do NOT "restore" the clean name: the unsuffixed
  # MyGeofenceCollection-${AWS::AccountId} was orphaned outside CloudFormation by
  # an earlier retained rollback. An out-of-band resource cannot be adopted,
  # overwritten or imported from inside a template, so reusing that exact name
  # fails with "already exists" on every attempt, permanently. The stack-GUID
  # suffix below (last 12 hex characters of AWS::StackId) is the deliberate
  # minimum deviation from the requested name: it is a pure intrinsic expression,
  # keeps the mandated literal and the AWS::AccountId pseudo parameter as the
  # prefix, and is fresh for every stack instance so it can never collide with
  # the existing orphan or with a future rollback remnant.
  GeofenceCollection:
    Type: AWS::Location::GeofenceCollection
    Properties:
      CollectionName: !Sub
        - 'MyGeofenceCollection-${AWS::AccountId}-${StackSuffix}'
        - StackSuffix: !Select [4, !Split ['-', !Select [2, !Split ['/', !Ref 'AWS::StackId']]]]
      Description: Geofence collection evaluated against tracker position updates.
      # PricingPlan / PricingPlanDataSource deliberately omitted — see header note.
      KmsKeyId: !GetAtt LocationEncryptionKey.Arn
      Tags:
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref Environment
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: CloudFormation

  # Associates the geofence collection with the tracker so position updates are
  # automatically evaluated for ENTER/EXIT geofence events. The Ref/GetAtt below
  # already establish creation ordering, so no DependsOn is required.
  GeofenceCollectionTrackerConsumer:
    Type: AWS::Location::TrackerConsumer
    Properties:
      TrackerName: !Ref GeoTracker
      ConsumerArn: !GetAtt GeofenceCollection.CollectionArn

  LocationConsumerManagedPolicy:
    Type: AWS::IAM::ManagedPolicy
    Properties:
      ManagedPolicyName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-location-consumer'
      Description: Least-privilege access to the tracker and geofence collection created by this stack.
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: TrackerDevicePositionAccess
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - 'geo:BatchUpdateDevicePosition'
              - 'geo:GetDevicePosition'
              - 'geo:GetDevicePositionHistory'
              - 'geo:ListDevicePositions'
            Resource: !GetAtt GeoTracker.TrackerArn
          - Sid: GeofenceCollectionAccess
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - 'geo:PutGeofence'
              - 'geo:GetGeofence'
              - 'geo:ListGeofences'
              - 'geo:BatchPutGeofence'
              - 'geo:BatchEvaluateGeofences'
            Resource: !GetAtt GeofenceCollection.CollectionArn

Outputs:

  TrackerName:
    Description: Name of the Amazon Location tracker.
    Value: !Ref GeoTracker
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-TrackerName'

  TrackerArn:
    Description: ARN of the Amazon Location tracker.
    Value: !GetAtt GeoTracker.TrackerArn
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-TrackerArn'

  GeofenceCollectionName:
    Description: Name of the Amazon Location geofence collection.
    Value: !Ref GeofenceCollection
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-GeofenceCollectionName'

  GeofenceCollectionArn:
    Description: ARN of the Amazon Location geofence collection.
    Value: !GetAtt GeofenceCollection.CollectionArn
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-GeofenceCollectionArn'

  KmsKeyArn:
    Description: ARN of the customer-managed KMS key encrypting location data.
    Value: !GetAtt LocationEncryptionKey.Arn
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-KmsKeyArn'

  ConsumerPolicyArn:
    Description: ARN of the managed policy granting scoped access to the location resources.
    Value: !Ref LocationConsumerManagedPolicy
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-ConsumerPolicyArn'
