AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  Provisions the foundational infrastructure for ECS Anywhere: an ECS cluster,
  the external-instance IAM role used by hybrid-activated nodes, an ECS task
  execution role, and the SSM Command document that registers an external
  container instance with the cluster. NOTE: hybrid activations are not an
  available CloudFormation resource type, so the activation id and activation
  code must be produced out-of-band with `aws ssm create-activation` (using the
  external instance role emitted in the Outputs) and supplied as document
  parameters at execution time.

Parameters:

  ClusterName:
    Type: String
    Default: ecs-anywhere-cluster
    Description: Name of the ECS cluster that external instances register with.
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9-_]{0,254}$'
    MinLength: 1
    MaxLength: 255
    ConstraintDescription: >-
      Must start with a letter or number and contain only letters, numbers,
      hyphens and underscores (1-255 characters).

  ContainerInstanceName:
    Type: String
    Default: ecs-anywhere-instance
    Description: >-
      Default name applied to the registered external container instance. Used
      as the default value of the SSM document's ContainerInstanceName
      parameter and may be overridden per document execution.
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9-_]{0,63}$'
    MinLength: 1
    MaxLength: 64
    ConstraintDescription: >-
      Must start with a letter or number and contain only letters, numbers,
      hyphens and underscores (1-64 characters).

Resources:

  # Log group for ECS Anywhere agent / ECS Exec session output. Retained on
  # stack delete and replace so operational history survives stack churn.
  EcsAnywhereLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: !Sub '/aws/ecs/anywhere/${ClusterName}'
      RetentionInDays: 30
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${ClusterName}-logs'
        - Key: Purpose
          Value: ecs-anywhere

  # ECS Anywhere external instances live outside AWS networking, so no VPC,
  # subnet, security group, AMI, key pair or capacity provider is created or
  # referenced anywhere in this template.
  EcsCluster:
    Type: AWS::ECS::Cluster
    Properties:
      ClusterName: !Ref ClusterName
      ClusterSettings:
        - Name: containerInsights
          Value: enabled
      Configuration:
        ExecuteCommandConfiguration:
          Logging: OVERRIDE
          LogConfiguration:
            CloudWatchLogGroupName: !Ref EcsAnywhereLogGroup
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Ref ClusterName
        - Key: Purpose
          Value: ecs-anywhere
        - Key: InstanceType
          Value: external

  # Role assumed by external instances: as an SSM hybrid managed node via
  # ssm.amazonaws.com, and as an ECS container instance via ec2.amazonaws.com.
  EcsAnywhereInstanceRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      Description: >-
        Allows on-premises / external instances to register as SSM managed
        nodes and as ECS Anywhere container instances.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service:
                - ssm.amazonaws.com
                - ec2.amazonaws.com
            Action: 'sts:AssumeRole'
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - 'arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore'
        - 'arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AmazonEC2ContainerServiceforEC2Role'
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: EcsAnywhereContainerInstanceRegistration
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: ClusterScopedRegistration
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - 'ecs:RegisterContainerInstance'
                  - 'ecs:DeregisterContainerInstance'
                  - 'ecs:UpdateContainerInstancesState'
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:ecs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:cluster/${ClusterName}'
              - Sid: ContainerInstanceScopedAgentCalls
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - 'ecs:Poll'
                  - 'ecs:StartTelemetrySession'
                  - 'ecs:Submit*'
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:ecs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:container-instance/${ClusterName}/*'
              - Sid: DiscoverPollEndpoint
                Effect: Allow
                # ecs:DiscoverPollEndpoint does not support resource-level
                # permissions and must be granted on "*".
                Action: 'ecs:DiscoverPollEndpoint'
                Resource: '*'
        - PolicyName: EcsAnywhereAgentLogging
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: WriteAgentLogs
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - 'logs:CreateLogStream'
                  - 'logs:PutLogEvents'
                  - 'logs:DescribeLogStreams'
                Resource: !Sub '${EcsAnywhereLogGroup.Arn}:*'
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${ClusterName}-external-instance-role'
        - Key: Purpose
          Value: ecs-anywhere

  # Task execution role so workloads placed on the external instances can pull
  # images and write logs without needing a second stack.
  EcsTaskExecutionRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      Description: Execution role for ECS tasks running on ECS Anywhere external instances.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com
            Action: 'sts:AssumeRole'
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                'aws:SourceAccount': !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'
              ArnLike:
                'aws:SourceArn': !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:ecs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:*'
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - 'arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AmazonECSTaskExecutionRolePolicy'
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: EcsAnywhereTaskLogging
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: WriteTaskLogs
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - 'logs:CreateLogStream'
                  - 'logs:PutLogEvents'
                Resource: !Sub '${EcsAnywhereLogGroup.Arn}:*'
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${ClusterName}-task-execution-role'
        - Key: Purpose
          Value: ecs-anywhere

  # Attach this policy to the operator or automation identity that runs
  # `aws ssm create-activation` — the activation itself cannot be created by
  # CloudFormation, so it is produced out-of-band.
  EcsAnywhereActivationOperatorPolicy:
    Type: AWS::IAM::ManagedPolicy
    Properties:
      ManagedPolicyName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-ecs-anywhere-activation-operator'
      Description: >-
        Permits creating SSM hybrid activations that pass the ECS Anywhere
        external instance role.
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: CreateHybridActivation
            Effect: Allow
            # ssm:CreateActivation does not support resource-level permissions.
            Action: 'ssm:CreateActivation'
            Resource: '*'
          - Sid: PassExternalInstanceRoleToSsm
            Effect: Allow
            Action: 'iam:PassRole'
            Resource: !GetAtt EcsAnywhereInstanceRole.Arn
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                'iam:PassedToService': ssm.amazonaws.com

  # Registration document. SSM mustache substitution ({{ Name }}) is used for
  # document parameters; CloudFormation ${...} substitution appears only inside
  # Fn::Sub blocks. ActivationId / ActivationCode have no defaults and must be
  # supplied at execution time — no secret material is embedded in this stack.
  EcsAnywhereRegistrationDocument:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Document
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-ecs-anywhere-registration'
      DocumentType: Command
      DocumentFormat: YAML
      TargetType: /
      UpdateMethod: NewVersion
      Content:
        schemaVersion: '2.2'
        description: >-
          Installs the ECS Anywhere agent on an external Linux host and
          registers it as a container instance in the ECS cluster created by
          this stack.
        parameters:
          ClusterName:
            type: String
            description: ECS cluster the external instance registers with.
            default: !Sub '${ClusterName}'
            allowedPattern: '^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9-_]{0,254}$'
          ContainerInstanceName:
            type: String
            description: Name recorded as a custom attribute on the container instance.
            default: !Sub '${ContainerInstanceName}'
            allowedPattern: '^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9-_]{0,63}$'
          ActivationId:
            type: String
            description: >-
              SSM hybrid activation id produced out-of-band by
              `aws ssm create-activation`. Supplied at execution time.
            allowedPattern: '^[a-f0-9-]{36}$'
          ActivationCode:
            type: String
            description: >-
              SENSITIVE. SSM hybrid activation code produced out-of-band by
              `aws ssm create-activation`. Must be supplied at execution time
              only and is never stored in this template or stack.
            allowedPattern: '^[a-zA-Z0-9+/=]{20,250}$'
        mainSteps:
          - action: 'aws:runShellScript'
            name: InstallAndRegisterEcsAnywhereAgent
            precondition:
              StringEquals:
                - platformType
                - Linux
            inputs:
              timeoutSeconds: '3600'
              runCommand:
                - '#!/bin/bash'
                - 'set -euo pipefail'
                - 'umask 077'
                - 'WORKDIR=$(mktemp -d)'
                - 'trap "rm -rf $WORKDIR" EXIT'
                - 'curl --proto "=https" --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://amazon-ecs-agent.s3.amazonaws.com/ecs-anywhere-install-latest.sh -o $WORKDIR/ecs-anywhere-install.sh'
                - 'curl --proto "=https" --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://amazon-ecs-agent.s3.amazonaws.com/ecs-anywhere-install-latest.sh.sha256 -o $WORKDIR/ecs-anywhere-install.sh.sha256'
                - 'cd $WORKDIR && sha256sum --check ecs-anywhere-install.sh.sha256'
                - !Sub >-
                  bash $WORKDIR/ecs-anywhere-install.sh
                  --region "${AWS::Region}"
                  --cluster "{{ ClusterName }}"
                  --activation-id "{{ ActivationId }}"
                  --activation-code "{{ ActivationCode }}"
                - 'mkdir -p /etc/ecs'
                - 'grep -q "^ECS_INSTANCE_ATTRIBUTES=" /etc/ecs/ecs.config 2>/dev/null || echo "ECS_INSTANCE_ATTRIBUTES={\"instance-name\":\"{{ ContainerInstanceName }}\"}" >> /etc/ecs/ecs.config'
                - 'grep -q "^ECS_CLUSTER=" /etc/ecs/ecs.config 2>/dev/null || echo "ECS_CLUSTER={{ ClusterName }}" >> /etc/ecs/ecs.config'
                - 'systemctl restart ecs'
                - 'systemctl is-active --quiet ecs && echo "ECS Anywhere agent registered instance {{ ContainerInstanceName }} into cluster {{ ClusterName }}"'
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${ClusterName}-registration-document'
        - Key: Purpose
          Value: ecs-anywhere

# Properties are limited to those confirmed in the official CloudFormation
# resource specification for AWS::ECS::Cluster, AWS::IAM::Role,
# AWS::IAM::ManagedPolicy, AWS::SSM::Document and AWS::Logs::LogGroup.
# Deliberately omitted because their validity for these resource types is not
# confirmed: AWS::SSM::Document VersionName/Requires, AWS::ECS::Cluster
# ServiceConnectDefaults and CapacityProviders (external instances do not use
# capacity providers), and AWS::Logs::LogGroup DataProtectionPolicy.
# No DependsOn is declared anywhere: !Ref / !GetAtt already establish the
# required ordering between the cluster, roles, log group and document.

Outputs:

  ClusterNameOutput:
    Description: Name of the ECS Anywhere cluster.
    Value: !Ref EcsCluster
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-ClusterName'

  ClusterArn:
    Description: ARN of the ECS Anywhere cluster.
    Value: !GetAtt EcsCluster.Arn
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-ClusterArn'

  ExternalInstanceRoleName:
    Description: >-
      Name of the external instance role. Pass to
      `aws ssm create-activation --iam-role <this value>`.
    Value: !Ref EcsAnywhereInstanceRole
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-ExternalInstanceRoleName'

  ExternalInstanceRoleArn:
    Description: ARN of the ECS Anywhere external instance role.
    Value: !GetAtt EcsAnywhereInstanceRole.Arn
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-ExternalInstanceRoleArn'

  TaskExecutionRoleArn:
    Description: ARN of the ECS task execution role for workloads on external instances.
    Value: !GetAtt EcsTaskExecutionRole.Arn
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-TaskExecutionRoleArn'

  RegistrationDocumentName:
    Description: Name of the SSM document that registers external container instances.
    Value: !Ref EcsAnywhereRegistrationDocument
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-RegistrationDocumentName'

  ActivationOperatorPolicyArn:
    Description: >-
      Managed policy granting ssm:CreateActivation and scoped iam:PassRole for
      the identity that creates hybrid activations out-of-band.
    Value: !Ref EcsAnywhereActivationOperatorPolicy
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-ActivationOperatorPolicyArn'

  LogGroupName:
    Description: CloudWatch Logs group for ECS Anywhere agent and ECS Exec output.
    Value: !Ref EcsAnywhereLogGroup
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-LogGroupName'

Description: >-
  Deployment IAM stack - creates a deployment IAM user, an IAM group, and a
  customer-managed policy granting CloudWatch Logs write access and CloudWatch
  metrics publish/read access. The user is added to the group and the managed
  policy is attached to the group. Self-contained: no external stacks, no
  dynamic references, no account-specific identifiers. Deploy with
  CAPABILITY_NAMED_IAM because explicit UserName, GroupName, and
  ManagedPolicyName values are set; if those names were omitted and left to
  CloudFormation, CAPABILITY_IAM would be sufficient.

Parameters:
  AppName:
    Type: String
    Default: deployment
    Description: Application name used to derive IAM resource names and tags.
    MinLength: 1
    MaxLength: 32
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-zA-Z0-9-]+$'
    ConstraintDescription: Must contain only alphanumeric characters and hyphens.

  Environment:
    Type: String
    Default: dev
    Description: Deployment environment used to derive IAM resource names and tags.
    AllowedValues:
      - dev
      - staging
      - prod

Resources:
  # IAM group that carries the deployment permissions. AWS::IAM::Group does not
  # support a Tags property in CloudFormation, so tags are omitted here.
  DeploymentGroup:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Group
    Properties:
      GroupName: !Sub '${AppName}-${Environment}-deploy-group'
      Path: /

  # IAM user for deployment automation. Membership is established with the
  # Groups property, which creates the implicit dependency on DeploymentGroup.
  DeploymentUser:
    Type: AWS::IAM::User
    Properties:
      UserName: !Sub '${AppName}-${Environment}-deploy-user'
      Path: /
      Groups:
        - !Ref DeploymentGroup
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref AppName
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref Environment
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: CloudFormation

  # Customer-managed policy attached to the group (not directly to the user).
  # AWS::IAM::ManagedPolicy does not support a Tags property, so tags are omitted.
  #
  # Resource: '*' is used as explicitly requested. Note that
  # cloudwatch:PutMetricData, cloudwatch:ListMetrics and cloudwatch:GetMetricData
  # do not support resource-level permissions and must be granted on '*'. The
  # logs:CreateLogGroup / logs:CreateLogStream / logs:PutLogEvents actions could
  # optionally be narrowed in a separate statement to
  # !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:logs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:log-group:*'
  # if tighter scoping is later required.
  DeploymentPolicy:
    Type: AWS::IAM::ManagedPolicy
    Properties:
      ManagedPolicyName: !Sub '${AppName}-${Environment}-deploy-policy'
      Description: !Sub 'CloudWatch Logs and CloudWatch metrics permissions for the ${AppName} ${Environment} deployment group.'
      Path: /
      Groups:
        - !Ref DeploymentGroup
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: CloudWatchLogsAndMetricsAccess
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - logs:CreateLogGroup
              - logs:CreateLogStream
              - logs:PutLogEvents
              - cloudwatch:PutMetricData
              - cloudwatch:ListMetrics
              - cloudwatch:GetMetricData
            Resource: '*'

Outputs:
  DeploymentUserName:
    Description: Name of the deployment IAM user.
    Value: !Ref DeploymentUser
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-DeploymentUserName'

  DeploymentUserArn:
    Description: ARN of the deployment IAM user.
    Value: !GetAtt DeploymentUser.Arn
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-DeploymentUserArn'

  DeploymentGroupName:
    Description: Name of the deployment IAM group.
    Value: !Ref DeploymentGroup
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-DeploymentGroupName'

  DeploymentGroupArn:
    Description: ARN of the deployment IAM group.
    Value: !GetAtt DeploymentGroup.Arn
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-DeploymentGroupArn'

  DeploymentPolicyArn:
    Description: ARN of the customer-managed deployment policy.
    Value: !Ref DeploymentPolicy
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-DeploymentPolicyArn'

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  Unauthenticated chatbot identity stack - creates a Cognito Identity Pool that
  grants guest (unauthenticated) users least-privilege credentials for Amazon Lex
  runtime, Amazon Translate, and Amazon Comprehend inference, plus Cognito Sync
  and Mobile Analytics. Identity-only stack; no networking, compute, or storage.

Parameters:
  AppName:
    Type: String
    Default: chatbot
    Description: >-
      Application/environment name used for resource naming, tagging, and output
      exports. Must be safe for use in IAM role and Cognito pool names.
    MinLength: 1
    MaxLength: 48
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9-]*$'
    ConstraintDescription: >-
      Must start with an alphanumeric character and contain only alphanumeric
      characters and hyphens (1-48 characters).

Resources:

  # Unauthenticated-only identity pool. No CognitoIdentityProviders,
  # SupportedLoginProviders, SamlProviderARNs, or OpenIdConnectProviderARNs are
  # configured: this is a greenfield account with no external identity provider,
  # and the chatbot serves anonymous guests exclusively.
  ChatbotIdentityPool:
    Type: AWS::Cognito::IdentityPool
    Properties:
      IdentityPoolName: !Sub '${AppName}-identity-pool'
      AllowUnauthenticatedIdentities: true
      AllowClassicFlow: false
      IdentityPoolTags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref AppName
        - Key: Purpose
          Value: unauthenticated-chatbot

  # Role assumed by anonymous internet clients via Cognito's web identity
  # federation. The trust policy references the pool (pool -> role is the only
  # dependency direction; the pool never references the role, so no cycle).
  ChatbotUnauthenticatedRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Sub '${AppName}-cognito-unauthenticated-role'
      Description: >-
        Least-privilege role for unauthenticated chatbot guests (Lex runtime,
        Translate, Comprehend inference, Cognito Sync, Mobile Analytics).
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: CognitoUnauthenticatedWebIdentity
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Federated: cognito-identity.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                'cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:aud': !Ref ChatbotIdentityPool
              'ForAnyValue:StringLike':
                'cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:amr': unauthenticated
      # Permissions are attached inline. No AWS-managed policies are attached:
      # these credentials are handed to anonymous internet clients, so anything
      # broader than the statements below (PowerUserAccess, ReadOnlyAccess, etc.)
      # would be an unacceptable exposure.
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: !Sub '${AppName}-chatbot-guest-access'
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:

              # UNCERTAINTY: Lex V1 (`lex:`) and Lex V2 (`lexv2:`) use distinct
              # action prefixes and distinct ARN formats. Both runtime action
              # sets are granted here because the target Lex version was not
              # specified; remove whichever set does not apply.
              # This template does not create the bot itself. If a bot must live
              # in the same stack, add an AWS::Lex::Bot (and alias) resource and
              # scope Resource below to its ARN via !GetAtt instead of '*'.
              # Runtime-only: all build-time/model-management actions (CreateBot,
              # PutIntent, BuildBotLocale, StartImport, ...) are excluded.
              - Sid: LexV1RuntimeAccess
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - lex:PostText
                  - lex:PostContent
                  - lex:PutSession
                  - lex:GetSession
                  - lex:DeleteSession
                Resource: '*'

              - Sid: LexV2RuntimeAccess
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - lexv2:RecognizeText
                  - lexv2:RecognizeUtterance
                  - lexv2:PutSession
                  - lexv2:GetSession
                  - lexv2:DeleteSession
                Resource: '*'

              # Amazon Translate and Amazon Comprehend synchronous inference
              # APIs do not support resource-level permissions, so '*' is the
              # only valid Resource. comprehend:DetectDominantLanguage is
              # required for Translate's automatic source-language detection.
              # Comprehend is limited to read-only Detect* inference: no
              # Start*Job, Create*, or model-training actions are granted.
              - Sid: TranslateAndComprehendInference
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - translate:TranslateText
                  - comprehend:DetectDominantLanguage
                  - comprehend:DetectSentiment
                  - comprehend:DetectEntities
                  - comprehend:DetectKeyPhrases
                  - comprehend:DetectSyntax
                Resource: '*'

              # Cognito Sync supports resource-level permissions, so this
              # statement is kept separate from the wildcard statements above
              # and scoped to the identity pool created by this stack.
              - Sid: CognitoSyncScopedToThisPool
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - cognito-sync:ListRecords
                  - cognito-sync:UpdateRecords
                  - cognito-sync:DescribeIdentityPoolUsage
                  - cognito-sync:ListDatasets
                Resource:
                  - !Sub 'arn:aws:cognito-sync:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:identitypool/${ChatbotIdentityPool}'
                  - !Sub 'arn:aws:cognito-sync:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:identitypool/${ChatbotIdentityPool}/*'

              # Amazon Mobile Analytics exposes no resource-level ARN for
              # PutEvents; the service accepts only Resource: '*'.
              - Sid: MobileAnalyticsPutEvents
                Effect: Allow
                Action: mobileanalytics:PutEvents
                Resource: '*'
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref AppName
        - Key: Purpose
          Value: unauthenticated-chatbot

  # Binds the pool to the guest role. The !Ref / !GetAtt references below
  # establish creation ordering on their own, so no DependsOn is declared.
  # Only the "unauthenticated" key is mapped; there is no authenticated flow.
  ChatbotIdentityPoolRoleAttachment:
    Type: AWS::Cognito::IdentityPoolRoleAttachment
    Properties:
      IdentityPoolId: !Ref ChatbotIdentityPool
      Roles:
        unauthenticated: !GetAtt ChatbotUnauthenticatedRole.Arn

# No DeletionPolicy/UpdateReplacePolicy Retain is set: this stack contains no
# stateful data resource. If a chat transcript bucket, DynamoDB table, or other
# durable store is later added here, that resource MUST carry both
# DeletionPolicy: Retain and UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain.

Outputs:
  IdentityPoolId:
    Description: >-
      ID of the Cognito Identity Pool that issues unauthenticated guest
      credentials for the chatbot client.
    Value: !Ref ChatbotIdentityPool
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-IdentityPoolId'

  UnauthenticatedRoleArn:
    Description: >-
      ARN of the IAM role assumed by unauthenticated chatbot guests (for
      operator verification).
    Value: !GetAtt ChatbotUnauthenticatedRole.Arn
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-UnauthenticatedRoleArn'

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  Retail Demo Store - core event-driven infrastructure. Provisions the
  "retaildemostore-bus" EventBridge custom event bus, a disabled catch-all rule
  that delivers every event to a CloudWatch Logs group, a 120-day event archive,
  an EventBridge schema discoverer, and the SSM parameter that publishes the bus
  name to downstream services.

Resources:

  EventBus:
    Type: AWS::Events::EventBus
    Properties:
      Name: retaildemostore-bus
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: RetailDemoStore
        - Key: Component
          Value: EventBus

  EventBusLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: /aws/events/retaildemostore-bus
      RetentionInDays: 120
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: RetailDemoStore
        - Key: Component
          Value: EventBus

  # The delivery permission stays a standalone AWS::Logs::ResourcePolicy:
  # AWS::Logs::LogGroup has no ResourcePolicyDocument property in the official
  # resource specification (only DataProtectionPolicy / FieldIndexPolicies /
  # KmsKeyId / LogGroupClass / LogGroupName / RetentionInDays / Tags), so
  # inlining the document there would fail template validation outright.
  # The serialization that objective 2 targets is removed instead by dropping
  # DependsOn from CatchAllRule below, and the policy contents carry every
  # other change: single events.amazonaws.com principal, no aws:SourceArn
  # clause, and both log-group ARN shapes under Resource.
  EventBusLogGroupResourcePolicy:
    Type: AWS::Logs::ResourcePolicy
    Properties:
      PolicyName: retaildemostore-bus-events-delivery
      PolicyDocument: !Sub |
        {
          "Version": "2012-10-17",
          "Statement": [
            {
              "Sid": "AllowEventBridgeDeliveryToLogGroup",
              "Effect": "Allow",
              "Principal": {
                "Service": "events.amazonaws.com"
              },
              "Action": [
                "logs:CreateLogStream",
                "logs:PutLogEvents"
              ],
              "Resource": [
                "arn:${AWS::Partition}:logs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:log-group:${EventBusLogGroup}",
                "arn:${AWS::Partition}:logs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:log-group:${EventBusLogGroup}:*"
              ],
              "Condition": {
                "StringEquals": {
                  "aws:SourceAccount": "${AWS::AccountId}"
                }
              }
            }
          ]
        }

  CatchAllRule:
    Type: AWS::Events::Rule
    Properties:
      Name: retaildemostore-bus-catch-all
      Description: >-
        Catch-all rule that forwards every event published to the Retail Demo
        Store event bus to CloudWatch Logs. Provisioned DISABLED; enable it
        explicitly when event tracing is required.
      EventBusName: !Ref EventBus
      State: DISABLED
      EventPattern:
        account:
          - !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'
      Targets:
        - Id: CatchAllLogTarget
          Arn: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:logs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:log-group:${EventBusLogGroup}'

  EventBusArchive:
    Type: AWS::Events::Archive
    Properties:
      ArchiveName: retaildemostore-bus-archive
      Description: >-
        Retains all events published to the Retail Demo Store event bus for 120
        days so they can be replayed onto the bus.
      SourceArn: !GetAtt EventBus.Arn
      RetentionDays: 120

  EventBusSchemaDiscoverer:
    Type: AWS::EventSchemas::Discoverer
    Properties:
      Description: >-
        Discovers and registers schemas for events published to the Retail Demo
        Store event bus.
      SourceArn: !GetAtt EventBus.Arn
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: RetailDemoStore
        - Key: Component
          Value: EventBus

  EventBusNameParameter:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Name: RetailDemoStore-eventbus
      Type: String
      Tier: Standard
      Description: >-
        Name of the Retail Demo Store EventBridge event bus. Downstream services
        read this parameter to resolve the bus they publish events to.
      Value: !Ref EventBus
      Tags:
        Application: RetailDemoStore
        Component: EventBus

Outputs:

  EventBusName:
    Description: Name of the Retail Demo Store EventBridge custom event bus.
    Value: !Ref EventBus
    Export:
      Name: retaildemostore-bus

  EventBusArn:
    Description: ARN of the Retail Demo Store EventBridge custom event bus.
    Value: !GetAtt EventBus.Arn

  EventBusLogGroupName:

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  Creates six local EventBridge sink event buses (CloudWatch, CloudFormation,
  GuardDuty, Slack, AutoScaling, CloudTrail), one shared forwarding IAM role
  with a CloudFormation-generated name, and eight rules on this account's
  default event bus that forward critical operational events onto those buses:
  CloudWatch alarm state changes, CloudFormation resource/stack/stack-set status
  changes, GuardDuty findings, Slack message relay payloads, EC2 Auto Scaling
  lifecycle and instance refresh events, and three classes of CloudTrail
  activity (root principal, IAM principal creation, IAM Identity Center
  administration). The stack creates an IAM role, so it must be deployed with
  CAPABILITY_IAM. See the Prerequisites entry in the Metadata section for the
  deviation from the original cross-account design.

Metadata:

  Prerequisites:
    Summary: >-
      This stack creates six AWS::Events::EventBus sink buses in the deploying
      account and region, one shared AWS::IAM::Role used by every rule target,
      and eight AWS::Events::Rule resources on the deploying account's default
      event bus. It creates no compute, no networking, and no stateful
      resources. Every rule target resolves its bus and its role with
      Fn::GetAtt, which also supplies create ordering, so no DependsOn is
      required anywhere.
    TargetAuthorization: >-
      Two conditions are jointly necessary for a rule whose target is an event
      bus, and each was independently proven by a failed deployment of an
      earlier revision of this template. First, the destination bus must exist
      and be reachable when PutTargets is called during rule creation: a bus
      that does not exist, or whose policy does not permit the operation, fails
      rule creation outright with AccessDenied rather than failing later at
      delivery time. Second, an EventBridge target whose ARN is an event bus
      ALWAYS requires a RoleArn - regardless of account or region. A bus target
      is never authorized implicitly the way a Lambda, SNS, or SQS target can be
      through a resource policy. Both conditions are satisfied here by creating
      the sink buses and the forwarding role in this same template.
    ForwardingRole: >-
      One shared forwarding role is created for all eight rule targets. Its
      physical name is generated by CloudFormation - no RoleName is set - so the
      stack deploys under CAPABILITY_IAM alone and cannot collide with rollback
      residue or a parallel deployment of this same template. Its trust policy
      admits only the service principal events.amazonaws.com for sts:AssumeRole,
      and its single inline policy grants only events:PutEvents on exactly the
      six local sink bus ARNs, each referenced with Fn::GetAtt so the policy
      stays in sync with the buses. Its ARN is published as the
      ForwardingRoleArn stack output. Note that this role and the per-bus
      resource policies described under CentralMonitoringAccountAccess point in
      opposite directions: the bus policies grant the central monitoring account
      INBOUND access to put events onto these buses, while this role authorizes
      OUTBOUND delivery from the rules into them.
    BusNaming: >-
      Event bus names are unique per account per region and are not scoped to a
      stack, so each bus name is built with Fn::Sub over AWS::StackName to avoid
      collisions with rollback residue or a parallel deployment of this same
      template. The canonical bus name requested originally is preserved on each
      bus as the RequestedBusName tag, and the live ARN of each bus is published
      as a stack output.
    CentralMonitoringAccountAccess: >-
      Each sink bus carries a resource policy whose single statement allows the
      principal arn:<partition>:iam::<CentralMonitoringAccountId>:root to call
      events:PutEvents on that one bus. The action is not broadened to events:*,
      the principal is not a wildcard, and the resource is the bus's own ARN
      only. This encodes the integration contract: the central monitoring
      account is the counterparty these staging buses exist to serve. It is an
      inbound grant and plays no part in rule creation or in delivery from the
      rules, which is authorized by the forwarding role instead.
    DeviationFromOriginalRequest: >-
      The originating request asked for rule targets on organization-level buses
      owned by the central monitoring account (CloudWatch-org-sink,
      CloudFormation-org-sink, GuardDuty-org-sink, Slack-org-sink,
      AutoScaling-org-sink, CloudTrail-org-sink), each target assuming a fixed
      IAM role named PRX-CloudWatchOrgSinkRole, PRX-CloudFormationOrgSinkRole,
      PRX-GuardDutyOrgSinkRole, PRX-SlackOrgSinkRole,
      PRX-AutoScalingOrgSinkRole, or PRX-CloudTrailOrgSinkRole. This template
      does neither. Those buses do not exist in the monitoring account and
      cannot be created from here, and rule creation fails with AccessDenied
      when a target names them; the PRX-* roles likewise do not exist in the
      deploying account and cannot be referenced by external name under the
      greenfield constraint. Each requested sink bus is therefore replaced
      one-for-one by a local, stack-scoped bus of the same canonical name, and
      the six requested per-class forwarding roles are replaced by a single
      shared role with a generated name. The PRX-* literals survive as
      documentation of intent only, in the mapping below.
    RestoringTrueCrossAccountDelivery: >-
      The forwarding role now exists in this template, so it is no longer
      something an operator must add. To restore the originally requested
      topology the remaining steps are: in the central monitoring account and
      region, create the six org-sink buses and attach to each a resource policy
      allowing events:PutEvents from this account or from its AWS Organization;
      then repoint each rule target's Arn at the remote bus ARN and replace the
      six local bus ARNs in the forwarding role's inline policy with those same
      remote ARNs. The role's trust policy and action scope need no change.
    RequestedToLocalMapping:
      - RequestedBus: CloudWatch-org-sink
        RequestedRole: PRX-CloudWatchOrgSinkRole
        LocalBusResource: CloudWatchOrgSinkBus
        ArnOutput: CloudWatchOrgSinkBusArn
      - RequestedBus: CloudFormation-org-sink
        RequestedRole: PRX-CloudFormationOrgSinkRole
        LocalBusResource: CloudFormationOrgSinkBus
        ArnOutput: CloudFormationOrgSinkBusArn
      - RequestedBus: GuardDuty-org-sink
        RequestedRole: PRX-GuardDutyOrgSinkRole
        LocalBusResource: GuardDutyOrgSinkBus
        ArnOutput: GuardDutyOrgSinkBusArn
      - RequestedBus: Slack-org-sink
        RequestedRole: PRX-SlackOrgSinkRole
        LocalBusResource: SlackOrgSinkBus
        ArnOutput: SlackOrgSinkBusArn
      - RequestedBus: AutoScaling-org-sink
        RequestedRole: PRX-AutoScalingOrgSinkRole
        LocalBusResource: AutoScalingOrgSinkBus
        ArnOutput: AutoScalingOrgSinkBusArn
      - RequestedBus: CloudTrail-org-sink
        RequestedRole: PRX-CloudTrailOrgSinkRole
        LocalBusResource: CloudTrailOrgSinkBus
        ArnOutput: CloudTrailOrgSinkBusArn

Parameters:

  CentralMonitoringAccountId:
    Type: String
    Description: >-
      Twelve-digit AWS account ID of the central monitoring account. It is
      granted events:PutEvents on each sink bus created by this stack, and is
      the account expected to consume or replicate from those buses. This is a
      user-controlled identifier rather than a reference to infrastructure
      created elsewhere.
    AllowedPattern: '^[0-9]{12}$'
    ConstraintDescription: Must be a 12-digit AWS account ID.
    Default: '578003269847'

  SlackRelayEventSource:
    Type: String
    Description: >-
      Custom (non-AWS) EventBridge source string carried by Slack message relay
      payloads published onto this account's default event bus. The originating
      request did not pin an exact value, so it is exposed here as a parameter;
      change it to match whatever source your Slack relay publisher sets.
    AllowedPattern: '^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$'
    ConstraintDescription: Must be a valid EventBridge source string.
    Default: slack.relay

Resources:

  CloudWatchOrgSinkBus:
    Type: AWS::Events::EventBus
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-CloudWatch-org-sink'
      Description: Sink event bus receiving forwarded CloudWatch alarm state change events.
      Policy:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllowCentralMonitoringAccountPutEvents
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              AWS: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::${CentralMonitoringAccountId}:root'
            Action: events:PutEvents
            Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:events:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:event-bus/${AWS::StackName}-CloudWatch-org-sink'
      Tags:
        - Key: RequestedBusName
          Value: CloudWatch-org-sink
        - Key: EventClass
          Value: CloudWatch

  CloudFormationOrgSinkBus:
    Type: AWS::Events::EventBus
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-CloudFormation-org-sink'
      Description: Sink event bus receiving forwarded CloudFormation resource, stack, and stack set status change events.
      Policy:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllowCentralMonitoringAccountPutEvents
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              AWS: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::${CentralMonitoringAccountId}:root'
            Action: events:PutEvents
            Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:events:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:event-bus/${AWS::StackName}-CloudFormation-org-sink'
      Tags:
        - Key: RequestedBusName
          Value: CloudFormation-org-sink
        - Key: EventClass
          Value: CloudFormation

  GuardDutyOrgSinkBus:
    Type: AWS::Events::EventBus
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-GuardDuty-org-sink'
      Description: Sink event bus receiving forwarded GuardDuty findings.
      Policy:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllowCentralMonitoringAccountPutEvents
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              AWS: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::${CentralMonitoringAccountId}:root'
            Action: events:PutEvents
            Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:events:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:event-bus/${AWS::StackName}-GuardDuty-org-sink'
      Tags:
        - Key: RequestedBusName
          Value: GuardDuty-org-sink
        - Key: EventClass
          Value: GuardDuty

  SlackOrgSinkBus:
    Type: AWS::Events::EventBus
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-Slack-org-sink'
      Description: Sink event bus receiving forwarded Slack message relay payloads.
      Policy:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllowCentralMonitoringAccountPutEvents
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              AWS: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::${CentralMonitoringAccountId}:root'
            Action: events:PutEvents
            Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:events:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:event-bus/${AWS::StackName}-Slack-org-sink'
      Tags:
        - Key: RequestedBusName
          Value: Slack-org-sink
        - Key: EventClass
          Value: SlackRelay

  AutoScalingOrgSinkBus:
    Type: AWS::Events::EventBus
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-AutoScaling-org-sink'
      Description: Sink event bus receiving forwarded EC2 Auto Scaling lifecycle and instance refresh events.
      Policy:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllowCentralMonitoringAccountPutEvents
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              AWS: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::${CentralMonitoringAccountId}:root'
            Action: events:PutEvents
            Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:events:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:event-bus/${AWS::StackName}-AutoScaling-org-sink'
      Tags:
        - Key: RequestedBusName
          Value: AutoScaling-org-sink
        - Key: EventClass
          Value: AutoScaling

  CloudTrailOrgSinkBus:
    Type: AWS::Events::EventBus
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-CloudTrail-org-sink'
      Description: Sink event bus receiving forwarded CloudTrail root, IAM principal creation, and Identity Center administration events.
      Policy:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllowCentralMonitoringAccountPutEvents
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              AWS: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::${CentralMonitoringAccountId}:root'
            Action: events:PutEvents
            Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:events:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:event-bus/${AWS::StackName}-CloudTrail-org-sink'
      Tags:
        - Key: RequestedBusName
          Value: CloudTrail-org-sink
        - Key: EventClass
          Value: CloudTrail

  EventForwardingRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      Description: >-
        Identity EventBridge assumes to deliver events from this stack's
        forwarding rules into this stack's six sink event buses.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: events.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: PutEventsToStackSinkBuses
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action: events:PutEvents
                Resource:
                  - !GetAtt CloudWatchOrgSinkBus.Arn
                  - !GetAtt CloudFormationOrgSinkBus.Arn
                  - !GetAtt GuardDutyOrgSinkBus.Arn
                  - !GetAtt SlackOrgSinkBus.Arn
                  - !GetAtt AutoScalingOrgSinkBus.Arn
                  - !GetAtt CloudTrailOrgSinkBus.Arn
      Tags:
        - Key: Purpose
          Value: EventBridgeOrgSinkForwarding

  CloudWatchAlarmForwardRule:
    Type: AWS::Events::Rule
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-cloudwatch-org-forward'
      Description: Forwards CloudWatch alarm state change events to this stack's CloudWatch-org-sink event bus.
      State: ENABLED
      EventPattern:
        source:
          - aws.cloudwatch
        detail-type:
          - CloudWatch Alarm State Change
      Targets:
        - Id: CentralSinkTarget
          Arn: !GetAtt CloudWatchOrgSinkBus.Arn
          RoleArn: !GetAtt EventForwardingRole.Arn

  CloudFormationStatusForwardRule:
    Type: AWS::Events::Rule
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-cloudformation-org-forward'
      Description: >-
        Forwards CloudFormation resource, stack, and stack set status change
        events to this stack's CloudFormation-org-sink event bus.
      State: ENABLED
      EventPattern:
        source:
          - aws.cloudformation
        detail-type:
          - CloudFormation Resource Status Change
          - CloudFormation Stack Status Change
          - CloudFormation StackSet Status Change
          - CloudFormation StackSet Operation Status Change
      Targets:
        - Id: CentralSinkTarget
          Arn: !GetAtt CloudFormationOrgSinkBus.Arn
          RoleArn: !GetAtt EventForwardingRole.Arn

  GuardDutyFindingForwardRule:
    Type: AWS::Events::Rule
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-guardduty-org-forward'
      Description: Forwards GuardDuty findings to this stack's GuardDuty-org-sink event bus.
      State: ENABLED
      EventPattern:
        source:
          - aws.guardduty
        detail-type:
          - GuardDuty Finding
      Targets:
        - Id: CentralSinkTarget
          Arn: !GetAtt GuardDutyOrgSinkBus.Arn
          RoleArn: !GetAtt EventForwardingRole.Arn

  SlackRelayForwardRule:
    Type: AWS::Events::Rule
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-slack-org-forward'
      Description: >-
        Forwards Slack message relay payloads published on the default event bus
        to this stack's Slack-org-sink event bus.
      State: ENABLED
      EventPattern:
        source:
          - !Ref SlackRelayEventSource
      Targets:
        - Id: CentralSinkTarget
          Arn: !GetAtt SlackOrgSinkBus.Arn
          RoleArn: !GetAtt EventForwardingRole.Arn

  AutoScalingEventForwardRule:
    Type: AWS::Events::Rule
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-autoscaling-org-forward'
      Description: >-
        Forwards EC2 Auto Scaling instance lifecycle and instance refresh events
        to this stack's AutoScaling-org-sink event bus.
      State: ENABLED
      EventPattern:
        source:
          - aws.autoscaling
        detail-type:
          - EC2 Instance Launch Successful
          - EC2 Instance Launch Unsuccessful
          - EC2 Instance Terminate Successful
          - EC2 Instance Terminate Unsuccessful
          - EC2 Auto Scaling Instance Refresh Checkpoint Reached
          - EC2 Auto Scaling Instance Refresh Started
          - EC2 Auto Scaling Instance Refresh Succeeded
          - EC2 Auto Scaling Instance Refresh Failed
          - EC2 Auto Scaling Instance Refresh Cancelled
      Targets:
        - Id: CentralSinkTarget
          Arn: !GetAtt AutoScalingOrgSinkBus.Arn
          RoleArn: !GetAtt EventForwardingRole.Arn

  CloudTrailRootActivityForwardRule:
    Type: AWS::Events::Rule
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-cloudtrail-root-org-forward'
      Description: >-
        Forwards root-principal API calls and console sign-ins recorded by
        CloudTrail to this stack's CloudTrail-org-sink event bus.
      State: ENABLED
      EventPattern:
        source:
          - aws.cloudtrail
        detail-type:
          - AWS API Call via CloudTrail
          - AWS Console Sign In via CloudTrail
        detail:
          userIdentity:
            type:
              - Root
      Targets:
        - Id: CentralSinkTarget
          Arn: !GetAtt CloudTrailOrgSinkBus.Arn
          RoleArn: !GetAtt EventForwardingRole.Arn

  CloudTrailIamPrincipalCreationForwardRule:
    Type: AWS::Events::Rule
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-cloudtrail-iam-org-forward'
      Description: >-
        Forwards IAM user and access key creation calls recorded by CloudTrail to
        this stack's CloudTrail-org-sink event bus.
      State: ENABLED
      EventPattern:
        source:
          - aws.cloudtrail
        detail-type:
          - AWS API Call via CloudTrail
        detail:
          eventSource:
            - iam.amazonaws.com
          eventName:
            - CreateUser
            - CreateAccessKey
      Targets:
        - Id: CentralSinkTarget
          Arn: !GetAtt CloudTrailOrgSinkBus.Arn
          RoleArn: !GetAtt EventForwardingRole.Arn

  CloudTrailIdentityCenterAdminForwardRule:
    Type: AWS::Events::Rule
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-cloudtrail-identity-center-org-forward'
      Description: >-
        Forwards IAM Identity Center administrative actions recorded by CloudTrail
        to this stack's CloudTrail-org-sink event bus. Permission-set management
        events are emitted by sso.amazonaws.com while user and group management
        events are emitted by sso-directory.amazonaws.com, so both event sources
        are matched by this single pattern.
      State: ENABLED
      EventPattern:
        source:
          - aws.cloudtrail
        detail-type:
          - AWS API Call via CloudTrail
        detail:
          eventSource:
            - sso.amazonaws.com
            - sso-directory.amazonaws.com
          eventName:
            - CreatePermissionSet
            - ProvisionPermissionSet
            - CreateTrustedTokenIssuer
            - PutInlinePolicyToPermissionSet
            - PutPermissionsBoundaryToPermissionSet
            - PutPermissionsPolicy
            - UpdatePermissionSet
            - CreateUser
            - EnableUser
            - AddMemberToGroup
            - UpdateUser
            - UpdateGroup
      Targets:
        - Id: CentralSinkTarget
          Arn: !GetAtt CloudTrailOrgSinkBus.Arn
          RoleArn: !GetAtt EventForwardingRole.Arn

  ForwardingRoleArn:

      ARN of the shared forwarding role. This is the identity EventBridge

  CloudFormationOrgSinkBusArn:
    Description: >-
      ARN of the CloudFormation status sink event bus (requested name

    Value: !GetAtt CloudFormationOrgSinkBus.Arn

  GuardDutyOrgSinkBusArn:
    Description: >-

  SlackOrgSinkBusArn:

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  Idempotency and deduplication store for hybrid (polling + event-driven) file
  processing. Creates a DynamoDB table that is the single dedup arbiter for both
  trigger paths, a least-privilege managed IAM policy for data-plane access to
  it, and Lambda plus Step Functions execution roles that attach that policy.
  Fully self-contained.

# This stack is fully self-contained: it references no external VPCs, subnets,
# security groups, secrets, SSM parameters, KMS keys, or cross-stack exports,
# and it defines no parameters for such resource IDs. No networking resources
# are created either — DynamoDB, IAM, and Step Functions are regional/global
# services reached over the AWS API, so no VPC, subnet, security group, or
# gateway endpoint is required for this stack.

Parameters:
  ProjectPrefix:
    Type: String
    Default: fsxn-s3ap
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{1,24}$'
    Description: >-
      Lowercase prefix applied to the name of every resource created by this
      stack (DynamoDB table, managed policy, IAM roles). Must start with a
      letter and contain only lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens.
    ConstraintDescription: >-
      Must start with a lowercase letter and be 2-25 characters of lowercase
      letters, digits, or hyphens.

  IdempotencyTtlDays:
    Type: Number
    Default: 7
    MinValue: 1
    MaxValue: 35
    Description: >-
      Lifetime in days of an idempotency record, used by writers to compute the
      "expiresAt" epoch-seconds value as now + (IdempotencyTtlDays * 86400).
      DynamoDB TTL configuration only names the attribute, not the retention
      duration, so this duration is published as a stack Output for the writing
      Lambda and Step Functions workflows to read.

Resources:
  # Single dedup arbiter shared by the polling path and the event-driven path.
  #
  # Usage contract for claimants (both the poller and the event handler):
  #   1. Compute a stable file identity and use it as "idempotencyKey" (for
  #      example a hash of bucket/volume + object key + version/ETag), so a
  #      polled discovery and an event notification for the same file produce
  #      the same value and land on the same partition.
  #   2. Use "operationId" to scope the entry to a workflow and stage, for
  #      example '<workflow>#<stage>', so distinct operations on one file can
  #      coexist while repeats of the same operation collapse onto one item.
  #   3. Claim with PutItem plus
  #      ConditionExpression: attribute_not_exists(idempotencyKey)
  #      to win the race between the polling and event paths. Exactly one
  #      claimant succeeds.
  #   4. The loser receives ConditionalCheckFailedException and MUST treat that
  #      as "already processed" (or "in flight"), then exit without
  #      reprocessing the file.
  #   5. Every writer sets "expiresAt" as a Number holding epoch seconds equal
  #      to now + (IdempotencyTtlDays * 86400); the duration lives in the
  #      IdempotencyTtlDays parameter and is published as a stack Output.
  #   6. Writers set a "status" attribute (for example 'IN_FLIGHT',
  #      'COMPLETED', 'FAILED') so the status-index GSI can sweep in-flight
  #      claims abandoned by a failed execution, using Query on status plus an
  #      expiresAt range.
  IdempotencyTable:
    Type: AWS::DynamoDB::Table
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      TableName: !Sub '${ProjectPrefix}-idempotency'
      BillingMode: PAY_PER_REQUEST
      # Only key attributes of the table and of the GSI are declared; all other
      # item attributes (claim timestamps, execution ARNs, and so on) are
      # schemaless.
      AttributeDefinitions:
        - AttributeName: idempotencyKey
          AttributeType: S
        - AttributeName: operationId
          AttributeType: S
        - AttributeName: status
          AttributeType: S
        - AttributeName: expiresAt
          AttributeType: N
      KeySchema:
        - AttributeName: idempotencyKey
          KeyType: HASH
        - AttributeName: operationId
          KeyType: RANGE
      GlobalSecondaryIndexes:
        # Stale-lock recovery: query status = 'IN_FLIGHT' with an expiresAt
        # range to sweep claims abandoned by a failed execution.
        - IndexName: status-index
          KeySchema:
            - AttributeName: status
              KeyType: HASH
            - AttributeName: expiresAt
              KeyType: RANGE
          Projection:
            ProjectionType: KEYS_ONLY
      TimeToLiveSpecification:
        AttributeName: expiresAt
        Enabled: true
      PointInTimeRecoverySpecification:
        PointInTimeRecoveryEnabled: true
      SSESpecification:
        # KMSMasterKeyId omitted on purpose so the AWS-managed aws/dynamodb key
        # is used; a customer-managed key would need a key policy that depends
        # on the consumer roles, which in turn depend on the table.
        SSEEnabled: true
        SSEType: KMS
      Tags:
        - Key: Project
          Value: !Ref ProjectPrefix
        - Key: Purpose
          Value: idempotency-store
      # Deliberately omitted because they were not requested and are not
      # verifiably needed here: StreamSpecification, global table Replicas,
      # ContributorInsightsSpecification, and any table-level ResourcePolicy.

  # Single reusable data-plane grant for both Lambda and Step Functions
  # consumers. Scan, dynamodb:*, and control-plane actions (DeleteTable,
  # UpdateTable, UpdateContinuousBackups) are intentionally excluded.
  IdempotencyAccessPolicy:
    Type: AWS::IAM::ManagedPolicy
    Properties:
      ManagedPolicyName: !Sub '${ProjectPrefix}-idempotency-access'
      Description: !Sub >-
        Least-privilege read/write access to the ${ProjectPrefix}-idempotency
        DynamoDB table and its status-index for Lambda and Step Functions
        deduplication consumers.
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: IdempotencyTableDataAccess
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - dynamodb:GetItem
              - dynamodb:PutItem
              - dynamodb:UpdateItem
              - dynamodb:DeleteItem
              - dynamodb:Query
              - dynamodb:ConditionCheckItem
              - dynamodb:BatchGetItem
              - dynamodb:BatchWriteItem
              - dynamodb:DescribeTable
            Resource:
              - !GetAtt IdempotencyTable.Arn
              - !Sub '${IdempotencyTable.Arn}/index/*'

  LambdaExecutionRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Sub '${ProjectPrefix}-idempotency-lambda-role'
      Description: >-
        Execution role for Lambda functions that claim and release idempotency
        records for polled and event-driven file processing.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: lambda.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - !Ref IdempotencyAccessPolicy
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole
      Tags:
        - Key: Project
          Value: !Ref ProjectPrefix
        - Key: Purpose
          Value: idempotency-store

  StepFunctionsExecutionRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Sub '${ProjectPrefix}-idempotency-states-role'
      Description: >-
        Execution role for Step Functions state machines that perform
        conditional idempotency claims directly against the dedup table.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: states.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                # Confused-deputy guard: only state machines in this account
                # may assume the role.
                aws:SourceAccount: !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - !Ref IdempotencyAccessPolicy
      Tags:
        - Key: Project
          Value: !Ref ProjectPrefix
        - Key: Purpose
          Value: idempotency-store

Outputs:
  IdempotencyTableName:
    Description: Name of the DynamoDB idempotency table.
    Value: !Ref IdempotencyTable
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-IdempotencyTableName'

  IdempotencyTableArn:
    Description: ARN of the DynamoDB idempotency table.
    Value: !GetAtt IdempotencyTable.Arn
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-IdempotencyTableArn'

  IdempotencyAccessPolicyArn:
    Description: >-
      ARN of the managed policy granting data-plane access to the idempotency
      table; attach it to any additional consumer role.
    Value: !Ref IdempotencyAccessPolicy
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-IdempotencyAccessPolicyArn'

  LambdaExecutionRoleArn:
    Description: ARN of the Lambda execution role with idempotency table access.
    Value: !GetAtt LambdaExecutionRole.Arn
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-LambdaExecutionRoleArn'

  StepFunctionsExecutionRoleArn:
    Description: ARN of the Step Functions execution role with idempotency table access.
    Value: !GetAtt StepFunctionsExecutionRole.Arn
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-StepFunctionsExecutionRoleArn'

  TtlAttributeName:
    Description: >-
      Name of the enabled TTL attribute; writers set it to epoch seconds equal
      to now + (IdempotencyTtlDays * 86400).
    Value: expiresAt
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-TtlAttributeName'

  IdempotencyTtlDays:
    Description: >-
      Record lifetime in days that writers must use when computing the
      expiresAt epoch-seconds value.
    Value: !Ref IdempotencyTtlDays
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-IdempotencyTtlDays'

Description: >-
  Cognito authentication layer for Amazon Elasticsearch / OpenSearch Kibana (Dashboards).
  Creates the "KibanaUsers" user pool with its hosted-UI domain and app client, the
  "KibanaIDPool" identity pool, the authenticated and unauthenticated identity-pool IAM
  roles, the role attachment, and the service role that Amazon OpenSearch Service assumes
  to configure Cognito authentication. The Elasticsearch/OpenSearch domain itself is
  created separately; the authenticated role is scoped to the domain named "<AppName>-es"
  in this account and region (see the EsDomainName output). Self-contained: no external
  VPC, secret, SSM parameter, or cross-stack import is referenced.
  SECURITY NOTE: unauthenticated identities are enabled as explicitly requested, which
  lets anonymous callers obtain AWS credentials from this identity pool. The
  unauthenticated role below is therefore created with an explicit deny-all policy and
  carries no Elasticsearch permissions.

Parameters:
  AppName:
    Type: String
    Default: kibana
    Description: Lowercase application name used for the Cognito hosted-UI domain prefix, the target Elasticsearch domain name, and resource tags.
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,20}$'
    ConstraintDescription: Must be 2-21 characters of lowercase alphanumerics and hyphens, starting with an alphanumeric.

  EnvironmentTag:
    Type: String
    Default: prod
    Description: Environment tag applied to every taggable resource for cost attribution.
    AllowedPattern: '^[A-Za-z0-9._:/=+@-]{1,64}$'
    ConstraintDescription: Must be a valid AWS tag value of 1-64 characters.

Resources:

  ############################################################################
  # Cognito user pool - email as username, admin-created users only
  ############################################################################
  UserPool:
    Type: AWS::Cognito::UserPool
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      UserPoolName: KibanaUsers
      UsernameAttributes:
        - email
      AutoVerifiedAttributes:
        - email
      UsernameConfiguration:
        CaseSensitive: false
      Schema:
        - Name: email
          AttributeDataType: String
          Required: true
          Mutable: true
      Policies:
        PasswordPolicy:
          MinimumLength: 8
          RequireUppercase: true
          RequireLowercase: true
          RequireNumbers: true
          RequireSymbols: true
          TemporaryPasswordValidityDays: 3
      AdminCreateUserConfig:
        AllowAdminCreateUserOnly: true
        InviteMessageTemplate:
          EmailSubject: Your Kibana (OpenSearch Dashboards) account
          EmailMessage: >-
            An administrator created a Kibana account for you. Your username is {username}
            and your temporary password is {####}. You will be asked to choose a new password
            and register a multi-factor authentication device at first sign-in.
          SMSMessage: 'Kibana account created. Username: {username} Temporary password: {####}'
      VerificationMessageTemplate:
        DefaultEmailOption: CONFIRM_WITH_CODE
        EmailSubject: Verify your Kibana account email address

      AccountRecoverySetting:
        RecoveryMechanisms:
          - Name: verified_email
            Priority: 1
      EmailConfiguration:
        EmailSendingAccount: COGNITO_DEFAULT
      MfaConfiguration: OPTIONAL
      EnabledMfas:
        - SOFTWARE_TOKEN_MFA
      UserPoolAddOns:
        AdvancedSecurityMode: ENFORCED
      UserPoolTags:
        Name: KibanaUsers
        Environment: !Ref EnvironmentTag
        Application: !Ref AppName

  # Hosted UI domain - required for the Cognito login redirect from Kibana/Dashboards.
  # The account ID component keeps this globally-unique prefix collision-free.
  UserPoolDomain:
    Type: AWS::Cognito::UserPoolDomain
    Properties:
      UserPoolId: !Ref UserPool
      Domain: !Sub '${AppName}-${AWS::AccountId}'

  # Public client (no secret) that the identity pool trusts.
  UserPoolClient:
    Type: AWS::Cognito::UserPoolClient
    Properties:
      ClientName: !Sub '${AppName}-dashboards-client'
      UserPoolId: !Ref UserPool
      GenerateSecret: false
      SupportedIdentityProviders:
        - COGNITO
      ExplicitAuthFlows:
        - ALLOW_USER_SRP_AUTH
        - ALLOW_REFRESH_TOKEN_AUTH
      PreventUserExistenceErrors: ENABLED
      EnableTokenRevocation: true
      RefreshTokenValidity: 1
      AccessTokenValidity: 60
      IdTokenValidity: 60
      TokenValidityUnits:
        RefreshToken: days
        AccessToken: minutes
        IdToken: minutes

  ############################################################################
  # Cognito identity pool - exchanges user pool tokens for AWS credentials
  ############################################################################
  IdentityPool:
    Type: AWS::Cognito::IdentityPool
    Properties:
      IdentityPoolName: KibanaIDPool
      AllowUnauthenticatedIdentities: true
      CognitoIdentityProviders:
        - ClientId: !Ref UserPoolClient
          ProviderName: !GetAtt UserPool.ProviderName
          ServerSideTokenCheck: true
      IdentityPoolTags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: KibanaIDPool
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentTag
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref AppName

  ############################################################################
  # IAM roles assumed through the identity pool

  CognitoAuthenticatedRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-cognito-authenticated'
      Description: Role assumed by users authenticated against the KibanaUsers pool; grants scoped Elasticsearch HTTP access.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Federated: cognito-identity.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                'cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:aud': !Ref IdentityPool
              'ForAnyValue:StringLike':
                'cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:amr': authenticated
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: KibanaElasticsearchHttpAccess
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: ElasticsearchHttpAccess
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - es:ESHttpGet
                  - es:ESHttpPost
                  - es:ESHttpPut
                  - es:ESHttpHead
                  - es:ESHttpDelete
                # Built entirely from pseudo-parameters plus the defaulted AppName, so the
                # grant is scoped to a single named domain without any hardcoded account ID
                # or cross-stack import. IAM does not require the domain to exist yet.
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:es:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:domain/${AppName}-es/*'
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-cognito-authenticated'
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentTag
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref AppName

  # Unauthenticated identities are enabled, so this role MUST exist and MUST hold
  # no usable permissions. Explicit deny-all defeats any future policy attachment drift.
  CognitoUnauthenticatedRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-cognito-unauthenticated'
      Description: Deny-all role assumed by anonymous callers of the KibanaIDPool identity pool.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Federated: cognito-identity.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                'cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:aud': !Ref IdentityPool
              'ForAnyValue:StringLike':
                'cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:amr': unauthenticated
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: DenyAllActions
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: DenyEverything
                Effect: Deny
                Action: '*'
                Resource: '*'
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-cognito-unauthenticated'
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentTag
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref AppName

  IdentityPoolRoleAttachment:
    Type: AWS::Cognito::IdentityPoolRoleAttachment
    Properties:
      IdentityPoolId: !Ref IdentityPool
      Roles:
        authenticated: !GetAtt CognitoAuthenticatedRole.Arn
        unauthenticated: !GetAtt CognitoUnauthenticatedRole.Arn

  ############################################################################
  # Service role letting the Elasticsearch/OpenSearch domain configure Cognito auth.
  # Pass this ARN as CognitoOptions.RoleArn when the domain is created.
  ############################################################################
  OpenSearchCognitoAccessRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-opensearch-cognito-access'
      Description: Allows Amazon OpenSearch Service to configure Cognito authentication for Dashboards.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: es.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AmazonESCognitoAccess
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-opensearch-cognito-access'
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentTag
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref AppName

Outputs:

  UserPoolId:
    Description: ID of the KibanaUsers Cognito user pool.
    Value: !Ref UserPool
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-UserPoolId'

  UserPoolArn:
    Description: ARN of the KibanaUsers Cognito user pool.
    Value: !GetAtt UserPool.Arn
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-UserPoolArn'

  IdentityPoolId:
    Description: ID of the KibanaIDPool Cognito identity pool.
    Value: !Ref IdentityPool
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-IdentityPoolId'

  UserPoolClientId:
    Description: App client ID trusted by the identity pool.
    Value: !Ref UserPoolClient

  UserPoolDomainName:
    Description: Cognito hosted UI domain prefix used for the Kibana sign-in redirect.
    Value: !Ref UserPoolDomain

  CognitoHostedUiUrl:
    Description: Base URL of the Cognito hosted UI that Kibana redirects to for sign-in.
    Value: !Sub 'https://${AppName}-${AWS::AccountId}.auth.${AWS::Region}.amazoncognito.com'

  EsDomainName:
    Description: Name of the Elasticsearch/OpenSearch domain the authenticated role is scoped to. Create the domain with exactly this name.
    Value: !Sub '${AppName}-es'

  EsDomainArnPattern:
    Description: Resource ARN pattern granted to the authenticated role for es:ESHttp* actions.
    Value: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:es:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:domain/${AppName}-es/*'

  KibanaDashboardsUrlPattern:
    Description: Expected Kibana / OpenSearch Dashboards URL once the domain is created; replace the placeholder with the domain's generated endpoint hash.
    Value: !Sub 'https://search-${AppName}-es-<endpoint-hash>.${AWS::Region}.es.amazonaws.com/_dashboards/'

  AuthenticatedRoleArn:
    Description: ARN of the IAM role assumed by authenticated Kibana users.
    Value: !GetAtt CognitoAuthenticatedRole.Arn

  UnauthenticatedRoleArn:
    Description: ARN of the deny-all IAM role assumed by anonymous identity pool callers.
    Value: !GetAtt CognitoUnauthenticatedRole.Arn

  OpenSearchCognitoAccessRoleArn:
    Description: ARN to pass as CognitoOptions.RoleArn when creating the Elasticsearch/OpenSearch domain.
    Value: !GetAtt OpenSearchCognitoAccessRole.Arn
