AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  Step Functions + DynamoDB integration test stack. Creates a STANDARD state
  machine that writes an item to a DynamoDB table with PutItem and reads it back
  with GetItem, together with the table, execution role and log group it needs.

Parameters:
  TableName:
    Type: String
    Default: my-table
    Description: >-
      Name of the DynamoDB table used by the integration test workflow.
      Must follow DynamoDB table naming rules (3-255 characters, letters,
      numbers, underscore, dot and dash only).
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-zA-Z0-9_.-]{3,255}$'
    ConstraintDescription: >-
      Must be 3-255 characters long and contain only a-z, A-Z, 0-9, underscore,
      dot or dash.

Resources:

  # Stateful resource: retained on stack delete/replace so test data is never
  # silently destroyed.
  DynamoDBTable:
    Type: AWS::DynamoDB::Table
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      TableName: !Ref TableName
      # PAY_PER_REQUEST is mutually exclusive with ProvisionedThroughput,
      # which is therefore intentionally omitted.
      BillingMode: PAY_PER_REQUEST
      AttributeDefinitions:
        - AttributeName: id
          AttributeType: S
      KeySchema:
        - AttributeName: id
          KeyType: HASH
      SSESpecification:
        SSEEnabled: true
      PointInTimeRecoverySpecification:
        PointInTimeRecoveryEnabled: true
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref 'AWS::StackName'
        - Key: Purpose
          Value: testing

  StateMachineLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    DeletionPolicy: Delete
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Delete
    Properties:
      # Step Functions requires the /aws/vendedlogs/ prefix for vended log delivery.
      LogGroupName: !Sub '/aws/vendedlogs/states/${AWS::StackName}-integration-test'
      RetentionInDays: 30
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref 'AWS::StackName'
        - Key: Purpose
          Value: testing

  StateMachineRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      Description: Execution role for the DynamoDB integration test state machine.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: states.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                # Confused-deputy protection: only this account's Step Functions
                # service may assume the role.
                aws:SourceAccount: !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'
              ArnLike:
                # Scoped to the state machine ARN. The ARN is composed from
                # pseudo-parameters rather than !Ref/!GetAtt on the state machine
                # itself, which would create a circular dependency.
                aws:SourceArn: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:states:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:stateMachine:${AWS::StackName}-integration-test'
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: DynamoDBItemAccess
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - dynamodb:PutItem
                  - dynamodb:GetItem
                Resource: !GetAtt DynamoDBTable.Arn
        - PolicyName: StateMachineLogDelivery
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              # Exception to least-privilege resource scoping: the CloudWatch Logs
              # vended-log-delivery APIs used by Step Functions logging do not
              # support resource-level permissions and require Resource "*".
              # See "Logging using CloudWatch Logs" in the AWS Step Functions
              # Developer Guide.
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - logs:CreateLogDelivery
                  - logs:GetLogDelivery
                  - logs:UpdateLogDelivery
                  - logs:DeleteLogDelivery
                  - logs:ListLogDeliveries
                  - logs:PutResourcePolicy
                  - logs:DescribeResourcePolicies
                  - logs:DescribeLogGroups
                Resource: '*'
        - PolicyName: XRayTracing
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              # X-Ray write APIs likewise do not support resource-level
              # permissions and require Resource "*".
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - xray:PutTraceSegments
                  - xray:PutTelemetryRecords
                  - xray:GetSamplingRules
                  - xray:GetSamplingTargets
                Resource: '*'
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref 'AWS::StackName'
        - Key: Purpose
          Value: testing

  StateMachine:
    Type: AWS::StepFunctions::StateMachine
    Properties:
      StateMachineName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-integration-test'
      StateMachineType: STANDARD
      RoleArn: !GetAtt StateMachineRole.Arn
      LoggingConfiguration:
        Level: ALL
        IncludeExecutionData: true
        Destinations:
          - CloudWatchLogsLogGroup:
              LogGroupArn: !GetAtt StateMachineLogGroup.Arn
      TracingConfiguration:
        Enabled: true
      DefinitionString: !Sub
        - |-
          {
            "Comment": "Writes an item keyed on the execution input id, then reads it back and returns only the item.",
            "StartAt": "PutItem",
            "States": {
              "PutItem": {
                "Type": "Task",
                "Resource": "arn:aws:states:::dynamodb:putItem",
                "Parameters": {
                  "TableName": "${TableName}",
                  "Item": {
                    "id": {
                      "S.$": "$.id"
                    },
                    "description": {
                      "S.$": "States.Format('Integration test item for id {}', $.id)"
                    }
                  }
                },
                "ResultPath": null,
                "Retry": [
                  {
                    "ErrorEquals": [
                      "DynamoDB.ThrottlingException",
                      "DynamoDB.ProvisionedThroughputExceededException",
                      "DynamoDB.RequestLimitExceeded",
                      "DynamoDB.InternalServerError"
                    ],
                    "IntervalSeconds": 1,
                    "MaxAttempts": 5,
                    "BackoffRate": 2.0
                  },
                  {
                    "ErrorEquals": [
                      "States.TaskFailed"
                    ],
                    "IntervalSeconds": 2,
                    "MaxAttempts": 3,
                    "BackoffRate": 2.0
                  }
                ],
                "Catch": [
                  {
                    "ErrorEquals": [
                      "States.ALL"
                    ],
                    "ResultPath": "$.error",
                    "Next": "WorkflowFailed"
                  }
                ],
                "Next": "GetItem"
              },
              "GetItem": {
                "Type": "Task",
                "Resource": "arn:aws:states:::dynamodb:getItem",
                "Parameters": {
                  "TableName": "${TableName}",
                  "ConsistentRead": true,
                  "Key": {
                    "id": {
                      "S.$": "$.id"
                    }
                  }
                },
                "Retry": [
                  {
                    "ErrorEquals": [
                      "DynamoDB.ThrottlingException",
                      "DynamoDB.ProvisionedThroughputExceededException",
                      "DynamoDB.RequestLimitExceeded",
                      "DynamoDB.InternalServerError"
                    ],
                    "IntervalSeconds": 1,
                    "MaxAttempts": 5,
                    "BackoffRate": 2.0
                  },
                  {
                    "ErrorEquals": [
                      "States.TaskFailed"
                    ],
                    "IntervalSeconds": 2,
                    "MaxAttempts": 3,
                    "BackoffRate": 2.0
                  }
                ],
                "Catch": [
                  {
                    "ErrorEquals": [
                      "States.ALL"
                    ],
                    "ResultPath": "$.error",
                    "Next": "WorkflowFailed"
                  }
                ],
                "OutputPath": "$.Item",
                "End": true
              },
              "WorkflowFailed": {
                "Type": "Fail",
                "Error": "DynamoDBIntegrationTestFailed",
                "Cause": "The PutItem or GetItem task failed after exhausting its retries."
              }
            }
          }
        # Resolves to the table name and establishes the implicit dependency on
        # the table, so no DependsOn is required.
        - TableName: !Ref DynamoDBTable
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref 'AWS::StackName'
        - Key: Purpose
          Value: testing

Outputs:

  StateMachineArn:
    Description: ARN of the DynamoDB integration test state machine.
    Value: !Ref StateMachine

  StateMachineName:
    Description: Name of the DynamoDB integration test state machine.
    Value: !GetAtt StateMachine.Name

  DynamoDBTableName:
    Description: Name of the DynamoDB table used by the workflow.
    Value: !Ref DynamoDBTable

  DynamoDBTableArn:
    Description: ARN of the DynamoDB table used by the workflow.
    Value: !GetAtt DynamoDBTable.Arn

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  Ask Around Me - realtime messaging backend (AWS IoT + Amazon Cognito).
  Provisions an IoT Thing, a Cognito User Pool and public app client, a
  federated Identity Pool permitting unauthenticated identities, and the
  authenticated/unauthenticated IAM roles attached to that Identity Pool.

Parameters:
  ApplicationName:
    Type: String
    Default: askAroundMe
    Description: Application name prefix used for tagging and output naming.
    MinLength: 1
    MaxLength: 64
    AllowedPattern: '[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9-]*'

Resources:

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # AWS IoT
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  RealtimeThing:
    Type: AWS::IoT::Thing
    Properties:
      ThingName: askaroundme-realtime

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Amazon Cognito - User Pool
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  UserPool:
    Type: AWS::Cognito::UserPool
    Properties:
      UserPoolName: askAroundMeUserPool
      AutoVerifiedAttributes:
        - email
      UsernameAttributes:
        - email
      MfaConfiguration: 'OFF'
      Schema:
        - Name: email
          AttributeDataType: String
          Required: true
          Mutable: false
      Policies:
        PasswordPolicy:
          MinimumLength: 12
          RequireUppercase: true
          RequireLowercase: true
          RequireNumbers: true
          RequireSymbols: true
          TemporaryPasswordValidityDays: 3
      AdminCreateUserConfig:
        AllowAdminCreateUserOnly: false
      AccountRecoverySetting:
        RecoveryMechanisms:
          - Name: verified_email
            Priority: 1
      UserPoolTags:
        Application: AskAroundMe
        Environment: prod
        Name: !Sub '${ApplicationName}-user-pool'

  UserPoolClient:
    Type: AWS::Cognito::UserPoolClient
    Properties:
      ClientName: !Sub '${ApplicationName}-web-client'
      UserPoolId: !Ref UserPool
      GenerateSecret: false
      ExplicitAuthFlows:
        - ALLOW_USER_SRP_AUTH
        - ALLOW_REFRESH_TOKEN_AUTH
      PreventUserExistenceErrors: ENABLED
      EnableTokenRevocation: true
      RefreshTokenValidity: 30
      AccessTokenValidity: 60
      IdTokenValidity: 60
      TokenValidityUnits:
        RefreshToken: days
        AccessToken: minutes
        IdToken: minutes
      SupportedIdentityProviders:
        - COGNITO

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Amazon Cognito - Identity Pool
  # NOTE: this resource must never reference the IAM roles below; the roles
  # reference the Identity Pool, and only IdentityPoolRoleAttachment joins them.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  IdentityPool:
    Type: AWS::Cognito::IdentityPool
    Properties:
      IdentityPoolName: askAroundMeIdentityPool
      AllowUnauthenticatedIdentities: true
      CognitoIdentityProviders:
        - ClientId: !Ref UserPoolClient
          ProviderName: !GetAtt UserPool.ProviderName
          ServerSideTokenCheck: true

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # IAM roles for Cognito federated identities
  #
  # NOTE ON WILDCARDS: iot:Subscribe and iot:Receive are granted with
  # Resource "*" because the original requirement asks for subscribe/receive
  # against any resource/topic. These wildcards are intentionally broad per the
  # stated requirements; for least privilege in production they should be
  # narrowed to specific topic filter ARNs, e.g.
  #   arn:aws:iot:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:topicfilter/askAroundMe/*
  #   arn:aws:iot:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:topic/askAroundMe/*
  # iot:DescribeEndpoint must use Resource "*" as it does not support
  # resource-level permissions.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  AuthenticatedRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      Description: Role assumed by authenticated Ask Around Me users via Cognito Identity.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Federated: cognito-identity.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                'cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:aud': !Ref IdentityPool
              'ForAnyValue:StringLike':
                'cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:amr': authenticated
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: AskAroundMeAuthenticatedPolicy
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: CognitoSyncScopedToIdentityPool
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - cognito-sync:ListRecords
                  - cognito-sync:UpdateRecords
                  - cognito-sync:DescribeDataset
                  - cognito-sync:ListDatasets
                  - cognito-sync:SubscribeToDataset
                  - cognito-sync:UnsubscribeFromDataset
                Resource:
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:cognito-sync:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:identitypool/${IdentityPool}'
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:cognito-sync:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:identitypool/${IdentityPool}/*'
              - Sid: CognitoIdentityCredentials
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - cognito-identity:GetCredentialsForIdentity
                Resource:
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:cognito-identity:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:identitypool/${IdentityPool}'
              - Sid: IoTConnectWithAskAroundMeClientPrefix
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - iot:Connect
                Resource:
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iot:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:client/askAroundMe-*'
              - Sid: IoTSubscribeAndReceiveBroadPerRequirements
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - iot:Subscribe
                  - iot:Receive
                Resource: '*'
              - Sid: IoTEndpointDiscoveryNoResourceScoping
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - iot:DescribeEndpoint
                Resource: '*'
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: AskAroundMe
        - Key: Environment
          Value: prod
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${ApplicationName}-authenticated-role'

  UnauthenticatedRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      Description: Role assumed by unauthenticated (guest) Ask Around Me users via Cognito Identity.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Federated: cognito-identity.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                'cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:aud': !Ref IdentityPool
              'ForAnyValue:StringLike':
                'cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:amr': unauthenticated
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: AskAroundMeUnauthenticatedPolicy
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: CognitoSyncScopedToIdentityPool
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - cognito-sync:ListRecords
                  - cognito-sync:UpdateRecords

final_template:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: ECS chaos-engineering resilience workflow - terminate the container instance, wait, re-check ECS service health and alert via SNS. Self-contained, no external stacks or account-specific IDs.

# LIMITATION 1: the Auto Scaling group is sized at 1, so recovery is a relaunch
# race rather than failover onto surviving capacity; Min/Max/Desired of 2 across
# both AZs would test true redundancy.
# LIMITATION 2: the workload image is served through an ECR pull-through cache of
# public.ecr.aws, so the first task pull populates the cache on the ECR service side.
# LIMITATION 3: the service ships at ServiceDesiredCount 0 so the stack creates
# without a multi-minute runtime-convergence wait (AWS::ECS::Service blocks until
# runningCount == desiredCount, with no deadline). The chaos experiment is only
# meaningful once an operator raises ServiceDesiredCount to 1 and confirms a task is
# running; until then the health-check Lambda reports unhealthy by design.
# LIMITATION 4: capacity and the interface endpoints are placed in one AZ only, and
# Container Insights is disabled, to keep provisioning time bounded. Both subnets are
# still created in distinct AZs; the redundancy upgrade is adding ChaosPrivateSubnetB
# back to every endpoint SubnetIds list AND to VPCZoneIdentifier together.
# NOTE: physical names that are unique per account/region are either stack-scoped or
# left to CloudFormation to generate, so a partial rollback can never block a retry.
# NOTE: the instance has no internet path, so it carries no cfn-signal apparatus.
# NOTE: the dependency graph is deliberately flat - the Lambdas and state machine do
# not reference the ECS service by GetAtt, so they provision in parallel with the
# networking branch instead of behind it.

Parameters:

  ProjectName:
    Type: String
    Default: ecs-chaos-lab
    Description: Lowercase name prefix applied to created resources and tags.
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]{1,38}[a-z0-9])$'
    ConstraintDescription: 3-40 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens; must start and end alphanumeric.

  EnvironmentTag:
    Type: String
    Default: test
    Description: Environment this chaos lab belongs to.
    AllowedValues: [dev, test, staging]

  VpcCidr:
    Type: String
    Default: 10.0.0.0/16
    Description: CIDR block for the created VPC; subnets are carved from it and it bounds instance egress.
    AllowedPattern: '^(\d{1,3}\.){3}\d{1,3}/(1[6-9]|2[0-4])$'
    ConstraintDescription: Must be an IPv4 CIDR with a prefix length between /16 and /24.

  ChaosWaitSeconds:
    Type: Number
    Default: 300
    MinValue: 30
    MaxValue: 3600
    Description: Seconds the state machine waits after the fault before re-checking ECS service health.

  ServiceDesiredCount:
    Type: Number
    Default: 0
    MinValue: 0
    MaxValue: 4
    Description: Tasks the ECS service should run. Ships at 0 so the stack creates without waiting on runtime convergence; raise to 1 after the container instance has registered and the cached image has been imported, then run the experiment.

  EcsOptimizedAmiId:
    Type: 'AWS::SSM::Parameter::Value<AWS::EC2::Image::Id>'
    Default: /aws/service/ecs/optimized-ami/amazon-linux-2023/recommended/image_id
    Description: ECS-optimized AMI resolved from the AWS-published public SSM parameter.

Resources:

  ChaosVpc:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPC
    Properties:
      CidrBlock: !Ref VpcCidr
      EnableDnsSupport: true
      EnableDnsHostnames: true
      Tags:
        - {Key: Name, Value: !Sub '${ProjectName}-vpc'}
        - {Key: Project, Value: !Ref ProjectName}
        - {Key: Environment, Value: !Ref EnvironmentTag}
        - {Key: Purpose, Value: chaos-engineering}

  # Subnet A carries all workload capacity and every endpoint ENI. Subnet B exists in
  # a second AZ so the two-AZ upgrade is one edit away, and keeps its route-table
  # association so it is not orphaned.
  ChaosPrivateSubnetA:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref ChaosVpc
      CidrBlock: !Select [0, !Cidr [!Ref VpcCidr, 4, 8]]
      AvailabilityZone: !Select [0, !GetAZs '']
      MapPublicIpOnLaunch: false
      Tags:
        - {Key: Name, Value: !Sub '${ProjectName}-private-a'}
        - {Key: Project, Value: !Ref ProjectName}
        - {Key: Environment, Value: !Ref EnvironmentTag}
        - {Key: Purpose, Value: chaos-engineering}

  ChaosPrivateSubnetB:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref ChaosVpc
      CidrBlock: !Select [1, !Cidr [!Ref VpcCidr, 4, 8]]
      AvailabilityZone: !Select [1, !GetAZs '']
      MapPublicIpOnLaunch: false
      Tags:
        - {Key: Name, Value: !Sub '${ProjectName}-private-b'}
        - {Key: Project, Value: !Ref ProjectName}
        - {Key: Environment, Value: !Ref EnvironmentTag}
        - {Key: Purpose, Value: chaos-engineering}

  # No Internet Gateway, attachment or default route: every AWS call leaves through
  # the PrivateLink endpoints below. This supersedes the original public-egress design.
  ChaosRouteTable:
    Type: AWS::EC2::RouteTable
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref ChaosVpc
      Tags:
        - {Key: Name, Value: !Sub '${ProjectName}-rt'}
        - {Key: Project, Value: !Ref ProjectName}
        - {Key: Environment, Value: !Ref EnvironmentTag}
        - {Key: Purpose, Value: chaos-engineering}

  ChaosSubnetARouteAssociation:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation
    Properties:
      SubnetId: !Ref ChaosPrivateSubnetA
      RouteTableId: !Ref ChaosRouteTable

  ChaosSubnetBRouteAssociation:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SubnetRouteTableAssociation
    Properties:
      SubnetId: !Ref ChaosPrivateSubnetB
      RouteTableId: !Ref ChaosRouteTable

  # Egress: 443 to the in-VPC endpoints, DNS to the VPC resolver (UDP and TCP - the
  # resolver falls back to TCP for large answers), and NTP to link-local Amazon Time
  # Sync. Without DNS no hostname resolves and every AWS call fails silently; without
  # NTP, clock drift breaks SigV4. No ingress, no key pair.
  ChaosInstanceSecurityGroup:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: VPC-scoped egress-only group for the chaos-target container instance; no ingress, no key pair.
      VpcId: !Ref ChaosVpc
      SecurityGroupEgress:
        - Description: HTTPS to in-VPC interface and gateway endpoints only
          IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 443
          ToPort: 443
          CidrIp: !Ref VpcCidr
        - Description: DNS over UDP to the VPC resolver
          IpProtocol: udp
          FromPort: 53
          ToPort: 53
          CidrIp: !Ref VpcCidr
        - Description: DNS over TCP to the VPC resolver
          IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 53
          ToPort: 53
          CidrIp: !Ref VpcCidr
        - Description: NTP to the link-local Amazon Time Sync service
          IpProtocol: udp
          FromPort: 123
          ToPort: 123
          CidrIp: 169.254.169.123/32
      Tags:
        - {Key: Name, Value: !Sub '${ProjectName}-instance-sg'}
        - {Key: Project, Value: !Ref ProjectName}
        - {Key: Environment, Value: !Ref EnvironmentTag}
        - {Key: Purpose, Value: chaos-engineering}

  VpcEndpointSecurityGroup:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: Security group for the PrivateLink interface endpoints serving ECS, ECR and CloudWatch Logs.
      VpcId: !Ref ChaosVpc
      SecurityGroupEgress:
        - Description: HTTPS responses within the VPC only
          IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 443
          ToPort: 443
          CidrIp: !Ref VpcCidr
        - Description: DNS over UDP within the VPC only
          IpProtocol: udp
          FromPort: 53
          ToPort: 53
          CidrIp: !Ref VpcCidr
        - Description: DNS over TCP within the VPC only
          IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 53
          ToPort: 53
          CidrIp: !Ref VpcCidr
        - Description: NTP to the link-local Amazon Time Sync service
          IpProtocol: udp
          FromPort: 123
          ToPort: 123
          CidrIp: 169.254.169.123/32
      Tags:
        - {Key: Name, Value: !Sub '${ProjectName}-endpoint-sg'}
        - {Key: Project, Value: !Ref ProjectName}
        - {Key: Environment, Value: !Ref EnvironmentTag}
        - {Key: Purpose, Value: chaos-engineering}

  # Standalone rules: keep the two groups free of a reference cycle. Ingress is
  # sourced by group ID, never by CIDR.
  VpcEndpointSecurityGroupIngress:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroupIngress
    Properties:
      Description: HTTPS from the chaos-target container instance security group
      GroupId: !Ref VpcEndpointSecurityGroup
      IpProtocol: tcp
      FromPort: 443
      ToPort: 443
      SourceSecurityGroupId: !Ref ChaosInstanceSecurityGroup

  VpcEndpointSecurityGroupDnsUdpIngress:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroupIngress
    Properties:
      Description: DNS over UDP from the chaos-target container instance security group
      GroupId: !Ref VpcEndpointSecurityGroup
      IpProtocol: udp
      FromPort: 53
      ToPort: 53
      SourceSecurityGroupId: !Ref ChaosInstanceSecurityGroup

  VpcEndpointSecurityGroupDnsTcpIngress:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroupIngress
    Properties:
      Description: DNS over TCP from the chaos-target container instance security group
      GroupId: !Ref VpcEndpointSecurityGroup
      IpProtocol: tcp
      FromPort: 53
      ToPort: 53
      SourceSecurityGroupId: !Ref ChaosInstanceSecurityGroup

  # ecs (control plane) and ecs-agent (ACS, the channel that delivers task payloads)
  # are both mandatory for a container instance with no internet path - do not trim
  # those two. ecs-telemetry was removed to shorten provisioning time; the cost is
  # Container Insights metrics, so the cluster setting below is disabled to match.
  # Every interface endpoint is single-subnet: halving the ENIs halves the wait, and
  # the ASG is pinned to the same subnet so an instance can never land where no
  # endpoint ENI exists. Session Manager access would additionally need ssm,
  # ssmmessages and ec2messages endpoints here.
  EcsEndpoint:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPCEndpoint
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref ChaosVpc
      ServiceName: !Sub 'com.amazonaws.${AWS::Region}.ecs'
      VpcEndpointType: Interface
      PrivateDnsEnabled: true
      SubnetIds: [!Ref ChaosPrivateSubnetA]
      SecurityGroupIds: [!Ref VpcEndpointSecurityGroup]

  EcsAgentEndpoint:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPCEndpoint
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref ChaosVpc
      ServiceName: !Sub 'com.amazonaws.${AWS::Region}.ecs-agent'
      VpcEndpointType: Interface
      PrivateDnsEnabled: true
      SubnetIds: [!Ref ChaosPrivateSubnetA]
      SecurityGroupIds: [!Ref VpcEndpointSecurityGroup]

  EcrApiEndpoint:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPCEndpoint
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref ChaosVpc
      ServiceName: !Sub 'com.amazonaws.${AWS::Region}.ecr.api'
      VpcEndpointType: Interface
      PrivateDnsEnabled: true
      SubnetIds: [!Ref ChaosPrivateSubnetA]
      SecurityGroupIds: [!Ref VpcEndpointSecurityGroup]

  EcrDkrEndpoint:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPCEndpoint
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref ChaosVpc
      ServiceName: !Sub 'com.amazonaws.${AWS::Region}.ecr.dkr'
      VpcEndpointType: Interface
      PrivateDnsEnabled: true
      SubnetIds: [!Ref ChaosPrivateSubnetA]
      SecurityGroupIds: [!Ref VpcEndpointSecurityGroup]

  CloudWatchLogsEndpoint:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPCEndpoint
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref ChaosVpc
      ServiceName: !Sub 'com.amazonaws.${AWS::Region}.logs'
      VpcEndpointType: Interface
      PrivateDnsEnabled: true
      SubnetIds: [!Ref ChaosPrivateSubnetA]
      SecurityGroupIds: [!Ref VpcEndpointSecurityGroup]

  # ECR image layers live in S3; the gateway endpoint needs no security group.
  S3GatewayEndpoint:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPCEndpoint
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref ChaosVpc
      ServiceName: !Sub 'com.amazonaws.${AWS::Region}.s3'
      VpcEndpointType: Gateway
      RouteTableIds: [!Ref ChaosRouteTable]

  # No KMS alias resource: a fixed alias/... name is account-unique, unreferenced by
  # anything here (the topic and all policies bind to the key itself), and makes the
  # stack non-idempotent across retries. No Retain policy anywhere, by design.
  ChaosKmsKey:
    Type: AWS::KMS::Key
    Properties:
      Description: !Sub 'CMK encrypting ${ProjectName} chaos alert notifications.'
      Enabled: true
      EnableKeyRotation: true
      KeyUsage: ENCRYPT_DECRYPT
      KeySpec: SYMMETRIC_DEFAULT
      PendingWindowInDays: 7
      KeyPolicy:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Id: !Sub '${ProjectName}-chaos-key-policy'
        Statement:
          - Sid: EnableAccountRootAdministration
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              AWS: !Sub 'arn:aws:iam::${AWS::AccountId}:root'
            Action: 'kms:*'
            Resource: '*'
          - Sid: AllowSnsToUseTheKey
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: sns.amazonaws.com
            Action: ['kms:GenerateDataKey*', 'kms:Decrypt']
            Resource: '*'
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                'aws:SourceAccount': !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'
      Tags:
        - {Key: Name, Value: !Sub '${ProjectName}-chaos-key'}
        - {Key: Project, Value: !Ref ProjectName}
        - {Key: Environment, Value: !Ref EnvironmentTag}
        - {Key: Purpose, Value: chaos-engineering}

  # Pull-through cache: ECR fetches the upstream public image on the service side, so
  # the instance still pulls only through the ecr.api/ecr.dkr/S3 endpoints. The prefix
  # must match the task definition Image path and the ContainerInstanceRole repository
  # ARN character-for-character, or the first pull returns AccessDenied.
  PublicEcrCacheRule:
    Type: AWS::ECR::PullThroughCacheRule
    Properties:
      EcrRepositoryPrefix: !Sub '${ProjectName}-public'
      UpstreamRegistry: ecr-public
      UpstreamRegistryUrl: public.ecr.aws

  EcsTaskLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: !Sub '/ecs/${ProjectName}/resilient-app'
      RetentionInDays: 14
      Tags:
        - {Key: Project, Value: !Ref ProjectName}
        - {Key: Environment, Value: !Ref EnvironmentTag}
        - {Key: Purpose, Value: chaos-engineering}

  # Built from the same ${AWS::StackName} expression as the function names below, so the
  # /aws/lambda/<function-name> correspondence holds and retention stays explicit.
  TerminateFunctionLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: !Sub '/aws/lambda/${AWS::StackName}-terminate-instance'
      RetentionInDays: 14
      Tags:
        - {Key: Project, Value: !Ref ProjectName}
        - {Key: Environment, Value: !Ref EnvironmentTag}
        - {Key: Purpose, Value: chaos-engineering}

  HealthCheckFunctionLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: !Sub '/aws/lambda/${AWS::StackName}-health-check'
      RetentionInDays: 14
      Tags:
        - {Key: Project, Value: !Ref ProjectName}
        - {Key: Environment, Value: !Ref EnvironmentTag}
        - {Key: Purpose, Value: chaos-engineering}

  ChaosStateMachineLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: !Sub '/aws/vendedlogs/states/${AWS::StackName}-chaos-workflow'
      RetentionInDays: 14
      Tags:
        - {Key: Project, Value: !Ref ProjectName}
        - {Key: Environment, Value: !Ref EnvironmentTag}
        - {Key: Purpose, Value: chaos-engineering}

  # ClusterName omitted: !Ref yields the generated name, which the UserData and the
  # health-check IAM scope both consume, and nothing can collide on a retry.
  # containerInsights is disabled to match the removed ecs-telemetry endpoint.
  ChaosCluster:
    Type: AWS::ECS::Cluster
    Properties:
      ClusterSettings:
        - Name: containerInsights
          Value: disabled
      Tags:
        - {Key: Project, Value: !Ref ProjectName}
        - {Key: Environment, Value: !Ref EnvironmentTag}
        - {Key: Purpose, Value: chaos-engineering}

  ContainerInstanceRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      Description: Lets the chaos-target instance join the ECS cluster and populate the pull-through cache.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: ec2.amazonaws.com
            Action: 'sts:AssumeRole'
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AmazonEC2ContainerServiceforEC2Role
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: pull-through-cache
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              # Cache population only. GetAuthorizationToken, BatchGetImage,
              # GetDownloadUrlForLayer and BatchCheckLayerAvailability are already
              # granted by AmazonEC2ContainerServiceforEC2Role - do not duplicate them.
              - Sid: PopulateCachedPublicImages
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - 'ecr:CreateRepository'
                  - 'ecr:BatchImportUpstreamImage'
                  - 'ecr:TagResource'
                  - 'ecr:ReplicateImage'
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:aws:ecr:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:repository/${ProjectName}-public/*'
      Tags:
        - {Key: Project, Value: !Ref ProjectName}
        - {Key: Environment, Value: !Ref EnvironmentTag}
        - {Key: Purpose, Value: chaos-engineering}

  ContainerInstanceProfile:
    Type: AWS::IAM::InstanceProfile
    Properties:
      Roles: [!Ref ContainerInstanceRole]

  ChaosTargetLaunchTemplate:
    Type: AWS::EC2::LaunchTemplate
    Properties:
      LaunchTemplateData:
        ImageId: !Ref EcsOptimizedAmiId
        InstanceType: t3.micro
        IamInstanceProfile:
          Arn: !GetAtt ContainerInstanceProfile.Arn
        SecurityGroupIds: [!Ref ChaosInstanceSecurityGroup]
        Monitoring:
          Enabled: true
        # IMDSv2 only; hop limit 2 because bridge-mode tasks cross an extra hop.
        MetadataOptions:
          HttpEndpoint: enabled
          HttpTokens: required
          HttpPutResponseHopLimit: 2
          InstanceMetadataTags: enabled
        BlockDeviceMappings:
          - DeviceName: /dev/xvda
            Ebs:
              VolumeSize: 30
              VolumeType: gp3
              Encrypted: true
              DeleteOnTermination: true
        # Role=chaos-target is load-bearing: the Lambda filter and its IAM condition select on it.
        TagSpecifications:
          - ResourceType: instance
            Tags:
              - {Key: Name, Value: !Sub '${ProjectName}-chaos-target'}
              - {Key: Role, Value: chaos-target}
              - {Key: Project, Value: !Ref ProjectName}
              - {Key: Environment, Value: !Ref EnvironmentTag}
              - {Key: Purpose, Value: chaos-engineering}
          - ResourceType: volume
            Tags:
              - {Key: Role, Value: chaos-target}
              - {Key: Project, Value: !Ref ProjectName}
              - {Key: Environment, Value: !Ref EnvironmentTag}
              - {Key: Purpose, Value: chaos-engineering}
        # Configuration only - no signal apparatus. The AWS CLI and cfn-bootstrap
        # cannot be installed in a subnet with no internet path, so a failure here
        # surfaces as an ECS placement failure at scale-up, not a silent timeout.
        UserData:
          Fn::Base64: !Sub |
            #!/bin/bash
            set -euo pipefail
            echo "ECS_CLUSTER=${ChaosCluster}" >> /etc/ecs/ecs.config
            echo "ECS_ENABLE_CONTAINER_METADATA=true" >> /etc/ecs/ecs.config
            echo "ECS_AVAILABLE_LOGGING_DRIVERS=[\"json-file\",\"awslogs\"]" >> /etc/ecs/ecs.config
            systemctl enable --now ecs
      TagSpecifications:
        - ResourceType: launch-template
          Tags:
            - {Key: Project, Value: !Ref ProjectName}
            - {Key: Environment, Value: !Ref EnvironmentTag}
            - {Key: Purpose, Value: chaos-engineering}

  # No DependsOn on the endpoints: with ServiceDesiredCount 0 nothing is placed and no
  # image is pulled at deploy time, so endpoint readiness is a scale-up precondition,
  # not a create-time one - and the ECS agent retries registration far longer than
  # endpoint provisioning takes. VPCZoneIdentifier is pinned to subnet A, the only
  # subnet holding endpoint ENIs.
  ChaosTargetAutoScalingGroup:
    Type: AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup
    Properties:
      MinSize: '1'
      MaxSize: '1'
      DesiredCapacity: '1'
      VPCZoneIdentifier: [!Ref ChaosPrivateSubnetA]
      LaunchTemplate:
        LaunchTemplateId: !Ref ChaosTargetLaunchTemplate
        Version: !GetAtt ChaosTargetLaunchTemplate.LatestVersionNumber
      HealthCheckType: EC2
      HealthCheckGracePeriod: 60
      Tags:
        - {Key: Project, Value: !Ref ProjectName, PropagateAtLaunch: true}

  ChaosTaskDefinition:
    Type: AWS::ECS::TaskDefinition
    # Image path must match PublicEcrCacheRule.EcrRepositoryPrefix character-for-character.
    DependsOn: PublicEcrCacheRule
    Properties:
      Family: !Sub '${ProjectName}-resilient-app'
      RequiresCompatibilities: [EC2]
      NetworkMode: bridge
      ContainerDefinitions:
        - Name: resilient-app
          # Upstream public.ecr.aws/docker/library/nginx:alpine - the Docker Hub
          # official-images mirror on ECR Public. Small layer set, so the cold
          # pull-through import is fast.
          Image: !Sub '${AWS::AccountId}.dkr.ecr.${AWS::Region}.amazonaws.com/${ProjectName}-public/docker/library/nginx:alpine'
          Cpu: 256
          Memory: 256
          Essential: true
          PortMappings:
            - ContainerPort: 80
              Protocol: tcp
          LogConfiguration:
            LogDriver: awslogs
            Options:
              awslogs-group: !Ref EcsTaskLogGroup
              awslogs-region: !Ref 'AWS::Region'
              awslogs-stream-prefix: resilient-app
      Tags:
        - {Key: Project, Value: !Ref ProjectName}
        - {Key: Environment, Value: !Ref EnvironmentTag}
        - {Key: Purpose, Value: chaos-engineering}

  # DesiredCount comes from ServiceDesiredCount (default 0) so CREATE returns as soon
  # as the service object exists: AWS::ECS::Service otherwise blocks until
  # runningCount == desiredCount with no deadline. With nothing to place, the service
  # needs no DependsOn on capacity either - ordering at scale-up is the operator's step.
  # MinimumHealthyPercent 0 / MaximumPercent 200 are unchanged: they are what let the
  # experiment drive running capacity to zero once the count is raised.
  # DeploymentCircuitBreaker is deliberately omitted (unverified interaction with
  # MinimumHealthyPercent 0); it is the intended follow-up for operator ergonomics.
  # ServiceName must stay character-identical to the health-check Lambda's SERVICE_NAME
  # and to the EcsServiceName output.
  ChaosService:
    Type: AWS::ECS::Service
    Properties:
      ServiceName: !Sub '${ProjectName}-service'
      Cluster: !Ref ChaosCluster
      TaskDefinition: !Ref ChaosTaskDefinition
      LaunchType: EC2
      DesiredCount: !Ref ServiceDesiredCount
      SchedulingStrategy: REPLICA
      DeploymentConfiguration:
        MinimumHealthyPercent: 0
        MaximumPercent: 200
      EnableECSManagedTags: true
      PropagateTags: SERVICE
      Tags:
        - {Key: Project, Value: !Ref ProjectName}
        - {Key: Environment, Value: !Ref EnvironmentTag}
        - {Key: Purpose, Value: chaos-engineering}

  # TopicName omitted: !Ref yields the ARN the Lambda and state machine consume.
  ChaosAlertTopic:
    Type: AWS::SNS::Topic
    Properties:
      DisplayName: !Sub '${ProjectName} chaos experiment alerts'
      KmsMasterKeyId: !Ref ChaosKmsKey
      Tags:
        - {Key: Project, Value: !Ref ProjectName}
        - {Key: Environment, Value: !Ref EnvironmentTag}
        - {Key: Purpose, Value: chaos-engineering}

  ChaosAlertTopicPolicy:
    Type: AWS::SNS::TopicPolicy
    Properties:
      Topics: [!Ref ChaosAlertTopic]
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllowHealthCheckLambdaRoleToPublish
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              AWS: !GetAtt HealthCheckFunctionRole.Arn
            Action: 'sns:Publish'
            Resource: !Ref ChaosAlertTopic
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                'aws:SourceAccount': !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'

  TerminateFunctionRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      Description: Least-privilege execution role for the chaos terminate Lambda.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: lambda.amazonaws.com
            Action: 'sts:AssumeRole'
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: terminate-chaos-target
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              # No fixed instance ID exists: the ASG replaces it, so scope by tag.
              - Sid: TerminateOnlyTaggedChaosTargets
                Effect: Allow
                Action: 'ec2:TerminateInstances'
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:aws:ec2:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:instance/*'
                Condition:
                  StringEquals:
                    'ec2:ResourceTag/Role': chaos-target
                    'ec2:ResourceTag/Project': !Ref ProjectName
              - Sid: DescribeInstancesInThisRegion
                Effect: Allow
                Action: 'ec2:DescribeInstances'
                Resource: '*'
                Condition:
                  StringEquals:
                    'ec2:Region': !Ref 'AWS::Region'
        - PolicyName: terminate-fn-logging
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: WriteToOwnLogGroupOnly
                Effect: Allow
                Action: ['logs:CreateLogStream', 'logs:PutLogEvents']
                Resource: !GetAtt TerminateFunctionLogGroup.Arn
      Tags:
        - {Key: Project, Value: !Ref ProjectName}
        - {Key: Environment, Value: !Ref EnvironmentTag}
        - {Key: Purpose, Value: chaos-engineering}

  HealthCheckFunctionRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      Description: Least-privilege execution role for the ECS health-check and alerting Lambda.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: lambda.amazonaws.com
            Action: 'sts:AssumeRole'
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: describe-chaos-service
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: DescribeServicesInThisClusterOnly
                Effect: Allow
                Action: 'ecs:DescribeServices'
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:aws:ecs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:service/${ChaosCluster}/*'
        - PolicyName: publish-chaos-alerts
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: PublishToChaosAlertTopicOnly
                Effect: Allow
                Action: 'sns:Publish'
                Resource: !Ref ChaosAlertTopic
              - Sid: UseChaosKeyForTopicEncryption
                Effect: Allow
                Action: ['kms:GenerateDataKey', 'kms:Decrypt']
                Resource: !GetAtt ChaosKmsKey.Arn
        - PolicyName: health-check-fn-logging
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: WriteToOwnLogGroupOnly
                Effect: Allow
                Action: ['logs:CreateLogStream', 'logs:PutLogEvents']
                Resource: !GetAtt HealthCheckFunctionLogGroup.Arn
      Tags:
        - {Key: Project, Value: !Ref ProjectName}
        - {Key: Environment, Value: !Ref EnvironmentTag}
        - {Key: Purpose, Value: chaos-engineering}

  TerminateInstanceFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    DependsOn: TerminateFunctionLogGroup
    Properties:
      FunctionName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-terminate-instance'
      Description: Discovers the tagged chaos-target instance, terminates it and records the start time.
      Runtime: python3.12
      Handler: index.lambda_handler
      Architectures: [arm64]
      Timeout: 60
      MemorySize: 256
      Role: !GetAtt TerminateFunctionRole.Arn
      Environment:
        Variables:
          TARGET_ASG_NAME: !Ref ChaosTargetAutoScalingGroup
          TARGET_TAG_KEY: Role
          TARGET_TAG_VALUE: chaos-target
          PROJECT_NAME: !Ref ProjectName
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          import datetime, os, boto3

          EC2 = boto3.client("ec2")

          def _find(tag_key, tag_value, project):
              pages = EC2.get_paginator("describe_instances").paginate(Filters=[
                  {"Name": "tag:" + tag_key, "Values": [tag_value]},
                  {"Name": "tag:Project", "Values": [project]},
                  {"Name": "instance-state-name", "Values": ["running"]}])
              for page in pages:
                  for res in page.get("Reservations", []):
                      for inst in res.get("Instances", []):
                          return inst
              return None

          def lambda_handler(event, context):
              tag_key = os.environ["TARGET_TAG_KEY"]
              tag_value = os.environ["TARGET_TAG_VALUE"]
              project = os.environ["PROJECT_NAME"]
              asg = os.environ["TARGET_ASG_NAME"]
              started_at = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat()
              target = _find(tag_key, tag_value, project)
              if target is None:
                  return {"terminated": False, "instanceId": None, "previousState": "none",
                          "currentState": "none", "autoScalingGroupName": asg,
                          "reason": "No running instance tagged %s=%s with Project=%s; capacity may still be launching." % (tag_key, tag_value, project),
                          "experimentStartedAt": started_at}
              instance_id = target["InstanceId"]
              changes = EC2.terminate_instances(InstanceIds=[instance_id]).get("TerminatingInstances") or [{}]
              return {"terminated": True, "instanceId": instance_id,
                      "previousState": changes[0].get("PreviousState", {}).get("name", "unknown"),
                      "currentState": changes[0].get("CurrentState", {}).get("name", "unknown"),
                      "autoScalingGroupName": asg,
                      "reason": "Chaos target terminated; the Auto Scaling group will relaunch capacity.",
                      "experimentStartedAt": started_at}
      Tags:
        - {Key: Project, Value: !Ref ProjectName}
        - {Key: Environment, Value: !Ref EnvironmentTag}
        - {Key: Purpose, Value: chaos-engineering}

  # SERVICE_NAME is built from the same Fn::Sub as ChaosService.ServiceName rather than
  # a GetAtt: the value is statically known, and the GetAtt would put this function,
  # the state machine and its role behind the whole networking branch. Keep the two
  # expressions in sync.
  HealthCheckFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    DependsOn: HealthCheckFunctionLogGroup
    Properties:
      FunctionName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-health-check'
      Description: Evaluates ECS service health after the fault and publishes an SNS alert when unhealthy.
      Runtime: python3.12
      Handler: index.lambda_handler
      Architectures: [arm64]
      Timeout: 60
      MemorySize: 256
      Role: !GetAtt HealthCheckFunctionRole.Arn
      Environment:
        Variables:
          CLUSTER_NAME: !Ref ChaosCluster
          SERVICE_NAME: !Sub '${ProjectName}-service'
          ALERT_TOPIC_ARN: !Ref ChaosAlertTopic
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          import datetime, json, os, boto3

          ECS = boto3.client("ecs")
          SNS = boto3.client("sns")

          def _alert(topic_arn, payload):
              SNS.publish(TopicArn=topic_arn,
                          Subject="Chaos experiment: ECS service UNHEALTHY",
                          Message=json.dumps(payload, indent=2, default=str),
                          MessageAttributes={"severity": {"DataType": "String", "StringValue": "HIGH"}})

          def lambda_handler(event, context):
              cluster = os.environ["CLUSTER_NAME"]
              service = os.environ["SERVICE_NAME"]
              topic_arn = os.environ["ALERT_TOPIC_ARN"]
              checked_at = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat()
              services = ECS.describe_services(cluster=cluster, services=[service]).get("services") or []
              if not services:
                  result = {"healthy": False, "clusterName": cluster, "serviceName": service,
                            "runningCount": 0, "desiredCount": 0, "rolloutStates": [],
                            "reason": "DescribeServices returned no matching service.",
                            "checkedAt": checked_at, "upstream": event}
                  _alert(topic_arn, result)
                  return result
              svc = services[0]
              running = int(svc.get("runningCount", 0))
              desired = int(svc.get("desiredCount", 0))
              states = [d.get("rolloutState", "UNKNOWN") for d in svc.get("deployments") or []]
              # A service scaled to zero has nothing to be healthy about: 0 == 0 would
              # otherwise report a passing experiment against a service running nothing.
              if desired == 0:
                  result = {"healthy": False, "clusterName": cluster,
                            "serviceName": svc.get("serviceName", service), "serviceArn": svc.get("serviceArn"),
                            "runningCount": running, "desiredCount": desired, "rolloutStates": states,
                            "reason": "Service %s has desiredCount 0 and is not scaled up; raise the ServiceDesiredCount parameter to 1 and confirm a task is running before judging the experiment." % service,
                            "checkedAt": checked_at, "upstream": event}
                  _alert(topic_arn, result)
                  return result
              reasons = []
              if running < desired:
                  reasons.append("runningCount %d below desiredCount %d" % (running, desired))
              degraded = [s for s in states if s != "COMPLETED"]
              if degraded:
                  reasons.append("rolloutState(s) not COMPLETED: " + ", ".join(degraded))
              result = {"healthy": not reasons, "clusterName": cluster,
                        "serviceName": svc.get("serviceName", service), "serviceArn": svc.get("serviceArn"),
                        "runningCount": running, "desiredCount": desired,
                        "pendingCount": int(svc.get("pendingCount", 0)), "rolloutStates": states,
                        "reason": "; ".join(reasons) or "Service is at desired capacity.",
                        "checkedAt": checked_at, "upstream": event}
              if reasons:
                  _alert(topic_arn, result)
              return result
      Tags:
        - {Key: Project, Value: !Ref ProjectName}
        - {Key: Environment, Value: !Ref EnvironmentTag}
        - {Key: Purpose, Value: chaos-engineering}

  ChaosStateMachineRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      Description: Execution role for the chaos engineering state machine.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: states.amazonaws.com
            Action: 'sts:AssumeRole'
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                'aws:SourceAccount': !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'
              ArnLike:
                # Must stay character-identical to StateMachineName below.
                'aws:SourceArn': !Sub 'arn:aws:states:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:stateMachine:${AWS::StackName}-chaos-workflow'
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: invoke-chaos-functions
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: InvokeOnlyTheTwoChaosFunctions
                Effect: Allow
                Action: 'lambda:InvokeFunction'
                Resource:
                  - !GetAtt TerminateInstanceFunction.Arn
                  - !GetAtt HealthCheckFunction.Arn
                  - !Sub '${TerminateInstanceFunction.Arn}:*'
                  - !Sub '${HealthCheckFunction.Arn}:*'
        - PolicyName: publish-failure-alerts
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: PublishWorkflowFailureAlerts
                Effect: Allow
                Action: 'sns:Publish'
                Resource: !Ref ChaosAlertTopic
              - Sid: UseChaosKeyForTopicEncryption
                Effect: Allow
                Action: ['kms:GenerateDataKey', 'kms:Decrypt']
                Resource: !GetAtt ChaosKmsKey.Arn
        - PolicyName: state-machine-log-delivery
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              # Log-delivery actions do not support resource-level permissions.
              - Sid: LogDeliveryManagement
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - 'logs:CreateLogDelivery'
                  - 'logs:GetLogDelivery'
                  - 'logs:UpdateLogDelivery'
                  - 'logs:DeleteLogDelivery'
                  - 'logs:ListLogDeliveries'
                  - 'logs:PutResourcePolicy'
                  - 'logs:DescribeResourcePolicies'
                  - 'logs:DescribeLogGroups'
                Resource: '*'
        - PolicyName: state-machine-xray
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: XRayTracing
                Effect: Allow
                Action: ['xray:PutTraceSegments', 'xray:PutTelemetryRecords', 'xray:GetSamplingRules', 'xray:GetSamplingTargets']
                Resource: '*'
      Tags:
        - {Key: Project, Value: !Ref ProjectName}
        - {Key: Environment, Value: !Ref EnvironmentTag}
        - {Key: Purpose, Value: chaos-engineering}

  ChaosStateMachine:
    Type: AWS::StepFunctions::StateMachine
    Properties:
      StateMachineName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-chaos-workflow'
      StateMachineType: STANDARD
      RoleArn: !GetAtt ChaosStateMachineRole.Arn
      TracingConfiguration:
        Enabled: true
      LoggingConfiguration:
        Level: ALL
        IncludeExecutionData: true
        Destinations:
          - CloudWatchLogsLogGroup:
              LogGroupArn: !GetAtt ChaosStateMachineLogGroup.Arn
      DefinitionSubstitutions:
        TerminateFunctionArn: !GetAtt TerminateInstanceFunction.Arn
        HealthCheckFunctionArn: !GetAtt HealthCheckFunction.Arn
        WaitSeconds: !Ref ChaosWaitSeconds
        AlertTopicArn: !Ref ChaosAlertTopic
      # ${!Name} escapes leave the DefinitionSubstitutions placeholders for Step Functions.
      DefinitionString: !Sub |
        {
          "Comment": "${ProjectName} chaos experiment",
          "StartAt": "TerminateInstance",
          "States": {
            "TerminateInstance": {
              "Type": "Task",
              "Resource": "arn:aws:states:::lambda:invoke",
              "Parameters": {
                "FunctionName": "${!TerminateFunctionArn}",
                "Payload.$": "$"
              },
              "Retry": [
                {
                  "ErrorEquals": [
                    "Lambda.ServiceException",
                    "Lambda.AWSLambdaException",
                    "Lambda.SdkClientException",
                    "Lambda.TooManyRequestsException"
                  ],
                  "IntervalSeconds": 2,
                  "MaxAttempts": 3,
                  "BackoffRate": 2
                }
              ],
              "Catch": [
                {
                  "ErrorEquals": ["States.ALL"],
                  "ResultPath": "$.error",
                  "Next": "NotifyWorkflowError"
                }
              ],
              "ResultPath": "$.termination",
              "Next": "WaitForRecovery"
            },
            "WaitForRecovery": {
              "Type": "Wait",
              "Seconds": ${!WaitSeconds},
              "Next": "CheckServiceHealth"
            },
            "CheckServiceHealth": {
              "Type": "Task",
              "Resource": "arn:aws:states:::lambda:invoke",
              "Parameters": {
                "FunctionName": "${!HealthCheckFunctionArn}",
                "Payload.$": "$"
              },
              "Retry": [
                {
                  "ErrorEquals": [
                    "Lambda.ServiceException",
                    "Lambda.AWSLambdaException",
                    "Lambda.SdkClientException",
                    "Lambda.TooManyRequestsException"
                  ],
                  "IntervalSeconds": 2,
                  "MaxAttempts": 3,
                  "BackoffRate": 2
                }
              ],
              "Catch": [
                {
                  "ErrorEquals": ["States.ALL"],
                  "ResultPath": "$.error",
                  "Next": "NotifyWorkflowError"
                }
              ],
              "Next": "EvaluateHealth"
            },
            "EvaluateHealth": {
              "Type": "Choice",
              "Choices": [
                {
                  "Variable": "$.Payload.healthy",
                  "BooleanEquals": true,
                  "Next": "ExperimentPassed"
                }
              ],
              "Default": "NotifyUnhealthy"
            },
            "NotifyUnhealthy": {
              "Type": "Task",
              "Resource": "arn:aws:states:::sns:publish",
              "Parameters": {
                "TopicArn": "${!AlertTopicArn}",
                "Subject": "Chaos experiment FAILED: ECS service did not recover",
                "Message": {
                  "verdict": "UNHEALTHY",
                  "detail.$": "$.Payload"
                }
              },
              "ResultPath": "$.notification",
              "Next": "ExperimentFailed"
            },
            "NotifyWorkflowError": {
              "Type": "Task",
              "Resource": "arn:aws:states:::sns:publish",
              "Parameters": {
                "TopicArn": "${!AlertTopicArn}",
                "Subject": "Chaos experiment ERROR: workflow step failed",
                "Message": {
                  "verdict": "WORKFLOW_ERROR",
                  "detail.$": "$.error"
                }
              },
              "ResultPath": "$.notification",
              "Next": "ExperimentFailed"
            },
            "ExperimentPassed": {
              "Type": "Succeed"
            },
            "ExperimentFailed": {
              "Type": "Fail",
              "Error": "ChaosExperimentFailed",
              "Cause": "Service unhealthy after the recovery window or a step errored; SNS alert published."
            }
          }
        }
      Tags:
        - {Key: Project, Value: !Ref ProjectName}
        - {Key: Environment, Value: !Ref EnvironmentTag}
        - {Key: Purpose, Value: chaos-engineering}

Description: >-
  DevOps Agent Space stack - provisions an AWS DevOps Agent (aidevops) Agent Space,
  the IAM service role the agent assumes to operate in this account, the IAM role
  backing the operator application, and the association that registers the deploying
  account as the primary (monitor) account for the agent space.

# Schema notes (verified against the CloudFormation resource specification for
# us-east-1 and the AWS::DevOpsAgent::* registry schemas):
#   * The agent space resource type is AWS::DevOpsAgent::AgentSpace. Its confirmed
#     properties are Name, Description, KmsKeyArn, Locale, Preferences, OperatorApp
#     and Tags; its confirmed attributes are AgentSpaceId, Arn, CreatedAt, UpdatedAt.
#   * OMITTED OBJECTIVE: the agent space schema exposes exactly one role property,
#     OperatorApp.Iam.OperatorAppRoleArn. There is no agent-service-role property on
#     the agent space, so the agent role ARN is wired where the schema actually
#     accepts it - Association.Configuration.Aws.AssumableRoleArn below. No property
#     name has been invented by analogy.
#   * OMITTED OBJECTIVE: the agent space schema exposes no operator/portal URL
#     attribute, so the OperatorUrl output is a constructed, region-parameterised
#     console URL rather than a !GetAtt.
#   * The monitoring-account association is modelled with the confirmed resource type
#     AWS::DevOpsAgent::Association using Configuration.Aws (AccountType enum value
#     "monitor", ServiceId fixed literal "aws" per the schema). The AWS::Oam::Sink
#     fallback shape is therefore NOT used - a dedicated, schema-confirmed association
#     exists for this requirement.
#   * Iteration 1 fix: the previous payload leaked Markdown code fences and trailing
#     prose into the validated document, which aborted the YAML tokenizer one line
#     past the template body. The template body itself is unchanged.

Parameters:
  AgentSpaceName:
    Type: String
    Default: devops-agent-space
    Description: Name of the DevOps Agent Space; also used to name the IAM roles.
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?$'
    ConstraintDescription: Must be lowercase alphanumeric characters and hyphens only, and must start and end with an alphanumeric character.
    MinLength: 1
    MaxLength: 64

  EnvironmentTag:
    Type: String
    Default: production
    Description: Environment classification applied as a tag to every taggable resource.
    AllowedValues:
      - development
      - staging
      - production

Resources:

  # IAM role the aidevops service assumes to operate in this account on the
  # customer's behalf. Referenced by the monitoring association below.
  AgentServiceRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Sub '${AgentSpaceName}-agent-role'
      Path: /service-role/
      MaxSessionDuration: 3600
      Description: !Sub 'Service role assumed by AWS DevOps Agent for agent space ${AgentSpaceName}.'
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllowAIDevOpsServiceToAssume
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: aidevops.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                aws:SourceAccount: !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'
              ArnLike:
                # Confused-deputy guard. The aidevops agent space ARN format is
                # arn:<partition>:aidevops:<region>:<account>:agentspace/<agentspace-id>,
                # where <agentspace-id> is a service-generated identifier rather than
                # AgentSpaceName, and !GetAtt on the agent space would invert the
                # dependency direction (the agent space consumes these role ARNs), so
                # the resource segment is wildcarded while partition, region and
                # account stay pinned to this deployment.
                aws:SourceArn: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:aidevops:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:agentspace/*'
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::aws:policy/AIDevOpsAgentAccessPolicy'
        - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::aws:policy/CloudWatchReadOnlyAccess'
        - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::aws:policy/AWSXrayReadOnlyAccess'
        - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::aws:policy/AWSCloudTrail_ReadOnlyAccess'
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: AgentServiceLinkedRoleCreation
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: CreateAIDevOpsServiceLinkedRole
                Effect: Allow
                Action: iam:CreateServiceLinkedRole
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::${AWS::AccountId}:role/aws-service-role/aidevops.amazonaws.com/*'
                Condition:
                  StringEquals:
                    iam:AWSServiceName: aidevops.amazonaws.com
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Ref AgentSpaceName
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentTag
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: CloudFormation

  # IAM role backing the operator application (OperatorApp IAM auth mode).
  # Deliberately narrower than AgentServiceRole - operator-app access plus
  # read-only visibility into the agent space, no observability data plane.
  OperatorRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Sub '${AgentSpaceName}-operator-role'
      Path: /service-role/
      MaxSessionDuration: 3600
      Description: !Sub 'Role used by the DevOps Agent operator application for agent space ${AgentSpaceName}.'
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllowAIDevOpsOperatorAppToAssume
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: aidevops.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                aws:SourceAccount: !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'
              ArnLike:
                aws:SourceArn: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:aidevops:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:agentspace/*'
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::aws:policy/AIDevOpsOperatorAppAccessPolicy'
        - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::aws:policy/AIDevOpsAgentReadOnlyAccess'
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Ref AgentSpaceName
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentTag
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: CloudFormation

  # Holds agent space configuration and investigation state - retained on stack
  # delete and on replacement.
  DevOpsAgentSpace:
    Type: AWS::DevOpsAgent::AgentSpace
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      Name: !Ref AgentSpaceName
      Description: !Sub 'DevOps Agent Space ${AgentSpaceName} managed by CloudFormation.'
      OperatorApp:
        Iam:
          OperatorAppRoleArn: !GetAtt OperatorRole.Arn
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Ref AgentSpaceName
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentTag
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: CloudFormation

  # Registers the deploying account as the primary monitoring ("monitor") account
  # for the agent space, and supplies the role the agent assumes there.
  PrimaryMonitoringAccountAssociation:
    Type: AWS::DevOpsAgent::Association
    Properties:
      AgentSpaceId: !GetAtt DevOpsAgentSpace.AgentSpaceId
      ServiceId: aws
      Configuration:
        Aws:
          AccountId: !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'
          AccountType: monitor
          AssumableRoleArn: !GetAtt AgentServiceRole.Arn

Outputs:

  AgentSpaceId:
    Description: Unique identifier of the DevOps Agent Space.
    Value: !GetAtt DevOpsAgentSpace.AgentSpaceId
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-AgentSpaceId'

  AgentSpaceArn:
    Description: ARN of the DevOps Agent Space.
    Value: !GetAtt DevOpsAgentSpace.Arn
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-AgentSpaceArn'

  AgentSpaceName:
    Description: Name of the DevOps Agent Space.
    Value: !Ref AgentSpaceName
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-AgentSpaceName'

  OperatorUrl:
    Description: Console URL for the DevOps Agent operator application for this agent space.
    Value: !Sub 'https://${AWS::Region}.console.aws.amazon.com/devops-agent/home?region=${AWS::Region}#/agentspaces/${DevOpsAgentSpace.AgentSpaceId}'
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-OperatorUrl'

  AgentServiceRoleArn:
    Description: ARN of the IAM role assumed by the DevOps Agent service.
    Value: !GetAtt AgentServiceRole.Arn
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-AgentServiceRoleArn'

  OperatorRoleArn:
    Description: ARN of the IAM role used by the operator application.
    Value: !GetAtt OperatorRole.Arn
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-OperatorRoleArn'
