AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  Greenfield demo stack that creates stack-scoped SSM Parameter Store parameters
  and a Secrets Manager secret with a generated password, plus a Python 3.12
  Lambda function (ParameterStoreDemo) that reads every parameter under the
  stack path and every secret matching the stack name prefix. No CloudFormation
  Parameters are declared: every value is either a literal, derived from a
  pseudo-parameter, or generated by a resource in this template.

Resources:

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # SSM Parameter Store
  #
  # All parameters live under /<stack-name>/config/ so a single
  # ssm:GetParametersByPath call (Recursive=True) retrieves the whole set.
  #
  # NOTE: AWS::SSM::Parameter supports only Type: String and Type: StringList in
  # CloudFormation. SecureString parameters cannot be created by CloudFormation,
  # so anything requiring encryption at rest is stored in the Secrets Manager
  # secret below instead of in Parameter Store.
  #
  # AWS::SSM::Parameter takes Tags as a map (key: value), not a list of
  # {Key, Value} objects, unlike Lambda / IAM / Secrets Manager.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  AppNameParameter:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '/${AWS::StackName}/config/app_name'
      Type: String
      Value: parameter-store-demo
      Description: Logical application name used by the demo Lambda function.
      Tier: Standard
      Tags:
        Application: parameter-store-demo
        StackName: !Ref 'AWS::StackName'

  EnvironmentParameter:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '/${AWS::StackName}/config/environment'
      Type: String
      Value: dev
      Description: Deployment environment label for the demo application.
      Tier: Standard
      Tags:
        Application: parameter-store-demo
        StackName: !Ref 'AWS::StackName'

  LogLevelParameter:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '/${AWS::StackName}/config/log_level'
      Type: String
      Value: INFO
      Description: Log verbosity level for the demo application.
      Tier: Standard
      Tags:
        Application: parameter-store-demo
        StackName: !Ref 'AWS::StackName'

  FeatureFlagsParameter:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '/${AWS::StackName}/config/feature_flags'
      Type: String
      Value: 'alpha,beta'
      Description: Comma-separated list of enabled feature flags.
      Tier: Standard
      Tags:
        Application: parameter-store-demo
        StackName: !Ref 'AWS::StackName'

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Secrets Manager
  #
  # The secret name is prefixed with the stack name so the Lambda can find it
  # with a name-prefix filter that matches the same stack scope as the SSM path.
  # The password is generated by Secrets Manager - no plaintext credential ever
  # appears in this template, and no {{resolve:...}} dynamic reference is used.
  #
  # Retained on delete/replace because it holds generated credential material.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  DemoSecret:
    Type: AWS::SecretsManager::Secret
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}/demo/db-credentials'
      Description: !Sub 'Demo database credentials generated for stack ${AWS::StackName}.'
      GenerateSecretString:
        SecretStringTemplate: '{"username": "admin"}'
        GenerateStringKey: password
        PasswordLength: 32
        ExcludeCharacters: '"@/\'
        ExcludePunctuation: false
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: parameter-store-demo
        - Key: StackName
          Value: !Ref 'AWS::StackName'

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # IAM execution role
  #
  # The AWS-managed basic execution policy is attached via ManagedPolicyArns
  # (a static, account-independent ARN); everything else is an inline policy.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  LambdaExecutionRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      Description: Execution role for the ParameterStoreDemo Lambda function.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: lambda.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: ParameterStoreDemoAccess
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              # Read access is scoped to this stack's parameter path only.
              # ssm:DescribeParameters is deliberately omitted: it does not
              # support resource-level permissions and would require
              # Resource '*'. GetParametersByPath with Recursive=True covers
              # the discovery use case within the scoped path.
              - Sid: ReadStackScopedParameters
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - ssm:GetParametersByPath
                  - ssm:GetParameter
                  - ssm:GetParameters
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:ssm:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:parameter/${AWS::StackName}/*'
              # secretsmanager:ListSecrets is an account-level listing API: it
              # does not support resource-level permissions, so it can only be
              # granted with Resource '*'. It is isolated in its own statement
              # so the scoped statement below is not weakened. ListSecrets
              # returns metadata only - it never returns secret values.
              - Sid: ListSecretsAccountWide
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - secretsmanager:ListSecrets
                Resource: '*'
              # Value access is scoped to the single secret created here.
              # !Ref on AWS::SecretsManager::Secret returns the secret ARN.
              - Sid: ReadDemoSecret
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - secretsmanager:GetSecretValue
                  - secretsmanager:DescribeSecret
                Resource: !Ref DemoSecret
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: parameter-store-demo
        - Key: StackName
          Value: !Ref 'AWS::StackName'

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Log group
  #
  # Created explicitly so retention is bounded (14 days) instead of the default
  # "never expire". Because the function name is a hardcoded literal
  # (ParameterStoreDemo), the log group name must be the matching literal
  # /aws/lambda/ParameterStoreDemo - therefore this template can only be
  # deployed once per account per region.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  LambdaLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: /aws/lambda/ParameterStoreDemo
      RetentionInDays: 14

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Lambda function
  #
  # The code is supplied inline via Code.ZipFile using the boto3 SDK bundled
  # with the python3.12 runtime, so no pre-existing S3 deployment bucket is
  # required. The body contains no ${...} sequences and is NOT wrapped in
  # Fn::Sub. The function is invoked manually - no custom resource invokes it
  # at deploy time.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  ParameterStoreDemoFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      FunctionName: ParameterStoreDemo
      Description: Prints stack-scoped SSM parameters and Secrets Manager secrets.
      Runtime: python3.12
      Handler: index.lambda_handler
      Timeout: 30
      MemorySize: 256
      Role: !GetAtt LambdaExecutionRole.Arn
      Environment:
        Variables:
          STACK_NAME: !Ref 'AWS::StackName'
          PARAMETER_PATH: !Sub '/${AWS::StackName}/'
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          import json
          import logging
          import os

          import boto3
          from botocore.exceptions import ClientError

          logger = logging.getLogger()
          logger.setLevel(logging.INFO)

          ssm = boto3.client('ssm')
          secretsmanager = boto3.client('secretsmanager')


          def collect_parameters(path):
              """Return every parameter under the given SSM path."""
              parameters = []
              next_token = None
              while True:
                  kwargs = {
                      'Path': path,
                      'Recursive': True,
                      'WithDecryption': True,
                      'MaxResults': 10,
                  }
                  if next_token:
                      kwargs['NextToken'] = next_token
                  response = ssm.get_parameters_by_path(**kwargs)
                  parameters.extend(response.get('Parameters', []))
                  next_token = response.get('NextToken')
                  if not next_token:
                      break
              return parameters


          def collect_secrets(name_prefix):
              """Return metadata for every secret whose name matches the prefix."""
              secrets = []
              next_token = None
              while True:
                  kwargs = {
                      'Filters': [{'Key': 'name', 'Values': [name_prefix]}],
                      'MaxResults': 20,
                  }
                  if next_token:
                      kwargs['NextToken'] = next_token
                  response = secretsmanager.list_secrets(**kwargs)
                  secrets.extend(response.get('SecretList', []))
                  next_token = response.get('NextToken')
                  if not next_token:
                      break
              return secrets


          def describe_secret_keys(secret_id):
              """Return the JSON key names in a secret, never the values."""
              response = secretsmanager.get_secret_value(SecretId=secret_id)
              raw = response.get('SecretString')
              if raw is None:
                  return ['<binary secret payload>']
              try:
                  parsed = json.loads(raw)
              except (TypeError, ValueError):
                  return ['<non-json secret payload>']
              if isinstance(parsed, dict):
                  return sorted(parsed.keys())
              return ['<non-object secret payload>']


          def lambda_handler(event, context):
              stack_name = os.environ['STACK_NAME']
              parameter_path = os.environ.get('PARAMETER_PATH', f'/{stack_name}/')

              parameter_count = 0
              secret_count = 0

              print(f'Reading SSM parameters under path: {parameter_path}')
              try:
                  for parameter in collect_parameters(parameter_path):
                      parameter_count += 1
                      print(
                          'SSM parameter -> '
                          f"Name: {parameter['Name']}, "
                          f"Type: {parameter['Type']}, "
                          f"Value: {parameter['Value']}"
                      )
              except ClientError as error:
                  code = error.response['Error']['Code']
                  logger.error('Failed to read SSM parameters (%s): %s', code, error)

              print(f'Listing Secrets Manager secrets with name prefix: {stack_name}')
              try:
                  for secret in collect_secrets(stack_name):
                      secret_count += 1
                      name = secret['Name']
                      arn = secret['ARN']
                      print(f'Secret -> Name: {name}, ARN: {arn}')
                      try:
                          keys = describe_secret_keys(arn)
                          # Only key names are logged. The generated password
                          # value is never written to CloudWatch Logs.
                          print(f"Secret -> Name: {name}, Keys: {', '.join(keys)}")
                      except ClientError as error:
                          code = error.response['Error']['Code']
                          logger.error(
                              'Failed to read secret value for %s (%s): %s',
                              name, code, error
                          )
              except ClientError as error:
                  code = error.response['Error']['Code']
                  logger.error('Failed to list secrets (%s): %s', code, error)

              result = {
                  'statusCode': 200,
                  'stackName': stack_name,
                  'parameterPath': parameter_path,
                  'parameterCount': parameter_count,
                  'secretCount': secret_count,
              }
              print(f'Summary: {json.dumps(result)}')
              return result
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: parameter-store-demo
        - Key: StackName
          Value: !Ref 'AWS::StackName'

final_template:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  Lambda blue-green CI/CD deployment environment. Provisions a main Lambda
  function with a published version and "live" alias, pre-traffic and
  post-traffic validation hook functions, IAM roles for Lambda execution and the
  CodeDeploy service, CloudWatch log groups and an error alarm, and a CodeDeploy
  application plus deployment group configured for canary traffic shifting.

Parameters:
  ApplicationName:
    Type: String
    Default: lambda-bluegreen-app
    Description: Base name used to derive the Lambda, CodeDeploy application and deployment group names.
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,48}[a-z0-9]$'
    ConstraintDescription: Must be 3-50 lowercase alphanumeric characters or hyphens.

  EnvironmentName:
    Type: String
    Default: prod
    Description: Logical environment name exposed to the application through APP_ENVIRONMENT.
    AllowedValues:
      - dev
      - staging
      - prod

Resources:

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # IAM
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  MainFunctionExecutionRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      Description: Execution role for the main application Lambda function.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: lambda.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole

  # The hook role grants PutLifecycleEventHookExecutionStatus scoped to this
  # stack's deployment group ARN, and InvokeFunction on the live alias only.
  # Both ARNs are constructed from pseudo-parameters and the literal alias name
  # rather than by referencing the deployment group or alias resources, so no
  # circular dependency is created and no policy document embeds a nested ARN.
  HookFunctionExecutionRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      Description: Execution role for the CodeDeploy pre-traffic and post-traffic validation hooks.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: lambda.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: CodeDeployLifecycleHookReporting
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: ReportLifecycleEventHookStatus
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - codedeploy:PutLifecycleEventHookExecutionStatus
                Resource:
                  - !Sub arn:${AWS::Partition}:codedeploy:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:deploymentgroup:${CodeDeployApplication}/${ApplicationName}-${EnvironmentName}-dg
        - PolicyName: InvokeFunctionUnderValidation
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: InvokeLiveAlias
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - lambda:InvokeFunction
                Resource:
                  - !Sub ${MainFunction.Arn}:live

  CodeDeployServiceRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      Description: Service role assumed by CodeDeploy to shift traffic between Lambda alias versions.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: codedeploy.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSCodeDeployRoleForLambda

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Main application function, version and traffic-shifting alias
  #
  # NOTE: ReservedConcurrentExecutions and ProvisionedConcurrencyConfig are
  # deliberately omitted — both draw from the account's concurrency pool, which
  # in a greenfield account cannot be reserved without dropping unreserved
  # concurrency below the hard floor of 10.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  MainFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      FunctionName: !Sub ${ApplicationName}-${EnvironmentName}-main
      Description: Main application function targeted by CodeDeploy blue-green traffic shifting.
      Runtime: python3.12
      Handler: index.handler
      Architectures:
        - arm64
      Timeout: 15
      MemorySize: 256
      Role: !GetAtt MainFunctionExecutionRole.Arn
      Environment:
        Variables:
          APP_ENVIRONMENT: !Ref EnvironmentName
          DEPLOYMENT_COLOR: blue
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          import json
          import os

          APP_ENVIRONMENT = os.environ.get("APP_ENVIRONMENT", "unknown")
          DEPLOYMENT_COLOR = os.environ.get("DEPLOYMENT_COLOR", "unknown")


          def handler(event, context):
              """Return a Lambda proxy-style response so alias invocations
              succeed immediately after stack creation."""
              body = {
                  "message": "ok",
                  "environment": APP_ENVIRONMENT,
                  "deploymentColor": DEPLOYMENT_COLOR,
                  "functionVersion": context.function_version,
              }
              return {
                  "statusCode": 200,
                  "headers": {"Content-Type": "application/json"},
                  "isBase64Encoded": False,
                  "body": json.dumps(body),
              }

  MainFunctionVersion:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Version
    Properties:
      FunctionName: !Ref MainFunction
      Description: Immutable published version used as the initial alias target.

  # CodeDeploy updates this alias at deploy time; the template deliberately
  # pins only the initial version and lets the AppSpec supply the target
  # version during each deployment.
  MainFunctionAlias:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Alias
    Properties:
      Name: live
      Description: Traffic-shifting target updated by CodeDeploy.
      FunctionName: !Ref MainFunction
      FunctionVersion: !GetAtt MainFunctionVersion.Version

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Validation hook functions
  #
  # NOTE: The BeforeAllowTraffic / AfterAllowTraffic hook wiring lives in the
  # CodeDeploy AppSpec supplied at deployment time, not in this template. This
  # template's responsibility is to create the hook functions, grant them the
  # permissions they need, and create the deployment group they report into.
  #
  # TARGET_ALIAS_ARN carries the alias ARN (the value of !Ref on an
  # AWS::Lambda::Alias), which is directly usable as the FunctionName argument
  # to lambda:Invoke.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  PreTrafficHookFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      FunctionName: !Sub CodeDeployHook-${ApplicationName}-${EnvironmentName}-pre-traffic
      Description: BeforeAllowTraffic hook validating the newly deployed function version.
      Runtime: python3.12
      Handler: index.handler
      Architectures:
        - arm64
      Timeout: 300
      MemorySize: 256
      Role: !GetAtt HookFunctionExecutionRole.Arn
      Environment:
        Variables:
          TARGET_FUNCTION_NAME: !Ref MainFunction
          TARGET_ALIAS_ARN: !Ref MainFunctionAlias
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          import json
          import logging
          import os

          import boto3

          logger = logging.getLogger()
          logger.setLevel(logging.INFO)

          codedeploy = boto3.client("codedeploy")
          lambda_client = boto3.client("lambda")

          TARGET_FUNCTION_NAME = os.environ["TARGET_FUNCTION_NAME"]
          TARGET_ALIAS_ARN = os.environ["TARGET_ALIAS_ARN"]


          def validate_new_version():
              """Invoke the alias under test and assert the response shape."""
              response = lambda_client.invoke(
                  FunctionName=TARGET_ALIAS_ARN,
                  InvocationType="RequestResponse",
                  Payload=json.dumps({"source": "codedeploy-pre-traffic-hook"}).encode(),
              )

              if response.get("FunctionError"):
                  raise RuntimeError(
                      "invocation returned FunctionError: %s" % response["FunctionError"]
                  )

              payload = json.loads(response["Payload"].read().decode())
              status_code = payload.get("statusCode")
              if status_code != 200:
                  raise RuntimeError("unexpected statusCode: %r" % (status_code,))

              body = json.loads(payload.get("body") or "{}")
              if body.get("message") != "ok":
                  raise RuntimeError("unexpected body: %r" % (body,))

              logger.info(
                  "pre-traffic validation passed for %s", TARGET_FUNCTION_NAME
              )


          def handler(event, context):
              deployment_id = event.get("DeploymentId")
              hook_execution_id = event.get("LifecycleEventHookExecutionId")
              status = "Failed"

              try:
                  validate_new_version()
                  status = "Succeeded"
              except Exception:
                  logger.exception("pre-traffic validation failed; reporting Failed")

              codedeploy.put_lifecycle_event_hook_execution_status(
                  deploymentId=deployment_id,
                  lifecycleEventHookExecutionId=hook_execution_id,
                  status=status,
              )
              return {"status": status}

  PostTrafficHookFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      FunctionName: !Sub CodeDeployHook-${ApplicationName}-${EnvironmentName}-post-traffic
      Description: AfterAllowTraffic hook validating the alias after traffic has shifted.
      Runtime: python3.12
      Handler: index.handler
      Architectures:
        - arm64
      Timeout: 300
      MemorySize: 256
      Role: !GetAtt HookFunctionExecutionRole.Arn
      Environment:
        Variables:
          TARGET_FUNCTION_NAME: !Ref MainFunction
          TARGET_ALIAS_ARN: !Ref MainFunctionAlias
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          import json
          import logging
          import os

          import boto3

          logger = logging.getLogger()
          logger.setLevel(logging.INFO)

          codedeploy = boto3.client("codedeploy")
          lambda_client = boto3.client("lambda")

          TARGET_FUNCTION_NAME = os.environ["TARGET_FUNCTION_NAME"]
          TARGET_ALIAS_ARN = os.environ["TARGET_ALIAS_ARN"]

          SMOKE_TEST_ATTEMPTS = 3


          def validate_shifted_alias():
              """Invoke the live alias repeatedly to confirm the shifted
              traffic is being served healthily."""
              for attempt in range(1, SMOKE_TEST_ATTEMPTS + 1):
                  response = lambda_client.invoke(
                      FunctionName=TARGET_ALIAS_ARN,
                      InvocationType="RequestResponse",
                      Payload=json.dumps(
                          {"source": "codedeploy-post-traffic-hook", "attempt": attempt}
                      ).encode(),
                  )

                  if response.get("FunctionError"):
                      raise RuntimeError(
                          "attempt %d returned FunctionError: %s"
                          % (attempt, response["FunctionError"])
                      )

                  payload = json.loads(response["Payload"].read().decode())
                  if payload.get("statusCode") != 200:
                      raise RuntimeError(
                          "attempt %d unexpected statusCode: %r"
                          % (attempt, payload.get("statusCode"))
                      )

                  body = json.loads(payload.get("body") or "{}")
                  if body.get("message") != "ok":
                      raise RuntimeError(
                          "attempt %d unexpected body: %r" % (attempt, body)
                      )

              logger.info(
                  "post-traffic validation passed for %s", TARGET_FUNCTION_NAME
              )


          def handler(event, context):
              deployment_id = event.get("DeploymentId")
              hook_execution_id = event.get("LifecycleEventHookExecutionId")
              status = "Failed"

              try:
                  validate_shifted_alias()
                  status = "Succeeded"
              except Exception:
                  logger.exception("post-traffic validation failed; reporting Failed")

              codedeploy.put_lifecycle_event_hook_execution_status(
                  deploymentId=deployment_id,
                  lifecycleEventHookExecutionId=hook_execution_id,
                  status=status,
              )
              return {"status": status}

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Log groups with managed retention
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  MainFunctionLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: !Sub /aws/lambda/${MainFunction}
      RetentionInDays: 90

  PreTrafficHookLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: !Sub /aws/lambda/${PreTrafficHookFunction}
      RetentionInDays: 90

  PostTrafficHookLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: !Sub /aws/lambda/${PostTrafficHookFunction}
      RetentionInDays: 90

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # CloudWatch alarm gating traffic shifting
  #
  # The Resource dimension must be "<functionName>:<aliasName>" — the literal
  # alias name, not the alias ARN returned by !Ref on AWS::Lambda::Alias.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  MainFunctionAliasErrorAlarm:
    Type: AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm
    Properties:
      AlarmName: !Sub ${ApplicationName}-${EnvironmentName}-alias-errors
      AlarmDescription: Errors on the live alias of the main function; triggers CodeDeploy rollback.
      Namespace: AWS/Lambda
      MetricName: Errors
      Dimensions:
        - Name: FunctionName
          Value: !Ref MainFunction
        - Name: Resource
          Value: !Sub ${MainFunction}:live
      Statistic: Sum
      Period: 60
      EvaluationPeriods: 1
      Threshold: 1
      ComparisonOperator: GreaterThanOrEqualToThreshold
      TreatMissingData: notBreaching

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # CodeDeploy application and deployment group
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  CodeDeployApplication:
    Type: AWS::CodeDeploy::Application
    Properties:
      ApplicationName: !Sub ${ApplicationName}-${EnvironmentName}
      ComputePlatform: Lambda

  DeploymentGroup:
    Type: AWS::CodeDeploy::DeploymentGroup
    Properties:
      ApplicationName: !Ref CodeDeployApplication
      DeploymentGroupName: !Sub ${ApplicationName}-${EnvironmentName}-dg
      ServiceRoleArn: !GetAtt CodeDeployServiceRole.Arn
      DeploymentConfigName: CodeDeployDefault.LambdaCanary10Percent5Minutes
      DeploymentStyle:
        DeploymentType: BLUE_GREEN
        DeploymentOption: WITH_TRAFFIC_CONTROL
      AutoRollbackConfiguration:
        Enabled: true
        Events:
          - DEPLOYMENT_FAILURE
          - DEPLOYMENT_STOP_ON_ALARM
      AlarmConfiguration:
        Enabled: true
        IgnorePollAlarmFailure: false
        Alarms:
          - Name: !Ref MainFunctionAliasErrorAlarm

Outputs:
  MainFunctionArn:
    Description: ARN of the main application Lambda function.
    Value: !GetAtt MainFunction.Arn

  MainFunctionName:
    Description: Name of the main application Lambda function.
    Value: !Ref MainFunction

  MainFunctionAliasArn:
    Description: ARN of the live alias targeted by CodeDeploy traffic shifting.
    Value: !Ref MainFunctionAlias

  MainFunctionPublishedVersion:
    Description: Initial published version of the main function.
    Value: !GetAtt MainFunctionVersion.Version

  PreTrafficHookFunctionName:
    Description: Name of the BeforeAllowTraffic validation hook function.
    Value: !Ref PreTrafficHookFunction

  PostTrafficHookFunctionName:
    Description: Name of the AfterAllowTraffic validation hook function.
    Value: !Ref PostTrafficHookFunction

  CodeDeployApplicationName:
    Description: Name of the CodeDeploy application.
    Value: !Ref CodeDeployApplication

  DeploymentGroupName:
    Description: Name of the CodeDeploy deployment group.
    Value: !Ref DeploymentGroup

final_template:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  AWS Service Catalog IAM foundation. Creates one end-user IAM group (AWS Service
  Catalog end users) plus four launch-constraint roles for the EC2-VPC, EMR, RDS
  and S3 product templates. Exports the group and launch role names/ARNs for
  consumption by downstream Service Catalog portfolio and launch-constraint stacks.
  NOTE: this stack creates IAM roles, an IAM group and managed policies with
  explicit names, so it must be deployed with the CAPABILITY_NAMED_IAM capability
  (CAPABILITY_IAM is not sufficient because resource names are set).

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# DEVIATION FROM THE ORIGINAL REQUEST (intentional, documented):
# The request asked for AWS::CloudFormation::Stack nested stacks pulling the IAM
# templates from a RepositoryRootURL parameter defaulting to the AWS Service
# Catalog reference-architecture S3 location. That pattern is NOT implemented
# here: a nested stack's TemplateURL is an external S3 object that does not exist
# in a greenfield account, the reference-architecture buckets are not a
# guaranteed/versioned dependency, and a 403/404 on template fetch fails the root
# stack immediately with no operator present to correct the URL. Every IAM
# resource is therefore declared directly in this single template, preserving the
# same logical grouping as commented sections below:
#   Section 1 - End-user IAM stack
#   Section 2 - EC2-VPC launch-constraint role
#   Section 3 - EMR launch-constraint role (+ EMR service/EC2 roles)
#   Section 4 - RDS launch-constraint role
#   Section 5 - S3 launch-constraint role
# Consequently no RepositoryRootURL (or any other template-location) parameter is
# defined - it would be unreferenced by any Resource, Condition or Output.
#
# DeletionPolicy / UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain is deliberately NOT set on any
# resource in this template. Every resource here is a stateless IAM identity,
# group, managed policy or instance profile that can be recreated from source.
# Those policies belong on the stateful resources created by the downstream
# product templates (RDS DB instances, S3 buckets, EMR-managed data stores).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Metadata:
  AWS::CloudFormation::Interface:
    ParameterGroups:
      - Label:
          default: Naming and tagging
        Parameters:
          - NamePrefix
          - EnvironmentTag
    ParameterLabels:
      NamePrefix:
        default: Prefix applied to IAM resource names and Name tags
      EnvironmentTag:
        default: Environment tag value

Parameters:

  NamePrefix:
    Type: String
    Default: servicecatalog
    Description: >-
      Prefix used for the generated IAM group name, role names and the Name tag on
      every role. Letters, digits and hyphens only.
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-zA-Z0-9-]{1,32}$'
    ConstraintDescription: 1-32 characters, letters, digits and hyphens only.
    MinLength: 1
    MaxLength: 32

  EnvironmentTag:
    Type: String
    Default: dev
    Description: Value applied to the Environment tag of every role created here.
    AllowedValues:
      - dev
      - test
      - prod

Resources:

  # =========================================================================
  # SECTION 1 - END-USER IAM STACK
  # The Service Catalog end-user group. Members can browse the catalog and
  # provision/update/terminate ONLY their own provisioned products. They receive
  # NO direct EC2, EMR, RDS or S3 mutation permissions: all provisioning
  # privilege flows through the launch-constraint roles in sections 2-5, which is
  # the entire purpose of a Service Catalog launch constraint.
  # =========================================================================

  ServiceCatalogEndUserGroup:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Group
    Properties:
      # ${AWS::StackName} keeps multiple copies of this stack collision-free
      # within a single account.
      GroupName: !Sub '${NamePrefix}-${AWS::StackName}-end-users'
      Path: /servicecatalog/
      # AWS-managed end-user policy attached directly to the group. Written as a
      # plain static string - no ${...} substitution, so no Fn::Sub.
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AWSServiceCatalogEndUserFullAccess

  ServiceCatalogEndUserSupplementalPolicy:
    Type: AWS::IAM::ManagedPolicy
    Properties:
      ManagedPolicyName: !Sub '${NamePrefix}-${AWS::StackName}-end-user-supplemental'
      Path: /servicecatalog/
      Description: >-
        Supplementary Service Catalog end-user permissions - self-scoped catalog
        browsing and provisioning, plus read-only visibility of the SC-* product
        stacks created on the end user's behalf by the launch roles.
      Groups:
        - !Ref ServiceCatalogEndUserGroup
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:

          # Catalog discovery, restricted to the caller's own view of the catalog
          # and to their own provisioned products via the servicecatalog:userLevel
          # condition key. Service Catalog control-plane list/search APIs do not
          # support resource-level permissions, so the access-level condition key
          # is the scoping mechanism here rather than a resource ARN.
          - Sid: CatalogSelfServiceDiscovery
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - servicecatalog:Describe*
              - servicecatalog:List*
              - servicecatalog:Scan*
              - servicecatalog:Search*
            Resource: '*'
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                servicecatalog:userLevel: self

          # Provisioning lifecycle, again limited to the caller's own provisioned
          # products. The launch constraint supplies the privileged role.
          - Sid: SelfProvisioningLifecycle
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - servicecatalog:ProvisionProduct
              - servicecatalog:TerminateProvisionedProduct
              - servicecatalog:UpdateProvisionedProduct
            Resource: '*'
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                servicecatalog:userLevel: self

          # Read-only visibility of the underlying CloudFormation stacks that
          # Service Catalog creates for provisioned products. Service Catalog
          # names those stacks SC-<accountid>-<provisioned product id>, so the
          # SC-* prefix confines this to catalog-managed stacks only.
          - Sid: ReadProductStacksOnly
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - cloudformation:DescribeStacks
              - cloudformation:DescribeStackEvents
              - cloudformation:GetTemplateSummary
              - cloudformation:ListStackResources
            Resource:
              - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:cloudformation:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:stack/SC-*'
              - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:cloudformation:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:stack/SC-*/*'

          # Explicit denial of direct infrastructure mutation. End users must not
          # be able to create or destroy EC2/VPC, EMR, RDS or S3 resources
          # outside of a provisioned product; only the launch roles may do so.
          - Sid: DenyDirectInfrastructureMutation
            Effect: Deny
            Action:
              - ec2:RunInstances
              - ec2:TerminateInstances
              - ec2:Create*
              - ec2:Delete*
              - ec2:Attach*
              - ec2:Detach*
              - ec2:AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress
              - ec2:AuthorizeSecurityGroupEgress
              - ec2:AllocateAddress
              - elasticmapreduce:RunJobFlow
              - elasticmapreduce:TerminateJobFlows
              - elasticmapreduce:AddInstanceGroups
              - rds:Create*
              - rds:Delete*
              - rds:Modify*
              - s3:CreateBucket
              - s3:DeleteBucket
              - s3:PutBucket*
              - s3:PutEncryptionConfiguration
              - iam:PassRole
            Resource: '*'

  # =========================================================================
  # SHARED LAUNCH-ROLE PERMISSIONS
  # Every launch role needs the same CloudFormation, template-staging and
  # provisioned-product-reporting permissions. Declaring them once as a managed
  # policy attached to all four roles keeps the four roles consistent.
  # =========================================================================

  LaunchRoleCommonPolicy:
    Type: AWS::IAM::ManagedPolicy
    Properties:
      ManagedPolicyName: !Sub '${NamePrefix}-${AWS::StackName}-launch-common'
      Path: /servicecatalog/
      Description: >-
        CloudFormation stack management, template staging read access and
        provisioned-product status reporting shared by all Service Catalog
        launch-constraint roles in this stack.
      Roles:
        - !Ref EC2VPCLaunchRole
        - !Ref EMRLaunchRole
        - !Ref RDSLaunchRole
        - !Ref S3LaunchRole
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:

          # Service Catalog drives the product stack through CloudFormation on
          # the launch role's behalf. Confined to the SC-* stacks and their
          # change sets so a launch role can never touch an unrelated stack.
          # (cloudformation:ValidateTemplate and GetTemplateSummary are
          # region-scoped APIs; they are listed here alongside the stack-scoped
          # actions rather than being broadened to Resource '*'.)
          - Sid: ManageProductStacks
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - cloudformation:CreateStack
              - cloudformation:DeleteStack
              - cloudformation:DescribeStacks
              - cloudformation:DescribeStackEvents
              - cloudformation:DescribeStackResource
              - cloudformation:DescribeStackResources
              - cloudformation:GetTemplateSummary
              - cloudformation:SetStackPolicy
              - cloudformation:UpdateStack
              - cloudformation:ValidateTemplate
              - cloudformation:ListStackResources
              - cloudformation:CreateChangeSet
              - cloudformation:DescribeChangeSet
              - cloudformation:ExecuteChangeSet
              - cloudformation:TagResource
              - cloudformation:UntagResource
            Resource:
              - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:cloudformation:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:stack/SC-*/*'
              - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:cloudformation:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:changeSet/SC-*/*'

          # Service Catalog stages product templates in CloudFormation/Service
          # Catalog managed buckets whose names embed the account id and region.
          # Account-agnostic wildcards only - no hardcoded bucket name, no
          # account-specific ARN.
          - Sid: ReadStagedProductTemplates
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - s3:GetObject
            Resource:
              - arn:aws:s3:::cf-templates-*/*
              - arn:aws:s3:::sc-*-cf-templates-*/*

          # Reporting provisioning outcomes back to the catalog.
          - Sid: ReportProvisioningOutcome
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - servicecatalog:DescribeProvisionedProduct
              - servicecatalog:DescribeProvisionedProductPlan
              - servicecatalog:ListProvisionedProductPlans
              - servicecatalog:ScanProvisionedProducts
              - servicecatalog:SearchProvisionedProducts
              - servicecatalog:UpdateProvisionedProduct
              - servicecatalog:TerminateProvisionedProduct
              - servicecatalog:DescribeRecord
            Resource: '*'

  # =========================================================================
  # SECTION 2 - EC2-VPC LAUNCH-CONSTRAINT ROLE
  # =========================================================================

  EC2VPCLaunchRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Sub '${NamePrefix}-${AWS::StackName}-ec2vpc-launch'
      Path: /servicecatalog/
      MaxSessionDuration: 3600
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: servicecatalog.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
            # Confused-deputy hardening: only Service Catalog acting for THIS
            # account may assume the launch role.
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                aws:SourceAccount: !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${NamePrefix}-ec2vpc-launch-role'
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentTag

  EC2VPCLaunchRolePolicy:
    Type: AWS::IAM::ManagedPolicy
    Properties:
      ManagedPolicyName: !Sub '${NamePrefix}-${AWS::StackName}-ec2vpc-launch-perms'
      Path: /servicecatalog/
      Description: VPC-construction permissions for the EC2-VPC Service Catalog product template.
      Roles:
        - !Ref EC2VPCLaunchRole
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:

          # EC2 network-construction APIs create resources that do not yet exist,
          # so they cannot be scoped to a resource ARN - Resource '*' is
          # unavoidable for these create/describe calls. Scoping is achieved by
          # restricting WHICH actions the role may call and by the launch
          # constraint restricting WHICH template it may deploy.
          - Sid: BuildAndTearDownVpc
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - ec2:CreateVpc
              - ec2:DeleteVpc
              - ec2:ModifyVpcAttribute
              - ec2:CreateSubnet
              - ec2:DeleteSubnet
              - ec2:ModifySubnetAttribute
              - ec2:CreateInternetGateway
              - ec2:DeleteInternetGateway
              - ec2:AttachInternetGateway
              - ec2:DetachInternetGateway
              - ec2:CreateRouteTable
              - ec2:DeleteRouteTable
              - ec2:CreateRoute
              - ec2:DeleteRoute
              - ec2:AssociateRouteTable
              - ec2:DisassociateRouteTable
              - ec2:CreateSecurityGroup
              - ec2:DeleteSecurityGroup
              - ec2:AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress
              - ec2:AuthorizeSecurityGroupEgress
              - ec2:RevokeSecurityGroupIngress
              - ec2:RevokeSecurityGroupEgress
              - ec2:CreateNatGateway
              - ec2:DeleteNatGateway
              - ec2:AllocateAddress
              - ec2:ReleaseAddress
              - ec2:AssociateAddress
              - ec2:DisassociateAddress
              - ec2:CreateTags
              - ec2:DeleteTags
              - ec2:RunInstances
              - ec2:TerminateInstances
              - ec2:StopInstances
              - ec2:StartInstances
            Resource: '*'

          # ec2:Describe* has no resource-level permission support at all; AWS
          # requires Resource '*' for every Describe call. Kept in its own
          # read-only statement so the blast radius is explicit.
          - Sid: DescribeEc2ReadOnly
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - ec2:Describe*
            Resource: '*'

  # =========================================================================
  # SECTION 3 - EMR LAUNCH-CONSTRAINT ROLE
  # A greenfield account has no EMR_DefaultRole / EMR_EC2_DefaultRole, so the
  # EMR service role, the EC2 instance role and its instance profile are created
  # here and passed to EMR by the launch role via a tightly scoped iam:PassRole.
  # =========================================================================

  EMRServiceRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Sub '${NamePrefix}-${AWS::StackName}-emr-service'
      Path: /servicecatalog/
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: elasticmapreduce.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AmazonElasticMapReduceRole
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${NamePrefix}-emr-service-role'
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentTag

  EMRInstanceRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Sub '${NamePrefix}-${AWS::StackName}-emr-ec2'
      Path: /servicecatalog/
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: ec2.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AmazonElasticMapReduceforEC2Role
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${NamePrefix}-emr-ec2-role'
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentTag

  EMRInstanceProfile:
    Type: AWS::IAM::InstanceProfile
    Properties:
      InstanceProfileName: !Sub '${NamePrefix}-${AWS::StackName}-emr-ec2'
      Path: /servicecatalog/
      Roles:
        - !Ref EMRInstanceRole

  EMRLaunchRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Sub '${NamePrefix}-${AWS::StackName}-emr-launch'
      Path: /servicecatalog/
      MaxSessionDuration: 3600
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: servicecatalog.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                aws:SourceAccount: !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${NamePrefix}-emr-launch-role'
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentTag

  EMRLaunchRolePolicy:
    Type: AWS::IAM::ManagedPolicy
    Properties:
      ManagedPolicyName: !Sub '${NamePrefix}-${AWS::StackName}-emr-launch-perms'
      Path: /servicecatalog/
      Description: EMR cluster lifecycle permissions for the EMR Service Catalog product template.
      Roles:
        - !Ref EMRLaunchRole
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:

          - Sid: ManageEmrClusters
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - elasticmapreduce:RunJobFlow
              - elasticmapreduce:TerminateJobFlows
              - elasticmapreduce:AddTags
              - elasticmapreduce:RemoveTags
              - elasticmapreduce:Describe*
              - elasticmapreduce:List*
              - elasticmapreduce:SetTerminationProtection
            Resource: '*'

          # EMR provisions its own EC2 capacity; these are the EC2 calls the
          # service makes on the cluster's behalf. Describe*/create calls have no
          # resource-level permission support, hence Resource '*'.
          - Sid: EmrManagedEc2Capacity
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - ec2:CreateSecurityGroup
              - ec2:DeleteSecurityGroup
              - ec2:AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress
              - ec2:AuthorizeSecurityGroupEgress
              - ec2:RevokeSecurityGroupIngress
              - ec2:RevokeSecurityGroupEgress
              - ec2:CreateTags
              - ec2:DeleteTags
              - ec2:RunInstances
              - ec2:TerminateInstances
              - ec2:CreateNetworkInterface
              - ec2:DeleteNetworkInterface
              - ec2:Describe*
            Resource: '*'

          # Cluster logs and job input/output staging.
          - Sid: EmrLogAndDataBuckets
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - s3:CreateBucket
              - s3:ListBucket
              - s3:GetBucketLocation
              - s3:GetObject
              - s3:PutObject
              - s3:DeleteObject
              - s3:AbortMultipartUpload
              - s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads
            Resource:
              - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:s3:::*'
              - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:s3:::*/*'

          # iam:PassRole is limited to exactly the two EMR roles created by this
          # template - never Resource '*', never a hardcoded account id.
          - Sid: PassOnlyEmrRolesCreatedHere
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - iam:PassRole
            Resource:
              - !GetAtt EMRServiceRole.Arn
              - !GetAtt EMRInstanceRole.Arn
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                iam:PassedToService:
                  - elasticmapreduce.amazonaws.com
                  - ec2.amazonaws.com

          # Required so CloudFormation can hand the instance profile to EMR.
          - Sid: ReadEmrInstanceProfile
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - iam:GetInstanceProfile
              - iam:GetRole
              - iam:ListInstanceProfiles
              - iam:ListRoles
            Resource:
              - !GetAtt EMRInstanceProfile.Arn
              - !GetAtt EMRServiceRole.Arn
              - !GetAtt EMRInstanceRole.Arn

  # =========================================================================
  # SECTION 4 - RDS LAUNCH-CONSTRAINT ROLE
  # No database password, API key or other secret literal appears anywhere in
  # this template, and no {{resolve:secretsmanager:...}} / {{resolve:ssm-secure:...}}
  # dynamic reference is used. This template creates IAM identities only; the RDS
  # product template must generate its own master credentials with
  # AWS::SecretsManager::Secret + GenerateSecretString, which is what the
  # secretsmanager grant below enables.
  # =========================================================================

  RDSLaunchRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Sub '${NamePrefix}-${AWS::StackName}-rds-launch'
      Path: /servicecatalog/
      MaxSessionDuration: 3600
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: servicecatalog.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                aws:SourceAccount: !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${NamePrefix}-rds-launch-role'
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentTag

  RDSLaunchRolePolicy:
    Type: AWS::IAM::ManagedPolicy
    Properties:
      ManagedPolicyName: !Sub '${NamePrefix}-${AWS::StackName}-rds-launch-perms'
      Path: /servicecatalog/
      Description: RDS provisioning permissions for the RDS Service Catalog product template.
      Roles:
        - !Ref RDSLaunchRole
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:

          - Sid: ManageRdsInstances
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - rds:CreateDBInstance
              - rds:CreateDBSubnetGroup
              - rds:CreateDBParameterGroup
              - rds:ModifyDBInstance
              - rds:DeleteDBInstance
              - rds:AddTagsToResource
              - rds:RemoveTagsFromResource
              - rds:ListTagsForResource
            Resource:
              - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:rds:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:db:*'
              - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:rds:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:subgrp:*'
              - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:rds:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:pg:*'
              - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:rds:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:og:*'
              - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:rds:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:secgrp:*'

          # rds:Describe* does not support resource-level permissions.
          - Sid: DescribeRdsReadOnly
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - rds:Describe*
            Resource: '*'

          # Subnet groups and security groups referenced by the DB instance are
          # created inside the product template; these lookups have no
          # resource-level permission support.
          - Sid: DescribeNetworkForRds
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - ec2:DescribeVpcs
              - ec2:DescribeSubnets
              - ec2:DescribeSecurityGroups
              - ec2:DescribeAvailabilityZones
              - ec2:DescribeAccountAttributes
            Resource: '*'

          # Encrypted storage: RDS needs a grant against the KMS key chosen by
          # the product template.
          - Sid: KmsForEncryptedStorage
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - kms:CreateGrant
              - kms:DescribeKey
            Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:kms:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:key/*'

          # Lets the product template generate and read back its OWN master
          # credential via AWS::SecretsManager::Secret / GenerateSecretString.
          # Scoped to the SC-* secrets belonging to catalog-provisioned products.
          - Sid: ProductGeneratedDatabaseCredentials
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - secretsmanager:CreateSecret
              - secretsmanager:TagResource
              - secretsmanager:GetSecretValue
              - secretsmanager:DescribeSecret
              - secretsmanager:DeleteSecret
            Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:secretsmanager:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:secret:SC-*'

  # =========================================================================
  # SECTION 5 - S3 LAUNCH-CONSTRAINT ROLE
  # Objective for downstream S3 product templates: they MUST configure access
  # with AWS::S3::BucketPolicy plus PublicAccessBlockConfiguration inside the
  # AWS::S3::Bucket resource, together with BucketEncryption, VersioningConfiguration
  # and LoggingConfiguration. They must NEVER use the deprecated AccessControl
  # property (bucket ACLs) - which is why no s3:PutBucketAcl / s3:PutObjectAcl
  # permission is granted below.
  # =========================================================================

  S3LaunchRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Sub '${NamePrefix}-${AWS::StackName}-s3-launch'
      Path: /servicecatalog/
      MaxSessionDuration: 3600
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: servicecatalog.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                aws:SourceAccount: !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${NamePrefix}-s3-launch-role'
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentTag

  S3LaunchRolePolicy:
    Type: AWS::IAM::ManagedPolicy
    Properties:
      ManagedPolicyName: !Sub '${NamePrefix}-${AWS::StackName}-s3-launch-perms'
      Path: /servicecatalog/
      Description: Bucket provisioning permissions for the S3 Service Catalog product template.
      Roles:
        - !Ref S3LaunchRole
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:

          # Bucket names are chosen by the product template at provisioning time
          # and cannot be known here, so the bucket ARN is wildcarded on name
          # only - it remains partition-scoped and contains no account id.
          - Sid: ManageProductBuckets
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - s3:CreateBucket
              - s3:DeleteBucket
              - s3:PutBucketPolicy
              - s3:DeleteBucketPolicy
              - s3:PutEncryptionConfiguration
              - s3:PutBucketPublicAccessBlock
              - s3:PutBucketVersioning
              - s3:PutBucketLogging
              - s3:PutBucketTagging
              - s3:GetBucketPolicy
              - s3:GetBucketLocation
              - s3:GetBucketVersioning
              - s3:GetBucketLogging
              - s3:GetBucketTagging
              - s3:GetBucketPublicAccessBlock
              - s3:GetEncryptionConfiguration
              - s3:ListBucket
            Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:s3:::*'

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  Basic Step Functions demonstration stack. Creates a STANDARD state machine
  named MyBasicStateMachine that runs a two-step Pass-state workflow emitting
  "Hello" then "World", together with its least-privilege execution role and a
  CloudWatch Logs log group. Self-contained: no Parameters, no imports, no
  external resource references.

# NOTE: This template intentionally declares no Parameters. Every value is either
# a literal or derived from pseudo parameters / intrinsic functions so the stack
# deploys unattended into a greenfield account.

# NOTE: StateMachineName is hardcoded to "MyBasicStateMachine" because the name was
# explicitly requested. Consequences: (1) the stack is single-instance per region --
# a second deployment in the same region will fail with a name collision; (2) any
# future change to the name forces replacement of the state machine resource.

Resources:

  # NOTE: A CloudWatch Logs log group holds stateful log data. Retain policies keep
  # execution history available after the stack is deleted or the resource replaced.
  StateMachineLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      # Built with Fn::Sub from the state machine name plus the stack name so the
      # group is unique per stack. No hardcoded account ID or region.
      LogGroupName: !Sub '/aws/vendedlogs/states/MyBasicStateMachine-${AWS::StackName}'
      RetentionInDays: 30
      Tags:
        - Key: 'stateMachine:createdBy'
          Value: 'SAM'

  StateMachineExecutionRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      Description: Execution role for the MyBasicStateMachine Step Functions state machine.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllowStepFunctionsServiceAssumeRole
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: states.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
            # Confused-deputy protection: only the Step Functions service acting on
            # behalf of this account, for this specific state machine ARN, may assume
            # the role.
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                aws:SourceAccount: !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'
              ArnLike:
                aws:SourceArn: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:states:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:stateMachine:MyBasicStateMachine'
      # Inline policies only -- no AWS managed policies are attached, so the role
      # grants exactly the permissions enumerated below and nothing more.
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: StateMachineLoggingAndTracing
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              # The workflow consists solely of Pass states, so no data-plane
              # permissions (lambda:InvokeFunction, states:StartExecution, sns:Publish,
              # etc.) are granted.
              #
              # cfn_nag: W12 -- IAM policy should not allow Resource: '*'
              # cfn-lint: The CloudWatch Logs vended-delivery actions below do not
              # support resource-level permissions and MUST be granted on '*'.
              # See https://docs.aws.amazon.com/step-functions/latest/dg/cw-logs.html
              # ("the IAM policy ... must include the following permissions with
              # Resource: '*'"). Narrowing these to a log-group ARN produces an
              # invalid policy and logging silently fails, so the wildcard is retained
              # deliberately rather than suppressed with a bogus ARN.
              - Sid: StepFunctionsVendedLogDelivery
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - logs:CreateLogDelivery
                  - logs:GetLogDelivery
                  - logs:UpdateLogDelivery
                  - logs:DeleteLogDelivery
                  - logs:ListLogDeliveries
                  - logs:PutResourcePolicy
                  - logs:DescribeResourcePolicies
                  - logs:DescribeLogGroups
                Resource: '*'
              # X-Ray sampling and segment APIs likewise do not support resource-level
              # permissions and are documented as requiring Resource: '*'.
              # cfn_nag: W12 -- see note above.
              - Sid: StepFunctionsXRayTracing
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - xray:PutTraceSegments
                  - xray:PutTelemetryRecords
                  - xray:GetSamplingRules
                  - xray:GetSamplingTargets
                Resource: '*'
      Tags:
        - Key: 'stateMachine:createdBy'
          Value: 'SAM'

  BasicStateMachine:
    Type: AWS::StepFunctions::StateMachine
    Properties:
      StateMachineName: MyBasicStateMachine
      StateMachineType: STANDARD
      # !GetAtt establishes the implicit dependency on the role, so no DependsOn is
      # needed for it. DependsOn on the role's inline policy is likewise unnecessary
      # because Policies are part of the AWS::IAM::Role resource itself.
      RoleArn: !GetAtt StateMachineExecutionRole.Arn
      # Plain JSON string literal -- no ${Variable} substitution is required here, so
      # Fn::Sub is deliberately not used.
      DefinitionString: |
        {
          "Comment": "Two-step Amazon States Language demonstration using Pass states only.",
          "StartAt": "Hello",
          "States": {
            "Hello": {
              "Type": "Pass",
              "Comment": "Emits the literal string \"Hello\" as the state output.",
              "Result": "Hello",
              "ResultPath": "$",
              "Next": "World"
            },
            "World": {
              "Type": "Pass",
              "Comment": "Emits the literal string \"World\" as the execution output.",
              "Result": "World",
              "ResultPath": "$",
              "End": true
            }
          }
        }
      LoggingConfiguration:
        Level: ALL
        IncludeExecutionData: true
        Destinations:
          - CloudWatchLogsLogGroup:
              LogGroupArn: !GetAtt StateMachineLogGroup.Arn
      TracingConfiguration:
        Enabled: true
      Tags:
        - Key: 'stateMachine:createdBy'
          Value: 'SAM'

Outputs:

  StateMachineArn:
    Description: ARN of the MyBasicStateMachine Step Functions state machine.
    Value: !Ref BasicStateMachine
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-StateMachineArn'

  StateMachineName:
    Description: Name of the MyBasicStateMachine Step Functions state machine.
    Value: !GetAtt BasicStateMachine.Name
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-StateMachineName'

  StateMachineExecutionRoleArn:
    Description: ARN of the IAM execution role assumed by the state machine.
    Value: !GetAtt StateMachineExecutionRole.Arn
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-StateMachineExecutionRoleArn'

  StateMachineLogGroupName:
    Description: Name of the CloudWatch Logs log group receiving execution logs.
    Value: !Ref StateMachineLogGroup
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-StateMachineLogGroupName'

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  Provisions GitHub Actions OIDC federation for the guardian/facia-scala-client
  repository, granting a dedicated IAM role read-only access to the
  facia-tool-store S3 bucket (including its DEV prefix). Self-contained:
  creates the GitHub Actions OIDC identity provider, a customer managed KMS
  key, the bucket, and the role.

Parameters:
  GitHubOrg:
    Type: String
    Default: guardian
    Description: GitHub organisation (owner) permitted to assume the role via OIDC.
    MinLength: 1
    MaxLength: 39
    AllowedPattern: '^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9-]*$'

  GitHubRepository:
    Type: String
    Default: facia-scala-client
    Description: GitHub repository name permitted to assume the role via OIDC.
    MinLength: 1
    MaxLength: 100
    AllowedPattern: '^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$'

  BucketBaseName:
    Type: String
    Default: facia-tool-store
    Description: >-
      Base name for the store bucket. The deployed bucket name is suffixed with
      the account ID and region to guarantee global uniqueness.
    MinLength: 3
    MaxLength: 40
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9]$'

  ApplicationName:
    Type: String
    Default: facia-scala-client
    Description: Application name used for resource naming and tagging.
    MinLength: 1
    MaxLength: 40
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$'

  Environment:
    Type: String
    Default: dev
    Description: Environment name used for resource naming and tagging.
    AllowedValues:
      - dev
      - code
      - staging
      - prod

Resources:
  GitHubActionsOIDCProvider:
    Type: AWS::IAM::OIDCProvider
    Properties:
      Url: https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com
      ClientIdList:
        - sts.amazonaws.com
      ThumbprintList:
        - 6938fd4d98bab03faadb97b34396831e3780aea1
        - 1c58a3a8518e8759bf075b76b750d4f2df264fcd
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref ApplicationName
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref Environment
        - Key: Stack
          Value: !Ref AWS::StackName

  FaciaToolStoreKey:
    Type: AWS::KMS::Key
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      Description: !Sub >-
        Customer managed key encrypting the ${ApplicationName} facia-tool-store
        S3 bucket (${Environment}).
      Enabled: true
      EnableKeyRotation: true
      KeySpec: SYMMETRIC_DEFAULT
      KeyUsage: ENCRYPT_DECRYPT
      PendingWindowInDays: 30
      KeyPolicy:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: EnableAccountRootKeyAdministration
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              AWS: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::${AWS::AccountId}:root'
            Action: 'kms:*'
            Resource: '*'
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref ApplicationName
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref Environment
        - Key: Stack
          Value: !Ref AWS::StackName

  FaciaToolStoreKeyAlias:
    Type: AWS::KMS::Alias
    Properties:
      AliasName: !Sub 'alias/${ApplicationName}-${Environment}-facia-tool-store'
      TargetKeyId: !Ref FaciaToolStoreKey

  FaciaToolStoreBucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      BucketName: !Sub '${BucketBaseName}-${AWS::AccountId}-${AWS::Region}'
      BucketEncryption:
        ServerSideEncryptionConfiguration:
          - ServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
              SSEAlgorithm: 'aws:kms'
              KMSMasterKeyID: !GetAtt FaciaToolStoreKey.Arn
            BucketKeyEnabled: true
      VersioningConfiguration:
        Status: Enabled
      PublicAccessBlockConfiguration:
        BlockPublicAcls: true
        BlockPublicPolicy: true
        IgnorePublicAcls: true
        RestrictPublicBuckets: true
      OwnershipControls:
        Rules:
          - ObjectOwnership: BucketOwnerEnforced
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref ApplicationName
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref Environment
        - Key: Stack
          Value: !Ref AWS::StackName

  FaciaToolStoreBucketPolicy:
    Type: AWS::S3::BucketPolicy
    Properties:
      Bucket: !Ref FaciaToolStoreBucket
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: DenyNonTlsRequests
            Effect: Deny
            Principal: '*'
            Action: 's3:*'
            Resource:
              - !GetAtt FaciaToolStoreBucket.Arn
              - !Sub '${FaciaToolStoreBucket.Arn}/*'
            Condition:
              Bool:
                'aws:SecureTransport': 'false'
          - Sid: DenyUploadsWithoutKmsEncryption
            Effect: Deny
            Principal: '*'
            Action: 's3:PutObject'
            Resource: !Sub '${FaciaToolStoreBucket.Arn}/*'
            Condition:
              StringNotEquals:
                's3:x-amz-server-side-encryption': 'aws:kms'

  GitHubActionsRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Sub '${ApplicationName}-${Environment}-github-actions'
      Description: !Sub >-
        Role assumed by GitHub Actions workflows in
        ${GitHubOrg}/${GitHubRepository} for read-only access to the
        facia-tool-store DEV prefix.
      MaxSessionDuration: 3600
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllowGitHubActionsOidcAssumeRole
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Federated: !Ref GitHubActionsOIDCProvider
            Action: 'sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity'
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                'token.actions.githubusercontent.com:aud': sts.amazonaws.com
              StringLike:
                'token.actions.githubusercontent.com:sub': !Sub 'repo:${GitHubOrg}/${GitHubRepository}:*'
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: facia-tool-store-dev-read-only
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: ReadDevPrefixObjects
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - 's3:GetObject'
                  - 's3:GetObjectVersion'
                  - 's3:GetObjectTagging'
                Resource: !Sub '${FaciaToolStoreBucket.Arn}/DEV/*'
              - Sid: ListDevPrefixOnly
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - 's3:ListBucket'
                  - 's3:GetBucketLocation'
                Resource: !GetAtt FaciaToolStoreBucket.Arn
                Condition:
                  StringLike:
                    's3:prefix':
                      - 'DEV/'
                      - 'DEV/*'
              - Sid: DecryptFaciaToolStoreObjects
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - 'kms:Decrypt'
                  - 'kms:DescribeKey'
                Resource: !GetAtt FaciaToolStoreKey.Arn
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref ApplicationName
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref Environment
        - Key: Stack
          Value: !Ref AWS::StackName

Outputs:
  GitHubActionsRoleArn:
    Description: ARN of the IAM role GitHub Actions workflows assume via OIDC.
    Value: !GetAtt GitHubActionsRole.Arn
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-GitHubActionsRoleArn'

  GitHubActionsOIDCProviderArn:
    Description: ARN of the GitHub Actions OIDC identity provider.
    Value: !Ref GitHubActionsOIDCProvider
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-GitHubActionsOIDCProviderArn'

  FaciaToolStoreBucketName:
    Description: Name of the facia-tool-store S3 bucket.
    Value: !Ref FaciaToolStoreBucket
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-FaciaToolStoreBucketName'

  FaciaToolStoreKeyArn:
    Description: ARN of the customer managed KMS key encrypting the bucket.
    Value: !GetAtt FaciaToolStoreKey.Arn
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-FaciaToolStoreKeyArn'

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: Scheduled time-logging Lambda stack - logs the current UTC time to CloudWatch Logs every 5 minutes.

Parameters:
  AppName:
    Type: String
    Default: time-logger
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-z0-9-]{3,32}$'
    Description: Lowercase name used for resource naming and tagging.

Resources:

  # No DeletionPolicy/UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain is used anywhere in this stack.
  # There are no stateful data resources (no RDS, DynamoDB, S3, or EFS). Attaching
  # Retain to the log group would orphan it and block re-deployment on the same name.
  LambdaLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: !Sub '/aws/lambda/${AppName}-fn'
      RetentionInDays: 14
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AppName}-log-group'
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: CloudFormation

  LambdaExecutionRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Sub '${AppName}-lambda-role'
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: lambda.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: !Sub '${AppName}-logs-write'
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - logs:CreateLogStream
                  - logs:PutLogEvents
                Resource: !Sub '${LambdaLogGroup.Arn}:*'
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AppName}-lambda-role'
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: CloudFormation

  LambdaFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    # Explicit ordering: the function has no Ref/GetAtt to the log group, so
    # DependsOn guarantees the retention-managed group exists before first write.
    DependsOn: LambdaLogGroup
    Properties:
      FunctionName: !Sub '${AppName}-fn'
      Role: !GetAtt LambdaExecutionRole.Arn
      Runtime: python3.12
      Handler: index.lambda_handler
      Timeout: 10
      MemorySize: 128
      Architectures:
        - arm64
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          import logging
          from datetime import datetime, timezone

          logger = logging.getLogger()
          logger.setLevel(logging.INFO)


          def lambda_handler(event, context):
              current_time = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
              logger.info("Current UTC time: %s", current_time)
              return {"timestamp": current_time}
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AppName}-fn'
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: CloudFormation

  ScheduledRule:
    Type: AWS::Events::Rule
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${AppName}-schedule'
      Description: Invokes the time-logging Lambda function every 5 minutes.
      ScheduleExpression: rate(5 minutes)
      State: ENABLED
      Targets:
        - Id: TimeLoggerLambdaTarget
          Arn: !GetAtt LambdaFunction.Arn
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AppName}-schedule'
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: CloudFormation

  PermissionForEventsToInvokeLambda:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Permission
    Properties:
      Action: lambda:InvokeFunction
      FunctionName: !GetAtt LambdaFunction.Arn
      Principal: events.amazonaws.com
      SourceArn: !GetAtt ScheduledRule.Arn
      SourceAccount: !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'

Outputs:
  LambdaFunctionName:
    Description: Name of the scheduled time-logging Lambda function.
    Value: !Ref LambdaFunction

  LambdaFunctionArn:
    Description: ARN of the scheduled time-logging Lambda function.
    Value: !GetAtt LambdaFunction.Arn

  ScheduledRuleArn:
    Description: ARN of the CloudWatch Events rule that triggers the function every 5 minutes.
    Value: !GetAtt ScheduledRule.Arn

  LogGroupName:
    Description: Name of the CloudWatch Logs log group receiving the function output.
    Value: !Ref LambdaLogGroup
