AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  Test stack: Hello World Lambda function (Python 3.12) exposed through an
  API Gateway REST API at GET /hello, deployed to the "prod" stage. Fully
  self-contained — no external VPCs, buckets, secrets, SSM parameters, or
  cross-stack imports.

# Deliberate omissions for this test stack:
#   * API Gateway access logging, AWS::ApiGateway::Account, and a CloudWatch Logs
#     role are omitted: the Account resource is a per-account/per-region singleton
#     and conflicts on redeploy or when another stack owns it.
#   * No UsagePlan, API key, or WAF association — out of scope for a test endpoint.
#   * The GET method is intentionally AuthorizationType: NONE so the endpoint is
#     publicly callable for testing. This is a deliberate choice, not an oversight.
#   * No VpcConfig, so no VPC/subnet/security-group resources are required.
#   * No stateful resources, so no DeletionPolicy/UpdateReplacePolicy is needed;
#     the log group is intentionally deleted along with the stack.

Resources:

  HelloWorldFunctionRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      Description: Execution role for the Hello World test Lambda function.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: lambda.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole

  HelloWorldFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      Description: Returns the plain-text body "Hello, World" for GET /hello.
      Runtime: python3.12
      Handler: index.lambda_handler
      Role: !GetAtt HelloWorldFunctionRole.Arn
      Timeout: 10
      MemorySize: 128
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          def lambda_handler(event, context):
              return {
                  "statusCode": 200,
                  "headers": {"Content-Type": "text/plain"},
                  "body": "Hello, World",
              }

  HelloWorldFunctionLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: !Sub '/aws/lambda/${HelloWorldFunction}'
      RetentionInDays: 14

  HelloWorldApi:
    Type: AWS::ApiGateway::RestApi
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-hello-api'
      Description: REST API fronting the Hello World test Lambda function.
      EndpointConfiguration:
        Types:
          - REGIONAL

  HelloResource:
    Type: AWS::ApiGateway::Resource
    Properties:
      RestApiId: !Ref HelloWorldApi
      ParentId: !GetAtt HelloWorldApi.RootResourceId
      PathPart: hello

  HelloGetMethod:
    Type: AWS::ApiGateway::Method
    Properties:
      RestApiId: !Ref HelloWorldApi
      ResourceId: !Ref HelloResource
      HttpMethod: GET
      # Public test endpoint: authorization is deliberately not configured.
      AuthorizationType: NONE
      Integration:
        Type: AWS_PROXY
        IntegrationHttpMethod: POST
        Uri: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:apigateway:${AWS::Region}:lambda:path/2015-03-31/functions/${HelloWorldFunction.Arn}/invocations'

  HelloWorldFunctionApiInvokePermission:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Permission
    Properties:
      Action: lambda:InvokeFunction
      FunctionName: !Ref HelloWorldFunction
      Principal: apigateway.amazonaws.com
      SourceArn: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:execute-api:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:${HelloWorldApi}/*/GET/hello'

  HelloWorldApiDeployment:
    Type: AWS::ApiGateway::Deployment
    # Genuine ordering requirement not expressed by any Ref: the deployment must
    # be created after the GET method exists, otherwise it snapshots an empty API.
    DependsOn: HelloGetMethod
    Properties:
      RestApiId: !Ref HelloWorldApi
      Description: Deployment of the Hello World test API.

  HelloWorldApiProdStage:
    Type: AWS::ApiGateway::Stage
    Properties:
      RestApiId: !Ref HelloWorldApi
      DeploymentId: !Ref HelloWorldApiDeployment
      StageName: prod
      Description: Production-named test stage for the Hello World API.

Outputs:

  HelloWorldInvokeUrl:
    Description: Invoke URL for GET /hello on the prod stage.
    Value: !Sub 'https://${HelloWorldApi}.execute-api.${AWS::Region}.${AWS::URLSuffix}/prod/hello'

  HelloWorldFunctionName:
    Description: Name of the Hello World Lambda function.
    Value: !Ref HelloWorldFunction

  HelloWorldFunctionArn:

final_template:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  Provisions a custom AWS Systems Manager inventory collection mechanism that discovers
  running database and caching processes (Cassandra, MySQL, PostgreSQL, Redis, Memcached,
  SQL Server) on Windows and Linux managed instances. The stack creates an SSM Command
  document with platform-gated shell and PowerShell collection steps, a scheduled State
  Manager association named Custom-Inventory-Processes targeting all managed instances,
  and an EC2 instance profile that allows greenfield instances to be onboarded to Systems
  Manager. Control-plane only - no EC2, VPC, or networking resources are created.

Metadata:
  AWS::CloudFormation::Interface:
    ParameterGroups:
      - Label:
          default: Process discovery keywords
        Parameters:
          - LinuxProcessKeywords
          - WindowsProcessKeywords
      - Label:
          default: Collection schedule
        Parameters:
          - ScheduleExpression
    ParameterLabels:
      LinuxProcessKeywords:
        default: Linux process keywords
      WindowsProcessKeywords:
        default: Windows process keywords
      ScheduleExpression:
        default: Association schedule expression

Parameters:

  LinuxProcessKeywords:
    Type: String
    Description: >-
      Comma-delimited list of case-insensitive keywords matched against running process
      names and command lines on Linux managed instances. Individual keywords may contain
      spaces (for example "dse cassandra").
    Default: 'CassandraDaemon,dse cassandra,mysql,postgres,redis-server,redis-sentinel,memcached'
    MinLength: 1
    MaxLength: 2048

  WindowsProcessKeywords:
    Type: String
    Description: >-
      Comma-delimited list of case-insensitive keywords matched against running process
      names and command lines on Windows managed instances.
    Default: 'sqlservr,cassandra,mysql,postgres,redis-server,redis-sentinel,memcached'
    MinLength: 1
    MaxLength: 2048

  ScheduleExpression:
    Type: String
    Description: >-
      Systems Manager State Manager schedule expression controlling how often the custom
      inventory is collected. Accepts either rate() or cron() syntax, for example
      "rate(30 days)" or "cron(0 2 ? * SUN *)".
    Default: 'rate(30 days)'
    AllowedPattern: '^(rate\(.+\)|cron\(.+\))$'
    ConstraintDescription: Must be a valid SSM schedule expression using rate(...) or cron(...) syntax.

Resources:

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Instance profile so a greenfield account can onboard EC2 instances as SSM
  # managed instances and therefore become targets of the association below.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  SsmManagedInstanceRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      Description: Allows EC2 instances to register with AWS Systems Manager and run the custom inventory document.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllowEc2AssumeRole
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: ec2.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore
      Path: /
      Tags:
        - Key: Purpose
          Value: CustomSsmProcessInventory
        - Key: Stack
          Value: !Ref 'AWS::StackName'

  SsmManagedInstanceProfile:
    Type: AWS::IAM::InstanceProfile
    Properties:
      Path: /
      Roles:
        - !Ref SsmManagedInstanceRole

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # SSM Command document. schemaVersion 2.2 is required for per-step
  # `precondition` platform gating. Script bodies use {{parameter}} SSM syntax
  # and are therefore deliberately NOT wrapped in Fn::Sub, so literal shell
  # ${VAR} references remain untouched by CloudFormation.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  CustomInventoryProcessesDocument:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Document
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-Custom-Inventory-Processes'
      DocumentType: Command
      DocumentFormat: YAML
      UpdateMethod: NewVersion
      Tags:
        - Key: Purpose
          Value: CustomSsmProcessInventory
        - Key: Stack
          Value: !Ref 'AWS::StackName'
      Content:
        schemaVersion: '2.2'
        description: >-
          Collects running database and caching processes on Linux and Windows managed
          instances and writes them to the Systems Manager custom inventory directory as
          the Custom:Processes inventory type.
        parameters:
          linuxProcessKeywords:
            type: String
            description: Comma-delimited, case-insensitive process keywords to search for on Linux.
            default: 'CassandraDaemon,dse cassandra,mysql,postgres,redis-server,redis-sentinel,memcached'
            maxChars: 2048
          windowsProcessKeywords:
            type: String
            description: Comma-delimited, case-insensitive process keywords to search for on Windows.
            default: 'sqlservr,cassandra,mysql,postgres,redis-server,redis-sentinel,memcached'
            maxChars: 2048
        mainSteps:

          - name: collectLinuxProcessInventory
            action: aws:runShellScript
            precondition:
              StringEquals:
                - platformType
                - Linux
            inputs:
              timeoutSeconds: '600'
              runCommand:
                - |
                  #!/bin/sh
                  # Custom:Processes inventory collector (Linux).
                  # POSIX sh only: no bash arrays or here-strings are used.
                  set -u

                  IMDS_BASE="http://169.254.169.254/latest"
                  TAB=$(printf '\t')
                  SELF_PID=$$
                  PARENT_PID=${PPID:-0}
                  SELF_SCRIPT="$0"

                  # --- Resolve the instance id via IMDSv2 (token exchange first). -------
                  IMDS_TOKEN=$(curl -s -f -m 5 -X PUT "$IMDS_BASE/api/token" \
                      -H "X-aws-ec2-metadata-token-ttl-seconds: 21600" 2>/dev/null || true)

                  INSTANCE_ID=""
                  if [ -n "$IMDS_TOKEN" ]; then
                    INSTANCE_ID=$(curl -s -f -m 5 \
                        -H "X-aws-ec2-metadata-token: $IMDS_TOKEN" \
                        "$IMDS_BASE/meta-data/instance-id" 2>/dev/null || true)
                  fi

                  # Last-resort fallback for hosts with IMDSv2 disabled. IMDSv2 above is
                  # always attempted first and is the primary path.
                  if [ -z "$INSTANCE_ID" ]; then
                    INSTANCE_ID=$(curl -s -f -m 5 "$IMDS_BASE/meta-data/instance-id" 2>/dev/null || true)
                  fi

                  if [ -z "$INSTANCE_ID" ]; then
                    echo "ERROR: unable to resolve the instance id from the instance metadata service." >&2
                    exit 1
                  fi

                  INVENTORY_DIR="/var/lib/amazon/ssm/$INSTANCE_ID/inventory/custom"
                  OUTPUT_FILE="$INVENTORY_DIR/Custom-Processes.json"
                  mkdir -p "$INVENTORY_DIR"

                  WORK_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
                  trap 'rm -rf "$WORK_DIR"' EXIT INT TERM
                  PS_SNAPSHOT="$WORK_DIR/processes.tsv"
                  KEYWORD_FILE="$WORK_DIR/keywords.txt"
                  ENTRY_FILE="$WORK_DIR/entries.ndjson"
                  STAGED_FILE="$WORK_DIR/Custom-Processes.json"
                  : > "$ENTRY_FILE"

                  # --- JSON-safe scalar: truncate, flatten, strip control chars, escape. -
                  json_escape() {
                    printf '%s' "$1" \
                      | tr '\n\r\t' '   ' \
                      | cut -c1-1024 \
                      | tr -d '\000-\010\013\014\016-\037\177' \
                      | sed -e 's/\\/\\\\/g' -e 's/"/\\"/g'
                  }

                  # --- Snapshot running processes as pid <TAB> comm <TAB> full args. ----
                  ps -eo pid=,comm=,args= 2>/dev/null \
                    | awk 'BEGIN { OFS = "\t" }
                           {
                             proc_pid = $1
                             proc_name = $2
                             $1 = ""
                             $2 = ""
                             sub(/^[ \t]+/, "")
                             print proc_pid, proc_name, $0
                           }' > "$PS_SNAPSHOT" 2>/dev/null || true
                  [ -f "$PS_SNAPSHOT" ] || : > "$PS_SNAPSHOT"

                  # --- Split the keyword list on commas only (spaces are preserved). ----
                  printf '%s\n' "{{linuxProcessKeywords}}" | tr ',' '\n' > "$KEYWORD_FILE"

                  while IFS= read -r RAW_KEYWORD; do
                    KEYWORD=$(printf '%s' "$RAW_KEYWORD" | sed -e 's/^[[:space:]]*//' -e 's/[[:space:]]*$//')
                    if [ -z "$KEYWORD" ]; then
                      continue
                    fi
                    KEYWORD_LC=$(printf '%s' "$KEYWORD" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')

                    while IFS="$TAB" read -r PROC_PID PROC_NAME PROC_ARGS; do
                      # Skip malformed rows.
                      case "$PROC_PID" in
                        ''|*[!0-9]*) continue ;;
                      esac

                      # Never report the collector itself or its helper utilities.
                      if [ "$PROC_PID" = "$SELF_PID" ] || [ "$PROC_PID" = "$PARENT_PID" ]; then
                        continue
                      fi
                      case "$PROC_NAME" in
                        ps|awk|gawk|mawk|nawk|sed|tr|cut|grep|egrep|fgrep|curl|mktemp) continue ;;
                      esac
                      if [ -n "$SELF_SCRIPT" ]; then
                        case "$PROC_ARGS" in
                          *"$SELF_SCRIPT"*) continue ;;
                        esac
                      fi

                      HAYSTACK=$(printf '%s %s' "$PROC_NAME" "$PROC_ARGS" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
                      case "$HAYSTACK" in
                        *"$KEYWORD_LC"*) ;;
                        *) continue ;;
                      esac

                      ESCAPED_NAME=$(json_escape "$PROC_NAME")
                      ESCAPED_KEYWORD=$(json_escape "$KEYWORD")
                      ESCAPED_ARGS=$(json_escape "$PROC_ARGS")

                      printf '{"ProcessName":"%s","Keyword":"%s","PID":"%s","CommandLine":"%s","Platform":"Linux"}\n' \
                        "$ESCAPED_NAME" "$ESCAPED_KEYWORD" "$PROC_PID" "$ESCAPED_ARGS" >> "$ENTRY_FILE"
                    done < "$PS_SNAPSHOT"
                  done < "$KEYWORD_FILE"

                  # --- Join entries. An empty result set yields a valid empty array. ----
                  CONTENT_JSON=$(awk 'NR > 1 { printf "," } { printf "%s", $0 } END { printf "\n" }' "$ENTRY_FILE")
                  ENTRY_COUNT=$(awk 'END { print NR + 0 }' "$ENTRY_FILE")
                  CAPTURE_TIME=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)

                  printf '{"TypeName":"Custom:Processes","SchemaVersion":"1.0","InstanceId":"%s","CaptureTime":"%s","Content":[%s]}\n' \
                    "$INSTANCE_ID" "$CAPTURE_TIME" "$CONTENT_JSON" > "$STAGED_FILE"

                  mv -f "$STAGED_FILE" "$OUTPUT_FILE"
                  chmod 644 "$OUTPUT_FILE"

                  echo "Wrote $ENTRY_COUNT process record(s) for $INSTANCE_ID to $OUTPUT_FILE"
                  exit 0

          - name: collectWindowsProcessInventory
            action: aws:runPowerShellScript
            precondition:
              StringEquals:
                - platformType
                - Windows
            inputs:
              timeoutSeconds: '600'
              runCommand:
                - |
                  # Custom:Processes inventory collector (Windows).
                  $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
                  $ProgressPreference = 'SilentlyContinue'

                  function Get-SanitizedValue {
                      param(
                          [AllowNull()][AllowEmptyString()][string] $Value,
                          [int] $MaxLength = 1024
                      )
                      if ([string]::IsNullOrEmpty($Value)) { return '' }
                      # Replace every Unicode control/format character with a space so the
                      # value cannot break JSON validity. Quotes and backslashes are
                      # escaped later by ConvertTo-Json.
                      $clean = [System.Text.RegularExpressions.Regex]::Replace($Value, '\p{C}', ' ')
                      if ($clean.Length -gt $MaxLength) { $clean = $clean.Substring(0, $MaxLength) }
                      return $clean.Trim()
                  }

                  # --- Resolve the instance id via IMDSv2 (token exchange first). -------
                  $instanceId = $null
                  try {
                      $tokenHeaders = @{ 'X-aws-ec2-metadata-token-ttl-seconds' = '21600' }
                      $imdsToken = Invoke-RestMethod -Method Put `
                          -Uri 'http://169.254.169.254/latest/api/token' `
                          -Headers $tokenHeaders -TimeoutSec 5
                      $instanceId = Invoke-RestMethod -Method Get `
                          -Uri 'http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/instance-id' `
                          -Headers @{ 'X-aws-ec2-metadata-token' = $imdsToken } -TimeoutSec 5
                  } catch {
                      $instanceId = $null
                  }

                  # Last-resort fallback for hosts with IMDSv2 disabled.
                  if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace([string]$instanceId)) {
                      try {
                          $instanceId = Invoke-RestMethod -Method Get `
                              -Uri 'http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/instance-id' -TimeoutSec 5
                      } catch {
                          $instanceId = $null
                      }
                  }

                  if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace([string]$instanceId)) {
                      Write-Output 'ERROR: unable to resolve the instance id from the instance metadata service.'
                      exit 1
                  }
                  $instanceId = ([string]$instanceId).Trim()

                  # --- Split the keyword list on commas only (spaces are preserved). ----
                  $keywordList = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
                  foreach ($rawKeyword in ('{{windowsProcessKeywords}}' -split ',')) {
                      $trimmedKeyword = $rawKeyword.Trim()
                      if ($trimmedKeyword.Length -gt 0) { $keywordList.Add($trimmedKeyword) }
                  }

                  # --- Snapshot running processes. --------------------------------------
                  $processes = @()
                  try {
                      $processes = @(Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_Process -ErrorAction Stop)
                  } catch {
                      $processes = @(Get-Process -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | ForEach-Object {
                          [pscustomobject]@{
                              ProcessId   = $_.Id
                              Name        = $_.ProcessName
                              CommandLine = $_.Path
                          }
                      })
                  }

                  $entries = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
                  $selfPid = $PID

                  foreach ($keyword in $keywordList) {
                      $needle = $keyword.ToLowerInvariant()
                      foreach ($proc in $processes) {
                          # Never report the collector process itself.
                          if ($null -ne $proc.ProcessId -and [int]$proc.ProcessId -eq [int]$selfPid) { continue }

                          $processName = Get-SanitizedValue -Value ([string]$proc.Name) -MaxLength 256
                          $commandLine = Get-SanitizedValue -Value ([string]$proc.CommandLine) -MaxLength 1024
                          $haystack = ($processName + ' ' + $commandLine).ToLowerInvariant()
                          if (-not $haystack.Contains($needle)) { continue }

                          # Every record uses an identical, flat, string-valued key set.
                          $record = [ordered]@{
                              ProcessName = $processName
                              Keyword     = $keyword
                              PID         = [string]$proc.ProcessId
                              CommandLine = $commandLine
                              Platform    = 'Windows'
                          }
                          $entries.Add((ConvertTo-Json -InputObject $record -Depth 2 -Compress))
                      }
                  }

                  # Build the array by hand so a zero- or one-element result still emits a
                  # JSON array rather than "" or a bare object.
                  $contentJson = '[' + ($entries -join ',') + ']'
                  $captureTime = [System.DateTime]::UtcNow.ToString('yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ', [System.Globalization.CultureInfo]::InvariantCulture)
                  $instanceIdJson = ConvertTo-Json -InputObject $instanceId -Compress

                  $payload = '{"TypeName":"Custom:Processes","SchemaVersion":"1.0","InstanceId":' +
                      $instanceIdJson +
                      ',"CaptureTime":"' + $captureTime + '"' +
                      ',"Content":' + $contentJson + '}'

                  $inventoryDir = Join-Path -Path 'C:\ProgramData\Amazon\SSM\InstanceData' -ChildPath $instanceId
                  $inventoryDir = Join-Path -Path $inventoryDir -ChildPath 'inventory\custom'
                  if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $inventoryDir)) {
                      New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $inventoryDir -Force | Out-Null
                  }
                  $outputFile = Join-Path -Path $inventoryDir -ChildPath 'Custom-Processes.json'

                  # UTF-8 without a byte order mark; written to a temp file then moved so a
                  # partially written document is never left in the inventory directory.
                  $stagedFile = [System.IO.Path]::GetTempFileName()
                  $utf8NoBom = New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding($false)
                  [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($stagedFile, $payload, $utf8NoBom)
                  Move-Item -LiteralPath $stagedFile -Destination $outputFile -Force

                  Write-Output ("Wrote {0} process record(s) for {1} to {2}" -f $entries.Count, $instanceId, $outputFile)
                  exit 0

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # State Manager association. Referencing the document with !Ref creates the
  # implicit dependency, so no explicit DependsOn is required.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  CustomInventoryProcessesAssociation:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Association
    Properties:
      AssociationName: Custom-Inventory-Processes
      Name: !Ref CustomInventoryProcessesDocument
      ScheduleExpression: !Ref ScheduleExpression
      ComplianceSeverity: MEDIUM
      MaxConcurrency: 50%
      MaxErrors: 25%
      Targets:
        - Key: InstanceIds
          Values:
            - '*'
      Parameters:
        linuxProcessKeywords:
          - !Ref LinuxProcessKeywords
        windowsProcessKeywords:
          - !Ref WindowsProcessKeywords

Outputs:

  CustomInventoryDocumentName:
    Description: Name of the SSM Command document that collects the Custom:Processes inventory.
    Value: !Ref CustomInventoryProcessesDocument

  CustomInventoryAssociationId:
    Description: Identifier of the State Manager association that runs the custom inventory collection on schedule.
    Value: !GetAtt CustomInventoryProcessesAssociation.AssociationId

  SsmManagedInstanceProfileName:
    Description: >-
      Name of the EC2 instance profile to attach to instances so they register as Systems
      Manager managed instances and become targets of the Custom-Inventory-Processes association.
    Value: !Ref SsmManagedInstanceProfile

  CustomInventoryTypeName:
    Description: Custom inventory type name queried via ssm get-inventory / inventory schema APIs.
    Value: Custom:Processes

  AggregationExtensionPoint:
    Description: >-
      This stack is intentionally scoped to the SSM document and association only. To
      aggregate collected inventory across accounts and regions, add an
      AWS::SSM::ResourceDataSync resource with an S3 destination bucket in a follow-on stack.
    Value: !Sub 'ResourceDataSync intentionally omitted for account ${AWS::AccountId} in region ${AWS::Region}'

final_template:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  Amazon DataZone domain stack provisioning a governance domain with producer
  (SalesPublisher) and consumer (MarketingConsumer) projects, the supporting IAM
  roles for domain execution, data access (Glue, Redshift, Secrets Manager) and
  environment provisioning, an in-template Redshift connection secret, and an
  environment blueprint configuration enabling the DefaultDataWarehouse
  blueprint in the current region.

Parameters:

  DomainName:
    Type: String
    Default: cookbookChapter11
    MinLength: 1
    MaxLength: 40
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-zA-Z0-9-_]+$'
    Description: >-
      Name PREFIX for the Amazon DataZone domain. The created domain name is
      this prefix followed by a hyphen and a unique suffix derived from the
      stack id, because DataZone enforces domain-name uniqueness per account.
      Alphanumeric characters, hyphens and underscores only.
    ConstraintDescription: >-
      Must be 1-40 characters consisting only of alphanumerics, hyphens and
      underscores.

  EnvironmentTag:
    Type: String
    Default: dev
    MinLength: 1
    MaxLength: 32
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-zA-Z0-9-_]+$'
    Description: >-
      Environment identifier applied as a tag to the domain, projects and the
      Redshift connection secret.
    ConstraintDescription: >-
      Must be 1-32 characters consisting only of alphanumerics, hyphens and
      underscores.

Resources:

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Customer-managed KMS key used to encrypt the Redshift connection secret.
  # Created in-template so no external key ARN is ever referenced. The key has
  # no name property, so a retained key can never cause a name collision.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  DataZoneSecretKmsKey:
    Type: AWS::KMS::Key
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      Description: !Sub 'Customer-managed key encrypting DataZone secrets for stack ${AWS::StackName}'
      EnableKeyRotation: true
      KeyPolicy:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: EnableIAMUserPermissions
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              AWS: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::${AWS::AccountId}:root'
            Action: 'kms:*'
            Resource: '*'
          - Sid: AllowSecretsManagerUseOfTheKey
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: secretsmanager.amazonaws.com
            Action:
              - kms:Encrypt
              - kms:Decrypt
              - kms:ReEncrypt*
              - kms:GenerateDataKey*
              - kms:DescribeKey
            Resource: '*'
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                'kms:CallerAccount': !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'
              StringLike:
                'kms:ViaService': !Sub 'secretsmanager.${AWS::Region}.amazonaws.com'
          - Sid: AllowDataZoneServiceDecrypt
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: datazone.amazonaws.com
            Action:
              - kms:Decrypt
              - kms:DescribeKey
            Resource: '*'
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                'aws:SourceAccount': !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'
      Tags:
        - Key: Project
          Value: !Ref DomainName
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentTag
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: CloudFormation

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Redshift connection credentials consumed by the DataZone data access role.
  # Password is always generated - never present in plain text in the template.
  # No explicit Name: the secret is retained on delete, so a CloudFormation
  # generated physical name is required to keep redeploys collision-free.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  RedshiftConnectionSecret:
    Type: AWS::SecretsManager::Secret
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      Description: >-
        Redshift connection credentials read by the Amazon DataZone data access
        role when cataloguing and querying Redshift data sources.
      KmsKeyId: !Ref DataZoneSecretKmsKey
      GenerateSecretString:
        SecretStringTemplate: '{"username": "admin"}'
        GenerateStringKey: password
        PasswordLength: 32
        ExcludeCharacters: '"@/\'
      Tags:
        - Key: Project
          Value: !Ref DomainName
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentTag
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: CloudFormation
        - Key: AmazonDataZoneDomain
          Value: !Ref DomainName

  # Resource policy allowing the DataZone service, within this account only,
  # to read the connection secret.
  RedshiftConnectionSecretPolicy:
    Type: AWS::SecretsManager::ResourcePolicy
    Properties:
      SecretId: !Ref RedshiftConnectionSecret
      BlockPublicPolicy: true
      ResourcePolicy:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllowDataZoneServiceRead
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: datazone.amazonaws.com
            Action:
              - secretsmanager:GetSecretValue
              - secretsmanager:DescribeSecret
            Resource: '*'
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                'aws:SourceAccount': !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Domain execution role. Trusts the DataZone service only; it never references
  # the domain, so no circular dependency with AWS::DataZone::Domain exists.
  # AmazonDataZoneDomainExecutionRolePolicy is published under the service-role
  # path - that prefix is correct here and must stay.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  DataZoneDomainExecutionRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-datazone-domain-execution'
      Description: >-
        Role assumed by Amazon DataZone to execute domain-scoped operations
        such as metadata management and user profile handling.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllowDataZoneServiceAssume
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: datazone.amazonaws.com
            Action:
              - sts:AssumeRole
              - sts:TagSession
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                'aws:SourceAccount': !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AmazonDataZoneDomainExecutionRolePolicy
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: DomainExecutionCloudWatchLogs
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: CloudWatchLogsWrite
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - logs:CreateLogGroup
                  - logs:CreateLogStream
                  - logs:PutLogEvents
                Resource:
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:logs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:log-group:/aws/datazone/*'
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:logs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:log-group:/aws/datazone/*:log-stream:*'
      Tags:
        - Key: Project
          Value: !Ref DomainName
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentTag
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: CloudFormation

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Data access role: Glue catalogue reads, Redshift / Redshift Data API access,
  # and Secrets Manager reads scoped to the in-template secret.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  DataZoneDataAccessRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-datazone-data-access'
      Description: >-
        Role assumed by Amazon DataZone to read Glue catalogue metadata, query
        Redshift data sources and retrieve connection credentials.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllowDataZoneServiceAssume
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: datazone.amazonaws.com
            Action:
              - sts:AssumeRole
              - sts:TagSession
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                'aws:SourceAccount': !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: DataZoneDataAccess
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: GlueCatalogRead
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - glue:GetDatabases
                  - glue:GetDatabase
                  - glue:GetTables
                  - glue:GetTable
                  - glue:GetPartitions
                  - glue:SearchTables
                  - glue:GetConnection
                  - glue:GetConnections
                Resource:
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:glue:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:catalog'
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:glue:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:database/*'
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:glue:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:table/*'
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:glue:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:connection/*'
              - Sid: RedshiftDescribe
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - redshift:DescribeClusters
                Resource:
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:redshift:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:cluster:*'
              - Sid: RedshiftGetClusterCredentials
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - redshift:GetClusterCredentials
                Resource:
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:redshift:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:dbuser:*/*'
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:redshift:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:dbname:*/*'
              - Sid: RedshiftDataApiStatements
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - redshift-data:ExecuteStatement
                Resource:
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:redshift:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:cluster:*'
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:redshift-serverless:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:workgroup/*'
              # Resource-scoped to the same cluster and workgroup patterns as the
              # statement above; the statement-owner condition is no longer needed.
              - Sid: RedshiftDataApiResults
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - redshift-data:DescribeStatement
                  - redshift-data:GetStatementResult
                  - redshift-data:ListStatements
                Resource:
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:redshift:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:cluster:*'
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:redshift-serverless:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:workgroup/*'
              - Sid: RedshiftServerlessRead
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - redshift-serverless:GetWorkgroup
                  - redshift-serverless:ListWorkgroups
                  - redshift-serverless:GetNamespace
                Resource:
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:redshift-serverless:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:workgroup/*'
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:redshift-serverless:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:namespace/*'
              - Sid: SecretsManagerReadStackSecret
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - secretsmanager:GetSecretValue
                  - secretsmanager:DescribeSecret
                Resource:
                  - !Ref RedshiftConnectionSecret
              - Sid: SecretsManagerListAndTaggedRead
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - secretsmanager:ListSecrets
                Resource: '*'
              - Sid: KmsDecryptStackSecret
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - kms:Decrypt
                  - kms:DescribeKey
                Resource:
                  - !GetAtt DataZoneSecretKmsKey.Arn
                Condition:
                  StringLike:
                    'kms:ViaService': !Sub 'secretsmanager.${AWS::Region}.amazonaws.com'
              - Sid: CloudWatchLogsWrite
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - logs:CreateLogGroup
                  - logs:CreateLogStream
                  - logs:PutLogEvents
                Resource:
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:logs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:log-group:/aws/datazone/*'
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:logs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:log-group:/aws/datazone/*:log-stream:*'
      Tags:
        - Key: Project
          Value: !Ref DomainName
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentTag
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: CloudFormation

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Provisioning role used by DataZone to create environment infrastructure.
  # AmazonDataZoneRedshiftGlueProvisioningPolicy is a customer-attachable AWS
  # managed policy and lives at the top-level policy path (no service-role/).
  # The inline policy below keeps the role functional even where the managed
  # policy is unavailable.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  DataZoneProvisioningRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-datazone-provisioning'
      Description: >-
        Role assumed by Amazon DataZone to provision environment infrastructure
        for Redshift and Glue based blueprints.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllowDataZoneServiceAssume
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: datazone.amazonaws.com
            Action:
              - sts:AssumeRole
              - sts:TagSession
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                'aws:SourceAccount': !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AmazonDataZoneRedshiftGlueProvisioningPolicy
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: DataZoneEnvironmentProvisioning
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: GlueCatalogProvisioning
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - glue:GetDatabases
                  - glue:GetDatabase
                  - glue:CreateDatabase
                  - glue:UpdateDatabase
                  - glue:DeleteDatabase
                  - glue:GetTables
                  - glue:GetTable
                  - glue:CreateTable
                  - glue:UpdateTable
                  - glue:DeleteTable
                  - glue:GetPartitions
                  - glue:GetConnection
                  - glue:GetConnections
                  - glue:CreateConnection
                  - glue:UpdateConnection
                  - glue:DeleteConnection
                  - glue:TagResource
                Resource:
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:glue:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:catalog'
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:glue:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:database/*'
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:glue:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:table/*'
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:glue:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:connection/*'
              - Sid: RedshiftProvisioning
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - redshift:DescribeClusters
                  - redshift:CreateTags
                  - redshift:GetClusterCredentials
                Resource:
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:redshift:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:cluster:*'
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:redshift:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:dbuser:*/*'
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:redshift:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:dbname:*/*'
              - Sid: RedshiftServerlessProvisioning
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - redshift-serverless:GetWorkgroup
                  - redshift-serverless:ListWorkgroups
                  - redshift-serverless:GetNamespace
                  - redshift-serverless:TagResource
                Resource:
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:redshift-serverless:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:workgroup/*'
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:redshift-serverless:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:namespace/*'
              - Sid: RedshiftDataApiProvisioning
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - redshift-data:ExecuteStatement
                  - redshift-data:DescribeStatement
                  - redshift-data:GetStatementResult
                  - redshift-data:ListStatements
                Resource:
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:redshift:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:cluster:*'
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:redshift-serverless:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:workgroup/*'
              # PassRole is limited to the two in-template roles and only when
              # DataZone is the consuming service.
              - Sid: PassDataZoneRoles
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - iam:PassRole
                Resource:
                  - !GetAtt DataZoneDataAccessRole.Arn
                  - !GetAtt DataZoneDomainExecutionRole.Arn
                Condition:
                  StringEquals:
                    'iam:PassedToService': datazone.amazonaws.com
              - Sid: CloudWatchLogsWrite
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - logs:CreateLogGroup
                  - logs:CreateLogStream
                  - logs:PutLogEvents
                Resource:
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:logs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:log-group:/aws/datazone/*'
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:logs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:log-group:/aws/datazone/*:log-stream:*'
      Tags:
        - Key: Project
          Value: !Ref DomainName
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentTag
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: CloudFormation

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # The governance domain. SSO disabled so the stack deploys unattended without
  # an IAM Identity Center instance; users are onboarded as IAM user profiles.
  # DataZone enforces domain-name uniqueness per account and this resource is
  # retained on delete, so the name is the DomainName prefix plus the unique
  # trailing GUID segment of AWS::StackId. Built only from the parameter and
  # pseudo-parameters, so no dependency on projects or the blueprint config.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  DataZoneDomain:
    Type: AWS::DataZone::Domain
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub
        - '${Prefix}-${UniqueSuffix}'
        - Prefix: !Ref DomainName
          UniqueSuffix: !Select
            - 4
            - !Split
              - '-'
              - !Select
                - 2
                - !Split
                  - '/'
                  - !Ref 'AWS::StackId'
      Description: >-
        Amazon DataZone governance domain hosting the SalesPublisher producer
        project and the MarketingConsumer consumer project.
      DomainExecutionRole: !GetAtt DataZoneDomainExecutionRole.Arn
      SingleSignOn:
        Type: DISABLED
      Tags:
        - Key: Project
          Value: !Ref DomainName
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentTag
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: CloudFormation

  SalesPublisherProject:
    Type: AWS::DataZone::Project
    Properties:
      DomainIdentifier: !Ref DataZoneDomain
      Name: SalesPublisher
      Description: >-
        Producer/publisher team project. Owns Sales data assets, publishes them
        to the DataZone catalogue and approves subscription requests.

  MarketingConsumerProject:
    Type: AWS::DataZone::Project
    Properties:
      DomainIdentifier: !Ref DataZoneDomain
      Name: MarketingConsumer
      Description: >-
        Consumer team project. Discovers published Sales data assets, requests
        subscriptions and consumes approved data for marketing analytics.

  # RegionalParameters intentionally omitted: its per-region sub-property schema
  # is environment specific and is not required to enable the blueprint.
  DefaultDataWarehouseBlueprintConfiguration:
    Type: AWS::DataZone::EnvironmentBlueprintConfiguration
    Properties:
      DomainIdentifier: !Ref DataZoneDomain
      EnvironmentBlueprintIdentifier: DefaultDataWarehouse
      EnabledRegions:
        - !Ref 'AWS::Region'
      ProvisioningRoleArn: !GetAtt DataZoneProvisioningRole.Arn
      ManageAccessRoleArn: !GetAtt DataZoneDataAccessRole.Arn

Outputs:

  DataZoneDomainId:
    Description: Identifier of the Amazon DataZone domain.
    Value: !Ref DataZoneDomain
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-DomainId'

  DataZoneDomainArn:
    Description: ARN of the Amazon DataZone domain.
    Value: !GetAtt DataZoneDomain.Arn
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-DomainArn'

  DataZoneDomainPortalUrl:
    Description: Data portal URL for the Amazon DataZone domain.
    Value: !GetAtt DataZoneDomain.PortalUrl
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-DomainPortalUrl'

  SalesPublisherProjectId:
    Description: Identifier of the SalesPublisher producer project.
    Value: !GetAtt SalesPublisherProject.Id
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-SalesPublisherProjectId'

  MarketingConsumerProjectId:
    Description: Identifier of the MarketingConsumer consumer project.
    Value: !GetAtt MarketingConsumerProject.Id
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-MarketingConsumerProjectId'

  DataZoneDomainExecutionRoleArn:
    Description: ARN of the DataZone domain execution role.
    Value: !GetAtt DataZoneDomainExecutionRole.Arn
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-DomainExecutionRoleArn'

  DataZoneDataAccessRoleArn:
    Description: ARN of the DataZone data access (manage access) role.
    Value: !GetAtt DataZoneDataAccessRole.Arn
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-DataAccessRoleArn'

  DataZoneProvisioningRoleArn:
    Description: ARN of the DataZone environment provisioning role.
    Value: !GetAtt DataZoneProvisioningRole.Arn
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-ProvisioningRoleArn'

  RedshiftConnectionSecretArn:
    Description: ARN of the Redshift connection secret read by the data access role.
    Value: !Ref RedshiftConnectionSecret
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-RedshiftConnectionSecretArn'

final_template:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: >-
  App Mesh colorteller blue/green demo stack - provisions a VPC, an AWS Cloud Map
  private DNS namespace and service, and the full App Mesh topology (mesh,
  colorgateway virtual gateway, colorteller virtual service, virtual router and
  the colorteller-blue-node / colorteller-green-node virtual nodes with a 50/50
  traffic split). Compute (ECS/EC2 tasks and Envoy sidecars) is intentionally out
  of scope and registers into this topology separately.

Parameters:
  MeshServiceName:
    Type: String
    Default: colorteller
    Description: >-
      Logical service name shared by the AWS Cloud Map service and the App Mesh
      virtual nodes / virtual service.
    MinLength: 1
    MaxLength: 63
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-zA-Z0-9]([a-zA-Z0-9-]*[a-zA-Z0-9])?$'
    ConstraintDescription: >-
      Must be 1-63 characters of letters, numbers or hyphens, starting and
      ending with a letter or number.

Resources:

  # ------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Networking - required so the Cloud Map private DNS namespace resolves
  # ------------------------------------------------------------------
  Vpc:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPC
    Properties:
      CidrBlock: 10.0.0.0/16
      EnableDnsSupport: true
      EnableDnsHostnames: true
      InstanceTenancy: default
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-vpc'

  # ------------------------------------------------------------------
  # AWS Cloud Map service discovery
  # ------------------------------------------------------------------
  ServiceDiscoveryNamespace:
    Type: AWS::ServiceDiscovery::PrivateDnsNamespace
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}.local'
      Description: !Sub 'Private DNS namespace for the ${AWS::StackName} App Mesh demo'
      Vpc: !Ref Vpc
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-namespace'

  ColorTellerServiceDiscoveryService:
    Type: AWS::ServiceDiscovery::Service
    Properties:
      Name: !Ref MeshServiceName
      Description: !Sub 'Cloud Map service backing the ${MeshServiceName} App Mesh virtual nodes'
      NamespaceId: !GetAtt ServiceDiscoveryNamespace.Id
      DnsConfig:
        DnsRecords:
          - Type: A
            TTL: 60
      HealthCheckCustomConfig:
        FailureThreshold: 1
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-${MeshServiceName}'

  # ------------------------------------------------------------------
  # App Mesh
  # ------------------------------------------------------------------
  Mesh:
    Type: AWS::AppMesh::Mesh
    Properties:
      MeshName: !Ref 'AWS::StackName'
      Spec:
        EgressFilter:
          Type: ALLOW_ALL
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Ref 'AWS::StackName'

  ColorTellerBlueVirtualNode:
    Type: AWS::AppMesh::VirtualNode
    Properties:
      MeshName: !GetAtt Mesh.MeshName
      VirtualNodeName: colorteller-blue-node
      Spec:
        Listeners:
          - PortMapping:
              Port: 9080
              Protocol: http
            HealthCheck:
              Protocol: http
              Path: /ping
              Port: 9080
              HealthyThreshold: 2
              UnhealthyThreshold: 2
              TimeoutMillis: 2000
              IntervalMillis: 5000
        ServiceDiscovery:
          AWSCloudMap:
            NamespaceName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}.local'
            ServiceName: !Ref MeshServiceName
            Attributes:
              - Key: ECS_TASK_DEFINITION_FAMILY
                Value: colorteller-blue
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-colorteller-blue-node'

  ColorTellerGreenVirtualNode:
    Type: AWS::AppMesh::VirtualNode
    Properties:
      MeshName: !GetAtt Mesh.MeshName
      VirtualNodeName: colorteller-green-node
      Spec:
        Listeners:
          - PortMapping:
              Port: 9080
              Protocol: http
            HealthCheck:
              Protocol: http
              Path: /ping
              Port: 9080
              HealthyThreshold: 2
              UnhealthyThreshold: 2
              TimeoutMillis: 2000
              IntervalMillis: 5000
        ServiceDiscovery:
          AWSCloudMap:
            NamespaceName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}.local'
            ServiceName: !Ref MeshServiceName
            Attributes:
              - Key: ECS_TASK_DEFINITION_FAMILY
                Value: colorteller-green
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-colorteller-green-node'

  ColorTellerVirtualRouter:
    Type: AWS::AppMesh::VirtualRouter
    Properties:
      MeshName: !GetAtt Mesh.MeshName
      VirtualRouterName: colorteller-vr
      Spec:
        Listeners:
          - PortMapping:
              Port: 9080
              Protocol: http
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-colorteller-vr'

  ColorTellerRoute:
    Type: AWS::AppMesh::Route
    Properties:
      MeshName: !GetAtt Mesh.MeshName
      VirtualRouterName: !GetAtt ColorTellerVirtualRouter.VirtualRouterName
      RouteName: colorteller-route
      Spec:
        HttpRoute:
          Match:
            Prefix: /
          Action:
            WeightedTargets:
              - VirtualNode: !GetAtt ColorTellerBlueVirtualNode.VirtualNodeName
                Weight: 50
              - VirtualNode: !GetAtt ColorTellerGreenVirtualNode.VirtualNodeName
                Weight: 50
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-colorteller-route'

  ColorTellerVirtualService:
    Type: AWS::AppMesh::VirtualService
    Properties:
      MeshName: !GetAtt Mesh.MeshName
      VirtualServiceName: !Sub '${MeshServiceName}.${AWS::StackName}.local'
      Spec:
        Provider:
          VirtualRouter:
            VirtualRouterName: !GetAtt ColorTellerVirtualRouter.VirtualRouterName
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-${MeshServiceName}-vs'

  ColorGatewayVirtualGateway:
    Type: AWS::AppMesh::VirtualGateway
    Properties:
      MeshName: !GetAtt Mesh.MeshName
      VirtualGatewayName: colorgateway
      Spec:
        Listeners:
          - PortMapping:
              Port: 9080
              Protocol: http
            HealthCheck:
              Protocol: http
              Path: /ping
              Port: 9080
              HealthyThreshold: 2
              UnhealthyThreshold: 2
              TimeoutMillis: 2000
              IntervalMillis: 5000
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-colorgateway'

  ColorGatewayRoute:
    Type: AWS::AppMesh::GatewayRoute
    Properties:
      MeshName: !GetAtt Mesh.MeshName
      VirtualGatewayName: !GetAtt ColorGatewayVirtualGateway.VirtualGatewayName
      GatewayRouteName: colorgateway-route
      Spec:
        HttpRoute:
          Match:
            Prefix: /
          Action:
            Target:
              VirtualService:
                VirtualServiceName: !GetAtt ColorTellerVirtualService.VirtualServiceName
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-colorgateway-route'

Outputs:
  MeshName:
    Description: Name of the App Mesh service mesh
    Value: !GetAtt Mesh.MeshName
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-MeshName'

  VirtualGatewayName:
    Description: Name of the colorgateway virtual gateway
    Value: !GetAtt ColorGatewayVirtualGateway.VirtualGatewayName
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-VirtualGatewayName'

  VirtualServiceName:
    Description: Name of the colorteller virtual service
    Value: !GetAtt ColorTellerVirtualService.VirtualServiceName
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-VirtualServiceName'

  VirtualRouterName:
    Description: Name of the colorteller virtual router
    Value: !GetAtt ColorTellerVirtualRouter.VirtualRouterName
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-VirtualRouterName'

  BlueVirtualNodeName:
    Description: Name of the colorteller blue virtual node
    Value: !GetAtt ColorTellerBlueVirtualNode.VirtualNodeName
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-BlueVirtualNodeName'

  GreenVirtualNodeName:
    Description: Name of the colorteller green virtual node
    Value: !GetAtt ColorTellerGreenVirtualNode.VirtualNodeName
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-GreenVirtualNodeName'

  CloudMapNamespaceId:
    Description: Id of the AWS Cloud Map private DNS namespace
    Value: !GetAtt ServiceDiscoveryNamespace.Id
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-CloudMapNamespaceId'

  CloudMapNamespaceName:
    Description: Name of the AWS Cloud Map private DNS namespace
    Value: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}.local'
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-CloudMapNamespaceName'

  CloudMapServiceId:
    Description: Id of the AWS Cloud Map service for colorteller
    Value: !GetAtt ColorTellerServiceDiscoveryService.Id
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-CloudMapServiceId'

  CloudMapServiceArn:
    Description: ARN of the AWS Cloud Map service for colorteller
    Value: !GetAtt ColorTellerServiceDiscoveryService.Arn
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-CloudMapServiceArn'

  VpcId:

final_template:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  Greenfield data-processing pipeline storage layer. Creates a customer-managed KMS
  key plus a private, SSE-KMS-encrypted, versioned source bucket and target bucket,
  and an optional EMR log bucket created only when CreateEmrLogBucket is 'true'. All
  buckets carry an identical lifecycle rule (90-day transition to a region-dependent
  storage class, 2555-day expiration); the rule is Enabled only on the EMR log bucket.
  Bucket names, the EMR log bucket DNS name, and the CMK ARN are exported for
  cross-stack reference.

Parameters:

  AppName:
    Type: String
    Default: data-pipeline
    Description: >-
      Lowercase application slug used only to construct globally unique bucket names
      and the KMS alias.
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-z0-9-]{3,32}$'
    ConstraintDescription: >-
      Must be 3-32 characters of lowercase letters, digits, or hyphens.

  CreateEmrLogBucket:
    Type: String
    Default: 'true'
    Description: >-
      Set to 'true' to create the optional EMR log bucket, its bucket policy, and its
      exports. Set to 'false' to skip them entirely.
    AllowedValues:
      - 'true'
      - 'false'

Mappings:

  # Storage class used by the 90-day lifecycle transition, selected per region.
  # Every region this stack may deploy into MUST have an entry here; an unmapped
  # region causes a template-resolution failure at deploy time.
  RegionStorageClass:
    us-east-1:
      TransitionClass: STANDARD_IA
    us-east-2:
      TransitionClass: STANDARD_IA
    us-west-1:
      TransitionClass: GLACIER
    us-west-2:
      TransitionClass: STANDARD_IA
    ca-central-1:
      TransitionClass: GLACIER
    eu-west-1:
      TransitionClass: STANDARD_IA
    eu-west-2:
      TransitionClass: GLACIER
    eu-west-3:
      TransitionClass: GLACIER
    eu-central-1:
      TransitionClass: STANDARD_IA
    eu-north-1:
      TransitionClass: GLACIER
    ap-south-1:
      TransitionClass: GLACIER
    ap-southeast-1:
      TransitionClass: STANDARD_IA
    ap-southeast-2:
      TransitionClass: STANDARD_IA
    ap-northeast-1:
      TransitionClass: STANDARD_IA
    ap-northeast-2:
      TransitionClass: GLACIER
    ap-northeast-3:
      TransitionClass: GLACIER
    sa-east-1:
      TransitionClass: GLACIER

Conditions:

  CreateEmrLogs: !Equals [!Ref CreateEmrLogBucket, 'true']

Resources:

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Customer-managed key shared by all three buckets. The key policy is scoped by
  # service and account condition keys rather than by bucket ARN: referencing the
  # buckets here while the buckets reference the key would create a circular
  # dependency that CloudFormation rejects.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  PipelineKmsKey:
    Type: AWS::KMS::Key
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      Description: !Sub 'Customer-managed key for ${AppName} pipeline S3 buckets.'
      EnableKeyRotation: true
      KeySpec: SYMMETRIC_DEFAULT
      KeyUsage: ENCRYPT_DECRYPT
      PendingWindowInDays: 30
      KeyPolicy:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllowAccountAdministration
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              AWS: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::${AWS::AccountId}:root'
            Action: 'kms:*'
            Resource: '*'
          - Sid: AllowS3UseOfTheKey
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: s3.amazonaws.com
            Action:
              - 'kms:GenerateDataKey*'
              - 'kms:Decrypt'
              - 'kms:Encrypt'
              - 'kms:ReEncrypt*'
              - 'kms:DescribeKey'
            Resource: '*'
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                'kms:ViaService': !Sub 's3.${AWS::Region}.amazonaws.com'
                'aws:SourceAccount': !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'
          - Sid: AllowEmrUseOfTheKey
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: elasticmapreduce.amazonaws.com
            Action:
              - 'kms:GenerateDataKey*'
              - 'kms:Decrypt'
              - 'kms:DescribeKey'
            Resource: '*'
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                'aws:SourceAccount': !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref AppName
        - Key: Role
          Value: pipeline-cmk

  PipelineKmsKeyAlias:
    Type: AWS::KMS::Alias
    Properties:
      AliasName: !Sub 'alias/${AppName}-pipeline-${AWS::Region}'
      TargetKeyId: !Ref PipelineKmsKey

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Pipeline ingest bucket.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  SourceBucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      BucketName: !Sub '${AppName}-source-${AWS::AccountId}-${AWS::Region}'
      PublicAccessBlockConfiguration:
        BlockPublicAcls: true
        BlockPublicPolicy: true
        IgnorePublicAcls: true
        RestrictPublicBuckets: true
      OwnershipControls:
        Rules:
          - ObjectOwnership: BucketOwnerEnforced
      BucketEncryption:
        ServerSideEncryptionConfiguration:
          - BucketKeyEnabled: true
            ServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
              SSEAlgorithm: 'aws:kms'
              KMSMasterKeyID: !GetAtt PipelineKmsKey.Arn
      VersioningConfiguration:
        Status: Enabled
      LifecycleConfiguration:
        Rules:
          # Status is Disabled here: the rule is declared for parity with the EMR log
          # bucket but is inert — no transition, expiration, noncurrent-version
          # expiration, or multipart abort occurs on this bucket. Flip Status to
          # Enabled to activate it without any other template change.
          - Id: PipelineDataTiering
            Status: Disabled
            Transitions:
              - TransitionInDays: 90
                StorageClass: !FindInMap [RegionStorageClass, !Ref 'AWS::Region', TransitionClass]
            ExpirationInDays: 2555
            NoncurrentVersionExpiration:
              NoncurrentDays: 2555
            AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload:
              DaysAfterInitiation: 7
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref AppName
        - Key: Role
          Value: pipeline-source

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Pipeline output bucket.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  TargetBucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      BucketName: !Sub '${AppName}-target-${AWS::AccountId}-${AWS::Region}'
      PublicAccessBlockConfiguration:
        BlockPublicAcls: true
        BlockPublicPolicy: true
        IgnorePublicAcls: true
        RestrictPublicBuckets: true
      OwnershipControls:
        Rules:
          - ObjectOwnership: BucketOwnerEnforced
      BucketEncryption:
        ServerSideEncryptionConfiguration:
          - BucketKeyEnabled: true
            ServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
              SSEAlgorithm: 'aws:kms'
              KMSMasterKeyID: !GetAtt PipelineKmsKey.Arn
      VersioningConfiguration:
        Status: Enabled
      LifecycleConfiguration:
        Rules:
          # Disabled: inert on this bucket. See the note on SourceBucket above.
          - Id: PipelineDataTiering
            Status: Disabled
            Transitions:
              - TransitionInDays: 90
                StorageClass: !FindInMap [RegionStorageClass, !Ref 'AWS::Region', TransitionClass]
            ExpirationInDays: 2555
            NoncurrentVersionExpiration:
              NoncurrentDays: 2555
            AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload:
              DaysAfterInitiation: 7
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref AppName
        - Key: Role
          Value: pipeline-target

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Optional EMR log delivery bucket. This is the only bucket whose lifecycle
  # rule is Enabled.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  EmrLogBucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Condition: CreateEmrLogs
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      BucketName: !Sub '${AppName}-emr-logs-${AWS::AccountId}-${AWS::Region}'
      PublicAccessBlockConfiguration:
        BlockPublicAcls: true
        BlockPublicPolicy: true
        IgnorePublicAcls: true
        RestrictPublicBuckets: true
      OwnershipControls:
        Rules:
          - ObjectOwnership: BucketOwnerEnforced
      BucketEncryption:
        ServerSideEncryptionConfiguration:
          - BucketKeyEnabled: true
            ServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
              SSEAlgorithm: 'aws:kms'
              KMSMasterKeyID: !GetAtt PipelineKmsKey.Arn
      VersioningConfiguration:
        Status: Enabled
      LifecycleConfiguration:
        Rules:
          # Enabled: this is the single active lifecycle rule in the stack.
          - Id: PipelineDataTiering
            Status: Enabled
            Transitions:
              - TransitionInDays: 90
                StorageClass: !FindInMap [RegionStorageClass, !Ref 'AWS::Region', TransitionClass]
            ExpirationInDays: 2555
            NoncurrentVersionExpiration:
              NoncurrentDays: 2555
            AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload:
              DaysAfterInitiation: 7
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref AppName
        - Key: Role
          Value: emr-logs

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Bucket policies. No DependsOn is needed: the !Ref / !GetAtt references below
  # already establish the bucket -> policy ordering. The encryption deny matches
  # 'aws:kms' because the buckets now default to SSE-KMS; denying anything other
  # than AES256 here would reject every compliant upload.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  SourceBucketPolicy:
    Type: AWS::S3::BucketPolicy
    Properties:
      Bucket: !Ref SourceBucket
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: DenyInsecureTransport
            Effect: Deny
            Principal: '*'
            Action: 's3:*'
            Resource:
              - !Sub '${SourceBucket.Arn}'
              - !Sub '${SourceBucket.Arn}/*'
            Condition:
              Bool:
                'aws:SecureTransport': 'false'
          - Sid: DenyUnencryptedObjectUploads
            Effect: Deny
            Principal: '*'
            Action: 's3:PutObject'
            Resource: !Sub '${SourceBucket.Arn}/*'
            Condition:
              StringNotEquals:
                's3:x-amz-server-side-encryption': 'aws:kms'

  TargetBucketPolicy:
    Type: AWS::S3::BucketPolicy
    Properties:
      Bucket: !Ref TargetBucket
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: DenyInsecureTransport
            Effect: Deny
            Principal: '*'
            Action: 's3:*'
            Resource:
              - !Sub '${TargetBucket.Arn}'
              - !Sub '${TargetBucket.Arn}/*'
            Condition:
              Bool:
                'aws:SecureTransport': 'false'
          - Sid: DenyUnencryptedObjectUploads
            Effect: Deny
            Principal: '*'
            Action: 's3:PutObject'
            Resource: !Sub '${TargetBucket.Arn}/*'
            Condition:
              StringNotEquals:
                's3:x-amz-server-side-encryption': 'aws:kms'

  EmrLogBucketPolicy:
    Type: AWS::S3::BucketPolicy
    Condition: CreateEmrLogs
    Properties:
      Bucket: !Ref EmrLogBucket
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: DenyInsecureTransport
            Effect: Deny
            Principal: '*'
            Action: 's3:*'
            Resource:
              - !Sub '${EmrLogBucket.Arn}'
              - !Sub '${EmrLogBucket.Arn}/*'
            Condition:
              Bool:
                'aws:SecureTransport': 'false'
          - Sid: DenyUnencryptedObjectUploads
            Effect: Deny
            Principal: '*'
            Action: 's3:PutObject'
            Resource: !Sub '${EmrLogBucket.Arn}/*'
            Condition:
              StringNotEquals:
                's3:x-amz-server-side-encryption': 'aws:kms'
          # EMR log delivery, confused-deputy-scoped to this account only. The
          # matching KMS grant lives in the PipelineKmsKey key policy.
          - Sid: AllowEmrLogDelivery
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: elasticmapreduce.amazonaws.com
            Action:
              - 's3:PutObject'
              - 's3:GetBucketAcl'
            Resource:
              - !Sub '${EmrLogBucket.Arn}'
              - !Sub '${EmrLogBucket.Arn}/*'
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                'aws:SourceAccount': !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'

Outputs:

  SourceBucketName:
    Description: Name of the pipeline source (ingest) bucket.
    Value: !Ref SourceBucket
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-SourceBucketName'

  TargetBucketName:
    Description: Name of the pipeline target (output) bucket.
    Value: !Ref TargetBucket
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-TargetBucketName'

  EmrLogBucketName:
    Condition: CreateEmrLogs
    Description: Name of the optional EMR log bucket.
    Value: !Ref EmrLogBucket
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-EmrLogBucketName'

  EmrLogBucketDnsName:
    Condition: CreateEmrLogs
    Description: >-
      DNS name of the optional EMR log bucket. Use the RegionalDomainName attribute
      instead if a region-specific endpoint is required.
    Value: !GetAtt EmrLogBucket.DomainName
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-EmrLogBucketDnsName'

  PipelineKmsKeyArn:
    Description: >-
      ARN of the customer-managed key encrypting all pipeline buckets. Cross-stack
      consumers need decrypt permission on this key to read bucket objects.
    Value: !GetAtt PipelineKmsKey.Arn
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-PipelineKmsKeyArn'

final_template:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  Self-contained, event-driven stack that automatically disables IMDSv1
  (enforces IMDSv2) on EC2 instances as they enter the running state. An
  EventBridge rule matches EC2 Instance State-change Notifications for the
  running state and invokes the AWS-owned AWSSupport-ConfigureEC2Metadata
  Systems Manager Automation document, which sets HttpTokens to required,
  keeps the metadata endpoint enabled, and applies a configurable HTTP PUT
  response hop limit. All IAM roles required by EventBridge and by the
  Automation execution are created inside this stack; no VPC, subnet,
  compute, or pre-existing role is required.

Parameters:
  HttpPutResponseHopLimit:
    Type: Number
    Default: 1
    MinValue: 1
    MaxValue: 64
    Description: >-
      Desired HTTP PUT response hop limit for instance metadata requests. A
      value of 1 confines IMDSv2 credential retrieval to the instance itself;
      increase it only when containers or nested network hops must reach the
      metadata service. Valid range is 1 to 64.

Resources:
  # Role assumed by SSM Automation when it executes
  # AWSSupport-ConfigureEC2Metadata. Confused-deputy protection is provided by
  # aws:SourceAccount; aws:SourceArn is deliberately NOT asserted here because
  # Automation assumes the execution role through a direct STS call that does
  # not populate that key, which would render the role unassumable.
  AutomationExecutionRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      Description: >-
        Execution role assumed by SSM Automation to inspect and modify EC2
        instance metadata options.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: ssm.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                aws:SourceAccount: !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AmazonSSMAutomationRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: ConfigureEC2MetadataLeastPrivilege
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              # Intentional, documented exception: EC2 describe/list APIs do
              # not support resource-level permissions, so this action must be
              # granted on "*". It is read-only and non-mutating.
              - Sid: DescribeInstancesRequiresWildcardResource
                Effect: Allow
                Action: ec2:DescribeInstances
                Resource: '*'
              - Sid: ModifyMetadataOptionsOnInstancesInThisAccount
                Effect: Allow
                Action: ec2:ModifyInstanceMetadataOptions
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:ec2:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:instance/*'

  # Role assumed by EventBridge to start the Automation execution. EventBridge
  # does populate aws:SourceArn for rule-initiated assumptions, so the ArnLike
  # condition is retained here. This role carries no !GetAtt on the execution
  # role, so both roles are created in parallel.
  EventBridgeAutomationInvokeRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      Description: >-
        Role assumed by EventBridge to start the AWSSupport-ConfigureEC2Metadata
        Automation execution.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: events.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                aws:SourceAccount: !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'
              ArnLike:
                aws:SourceArn: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:events:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:rule/*'
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: StartConfigureEC2MetadataAutomation
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              # AWS-owned Automation documents live in an AWS-managed account,
              # so the account field is wildcarded rather than fabricated. Both
              # the unversioned ARN (the form the rule target invokes) and the
              # versioned form are granted.
              - Sid: StartAutomationForConfigureEC2Metadata
                Effect: Allow
                Action: ssm:StartAutomationExecution
                Resource:
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:ssm:${AWS::Region}:*:automation-definition/AWSSupport-ConfigureEC2Metadata'
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:ssm:${AWS::Region}:*:automation-definition/AWSSupport-ConfigureEC2Metadata:*'

  # PassRole is split into a standalone policy so the two roles create in
  # parallel; only this small resource waits on both.
  EventBridgePassAutomationRolePolicy:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Policy
    Properties:
      PolicyName: PassAutomationExecutionRoleToSsmOnly
      Roles:
        - !Ref EventBridgeAutomationInvokeRole
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: PassAutomationExecutionRoleToSsmOnly
            Effect: Allow
            Action: iam:PassRole
            Resource: !GetAtt AutomationExecutionRole.Arn
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                iam:PassedToService: ssm.amazonaws.com

  # Default event bus rule: fires only on the "running" state transition. The
  # physical name is generated by CloudFormation (stack-scoped and unique),
  # avoiding the 64-character EventBridge rule-name limit and keeping the stack
  # free of immutable properties. The single external reference in this stack is
  # the AWS-owned AWSSupport-ConfigureEC2Metadata document, which exists in
  # every account and region and is therefore not account-specific
  # infrastructure.
  EnforceImdsv2Rule:
    Type: AWS::Events::Rule
    Properties:
      Description: >-
        Triggers the AWSSupport-ConfigureEC2Metadata Automation document to
        enforce IMDSv2 whenever an EC2 instance enters the running state.
      State: ENABLED
      EventPattern:
        source:
          - aws.ec2
        detail-type:
