AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  AWS AppSync GraphQL API (AWS_IAM authentication) for a Note type, backed by an
  AMAZON_EVENTBRIDGE data source that publishes getNote/saveNote events to a
  custom EventBridge event bus created in this template, including the least
  privilege IAM roles, X-Ray tracing, field level logging, and an observability
  rule that archives emitted events to CloudWatch Logs.

# Design note (objective): EventBridge is fire-and-forget. PutEvents returns only an
# event id, so the Query.getNote resolver CANNOT return persisted data read back from
# the bus. Both resolvers therefore return an acknowledgement shaped as the Note type
# (echoed from ctx.args). Real persistence and real reads would require an additional
# data source (for example a table or a Lambda function) which is outside the scope of
# this request and is intentionally not created here.

Parameters:
  AppName:
    Type: String
    Default: notes-api
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{2,30}$'
    Description: >-
      Lowercase application name used to build resource names, event sources and tags.
      Must start with a letter and contain only lowercase letters, digits and hyphens.

Resources:

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Custom event bus (created here; the default bus is never used)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  NotesEventBus:
    Type: AWS::Events::EventBus
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${AppName}-notes-bus'
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AppName}-notes-bus'
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref AppName

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # IAM role letting AppSync push field logs to CloudWatch Logs
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  AppSyncLogsRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      Description: !Sub 'Allows AppSync API ${AppName}-graphql-api to write field logs to CloudWatch Logs.'
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: appsync.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                aws:SourceAccount: !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'
              ArnLike:
                aws:SourceArn: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:appsync:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:apis/*'
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSAppSyncPushToCloudWatchLogs
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref AppName

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # IAM role letting AppSync publish to the custom bus (events:PutEvents only)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  AppSyncEventBridgeRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      Description: !Sub 'Allows AppSync API ${AppName}-graphql-api to put events on the ${AppName}-notes-bus event bus.'
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: appsync.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                aws:SourceAccount: !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'
              ArnLike:
                aws:SourceArn: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:appsync:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:apis/*'
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: !Sub '${AppName}-appsync-putevents'
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: PutEventsOnNotesBusOnly
                Effect: Allow
                Action: events:PutEvents
                Resource: !GetAtt NotesEventBus.Arn
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref AppName

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # GraphQL API
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  NotesGraphQLApi:
    Type: AWS::AppSync::GraphQLApi
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${AppName}-graphql-api'
      AuthenticationType: AWS_IAM
      XrayEnabled: true
      LogConfig:
        FieldLogLevel: ERROR
        ExcludeVerboseContent: true
        CloudWatchLogsRoleArn: !GetAtt AppSyncLogsRole.Arn
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AppName}-graphql-api'
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref AppName

  # Bounded retention for the AppSync field logs written by the API above.
  NotesGraphQLApiLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: !Sub '/aws/appsync/apis/${NotesGraphQLApi.ApiId}'
      RetentionInDays: 14
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref AppName

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Schema
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  NotesGraphQLSchema:
    Type: AWS::AppSync::GraphQLSchema
    Properties:
      ApiId: !GetAtt NotesGraphQLApi.ApiId
      Definition: |
        type Note {
          NoteId: ID!
          title: String
          content: String
        }

        type Query {
          getNote(NoteId: ID!): Note
        }

        type Mutation {
          saveNote(NoteId: ID!, title: String!, content: String): Note
        }

        schema {
          query: Query
          mutation: Mutation
        }

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # EventBridge data source
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  NotesEventBridgeDataSource:
    Type: AWS::AppSync::DataSource
    Properties:
      ApiId: !GetAtt NotesGraphQLApi.ApiId
      Name: NotesEventBridgeDataSource
      Description: !Sub 'Publishes Note events to the ${AppName}-notes-bus custom event bus.'
      Type: AMAZON_EVENTBRIDGE
      ServiceRoleArn: !GetAtt AppSyncEventBridgeRole.Arn
      EventBridgeConfig:
        EventBusArn: !GetAtt NotesEventBus.Arn

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Resolvers (DependsOn the schema: a genuine ordering requirement that no
  # Ref/GetAtt expresses, because resolvers bind to fields the schema declares)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  GetNoteResolver:
    Type: AWS::AppSync::Resolver
    DependsOn: NotesGraphQLSchema
    Properties:
      ApiId: !GetAtt NotesGraphQLApi.ApiId
      TypeName: Query
      FieldName: getNote
      DataSourceName: !GetAtt NotesEventBridgeDataSource.Name
      Runtime:
        Name: APPSYNC_JS
        RuntimeVersion: '1.0.0'
      Code: !Sub |
        import { util } from '@aws-appsync/utils';

        /**
         * Emits a getNote event onto the custom bus. PutEvents is fire-and-forget,
         * so no persisted Note can be read back here.
         */
        export function request(ctx) {
          return {
            operation: 'PutEvents',
            Entries: [
              {
                Source: '${AppName}.appsync',
                DetailType: 'getNote',
                Detail: ctx.args,
                EventBusName: '${NotesEventBus}',
              },
            ],
          };
        }

        export function response(ctx) {
          if (ctx.error) {
            util.error(ctx.error.message, ctx.error.type, null, ctx.error);
          }
          const args = ctx.args;
          return {
            NoteId: args.NoteId,
            title: null,
            content: null,
          };
        }

  SaveNoteResolver:
    Type: AWS::AppSync::Resolver
    DependsOn: NotesGraphQLSchema
    Properties:
      ApiId: !GetAtt NotesGraphQLApi.ApiId
      TypeName: Mutation
      FieldName: saveNote
      DataSourceName: !GetAtt NotesEventBridgeDataSource.Name
      Runtime:
        Name: APPSYNC_JS
        RuntimeVersion: '1.0.0'
      Code: !Sub |
        import { util } from '@aws-appsync/utils';

        /**
         * Emits a saveNote event onto the custom bus. The returned Note is an
         * acknowledgement echoed from the arguments, not a stored record.
         */
        export function request(ctx) {
          return {
            operation: 'PutEvents',
            Entries: [
              {
                Source: '${AppName}.appsync',
                DetailType: 'saveNote',
                Detail: ctx.args,
                EventBusName: '${NotesEventBus}',
              },
            ],
          };
        }

        export function response(ctx) {
          if (ctx.error) {
            util.error(ctx.error.message, ctx.error.type, null, ctx.error);
          }
          const args = ctx.args;
          return {
            NoteId: args.NoteId,
            title: args.title,
            content: args.content === undefined ? null : args.content,
          };
        }

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Observability: archive events emitted by the API to CloudWatch Logs
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  NotesEventsLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: !Sub '/aws/events/${AppName}-notes-bus'
      RetentionInDays: 14
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref AppName

  NotesEventsLogGroupResourcePolicy:
    Type: AWS::Logs::ResourcePolicy
    Properties:
      PolicyName: !Sub '${AppName}-notes-events-to-logs'
      PolicyDocument: !Sub |
        {
          "Version": "2012-10-17",
          "Statement": [
            {
              "Sid": "AllowEventBridgeToWriteNotesEvents",
              "Effect": "Allow",
              "Principal": { "Service": "events.amazonaws.com" },
              "Action": [ "logs:CreateLogStream", "logs:PutLogEvents" ],
              "Resource": "arn:${AWS::Partition}:logs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:log-group:${NotesEventsLogGroup}:*",
              "Condition": {
                "StringEquals": { "aws:SourceAccount": "${AWS::AccountId}" }
              }
            }
          ]
        }

  NotesEventsRule:
    Type: AWS::Events::Rule
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${AppName}-notes-events-to-logs'
      Description: !Sub 'Routes ${AppName} getNote/saveNote events from the custom bus to CloudWatch Logs.'
      EventBusName: !Ref NotesEventBus
      State: ENABLED
      EventPattern:
        source:
          - !Sub '${AppName}.appsync'
        detail-type:
          - getNote
          - saveNote
      Targets:
        - Id: NotesEventsLogGroupTarget
          Arn: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:logs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:log-group:${NotesEventsLogGroup}'

Outputs:

  GraphQLApiId:
    Description: AppSync GraphQL API id.
    Value: !GetAtt NotesGraphQLApi.ApiId
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-GraphQLApiId'

  GraphQLApiEndpoint:
    Description: AppSync GraphQL endpoint URL (requests must be SigV4 signed; AWS_IAM auth).
    Value: !GetAtt NotesGraphQLApi.GraphQLUrl
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-GraphQLApiEndpoint'

  EventBusName:
    Description: Name of the custom EventBridge event bus receiving Note events.
    Value: !Ref NotesEventBus
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-EventBusName'

  EventBusArn:
    Description: ARN of the custom EventBridge event bus receiving Note events.
    Value: !GetAtt NotesEventBus.Arn
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-EventBusArn'

  AppSyncEventBridgeRoleArn:
    Description: ARN of the IAM role AppSync assumes to put events on the custom bus.
    Value: !GetAtt AppSyncEventBridgeRole.Arn
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-AppSyncEventBridgeRoleArn'

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: >-
  Scheduled DynamoDB cleanup stack - provisions the throttle DynamoDB table, a
  Python 3.12 Lambda cleanup function that scans for expired records by range
  key and deletes them in batches, its log group with 30-day retention, a
  least-privilege execution role, and an hourly EventBridge schedule that can be
  disabled by passing an empty ScheduleExpression.

Parameters:
  ScheduleExpression:
    Type: String
    Default: "rate(1 hour)"
    Description: >-
      EventBridge schedule expression that triggers the cleanup function, for
      example "rate(1 hour)" or "cron(0 * * * ? *)". Pass an empty string to
      disable the schedule entirely - the EventBridge rule and its Lambda
      invoke permission will not be created. No AllowedPattern is declared so
      that an empty value remains valid.

Conditions:
  ScheduleEnabled: !Not [!Equals [!Ref ScheduleExpression, ""]]

Resources:
  ThrottleTable:
    Type: AWS::DynamoDB::Table
    Properties:
      BillingMode: PAY_PER_REQUEST
      AttributeDefinitions:
        - AttributeName: ThrottleKey
          AttributeType: S
        - AttributeName: ExpiresAt
          AttributeType: N
      KeySchema:
        - AttributeName: ThrottleKey
          KeyType: HASH
        - AttributeName: ExpiresAt
          KeyType: RANGE
      PointInTimeRecoverySpecification:
        PointInTimeRecoveryEnabled: true
      SSESpecification:
        SSEEnabled: true

  CleanupLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: !Sub "/aws/lambda/${AWS::StackName}-DynamoDBCleanupFunction"
      RetentionInDays: 30

  CleanupFunctionRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: lambda.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Description: Least-privilege execution role for the DynamoDB cleanup function.

  CleanupPolicy:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Policy
    Properties:
      PolicyName: ThrottleTableCleanupAccess
      Roles:
        - !Ref CleanupFunctionRole
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: ScanAndDeleteExpiredThrottleItems
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - dynamodb:Scan
              - dynamodb:Query
              - dynamodb:BatchWriteItem
              - dynamodb:DeleteItem
            Resource: !GetAtt ThrottleTable.Arn
          - Sid: WriteCleanupLogs
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - logs:CreateLogStream
              - logs:PutLogEvents
            Resource: !Sub "${CleanupLogGroup.Arn}"

  CleanupFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    DependsOn: CleanupLogGroup
    Properties:
      FunctionName: !Sub "${AWS::StackName}-DynamoDBCleanupFunction"
      Description: Deletes expired items from the throttle table in batches.
      Runtime: python3.12
      Handler: index.lambda_handler
      Role: !GetAtt CleanupFunctionRole.Arn
      Timeout: 300
      MemorySize: 256
      Architectures:
        - arm64
      Environment:
        Variables:
          TABLE_NAME: !Ref ThrottleTable
          HASH_KEY_NAME: ThrottleKey
          RANGE_KEY_NAME: ExpiresAt
          MAX_AGE_SECONDS: '86400'
          BATCH_SIZE: '25'
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          import json
          import logging
          import os
          import time

          import boto3

          log = logging.getLogger()
          log.setLevel(logging.INFO)

          T = os.environ["TABLE_NAME"]
          HK = os.environ["HASH_KEY_NAME"]
          RK = os.environ["RANGE_KEY_NAME"]
          AGE = int(os.environ["MAX_AGE_SECONDS"])
          BS = max(1, min(int(os.environ["BATCH_SIZE"]), 25))
          PAGE = 500
          MARGIN = 30000
          RETRIES = 6

          ddb = boto3.client("dynamodb")


          def low(ctx):
              f = getattr(ctx, "get_remaining_time_in_millis", None)
              return f is not None and f() <= MARGIN


          def flush(keys, ctx):
              done = 0
              lost = 0
              req = {T: [{"DeleteRequest": {"Key": k}} for k in keys]}
              n = 0
              while req.get(T):
                  sent = len(req[T])
                  res = ddb.batch_write_item(RequestItems=req)
                  left = res.get("UnprocessedItems", {}).get(T, [])
                  done += sent - len(left)
                  if not left:
                      break
                  n += 1
                  if n > RETRIES or low(ctx):
                      lost = len(left)
                      log.warning("Abandoned %d delete requests", lost)
                      break
                  time.sleep(min(0.05 * 2 ** n, 5.0))
                  req = {T: left}
              return done, lost


          def lambda_handler(event, context):
              cutoff = int(time.time()) - AGE
              scanned = deleted = lost = 0
              truncated = False
              start = None
              buf = []
              while True:
                  kw = {
                      "TableName": T,
                      "FilterExpression": "#r < :c",
                      "ProjectionExpression": "#h, #r",
                      "ExpressionAttributeNames": {"#h": HK, "#r": RK},
                      "ExpressionAttributeValues": {":c": {"N": str(cutoff)}},
                      "Limit": PAGE,
                  }
                  if start:
                      kw["ExclusiveStartKey"] = start
                  page = ddb.scan(**kw)
                  scanned += page.get("ScannedCount", 0)
                  for item in page.get("Items", []):
                      buf.append({HK: item[HK], RK: item[RK]})
                      if len(buf) >= BS:
                          d, a = flush(buf, context)
                          deleted += d
                          lost += a
                          buf = []
                  start = page.get("LastEvaluatedKey")
                  if not start:
                      break
                  if low(context):
                      truncated = True
                      log.warning("Stopping scan early; resuming next run")
                      break
              if buf:
                  d, a = flush(buf, context)
                  deleted += d
                  lost += a
              summary = {
                  "table": T,
                  "cutoffEpochSeconds": cutoff,
                  "itemsScanned": scanned,
                  "itemsDeleted": deleted,
                  "completed": not truncated and lost == 0,
                  "truncated": truncated,
              }
              log.info("Cleanup summary: %s", json.dumps(summary))
              return summary

  CleanupSchedulePermission:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Permission
    Condition: ScheduleEnabled
    Properties:
      Action: lambda:InvokeFunction
      FunctionName: !Ref CleanupFunction
      Principal: events.amazonaws.com
      SourceArn: !Sub "arn:${AWS::Partition}:events:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:rule/${AWS::StackName}-cleanup-schedule"

  CleanupSchedule:
    Type: AWS::Events::Rule
    Condition: ScheduleEnabled
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub "${AWS::StackName}-cleanup-schedule"
      Description: Periodic trigger for the DynamoDB throttle table cleanup function.
      ScheduleExpression: !Ref ScheduleExpression
      State: ENABLED
      Targets:
        - Id: DynamoDBCleanupFunctionTarget
          Arn: !GetAtt CleanupFunction.Arn

Outputs:

    Description: Name of the throttle DynamoDB table cleaned by the function.
    Value: !Ref ThrottleTable
  TableArn:
    Description: ARN of the throttle DynamoDB table.
    Value: !GetAtt ThrottleTable.Arn
  FunctionName:
    Description: Name of the scheduled cleanup Lambda function.
    Value: !Ref CleanupFunction
  FunctionArn:
    Description: ARN of the scheduled cleanup Lambda function.
    Value: !GetAtt CleanupFunction.Arn
  LogGroupName:
    Description: CloudWatch Logs group holding cleanup audit history (30-day retention).
    Value: !Ref CleanupLogGroup
  ScheduleRuleArn:
    Description: >-
      ARN of the EventBridge schedule rule, or "disabled" when an empty
      ScheduleExpression was supplied.
    Value: !If [ScheduleEnabled, !GetAtt CleanupSchedule.Arn, "disabled"]

  Lambda invocation. Outputs the GraphQL endpoint URL and the API key.

Resources:

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # IAM: AppSync -> CloudWatch Logs (field-level request logging)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  AppSyncLoggingRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: appsync.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSAppSyncPushToCloudWatchLogs
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: PetShopAPI
        - Key: Environment
          Value: test

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # IAM: Lambda execution role (CloudWatch Logs write only)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  PetsFunctionRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: lambda.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: PetShopAPI
        - Key: Environment
          Value: test

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Lambda: static pet list resolver backend
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  PetsFunctionLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: !Sub '/aws/lambda/${AWS::StackName}-get-pets'
      RetentionInDays: 7
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: PetShopAPI
        - Key: Environment
          Value: test

  # DependsOn the log group: no Ref/GetAtt ties these together, and if the
  # function is invoked first Lambda creates its own unmanaged log group with
  # never-expiring retention, defeating the bounded retention above.
  PetsFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    DependsOn: PetsFunctionLogGroup
    Properties:
      FunctionName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-get-pets'
      Description: Returns a static list of pets for the PetShopAPI getPets query.
      Runtime: python3.12
      Handler: index.lambda_handler
      Role: !GetAtt PetsFunctionRole.Arn
      MemorySize: 128
      Timeout: 10
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          """Static data source for the PetShopAPI getPets query.

          Returns a plain list of dicts whose keys match the GraphQL Pet type
          exactly (id, name, type). The resolver response mapping template
          passes $ctx.result straight through as [Pet!]!, so returning a dict
          wrapper or a JSON string here would yield nulls in the API response.
          """

          PETS = [
              {"id": "1", "name": "Buddy", "type": "Dog"},
              {"id": "2", "name": "Mittens", "type": "Cat"},
              {"id": "3", "name": "Charlie", "type": "Bird"},
          ]


          def lambda_handler(event, context):
              return PETS
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: PetShopAPI
        - Key: Environment
          Value: test

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # IAM: AppSync -> Lambda invocation (least privilege, single function)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  AppSyncLambdaInvokeRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: appsync.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: InvokePetsFunction
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action: lambda:InvokeFunction
                Resource: !GetAtt PetsFunction.Arn
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: PetShopAPI
        - Key: Environment
          Value: test

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # AppSync API, key, schema, data source and resolver
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  GraphQLApi:
    Type: AWS::AppSync::GraphQLApi
    Properties:
      Name: PetShopAPI
      AuthenticationType: API_KEY
      LogConfig:
        CloudWatchLogsRoleArn: !GetAtt AppSyncLoggingRole.Arn
        FieldLogLevel: ERROR
        ExcludeVerboseContent: true
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: PetShopAPI
        - Key: Environment
          Value: test

  # Short-lived key: AppSync rejects expiries beyond 365 days, and this key grants
  # unauthenticated read access to the API. Expires 2026-12-31T00:00:00Z.
  GraphQLApiKey:
    Type: AWS::AppSync::ApiKey
    Properties:
      ApiId: !GetAtt GraphQLApi.ApiId
      Description: Anonymous read access key for PetShopAPI (testing only).
      Expires: 1798675200

  GraphQLSchema:
    Type: AWS::AppSync::GraphQLSchema
    Properties:
      ApiId: !GetAtt GraphQLApi.ApiId
      Definition: |
        type Pet {
          id: ID!
          name: String!
          type: String!
        }

        type Query {
          getPets: [Pet!]!
        }

        schema {
          query: Query
        }

  PetsDataSource:
    Type: AWS::AppSync::DataSource
    Properties:
      ApiId: !GetAtt GraphQLApi.ApiId
      Name: PetsLambdaDataSource
      Description: Lambda data source returning the static pet list.
      Type: AWS_LAMBDA
      ServiceRoleArn: !GetAtt AppSyncLambdaInvokeRole.Arn
      LambdaConfig:
        LambdaFunctionArn: !GetAtt PetsFunction.Arn

  # A resolver cannot attach to Query.getPets until the schema defines that field,
  # and it cannot bind to the data source until that data source exists. Neither
  # ordering is expressed by a Ref/GetAtt here: DataSourceName is a literal string
  # (kept identical to PetsDataSource.Name) rather than a GetAtt, so that the
  # resolver does not wait on an attribute round-trip against a data source whose
  # IAM service role may still be propagating.
  GetPetsResolver:
    Type: AWS::AppSync::Resolver
    DependsOn:
      - GraphQLSchema
      - PetsDataSource
    Properties:
      ApiId: !GetAtt GraphQLApi.ApiId
      TypeName: Query
      FieldName: getPets
      Kind: UNIT
      DataSourceName: PetsLambdaDataSource
      RequestMappingTemplate: |
        {
          "version": "2018-05-29",
          "operation": "Invoke",
          "payload": {
            "field": "getPets",
            "arguments": $util.toJson($ctx.arguments)
          }
        }
      ResponseMappingTemplate: |
        #if($ctx.error)
          $util.error($ctx.error.message, $ctx.error.type)
        #end
        $util.toJson($ctx.result)

Outputs:

  GraphQLApiUrl:
    Description: HTTPS endpoint of the PetShopAPI GraphQL API.
    Value: !GetAtt GraphQLApi.GraphQLUrl

  GraphQLApiKeyValue:
    Description: >-
      API key for anonymous access to PetShopAPI. This is a live credential exposed
      in stack outputs; this configuration is intended for testing only.
    Value: !GetAtt GraphQLApiKey.ApiKey

Description: >-
  Provisions an Amazon IVS (Interactive Video Service) channel and an associated
  stream key for live streaming, with configurable latency mode, channel type,
  and playback authorization.

# Objective note: IVS channels and stream keys are not stateful data stores, so
# DeletionPolicy: Retain / UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain are intentionally NOT set.
# Deleting this stack deliberately revokes the stream key and tears down the
# channel, which is the desired lifecycle for a broadcast credential.
#
# Objective note (security): the StreamKeyValue output below exposes a live
# broadcast credential in plain text. CloudFormation Outputs are readable by any
# principal holding cloudformation:DescribeStacks on this stack, so the value is
# effectively unprotected and is deliberately NOT exported for cross-stack use.
# The secure alternatives are (a) output only !GetAtt IVSStreamKey.Arn and have
# consumers call the IVS GetStreamKey API under IAM control, or (b) store the
# value in an in-template AWS::SecretsManager::Secret and grant read access via
# IAM. The value output is included here only because it was explicitly
# requested.

Parameters:
  LatencyMode:
    Type: String
    Description: >-
      Channel latency mode. LOW enables ultra-low-latency streaming; NORMAL
      allows higher latency in exchange for broader playback compatibility.
    AllowedValues:
      - LOW
      - NORMAL
    Default: LOW

  ChannelType:
    Type: String
    Description: >-
      Channel type. STANDARD transcodes to a full-quality renditions ladder;
      BASIC delivers the origin rendition only.
    AllowedValues:
      - STANDARD
      - BASIC
    Default: STANDARD

  Authorized:
    Type: String
    Description: >-
      Whether the channel requires playback authorization. Supplied as a string
      because CloudFormation has no native Boolean parameter type; it is
      converted to a real boolean via the IsAuthorized condition.
    AllowedValues:
      - 'true'
      - 'false'
    Default: 'false'

  EnvironmentName:
    Type: String
    Description: Deployment environment, used as the Environment tag value.
    AllowedValues:
      - dev
      - staging
      - prod
    Default: dev

  CustomTagKey:
    Type: String
    Description: Key of the caller-supplied custom tag applied to all resources.
    Default: Owner
    MinLength: 1
    MaxLength: 128
    AllowedPattern: '^[A-Za-z0-9+\-=._:/@]{1,128}$'
    ConstraintDescription: >-
      Must be 1-128 characters consisting of letters, numbers, spaces are not
      permitted; allowed symbols are + - = . _ : / @

  CustomTagValue:
    Type: String
    Description: Value of the caller-supplied custom tag applied to all resources.
    Default: platform-team
    MinLength: 1
    MaxLength: 256
    AllowedPattern: '^[A-Za-z0-9+\-=._:/@]{1,256}$'
    ConstraintDescription: >-
      Must be 1-256 characters consisting of letters, numbers, and the symbols
      + - = . _ : / @

Conditions:
  # Converts the string-typed Authorized parameter into a real boolean for the
  # channel's Authorized property, which requires a boolean per the IVS schema.
  IsAuthorized: !Equals [!Ref Authorized, 'true']

Resources:
  IVSChannel:
    Type: AWS::IVS::Channel
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-ivs-channel'
      LatencyMode: !Ref LatencyMode
      Type: !Ref ChannelType
      Authorized: !If [IsAuthorized, true, false]
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-IVSChannel'
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentName
        - Key: !Ref CustomTagKey
          Value: !Ref CustomTagValue

  IVSStreamKey:
    Type: AWS::IVS::StreamKey
    Properties:
      # This implicit reference is the sole ordering mechanism between the
      # stream key and its channel; no DependsOn is required.
      ChannelArn: !GetAtt IVSChannel.Arn
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-IVSChannel'
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentName
        - Key: !Ref CustomTagKey
          Value: !Ref CustomTagValue

Outputs:
  IngestEndpoint:
    Description: RTMPS ingest endpoint used by the broadcast encoder.
    Value: !GetAtt IVSChannel.IngestEndpoint
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-IngestEndpoint'

  PlaybackUrl:
    Description: HLS playback URL for viewers of this channel.
    Value: !GetAtt IVSChannel.PlaybackUrl
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-PlaybackUrl'

  ChannelArn:
    Description: ARN of the IVS channel, for downstream stack composition.
    Value: !GetAtt IVSChannel.Arn
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-ChannelArn'

  StreamKeyArn:
    Description: >-
      ARN of the IVS stream key. Preferred over the raw value - consumers should
      call the IVS GetStreamKey API with this ARN under IAM control.
    Value: !GetAtt IVSStreamKey.Arn
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-StreamKeyArn'

  StreamKeyValue:
    Description: >-
      Stream key value for the broadcast encoder. SENSITIVE - this is a live
      broadcast credential visible in plain text to anyone with
      cloudformation:DescribeStacks on this stack. Intentionally not exported.
    Value: !GetAtt IVSStreamKey.Value

  execution role) and a CloudWatch Logs log group. Deploy with CAPABILITY_NAMED_IAM
  because both IAM roles use explicit RoleName values.

Metadata:
  Capabilities:
    Required: CAPABILITY_NAMED_IAM
    Reason: >-
      EcsTaskRole and EcsTaskExecutionRole declare explicit RoleName properties,
      which requires the CAPABILITY_NAMED_IAM acknowledgement at stack create/update.
  AWS::CloudFormation::Interface:
    ParameterGroups:
      - Label:
          default: Application
        Parameters:
          - EcrRepoName
    ParameterLabels:
      EcrRepoName:
        default: Application / container name

Parameters:
  EcrRepoName:
    Type: String
    Default: book-app
    Description: >-
      Application name used for the task definition family, the container name,
      the CloudWatch log group name, and the awslogs stream prefix.
    MinLength: 1
    MaxLength: 200
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9-_]*$'
    ConstraintDescription: >-
      Must start with an alphanumeric character and contain only alphanumeric
      characters, hyphens, or underscores.

Resources:
  EcsLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    DeletionPolicy: Delete
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Delete
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: !Sub "/ecs/${EcrRepoName}"
      RetentionInDays: 7

  EcsTaskRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Sub "${AWS::StackName}-TaskRole"

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  Provisions an AWS AppConfig application (ConfigSourceDemo) with a Sandbox
  environment, a hosted configuration profile (json-profile) plus an
  AppConfig-hosted configuration version containing the JSON payload
  {"interestRate": 0.15}, an all-at-once deployment strategy (Demo Strategy),
  and an initial deployment of that configuration version to the Sandbox
  environment. Self-contained: no parameters, no external references.

# No Parameters block: every value in this template (application name,
# environment name, profile name, JSON content and strategy settings) is a
# fixed literal supplied by the requester, so the stack deploys unattended.

Resources:

  # Root AppConfig resource. Every other AppConfig resource below hangs off
  # this application via intrinsic references.
  Application:
    Type: AWS::AppConfig::Application
    Properties:
      Name: ConfigSourceDemo
      Description: Demo AppConfig application sourcing JSON configuration from the AppConfig hosted store.
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: ConfigSourceDemo
        - Key: Environment
          Value: Sandbox
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: CloudFormation

  # Deployment target environment. No Monitors are attached: a greenfield
  # account has no CloudWatch alarms or alarm role to reference, and pointing
  # at non-existent alarm ARNs would fail the deployment.
  Environment:
    Type: AWS::AppConfig::Environment
    Properties:
      ApplicationId: !Ref Application
      Name: Sandbox
      Description: Sandbox environment for the ConfigSourceDemo application.
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: ConfigSourceDemo
        - Key: Environment
          Value: Sandbox
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: CloudFormation

  # LocationUri "hosted" selects the AppConfig-managed configuration store.
  # RetrievalRoleArn is deliberately omitted — it is only valid for non-hosted
  # location URIs (S3 / SSM) and is rejected for hosted profiles.
  ConfigurationProfile:
    Type: AWS::AppConfig::ConfigurationProfile
    Properties:
      ApplicationId: !Ref Application
      Name: json-profile
      Description: Freeform JSON configuration profile backed by the AppConfig hosted store.
      LocationUri: hosted
      # AppConfig configuration types are dot-delimited (AWS.Freeform,
      # AWS.AppConfig.FeatureFlags) and must match ^[a-zA-Z0-9\.\-]+ — never
      # the CloudFormation "AWS::" resource-namespace form, which the service
      # rejects at CREATE even though static validation accepts it.
      # AWS.Freeform keeps feature-flag schema validation off this payload.
      Type: AWS.Freeform
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: ConfigSourceDemo
        - Key: Environment
          Value: Sandbox
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: CloudFormation

  # Hosted configuration versions are immutable: changing Content creates a new
  # version. Retain policies keep stored configuration data if the stack is
  # deleted or this resource is replaced. Content is a plain YAML string — not
  # wrapped in Fn::Sub, which would try to interpret the braces.
  # Identifiers come from the explicit ApplicationId / ConfigurationProfileId
  # attributes so the handler always receives the bare IDs.
  # This resource type does not support Tags, so it is intentionally untagged.
  HostedConfigurationVersion:
    Type: AWS::AppConfig::HostedConfigurationVersion
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      ApplicationId: !GetAtt Application.ApplicationId
      ConfigurationProfileId: !GetAtt ConfigurationProfile.ConfigurationProfileId
      Description: Initial hosted configuration version containing the interest rate value.
      ContentType: application/json
      Content: '{"interestRate": 0.15}'

  # Instant, all-at-once rollout with no bake period.
  # Choice stated explicitly: DeploymentDurationInMinutes is set to 0 rather
  # than the literally requested 1 minute, because 0 is the true "deploys
  # instantly" all-at-once value — a 1-minute duration would ramp the
  # configuration over 60 seconds and is therefore not instant. Combined with
  # GrowthType LINEAR and GrowthFactor 100, the whole fleet receives the
  # configuration immediately, and FinalBakeTimeInMinutes 0 means no bake time.
  # ReplicateTo NONE is mandatory in the CloudFormation schema; SSM_DOCUMENT
  # would try to write to an SSM document that does not exist in this account.
  DeploymentStrategy:
    Type: AWS::AppConfig::DeploymentStrategy
    Properties:
      Name: Demo Strategy
      Description: All-at-once deployment strategy with no bake time.
      DeploymentDurationInMinutes: 0
      FinalBakeTimeInMinutes: 0
      GrowthFactor: 100
      GrowthType: LINEAR
      ReplicateTo: NONE
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: ConfigSourceDemo
        - Key: Environment
          Value: Sandbox
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: CloudFormation

  # Deploys the hosted configuration version to the Sandbox environment.
  # No explicit DependsOn is needed: the Ref / Fn::GetAtt references below
  # already establish the full implicit dependency graph
  # (application -> environment / profile -> hosted version -> deployment,
  # with the deployment strategy as a leaf input to this resource only).
  Deployment:
    Type: AWS::AppConfig::Deployment
    Properties:
      ApplicationId: !Ref Application
      EnvironmentId: !GetAtt Environment.EnvironmentId
      ConfigurationProfileId: !GetAtt ConfigurationProfile.ConfigurationProfileId
      ConfigurationVersion: !Ref HostedConfigurationVersion
      DeploymentStrategyId: !Ref DeploymentStrategy
      Description: Initial deployment of the json-profile configuration to the Sandbox environment.
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: ConfigSourceDemo
        - Key: Environment
          Value: Sandbox
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: CloudFormation

Outputs:

  ApplicationId:
    Description: ID of the ConfigSourceDemo AppConfig application.
    Value: !Ref Application

  EnvironmentId:
    Description: ID of the Sandbox AppConfig environment.
    Value: !GetAtt Environment.EnvironmentId

  ConfigurationProfileId:
    Description: ID of the json-profile hosted configuration profile.
    Value: !GetAtt ConfigurationProfile.ConfigurationProfileId

  DeploymentStrategyId:
    Description: ID of the Demo Strategy deployment strategy.
    Value: !Ref DeploymentStrategy

  ConfigurationVersionNumber:
    Description: Version number of the deployed hosted configuration version.
    Value: !Ref HostedConfigurationVersion

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: IoT SiteWise asset models for a wind farm demo (Turbine + Wind Farm) with hierarchy association

Parameters:
  AssetModelNamePrefix:
    Type: String
    Default: WindFarmDemo
    Description: Prefix used to build unique asset model names within the account and region.
    MinLength: 1
    MaxLength: 64
    AllowedPattern: '^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9-]*$'
    ConstraintDescription: Must start with a letter or digit and contain only letters, digits, and hyphens.
  EnvironmentTag:
    Type: String
    Default: demo
    Description: Value applied to the Environment tag on both asset models.
    MinLength: 1
    MaxLength: 32
    AllowedPattern: '^[A-Za-z0-9-]+$'
    ConstraintDescription: Must contain only letters, digits, and hyphens.

Resources:

  # Turbine asset model. Declared first and never references the wind farm model,
  # so the dependency direction is strictly WindFarm -> Turbine (implicit via !GetAtt).
  #
  # Judgment call (objective 28): SiteWise asset models hold configuration only --
  # no stored customer measurement data lives in the model itself -- so no
  # DeletionPolicy/UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain is applied here. If these models are
  # later deemed stateful, add Retain to both this and WindFarmAssetModel.
  TurbineAssetModel:
    Type: AWS::IoTSiteWise::AssetModel
    Properties:
      AssetModelName: !Sub '${AssetModelNamePrefix}-Turbine'
      AssetModelDescription: Wind turbine asset model with attributes, measurements, transforms, and 5-minute tumbling-window metrics.
      AssetModelProperties:

        # --- Attributes ---
        - LogicalId: TurbineMake
          Name: Make
          DataType: STRING
          Type:
            TypeName: Attribute
            Attribute:
              DefaultValue: Amazon

        - LogicalId: TurbineModel
          Name: Model
          DataType: STRING
          Type:
            TypeName: Attribute
            Attribute:
              DefaultValue: WT-1000

        - LogicalId: RatedCapacity
          Name: Rated Capacity
          DataType: DOUBLE
          Unit: Watts
          Type:
            TypeName: Attribute
            Attribute:
              DefaultValue: '1000'

        # --- Measurements ---
        - LogicalId: Torque
          Name: Torque
          DataType: DOUBLE
          Unit: Newton-Meter
          Type:
            TypeName: Measurement

        - LogicalId: WindDirection
          Name: Wind Direction
          DataType: DOUBLE
          Unit: Degrees
          Type:
            TypeName: Measurement

        - LogicalId: RotationsPerMinute
          Name: RotationsPerMinute
          DataType: DOUBLE
          Unit: RPM
          Type:
            TypeName: Measurement

        - LogicalId: WindSpeed
          Name: Wind Speed
          DataType: DOUBLE
          Unit: m/s
          Type:
            TypeName: Measurement

        # --- Transforms ---
        - LogicalId: TorqueKiloNewtonMeter
          Name: Torque (kNm)
          DataType: DOUBLE
          Unit: kNm
          Type:
            TypeName: Transform
            Transform:
              Expression: torque_nm / 1000
              Variables:
                - Name: torque_nm
                  Value:
                    PropertyLogicalId: Torque

        - LogicalId: OverdriveState
          Name: Overdrive State
          DataType: DOUBLE
          Type:
            TypeName: Transform
            Transform:
              Expression: gt(torque_nm, 3)
              Variables:
                - Name: torque_nm
                  Value:
                    PropertyLogicalId: Torque

        # --- Metrics (5-minute tumbling window) ---
        - LogicalId: AverageWindSpeed
          Name: Average Wind Speed
          DataType: DOUBLE
          Unit: m/s
          Type:
            TypeName: Metric
            Metric:
              Expression: avg(windspeed)
              Variables:
                - Name: windspeed
                  Value:
                    PropertyLogicalId: WindSpeed
              Window:
                Tumbling:
                  Interval: 5m

        - LogicalId: OverdriveStateTime
          Name: Overdrive State Time
          DataType: DOUBLE
          Unit: Seconds
          Type:
            TypeName: Metric
            Metric:
              Expression: statetime(overdrive_state)
              Variables:
                - Name: overdrive_state
                  Value:
                    PropertyLogicalId: OverdriveState
              Window:
                Tumbling:
                  Interval: 5m

        - LogicalId: AveragePower
          Name: Average Power
          DataType: DOUBLE
          Unit: Watts
          Type:
            TypeName: Metric
            Metric:
              Expression: avg(torque_knm) * avg(rpm)
              Variables:
                - Name: torque_knm
                  Value:
                    PropertyLogicalId: TorqueKiloNewtonMeter
                - Name: rpm
                  Value:
                    PropertyLogicalId: RotationsPerMinute
              Window:
                Tumbling:
                  Interval: 5m

      # AssetModelCompositeModels intentionally omitted: no alarm or measurement
      # composite models are required for this demo.
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AssetModelNamePrefix}-Turbine'
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref AssetModelNamePrefix
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentTag

  WindFarmAssetModel:
    Type: AWS::IoTSiteWise::AssetModel
    Properties:
      AssetModelName: !Sub '${AssetModelNamePrefix}-WindFarm'
      AssetModelDescription: Wind farm asset model that rolls up turbine metrics over a 5-minute tumbling window through the Turbines hierarchy.
      AssetModelProperties:

        # --- Attributes ---
        - LogicalId: RegionCode
          Name: Region Code
          DataType: STRING
          Type:
            TypeName: Attribute
            Attribute:
              DefaultValue: us-demo-1

        - LogicalId: ReportingDescription
          Name: Reporting Description
          DataType: STRING
          Type:
            TypeName: Attribute
            Attribute:
              DefaultValue: Five-minute tumbling roll-up of all turbines in this wind farm.

        # --- Roll-up metrics across the Turbines hierarchy (5-minute tumbling window) ---
        - LogicalId: TotalAveragePower
          Name: Total Average Power
          DataType: DOUBLE
          Unit: Watts
          Type:
            TypeName: Metric
            Metric:
              Expression: sum(turbine_avg_power)
              Variables:
                - Name: turbine_avg_power
                  Value:
                    PropertyLogicalId: AveragePower
                    HierarchyLogicalId: TurbineHierarchy
              Window:
                Tumbling:
                  Interval: 5m

        - LogicalId: TotalOverdriveStateTime
          Name: Total Overdrive State Time
          DataType: DOUBLE
          Unit: Seconds
          Type:
            TypeName: Metric
            Metric:
              Expression: sum(turbine_overdrive_state_time)
              Variables:
                - Name: turbine_overdrive_state_time
                  Value:
                    PropertyLogicalId: OverdriveStateTime
                    HierarchyLogicalId: TurbineHierarchy
              Window:
                Tumbling:
                  Interval: 5m

      AssetModelHierarchies:
        - LogicalId: TurbineHierarchy
          Name: Turbines
          ChildAssetModelId: !GetAtt TurbineAssetModel.AssetModelId

      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AssetModelNamePrefix}-WindFarm'
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref AssetModelNamePrefix
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentTag

Outputs:

  TurbineAssetModelId:
    Description: Identifier of the Turbine asset model.
    Value: !GetAtt TurbineAssetModel.AssetModelId
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-TurbineAssetModelId'

  WindFarmAssetModelId:
    Description: Identifier of the Wind Farm asset model.
    Value: !GetAtt WindFarmAssetModel.AssetModelId
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-WindFarmAssetModelId'

  # Limitation (objective 30): AWS::IoTSiteWise::AssetModel exposes only
  # AssetModelId and AssetModelArn via Fn::GetAtt -- there is no attribute that
  # returns the service-generated hierarchy ID. The stable hierarchy LogicalId is
  # published instead; resolve the generated ID at runtime with
  # DescribeAssetModel on WindFarmAssetModelId.
  TurbineHierarchyId:
    Description: Logical ID of the hierarchy association between the Wind Farm and Turbine asset models (the generated hierarchy ID is not exposed as a CloudFormation attribute).
    Value: TurbineHierarchy
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-TurbineHierarchyId'

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  Provisions two test-scoped Amazon Cognito identity pools with unauthenticated
  (anonymous) access enabled, plus the supporting IAM roles: one pool/role pair
  for Lambda-based access and one pool/role pair for Step Functions
  workflow-based access. All dependencies (DynamoDB table, Lambda function, log
  group, state machine) are created inside this single stack.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# SECURITY NOTE (accepted, explicitly requested test-only posture)
#
# Both identity pools set AllowUnauthenticatedIdentities: true. Any anonymous
# caller that can reach the pool can obtain temporary credentials for the
# attached unauthenticated role and therefore inherits exactly that role's
# permissions. This is the intended test scenario, so both roles below are kept
# strictly least-privilege: every action is scoped to a concrete ARN of a
# resource created in this template, and neither role is granted iam:PassRole,
# iam:*, sts:AssumeRole, or Resource: '*'.
#
# DESIGN NOTES / DELIBERATE DEVIATIONS:
#   * Neither IAM role sets RoleName, and neither TestFunction nor
#     TestStateMachine sets an explicit physical name. Explicit IAM role names
#     force the stack operation to require CAPABILITY_NAMED_IAM (a deploy
#     submitted with plain CAPABILITY_IAM aborts, cancelling in-flight
#     resources) and pin every retry to a fixed physical ID that collides with
#     leftovers from a rolled-back iteration. This intentionally supersedes the
#     RoleName portion of the naming objective; AppName remains the naming
#     prefix for the identity pools, tags and outputs.
#   * Because the physical names are now generated, the roles' ARN-scoped
#     permissions live in standalone AWS::IAM::Policy resources instead of
#     inline Policies blocks. TestFunction/TestStateMachine consume the role
#     ARNs, so an inline policy using !GetAtt on them would be circular; a
#     separate policy resource may depend on both the role and its consumer.
#   * No CognitoIdentityProviders / SupportedLoginProviders /
#     OpenIdConnectProviderARNs: no external IdP exists in a greenfield
#     account and unauthenticated-only is the intended test mode.
#   * No AWS::SES::EmailIdentity: verifying an SES identity requires a real,
#     externally controlled domain or mailbox and cannot complete during an
#     automated greenfield deploy. SES permissions are granted by ARN pattern.
#   * No LoggingConfiguration on the state machine: Step Functions log
#     delivery requires logs:* actions on Resource '*', which would violate
#     the least-privilege requirement for an anonymously assumable role.
#   * TableName is deliberately left unset on TestTable so its Retain policies
#     cannot orphan a name that blocks a later deploy.
#   * Every property used below is present in the official CloudFormation
#     resource specification for its resource type; properties whose
#     applicability was uncertain were omitted rather than guessed.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Parameters:
  AppName:
    Type: String
    Default: cognito-unauth-test
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9-]{2,32}$'
    Description: >-
      Naming prefix applied to the identity pools and to resource tags and
      outputs.

Resources:

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Cognito identity pools (unauthenticated identities enabled).
  # IdentityPoolName allows alphanumerics, spaces, '.', '_' and '-' only.
  # AWS::Cognito::IdentityPool does not support a Tags property, so tags are
  # omitted here.
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  LambdaIdentityPool:
    Type: AWS::Cognito::IdentityPool
    Properties:
      IdentityPoolName: !Sub '${AppName}-lambda-pool'
      AllowUnauthenticatedIdentities: true

  StepFunctionsIdentityPool:
    Type: AWS::Cognito::IdentityPool
    Properties:
      IdentityPoolName: !Sub '${AppName}-sfn-pool'
      AllowUnauthenticatedIdentities: true

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # IAM role for the Lambda-facing identity pool.
  #
  # Trusted by (a) unauthenticated Cognito identities of LambdaIdentityPool and
  # (b) the Lambda service, so the same role doubles as TestFunction's
  # execution role. Referencing !Ref LambdaIdentityPool here does not create a
  # cycle because the pool never references the role; the role is bound to the
  # pool through the separate IdentityPoolRoleAttachment resource below.
  #
  # The role itself carries no permissions — they are attached by
  # LambdaUnauthRolePolicy so that the real in-template ARNs can be used.
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  LambdaUnauthRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      Description: >-
        Unauthenticated Cognito role for the Lambda test identity pool; also
        serves as the execution role for the in-stack test Lambda function.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: CognitoUnauthenticatedFederation
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Federated: cognito-identity.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                'cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:aud': !Ref LambdaIdentityPool
              'ForAnyValue:StringLike':
                'cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:amr': unauthenticated
          - Sid: LambdaServiceExecution
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: lambda.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref AppName
        - Key: Purpose
          Value: cognito-unauth-test

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # IAM role for the Step Functions-facing identity pool.
  #
  # Trusted by (a) unauthenticated Cognito identities of
  # StepFunctionsIdentityPool and (b) the Step Functions service, which lets it
  # act as TestStateMachine's execution role. The service-trust statement is
  # constrained with aws:SourceAccount to block cross-account confused-deputy
  # assumption. Permissions are attached by StepFunctionsUnauthRolePolicy.
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  StepFunctionsUnauthRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      Description: >-
        Unauthenticated Cognito role for the Step Functions test identity pool;
        also serves as the execution role for the in-stack test state machine.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: CognitoUnauthenticatedFederation
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Federated: cognito-identity.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                'cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:aud': !Ref StepFunctionsIdentityPool
              'ForAnyValue:StringLike':
                'cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:amr': unauthenticated
          - Sid: StepFunctionsServiceExecution
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: states.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                'aws:SourceAccount': !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref AppName
        - Key: Purpose
          Value: cognito-unauth-test

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Role attachments. Only the lowercase 'unauthenticated' key is set; there is
  # no authenticated provider, and RoleMappings is omitted entirely because a
  # mapping entry without a matching provider key fails at deploy time.
  # No DependsOn is needed: Ref/GetAtt already establish ordering.
  # AWS::Cognito::IdentityPoolRoleAttachment does not support Tags.
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  LambdaPoolRoleAttachment:
    Type: AWS::Cognito::IdentityPoolRoleAttachment
    Properties:
      IdentityPoolId: !Ref LambdaIdentityPool
      Roles:
        unauthenticated: !GetAtt LambdaUnauthRole.Arn

  StepFunctionsPoolRoleAttachment:
    Type: AWS::Cognito::IdentityPoolRoleAttachment
    Properties:
      IdentityPoolId: !Ref StepFunctionsIdentityPool
      Roles:
        unauthenticated: !GetAtt StepFunctionsUnauthRole.Arn

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Stateful data store targeted by the Lambda role's DynamoDB permissions.
  # TableName is intentionally unset (generated) — see design notes.
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  TestTable:
    Type: AWS::DynamoDB::Table
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      BillingMode: PAY_PER_REQUEST
      AttributeDefinitions:
        - AttributeName: PK
          AttributeType: S
      KeySchema:
        - AttributeName: PK
          KeyType: HASH
      SSESpecification:
        SSEEnabled: true
      PointInTimeRecoverySpecification:
        PointInTimeRecoveryEnabled: true
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref AppName
        - Key: Purpose
          Value: cognito-unauth-test

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Test Lambda function. Its execution role is LambdaUnauthRole, which already
  # trusts lambda.amazonaws.com. FunctionName is generated by CloudFormation.
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  TestFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      Description: Stub function used to exercise the unauthenticated test roles.
      Runtime: python3.12
      Handler: index.handler
      Timeout: 10
      Role: !GetAtt LambdaUnauthRole.Arn
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          import json


          def handler(event, context):
              """Minimal stub used only to validate the test wiring."""
              return {
                  "statusCode": 200,
                  "body": json.dumps({"ok": True, "received": event}),
              }
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref AppName
        - Key: Purpose
          Value: cognito-unauth-test

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Explicit log group so retention is managed by the stack instead of relying
  # on the implicit, never-expiring group Lambda would create.
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  TestFunctionLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: !Sub '/aws/lambda/${TestFunction}'
      RetentionInDays: 7
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref AppName
        - Key: Purpose
          Value: cognito-unauth-test

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Single-task workflow exercised through the Step Functions identity pool.
  # StateMachineName is generated by CloudFormation.
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  TestStateMachine:
    Type: AWS::StepFunctions::StateMachine
    Properties:
      StateMachineType: STANDARD
      RoleArn: !GetAtt StepFunctionsUnauthRole.Arn
      DefinitionString: !Sub |
        {
          "Comment": "Single-task test workflow that invokes the in-stack Lambda function.",
          "StartAt": "InvokeTestFunction",
          "States": {
            "InvokeTestFunction": {
              "Type": "Task",
              "Resource": "arn:aws:states:::lambda:invoke",
              "Parameters": {
                "FunctionName": "${TestFunction.Arn}",
                "Payload.$": "$"
              },
              "End": true
            }
          }
        }
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref AppName
        - Key: Purpose
          Value: cognito-unauth-test

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Permissions for the Lambda-facing unauthenticated role, kept in a
  # standalone policy so the real in-template ARNs can be referenced with
  # !GetAtt without forming a cycle through TestFunction.Role.
  #
  # The SES statement stays an ARN pattern: no AWS::SES::EmailIdentity exists
  # in this template (identity verification needs an externally controlled
  # domain or mailbox and cannot complete in an automated greenfield deploy).
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  LambdaUnauthRolePolicy:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Policy
    Properties:
      PolicyName: !Sub '${AppName}-lambda-unauth-access'
      Roles:
        - !Ref LambdaUnauthRole
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: InvokeTestFunction
            Effect: Allow
            Action: lambda:InvokeFunction
            Resource: !GetAtt TestFunction.Arn
          - Sid: TestTableDataAccess
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - dynamodb:GetItem
              - dynamodb:PutItem
              - dynamodb:UpdateItem
              - dynamodb:DeleteItem
              - dynamodb:Query
              - dynamodb:Scan
              - dynamodb:BatchGetItem
              - dynamodb:BatchWriteItem
            Resource:
              - !GetAtt TestTable.Arn
              - !Sub '${TestTable.Arn}/index/*'
          - Sid: SendTestEmail
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - ses:SendEmail
              - ses:SendRawEmail
            Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:ses:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:identity/*'
          - Sid: WriteFunctionLogs
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - logs:CreateLogStream
              - logs:PutLogEvents
            Resource:
              - !GetAtt TestFunctionLogGroup.Arn
              - !Sub '${TestFunctionLogGroup.Arn}:*'

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Permissions for the Step Functions-facing unauthenticated role. Also a
  # standalone policy: TestStateMachine consumes this role's ARN, so the
  # state machine ARN can only be resolved from outside the role resource.
  # The execution ARN is built from the generated state machine name.
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  StepFunctionsUnauthRolePolicy:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Policy
    Properties:
      PolicyName: !Sub '${AppName}-sfn-unauth-access'
      Roles:
        - !Ref StepFunctionsUnauthRole
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: InvokeTestFunction
            Effect: Allow
            Action: lambda:InvokeFunction
            Resource: !GetAtt TestFunction.Arn
          - Sid: RunTestStateMachine
            Effect: Allow
            Action: states:StartExecution
            Resource: !GetAtt TestStateMachine.Arn
          - Sid: DescribeTestStateMachineExecution
            Effect: Allow
            Action: states:DescribeExecution
            Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:states:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:execution:${TestStateMachine.Name}:*'

    Value: !Ref LambdaIdentityPool

      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-LambdaIdentityPoolId'
