final_template:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  PCI Conformance Pack SSM Automation remediation document set - creates the
  prerequisite IAM automation assume role plus four custom AWS Systems Manager
  Automation documents used as RemediationConfiguration targets by AWS Config
  PCI-DSS conformance packs (restrict VPC default security group, delete unused
  security group, release unassociated Elastic IP, set Auto Scaling group health
  check to ELB with a 300 second grace period).
  NOTE: No stateful data resources (RDS, DynamoDB, S3 with data, EFS) are
  created by this template, so DeletionPolicy / UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain is
  intentionally omitted rather than overlooked. Likewise, no VPC, subnet,
  security group, Elastic IP or Auto Scaling group is created here - the
  documents act on resources discovered at remediation time via runtime inputs.

Parameters:

  RoleNamePrefix:
    Type: String
    Default: pciautomationassumerole
    Description: >-
      Prefix for the SSM Automation assume role name. The region is appended by
      the template so the role name is unique per region.
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-zA-Z0-9+=,.@_-]{1,48}$'
    ConstraintDescription: >-
      Must contain only alphanumeric characters and the characters +=,.@_- and
      be between 1 and 48 characters long.

Resources:

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Prerequisite IAM role assumed by SSM Automation when executing the
  # remediation documents below. EventBridge (Events) and EC2 are included as
  # trusted principals so the same role can be used for event driven and
  # instance driven invocation of the same documents.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  AutomationRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Sub '${RoleNamePrefix}-${AWS::Region}'
      Description: >-
        Assume role used by custom SSM Automation documents that perform PCI DSS
        conformance pack remediations.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllowAutomationServicesToAssumeRole
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service:
                - ssm.amazonaws.com
                - ec2.amazonaws.com
                - events.amazonaws.com
            Action: 'sts:AssumeRole'
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        # Static AWS managed policy ARN - account independent, grants the
        # Automation execution APIs (ssm:StartAutomationExecution etc.).
        - 'arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AmazonSSMAutomationRole'
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: PciRemediationDocumentPermissions
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              # EC2 permissions required by the security group and Elastic IP
              # remediation scripts. Resource is '*' because the EC2 Describe
              # APIs (DescribeAddresses, DescribeSecurityGroups) do not support
              # resource level permissions at all, and the mutating calls target
              # security groups and Elastic IP allocations that are discovered
              # at remediation time and therefore cannot be enumerated as ARNs
              # in this template. The action list is kept to the exact minimum
              # set the scripts invoke.
              - Sid: Ec2SecurityGroupAndAddressRemediation
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - 'ec2:ReleaseAddress'
                  - 'ec2:DescribeAddresses'
                  - 'ec2:DescribeSecurityGroups'
                  - 'ec2:DeleteSecurityGroup'
                  - 'ec2:RevokeSecurityGroupIngress'
                  - 'ec2:RevokeSecurityGroupEgress'
                Resource: '*'
              # The Auto Scaling health check document calls the Auto Scaling
              # API rather than EC2, so those two actions are granted
              # separately and nothing more. DescribeAutoScalingGroups does not
              # support resource level permissions, and the target group is
              # supplied at remediation time, hence Resource '*'.
              - Sid: AutoScalingHealthCheckRemediation
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - 'autoscaling:UpdateAutoScalingGroup'
                  - 'autoscaling:DescribeAutoScalingGroups'
                Resource: '*'
              # Automation execution logging, scoped to this account, this
              # region and the SSM log group namespace only.
              - Sid: AutomationExecutionLogging
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - 'logs:CreateLogGroup'
                  - 'logs:CreateLogStream'
                  - 'logs:PutLogEvents'
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:logs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:log-group:/aws/ssm/*'
      Tags:
        - Key: Compliance
          Value: PCI-DSS
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: CloudFormation

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # PCI DSS 1.2.1 / 1.3 - the VPC default security group must restrict all
  # traffic. Revokes every ingress and egress rule on the supplied group.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  RestrictDefaultSecurityGroupDocument:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Document
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub 'PCI-RestrictVpcDefaultSecurityGroup-${AWS::Region}'
      DocumentType: Automation
      DocumentFormat: YAML
      TargetType: '/AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup'
      Tags:
        - Key: Compliance
          Value: PCI-DSS
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: CloudFormation
      Content:
        schemaVersion: '0.3'
        description: >-
          Restricts all traffic on a VPC default security group by revoking
          every ingress and egress rule. The operation is idempotent: a group
          that already has no rules is reported as compliant without error.
        assumeRole: '{{ AutomationAssumeRole }}'
        parameters:
          GroupId:
            type: String
            description: The ID of the VPC default security group to restrict.
            allowedPattern: '^sg-[a-f0-9]{8,17}$'
          AutomationAssumeRole:
            type: String
            description: >-
              ARN of the IAM role that Systems Manager Automation assumes to
              perform the remediation.
            default: !GetAtt AutomationRole.Arn
        outputs:
          - RestrictDefaultSecurityGroup.RevokedIngressRuleCount
          - RestrictDefaultSecurityGroup.RevokedEgressRuleCount
          - RestrictDefaultSecurityGroup.Status
        mainSteps:
          - name: RestrictDefaultSecurityGroup
            action: 'aws:executeScript'
            timeoutSeconds: 600
            onFailure: Abort
            isEnd: true
            description: >-
              Describes the security group, revokes all existing ingress and
              egress permissions, then re-describes the group to verify that no
              rules remain.
            inputs:
              Runtime: python3.11
              Handler: handler
              InputPayload:
                GroupId: '{{ GroupId }}'
              Script: |-
                import boto3


                def handler(events, context):
                    group_id = events['GroupId']
                    # Region intentionally not pinned: boto3 resolves it from
                    # the Automation execution environment.
                    ec2 = boto3.client('ec2')

                    groups = ec2.describe_security_groups(
                        GroupIds=[group_id]
                    ).get('SecurityGroups', [])
                    if not groups:
                        raise Exception(
                            'Security group {0} was not found.'.format(group_id)
                        )

                    group = groups[0]
                    ingress_rules = group.get('IpPermissions', [])
                    egress_rules = group.get('IpPermissionsEgress', [])

                    # Empty rule sets are tolerated so repeated remediation of
                    # an already compliant group succeeds.
                    if ingress_rules:
                        ec2.revoke_security_group_ingress(
                            GroupId=group_id,
                            IpPermissions=ingress_rules,
                        )
                    if egress_rules:
                        ec2.revoke_security_group_egress(
                            GroupId=group_id,
                            IpPermissions=egress_rules,
                        )

                    verified = ec2.describe_security_groups(
                        GroupIds=[group_id]
                    )['SecurityGroups'][0]
                    remaining_ingress = len(verified.get('IpPermissions', []))
                    remaining_egress = len(
                        verified.get('IpPermissionsEgress', [])
                    )
                    if remaining_ingress or remaining_egress:
                        raise Exception(
                            'Security group {0} still has {1} ingress and {2} '
                            'egress rules after remediation.'.format(
                                group_id, remaining_ingress, remaining_egress
                            )
                        )

                    return {
                        'RevokedIngressRuleCount': len(ingress_rules),
                        'RevokedEgressRuleCount': len(egress_rules),
                        'Status': 'Restricted',
                    }
            outputs:
              - Name: RevokedIngressRuleCount
                Selector: '$.Payload.RevokedIngressRuleCount'
                Type: Integer
              - Name: RevokedEgressRuleCount
                Selector: '$.Payload.RevokedEgressRuleCount'
                Type: Integer
              - Name: Status
                Selector: '$.Payload.Status'
                Type: String

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Deletes a security group that is no longer in use.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  DeleteUnusedSecurityGroupDocument:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Document
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub 'PCI-DeleteUnusedSecurityGroup-${AWS::Region}'
      DocumentType: Automation
      DocumentFormat: YAML
      TargetType: '/AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup'
      Tags:
        - Key: Compliance
          Value: PCI-DSS
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: CloudFormation
      Content:
        schemaVersion: '0.3'
        description: >-
          Deletes an unused security group. The group is verified to have no
          attached elastic network interfaces before deletion, and a
          DependencyViolation returned by EC2 is handled explicitly so the
          remediation fails with an actionable message instead of a raw API
          error.
        assumeRole: '{{ AutomationAssumeRole }}'
        parameters:
          GroupId:
            type: String
            description: The ID of the unused security group to delete.
            allowedPattern: '^sg-[a-f0-9]{8,17}$'
          AutomationAssumeRole:
            type: String
            description: >-
              ARN of the IAM role that Systems Manager Automation assumes to
              perform the remediation.
            default: !GetAtt AutomationRole.Arn
        outputs:
          - DeleteUnusedSecurityGroup.Status
          - DeleteUnusedSecurityGroup.GroupId
        mainSteps:
          - name: DeleteUnusedSecurityGroup
            action: 'aws:executeScript'
            timeoutSeconds: 600
            onFailure: Abort
            isEnd: true
            description: >-
              Confirms the security group exists and has no attached network
              interfaces, then deletes it.
            inputs:
              Runtime: python3.11
              Handler: handler
              InputPayload:
                GroupId: '{{ GroupId }}'
              Script: |-
                import boto3
                from botocore.exceptions import ClientError


                def attached_interface_ids(ec2, group_id):
                    """Return the ENI ids still attached to the group.

                    DescribeNetworkInterfaces is deliberately NOT granted by
                    the minimal remediation policy, so if the call is denied we
                    return None to signal 'unknown' and rely on the
                    authoritative DependencyViolation check performed by EC2
                    during deletion.
                    """
                    paginator = ec2.get_paginator('describe_network_interfaces')
                    interface_ids = []
                    try:
                        pages = paginator.paginate(
                            Filters=[
                                {'Name': 'group-id', 'Values': [group_id]}
                            ]
                        )
                        for page in pages:
                            for eni in page.get('NetworkInterfaces', []):
                                interface_ids.append(
                                    eni['NetworkInterfaceId']
                                )
                    except ClientError as error:
                        code = error.response['Error']['Code']
                        if code in ('UnauthorizedOperation', 'AccessDenied',
                                    'AccessDeniedException'):
                            return None
                        raise
                    return interface_ids


                def handler(events, context):
                    group_id = events['GroupId']
                    ec2 = boto3.client('ec2')

                    try:
                        ec2.describe_security_groups(GroupIds=[group_id])
                    except ClientError as error:
                        if error.response['Error']['Code'] == \
                                'InvalidGroup.NotFound':
                            return {
                                'GroupId': group_id,
                                'Status': 'AlreadyDeleted',
                            }
                        raise

                    interface_ids = attached_interface_ids(ec2, group_id)
                    if interface_ids:
                        raise Exception(
                            'Security group {0} is still attached to network '
                            'interfaces {1} and was not deleted.'.format(
                                group_id, ', '.join(interface_ids)
                            )
                        )

                    try:
                        ec2.delete_security_group(GroupId=group_id)
                    except ClientError as error:
                        code = error.response['Error']['Code']
                        if code == 'InvalidGroup.NotFound':
                            return {
                                'GroupId': group_id,
                                'Status': 'AlreadyDeleted',
                            }
                        if code == 'DependencyViolation':
                            raise Exception(
                                'Security group {0} cannot be deleted because '
                                'it is still in use (DependencyViolation). '
                                'Detach every network interface and remove '
                                'references from other security group rules, '
                                'then retry the remediation.'.format(group_id)
                            )
                        raise

                    return {
                        'GroupId': group_id,
                        'Status': 'Deleted',
                    }
            outputs:
              - Name: Status
                Selector: '$.Payload.Status'
                Type: String
              - Name: GroupId
                Selector: '$.Payload.GroupId'
                Type: String

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Releases an Elastic IP address that is not associated with any resource.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ReleaseUnassociatedEipDocument:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Document
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub 'PCI-ReleaseUnassociatedElasticIp-${AWS::Region}'
      DocumentType: Automation
      DocumentFormat: YAML
      TargetType: '/AWS::EC2::EIP'
      Tags:
        - Key: Compliance
          Value: PCI-DSS
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: CloudFormation
      Content:
        schemaVersion: '0.3'
        description: >-
          Releases an unassociated Elastic IP address using its allocation ID.
          The address is confirmed to have no AssociationId before it is
          released, so in-use addresses are never removed.
        assumeRole: '{{ AutomationAssumeRole }}'
        parameters:
          AllocationId:
            type: String
            description: >-
              The allocation ID of the Elastic IP address to release (not the
              public IP address).
            allowedPattern: '^eipalloc-[a-f0-9]{8,17}$'
          AutomationAssumeRole:
            type: String
            description: >-
              ARN of the IAM role that Systems Manager Automation assumes to
              perform the remediation.
            default: !GetAtt AutomationRole.Arn
        outputs:
          - ReleaseUnassociatedAddress.Status
          - ReleaseUnassociatedAddress.AllocationId
        mainSteps:
          - name: ReleaseUnassociatedAddress
            action: 'aws:executeScript'
            timeoutSeconds: 600
            onFailure: Abort
            isEnd: true
            description: >-
              Describes the Elastic IP address by allocation ID, verifies it is
              unassociated, then releases it.
            inputs:
              Runtime: python3.11
              Handler: handler
              InputPayload:
                AllocationId: '{{ AllocationId }}'
              Script: |-
                import boto3
                from botocore.exceptions import ClientError


                def handler(events, context):
                    allocation_id = events['AllocationId']
                    ec2 = boto3.client('ec2')

                    try:
                        addresses = ec2.describe_addresses(
                            AllocationIds=[allocation_id]
                        ).get('Addresses', [])
                    except ClientError as error:
                        if error.response['Error']['Code'] in (
                                'InvalidAllocationID.NotFound',
                                'InvalidAllocationId.NotFound'):
                            return {
                                'AllocationId': allocation_id,
                                'Status': 'AlreadyReleased',
                            }
                        raise

                    if not addresses:
                        return {
                            'AllocationId': allocation_id,
                            'Status': 'AlreadyReleased',
                        }

                    address = addresses[0]
                    association_id = address.get('AssociationId')
                    if association_id:
                        raise Exception(
                            'Elastic IP allocation {0} is associated with {1} '
                            'and was not released.'.format(
                                allocation_id, association_id
                            )
                        )

                    ec2.release_address(AllocationId=allocation_id)

                    return {
                        'AllocationId': allocation_id,
                        'Status': 'Released',
                    }
            outputs:
              - Name: Status
                Selector: '$.Payload.Status'
                Type: String
              - Name: AllocationId
                Selector: '$.Payload.AllocationId'
                Type: String

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Sets an Auto Scaling group health check type to ELB with a 300 second
  # grace period, then verifies both values.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  UpdateAsgHealthCheckDocument:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Document
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub 'PCI-UpdateAutoScalingGroupHealthCheck-${AWS::Region}'
      DocumentType: Automation
      DocumentFormat: YAML
      TargetType: '/AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup'
      Tags:
        - Key: Compliance
          Value: PCI-DSS
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: CloudFormation
      Content:
        schemaVersion: '0.3'
        description: >-
          Updates an Auto Scaling group to use ELB health checks with a health
          check grace period of 300 seconds, then re-describes the group to
          verify both settings were applied.
        assumeRole: '{{ AutomationAssumeRole }}'
        parameters:
          AutoScalingGroupName:
            type: String
            description: The name of the Auto Scaling group to update.
            allowedPattern: '^[a-zA-Z0-9\-_/:.+=@]{1,255}$'

              perform the remediation.

        outputs:
          - VerifyHealthCheckConfiguration.HealthCheckType
          - VerifyHealthCheckConfiguration.HealthCheckGracePeriod
        mainSteps:
          - name: UpdateHealthCheckConfiguration
            action: 'aws:executeScript'
            timeoutSeconds: 600
            onFailure: Abort
            description: >-
              Sets HealthCheckType to ELB and HealthCheckGracePeriod to 300
              seconds on the target Auto Scaling group.
            inputs:
              Runtime: python3.11
              Handler: handler
              InputPayload:
                AutoScalingGroupName: '{{ AutoScalingGroupName }}'
              Script: |-
                import boto3

                HEALTH_CHECK_TYPE = 'ELB'
                HEALTH_CHECK_GRACE_PERIOD = 300


                def handler(events, context):
                    group_name = events['AutoScalingGroupName']
                    autoscaling = boto3.client('autoscaling')

                    groups = autoscaling.describe_auto_scaling_groups(
                        AutoScalingGroupNames=[group_name]
                    ).get('AutoScalingGroups', [])

                            )
                        )

                        AutoScalingGroupName=group_name,
                        HealthCheckType=HEALTH_CHECK_TYPE,

              - Name: Status

          - name: VerifyHealthCheckConfiguration
            action: 'aws:executeScript'
            timeoutSeconds: 600
            onFailure: Abort
            isEnd: true
            description: >-
              Re-describes the Auto Scaling group and confirms the health check
              type is ELB and the grace period is 300 seconds.
            inputs:
              Runtime: python3.11
              Handler: handler
              InputPayload:
                AutoScalingGroupName: '{{ AutoScalingGroupName }}'
              Script: |-
                import boto3

                EXPECTED_HEALTH_CHECK_TYPE = 'ELB'
                EXPECTED_GRACE_PERIOD = 300


                def handler(events, context):
                    group_name = events['AutoScalingGroupName']
                    autoscaling = boto3.client('autoscaling')

                    groups = autoscaling.describe_auto_scaling_groups(
                        AutoScalingGroupNames=[group_name]
                    ).get('AutoScalingGroups', [])

                        raise Exception(
                            'Auto Scaling group {0} was not found during '
                            'verification.'.format(group_name)
                        )

                    group = groups[0]
                    health_check_type = group.get('HealthCheckType')
                    grace_period = group.get('HealthCheckGracePeriod')

                        raise Exception(
                            'Auto Scaling group {0} health check type is {1}, '
                            'expected {2}.'.format(
                                group_name,
                                health_check_type,

                            )

                            'Auto Scaling group {0} health check grace period '
                            'is {1}, expected {2}.'.format(
                                group_name,
                                grace_period,
                                EXPECTED_GRACE_PERIOD,
                            )
                        )

                    return {
                        'AutoScalingGroupName': group_name,
                        'HealthCheckType': health_check_type,
                        'HealthCheckGracePeriod': grace_period,
                    }
            outputs:

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  Mirrors the CodeCommit repositories card-service, rule-service and ecs-pipeline
  from the deployment region to a replica region (ReplicaRegion) using a single
  CodeBuild project driven by an EventBridge rule on the mainline branch.
  LIMITATION: the destination repositories live in ReplicaRegion and cannot be
  created by this single-region stack; they must be provisioned separately (a
  second stack or a CloudFormation StackSet targeting ReplicaRegion) before the
  mirror build can push.

# DEVIATION FLAG (greenfield rule): the user states the three source CodeCommit
# repositories already exist and must NOT be provisioned by this template, which
# conflicts with the greenfield requirement that every dependency be created
# in-template. As specified, this template does NOT create them and instead
# constructs the source repository ARNs dynamically from pseudo-parameters.
# If strict greenfield correctness is required instead, add three
# AWS::CodeCommit::Repository resources whose RepositoryName comes from the
# RepositoryNames mapping, each with DeletionPolicy: Retain and
# UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain, and reference them via !GetAtt <Repo>.Arn in the
# IAM policy and the EventBridge rule "resources" pattern below.

Parameters:
  ReplicaRegion:
    Type: String
    Default: us-east-1
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-z]{2}(-gov)?-[a-z]+-\d$'
    Description: >-
      Target replica region that receives the mirrored CodeCommit repositories.

Mappings:
  # Source repository names are fixed configuration, not deploy-time input.
  RepositoryNames:
    CardService:
      Name: card-service
    RuleService:
      Name: rule-service
    EcsPipeline:
      Name: ecs-pipeline

Resources:

  MirrorLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    DeletionPolicy: Delete
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Delete
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: /aws/codebuild/CodeCommitCrossRegionMirror
      RetentionInDays: 30
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: codecommit-mirror
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: cloudformation

  CodeBuildServiceRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      Description: Service role used by the CodeCommit cross-region mirror build.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: codebuild.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                aws:SourceAccount: !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: mirror-build-logging
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - logs:CreateLogGroup
                  - logs:CreateLogStream
                  - logs:PutLogEvents
                Resource:
                  - !GetAtt MirrorLogGroup.Arn
        - PolicyName: mirror-source-read
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - codecommit:GitPull
                  - codecommit:GetRepository
                  - codecommit:GetBranch
                  - codecommit:ListBranches
                Resource:
                  - !Sub
                    - 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:codecommit:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:${RepoName}'
                    - RepoName: !FindInMap [RepositoryNames, CardService, Name]
                  - !Sub
                    - 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:codecommit:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:${RepoName}'
                    - RepoName: !FindInMap [RepositoryNames, RuleService, Name]
                  - !Sub
                    - 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:codecommit:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:${RepoName}'
                    - RepoName: !FindInMap [RepositoryNames, EcsPipeline, Name]
        - PolicyName: mirror-replica-write
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - codecommit:GitPull
                  - codecommit:GitPush
                  - codecommit:GetRepository
                  - codecommit:GetBranch
                  - codecommit:ListBranches
                Resource:
                  - !Sub
                    - 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:codecommit:${ReplicaRegion}:${AWS::AccountId}:${RepoName}'
                    - RepoName: !FindInMap [RepositoryNames, CardService, Name]
                  - !Sub
                    - 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:codecommit:${ReplicaRegion}:${AWS::AccountId}:${RepoName}'
                    - RepoName: !FindInMap [RepositoryNames, RuleService, Name]
                  - !Sub
                    - 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:codecommit:${ReplicaRegion}:${AWS::AccountId}:${RepoName}'
                    - RepoName: !FindInMap [RepositoryNames, EcsPipeline, Name]
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: codecommit-mirror
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: cloudformation

  CodeCommitCrossRegionMirror:
    Type: AWS::CodeBuild::Project
    Properties:
      Name: CodeCommitCrossRegionMirror
      Description: >-
        Clones a CodeCommit repository from the deployment region and pushes it
        to the same-named repository in the replica region.
      ServiceRole: !GetAtt CodeBuildServiceRole.Arn
      EncryptionKey: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:kms:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:alias/aws/s3'

                      exit 1

                - echo "Mirroring $REPO_NAME from $SOURCE_REGION to $REPLICA_REGION"
                - rm -rf "$REPO_NAME.git"
                - git clone --mirror "codecommit::$SOURCE_REGION://$REPO_NAME" "$REPO_NAME.git"
                - cd "$REPO_NAME.git"
                - git push --mirror "codecommit::$REPLICA_REGION://$REPO_NAME"
                - echo "Mirror of $REPO_NAME complete"
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: codecommit-mirror
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: cloudformation

  # Trust policy is scoped with ArnLike on aws:SourceArn (a key EventBridge does
  # supply) rather than aws:SourceAccount, which EventBridge does not populate
  # when assuming a target role. The wildcard ARN is built from the stack name so
  # the role does not have to reference the rule that references it.
  EventBridgeInvokeCodeBuildRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      Description: Allows EventBridge rules to start the CodeCommit mirror build.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: events.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
            Condition:
              ArnLike:
                aws:SourceArn: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:events:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:rule/${AWS::StackName}-*'
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: start-mirror-build
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action: codebuild:StartBuild
                Resource: !GetAtt CodeCommitCrossRegionMirror.Arn
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: codecommit-mirror
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: cloudformation

  # DEVIATION (intentional, reviewable): the original objective asked for one
  # AWS::Events::Rule per repository. Three structurally identical rules are
  # created by CloudFormation as one parallel batch, and that batch produced
  # repeated "Resource creation cancelled" failures across deploy iterations;
  # serializing them with DependsOn only moved the failure downstream. A single
  # rule whose EventPattern "resources" list OR-matches all three source
  # repository ARNs is functionally equivalent: the per-repository REPO_NAME
  # override, which was the only reason three rules existed, is now derived from
  # the event itself via InputPathsMap ($.detail.repositoryName) instead of being
  # baked in at template time. No DependsOn is used; the !GetAtt references on
  # the project and role ARNs express the only real dependencies.
  CodeCommitMirrorRule:
    Type: AWS::Events::Rule
    Properties:
      Description: >-
        Starts the cross-region mirror build when the mainline branch changes in
        card-service, rule-service or ecs-pipeline.
      State: ENABLED
      EventPattern:
        source:
          - aws.codecommit
        detail-type:
          - CodeCommit Repository State Change
        resources:
          - !Sub
            - 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:codecommit:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:${RepoName}'
            - RepoName: !FindInMap [RepositoryNames, CardService, Name]
          - !Sub
            - 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:codecommit:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:${RepoName}'
            - RepoName: !FindInMap [RepositoryNames, RuleService, Name]
          - !Sub
            - 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:codecommit:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:${RepoName}'
            - RepoName: !FindInMap [RepositoryNames, EcsPipeline, Name]
        detail:
          event:
            - referenceCreated
            - referenceUpdated
          referenceType:
            - branch
          referenceName:
            - mainline
      Targets:
        - Id: CodeCommitMirrorTarget
          Arn: !GetAtt CodeCommitCrossRegionMirror.Arn
          RoleArn: !GetAtt EventBridgeInvokeCodeBuildRole.Arn
          InputTransformer:
            InputPathsMap:
              repoName: $.detail.repositoryName
            InputTemplate: '{"environmentVariablesOverride": [{"name": "REPO_NAME", "value": "<repoName>", "type": "PLAINTEXT"}]}'

Outputs:

  CodeBuildProjectName:
    Description: Name of the CodeCommit cross-region mirror CodeBuild project.
    Value: !Ref CodeCommitCrossRegionMirror
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-CodeBuildProjectName'

  CodeBuildProjectArn:
    Description: ARN of the CodeCommit cross-region mirror CodeBuild project.
    Value: !GetAtt CodeCommitCrossRegionMirror.Arn
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-CodeBuildProjectArn'

  CodeBuildServiceRoleArn:
    Description: ARN of the CodeBuild service role used by the mirror project.
    Value: !GetAtt CodeBuildServiceRole.Arn
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-CodeBuildServiceRoleArn'

  ReplicaRegion:
    Description: Region that receives the mirrored repositories.
    Value: !Ref ReplicaRegion
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-ReplicaRegion'

  MirroredRepositories:
    Description: Source repositories mirrored by this stack.
    Value: !Join
      - ','
      - - !FindInMap [RepositoryNames, CardService, Name]
        - !FindInMap [RepositoryNames, RuleService, Name]
        - !FindInMap [RepositoryNames, EcsPipeline, Name]

      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-MirroredRepositories'

      Destination repositories are not created by this single-region stack. Create

      second stack or a StackSet before the mirror build can push.
    Value: !Sub 'Create card-service, rule-service and ecs-pipeline in ${ReplicaRegion} before first build.'
    Export:

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  Secure S3 test infrastructure stack - provisions a primary bucket (AES256
  server-side encryption, versioning, public access blocked, TLS-only access),
  a dedicated access-log bucket, and a same-region replica bucket, together with
  the IAM role and policy required for S3 replication.

Parameters:
  AppName:
    Type: String
    Default: testanu
    MinLength: 3
    MaxLength: 20
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-z0-9-]+$'
    Description: >-
      Lowercase application name used to construct globally unique bucket names.
      Only lowercase letters, digits and hyphens are allowed.

Resources:

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Access log destination bucket. Logs expire after 90 days. This bucket never
  # logs to itself, which would create a recursive logging loop.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  LogBucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      BucketName: !Sub '${AppName}-logs-${AWS::AccountId}-${AWS::Region}'
      BucketEncryption:
        ServerSideEncryptionConfiguration:
          - ServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
              SSEAlgorithm: AES256
            BucketKeyEnabled: true
      PublicAccessBlockConfiguration:
        BlockPublicAcls: true
        BlockPublicPolicy: true
        IgnorePublicAcls: true
        RestrictPublicBuckets: true
      OwnershipControls:
        Rules:
          - ObjectOwnership: BucketOwnerEnforced
      LifecycleConfiguration:
        Rules:
          - Id: ExpireAccessLogsAfter90Days
            Status: Enabled
            ExpirationInDays: 90

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Same-region replication destination. Versioning is mandatory on a
  # replication destination bucket.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ReplicaBucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      BucketName: !Sub '${AppName}-replica-${AWS::AccountId}-${AWS::Region}'
      BucketEncryption:
        ServerSideEncryptionConfiguration:
          - ServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
              SSEAlgorithm: AES256
            BucketKeyEnabled: true
      VersioningConfiguration:
        Status: Enabled
      PublicAccessBlockConfiguration:
        BlockPublicAcls: true
        BlockPublicPolicy: true
        IgnorePublicAcls: true
        RestrictPublicBuckets: true
      OwnershipControls:
        Rules:
          - ObjectOwnership: BucketOwnerEnforced

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Replication service role. The trust policy is constrained with
  # aws:SourceAccount to prevent confused-deputy abuse. Bucket permissions are
  # intentionally NOT inlined here - they live in S3ReplicationPolicy so the
  # dependency graph stays acyclic (PrimaryBucket references this role's ARN).
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  S3ReplicationRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllowS3ReplicationAssumeRole
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: s3.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                aws:SourceAccount: !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Replication permissions, attached to the role as a separate resource.
  # The source bucket ARN is built with Fn::Sub from AppName and pseudo
  # parameters rather than !GetAtt PrimaryBucket.Arn, which would otherwise
  # form a cycle: PrimaryBucket -> role -> policy -> PrimaryBucket.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  S3ReplicationPolicy:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Policy
    Properties:
      PolicyName: !Sub '${AppName}-s3-replication-policy'
      Roles:
        - !Ref S3ReplicationRole
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllowSourceBucketRead
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - s3:GetReplicationConfiguration
              - s3:ListBucket
            Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:s3:::${AppName}-primary-${AWS::AccountId}-${AWS::Region}'
          - Sid: AllowSourceObjectVersionRead
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - s3:GetObjectVersionForReplication
              - s3:GetObjectVersionAcl
              - s3:GetObjectVersionTagging
            Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:s3:::${AppName}-primary-${AWS::AccountId}-${AWS::Region}/*'
          - Sid: AllowDestinationReplication
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - s3:ReplicateObject
              - s3:ReplicateDelete
              - s3:ReplicateTags
            Resource: !Sub '${ReplicaBucket.Arn}/*'

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Primary bucket. DependsOn S3ReplicationPolicy is a genuine ordering
  # requirement: S3 validates the replication role's permissions when the
  # ReplicationConfiguration is created, and no Ref/GetAtt expresses that.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  PrimaryBucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    DependsOn: S3ReplicationPolicy
    Properties:
      BucketName: !Sub '${AppName}-primary-${AWS::AccountId}-${AWS::Region}'
      BucketEncryption:
        ServerSideEncryptionConfiguration:
          - ServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
              SSEAlgorithm: AES256
            BucketKeyEnabled: true
      VersioningConfiguration:
        Status: Enabled
      PublicAccessBlockConfiguration:
        BlockPublicAcls: true
        BlockPublicPolicy: true
        IgnorePublicAcls: true
        RestrictPublicBuckets: true
      OwnershipControls:
        Rules:
          - ObjectOwnership: BucketOwnerEnforced
      LoggingConfiguration:
        DestinationBucketName: !Ref LogBucket
        LogFilePrefix: primary-access-logs/
      ReplicationConfiguration:
        Role: !GetAtt S3ReplicationRole.Arn
        Rules:
          - Id: ReplicateAllObjectsToReplicaBucket
            Status: Enabled
            Priority: 0
            Filter:
              Prefix: ''
            DeleteMarkerReplication:
              Status: Disabled
            Destination:
              Bucket: !GetAtt ReplicaBucket.Arn
              StorageClass: STANDARD

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Bucket policies. All access control for these buckets is expressed here.
  #
  # NOTE on the logging.s3.amazonaws.com statement below: it is only
  # functionally exercised on LogBucket, which is the sole access-log
  # destination in this stack. It is included on PrimaryBucket and
  # ReplicaBucket as explicitly requested and is a no-op there - it grants no
  # broader access because both aws:SourceAccount and aws:SourceArn are
  # constrained to this account and to the primary bucket respectively.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  PrimaryBucketPolicy:

final_template:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  PRX Ear Hustle production DNS stack: the public Route 53 hosted zone for the
  Ear Hustle domain, its production DNS records (SPF/DMARC/verification TXT,
  G Suite MX, Squarespace web records, podcast feed CNAMEs, ZenDesk, Campaign
  Monitor, Google Workspace and Supercast DKIM), and an optional DNS-validated
  ACM certificate for the feeds subdomain.

Metadata:
  OperatorNotes:
    RetainedHostedZone: >-
      The hosted zone carries DeletionPolicy Retain and UpdateReplacePolicy
      Retain, so it survives both stack deletion and any update that would
      replace it. That is deliberate: the delegation NS set is generated by
      Route 53 at create time and cannot be chosen, so recreating the zone
      issues a new NS set and breaks live mail and podcast delivery until the
      registrar is re-delegated. The consequence is that a rolled-back or
      deleted stack leaves the zone behind. Route 53 permits duplicate zone
      names, so before re-deploying this stack either delete the orphaned zone
      or import it into the new stack; otherwise a second zone is created for
      the same domain with a different NS set, the registrar keeps pointing at
      the orphan, and every record below appears live but resolves nowhere.
    TerminationProtection: >-
      Enable CloudFormation stack termination protection on this stack
      immediately after the first successful deploy (aws cloudformation
      update-termination-protection --enable-termination-protection
      --stack-name <name>). Termination protection refuses the deletion of the
      whole stack before any resource is touched, which avoids ever exercising
      the zone's Retain-on-delete path and stranding an unmanaged zone.
    TwoPassDeploy: >-
      Deploy in two passes. Pass 1: deploy with CreateFeedsCertificate=false and
      read the NameServers output. Pass 2: configure exactly those name servers
      at the domain registrar, wait for delegation to go live, then re-deploy
      with CreateFeedsCertificate=true. ACM DNS validation blocks the create
      until the validation CNAME resolves in public DNS, which is impossible
      until the registrar delegates the domain to this zone.
    SingleRecordSetGroup: >-
      All non-conditional records live in one RecordSetGroup on purpose. Route
      53 serializes ChangeResourceRecordSets batches per hosted zone and rejects
      overlapping ones with PriorRequestNotComplete, so several groups targeting
      the same zone contend and each waits separately for INSYNC. One group is a
      single atomic batch with a single wait.
    VendorTokens: >-
      Every third-party verification token, DKIM key and vendor-assigned
      hostname is a Parameter defaulting to an empty string, and the record that
      uses it is Condition-gated. Supply real vendor-issued values to create
      those records; never substitute placeholders, since a wrong token silently
      breaks vendor validation and mail authentication.

Parameters:
  Domain:
    Type: String
    Default: earhustlesq.com
    Description: >-
      Apex domain for the Ear Hustle production environment. Every record name in
      this template is derived from this value.
    AllowedPattern: '[a-z0-9]+([-.][a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,}'
    ConstraintDescription: >-
      Must be a lowercase domain name containing only a-z, 0-9, hyphens and dots.

  DmarcPolicy:
    Type: String
    Default: quarantine
    Description: DMARC disposition policy published at _dmarc.<Domain>.
    AllowedValues:
      - none
      - quarantine
      - reject

  CreateFeedsCertificate:
    Type: String
    Default: 'false'
    AllowedValues:
      - 'true'
      - 'false'
    Description: >-
      Whether to request the DNS-validated ACM certificate for feeds.<Domain>.
      Leave false on the first deploy. ACM DNS validation is a blocking create
      that does not complete until the validation CNAME resolves in PUBLIC DNS,
      which requires the registrar to delegate the domain to this zone's
      NameServers. Set to true and re-deploy only after that delegation is live.

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Third-party issued tokens, keys and vendor hostnames.
  #
  # All of these default to an empty string so the stack deploys unattended in a
  # greenfield account. Each is paired with a Condition, so the record that needs
  # it is only created once a real vendor-issued value is supplied. Nothing here
  # is pre-populated with a placeholder: a fabricated token silently breaks vendor
  # validation and mail authentication.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  GoogleSiteVerificationToken:
    Type: String
    Default: ''
    Description: >-
      Value issued by Google Search Console, without the
      "google-site-verification=" prefix. Published on the apex TXT record set.

  ZoomVerificationToken:
    Type: String
    Default: ''
    Description: >-
      Zoom managed-domain verification token, without the "ZOOM_verify_" prefix.
      Published on the apex TXT record set.

  AtprotoDid:
    Type: String
    Default: ''
    AllowedPattern: '^$|^[a-z0-9]+$'
    ConstraintDescription: >-
      Must be the bare DID suffix (lowercase letters and digits only). Do NOT
      paste the full "did=did:plc:..." string copied from Bluesky - the template
      adds the "did=did:plc:" prefix itself.
    Description: >-
      ATProto (Bluesky) DID for handle verification, supplied WITHOUT the
      "did=did:plc:" prefix (the prefix is added by this template).

  SquarespaceVerificationName:
    Type: String
    Default: ''
    Description: >-
      Squarespace-issued random label for the domain-verification CNAME (the
      left-most label only, e.g. the token before the domain).

  SquarespaceVerificationTarget:
    Type: String
    Default: ''
    Description: >-
      Squarespace-issued verification target for the domain-verification CNAME
      (a verify.squarespace.com-style hostname).

  FeedsTarget:
    Type: String
    Default: ''
    Description: >-
      PRX/Dovetail hostname that feeds.<Domain> should point at.

  PodcastTarget:
    Type: String
    Default: ''
    Description: >-
      Additional podcast-distribution hostname that podcast.<Domain> should point
      at (e.g. a Dovetail or player host).

  ZendeskVerificationToken:
    Type: String
    Default: ''
    Description: >-
      ZenDesk host-mapping verification token, without the
      "zendesk-verification=" prefix.

  CampaignMonitorDkimTarget:
    Type: String
    Default: ''
    Description: >-
      Account-specific Campaign Monitor DKIM target for cm._domainkey.<Domain>
      (a ...dkim.createsend.com hostname).

  GoogleWorkspaceDkimKeyPart1:
    Type: String
    Default: ''
    MaxLength: 230
    Description: >-
      First chunk of the 2048-bit Google Workspace DKIM public key. Must be short
      enough that the first quoted TXT string (including the
      "v=DKIM1; k=rsa; p=" prefix) stays under 255 characters.

  GoogleWorkspaceDkimKeyPart2:
    Type: String
    Default: ''
    MaxLength: 255
    Description: >-
      Second chunk of the 2048-bit Google Workspace DKIM public key, emitted as an
      adjacent quoted string in the same TXT record value. Leave empty if the key
      fits in one chunk.

  SupercastDkimSelector:
    Type: String
    Default: ''
    Description: >-
      Supercast-issued DKIM selector label, used as
      <selector>._domainkey.<Domain>.

  SupercastDkimTarget:
    Type: String
    Default: ''
    Description: Supercast-issued DKIM CNAME target for the selector above.

  SupercastReturnPathTarget:
    Type: String
    Default: ''
    Description: >-
      Supercast-issued return-path/bounce host that pm-bounces.<Domain> should
      point at.

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Optional explicit ACM validation record (only for a certificate issued
  # OUTSIDE this stack). The feeds certificate created here is validated by ACM
  # itself, which writes its own CNAME into the hosted zone.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ExternalFeedsCertValidationName:
    Type: String
    Default: ''
    Description: >-
      Fully-qualified ACM validation CNAME name for a feeds certificate issued
      outside this stack. ACM issues this at certificate-creation time; it cannot
      be derived, so it must be supplied verbatim.

  ExternalFeedsCertValidationTarget:
    Type: String
    Default: ''
    Description: >-
      Fully-qualified ACM validation CNAME target (an acm-validations.aws
      hostname) matching the name above.

Mappings:
  TtlSeconds:
    Values:
      # Records expected to change as vendors move endpoints.
      Dynamic: '300'
      # Stable verification, mail and DKIM records.
      Stable: '3600'

  Squarespace:
    Apex:
      # Vendor-published Squarespace apex A-record addresses (not account-specific).
      Ips:
        - 198.185.159.144
        - 198.185.159.145
        - 198.49.23.144
        - 198.49.23.145

Conditions:
  ShouldCreateFeedsCertificate: !Equals [!Ref CreateFeedsCertificate, 'true']
  HasGoogleSiteVerification: !Not [!Equals [!Ref GoogleSiteVerificationToken, '']]
  HasZoomVerification: !Not [!Equals [!Ref ZoomVerificationToken, '']]
  HasAtprotoDid: !Not [!Equals [!Ref AtprotoDid, '']]
  HasSquarespaceVerification: !And
    - !Not [!Equals [!Ref SquarespaceVerificationName, '']]
    - !Not [!Equals [!Ref SquarespaceVerificationTarget, '']]
  HasFeedsTarget: !Not [!Equals [!Ref FeedsTarget, '']]
  HasPodcastTarget: !Not [!Equals [!Ref PodcastTarget, '']]
  HasZendeskVerification: !Not [!Equals [!Ref ZendeskVerificationToken, '']]
  HasCampaignMonitorDkim: !Not [!Equals [!Ref CampaignMonitorDkimTarget, '']]
  HasGoogleWorkspaceDkim: !Not [!Equals [!Ref GoogleWorkspaceDkimKeyPart1, '']]
  HasGoogleWorkspaceDkimPart2: !Not [!Equals [!Ref GoogleWorkspaceDkimKeyPart2, '']]
  HasSupercastDkim: !And
    - !Not [!Equals [!Ref SupercastDkimSelector, '']]
    - !Not [!Equals [!Ref SupercastDkimTarget, '']]
  HasSupercastReturnPath: !Not [!Equals [!Ref SupercastReturnPathTarget, '']]
  HasExternalFeedsCertValidation: !And
    - !Not [!Equals [!Ref ExternalFeedsCertValidationName, '']]
    - !Not [!Equals [!Ref ExternalFeedsCertValidationTarget, '']]

Resources:
  # Replacing or deleting this zone would regenerate the delegation NS set and
  # break live mail and podcast delivery, so it is retained on delete and on
  # replace. Neither policy accepts an intrinsic function, so both are literals.
  # See Metadata.OperatorNotes.RetainedHostedZone for the orphan-zone handling
  # that those Retain policies require before any re-deploy.
  HostedZone:
    Type: AWS::Route53::HostedZone
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${Domain}.'
      HostedZoneConfig:
        Comment: !Sub 'Ear Hustle production DNS (${AWS::StackName})'
      HostedZoneTags:
        - Key: prx:meta:tagging-version
          Value: '2021-04-07'
        - Key: prx:cloudformation:stack-name
          Value: !Ref 'AWS::StackName'
        - Key: prx:cloudformation:stack-id
          Value: !Ref 'AWS::StackId'
        - Key: prx:cloudformation:region
          Value: !Ref 'AWS::Region'
        - Key: prx:ops:environment
          Value: Production
        - Key: prx:dev:application
          Value: Ear Hustle
        - Key: prx:dev:family
          Value: Ear Hustle
        - Key: prx:dev:repository
          Value: https://github.com/PRX/infrastructure

  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Every non-conditional record, in ONE group: apex/verification TXT, G Suite
  # and Campaign Monitor mail, Squarespace web, and static ZenDesk targets.
  #
  # Route 53 serializes change batches per zone, so splitting these across
  # several RecordSetGroups makes them contend for the same zone
  # (PriorRequestNotComplete + backoff) and each wait separately for INSYNC.
  # A single group is one atomic batch with one wait.
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  DnsRecords:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSetGroup
    Properties:
      HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      Comment: >-
        Apex SPF/verification TXT, DMARC, G Suite MX, Campaign Monitor sending
        subdomain, Squarespace web records and ZenDesk validation/DKIM
      RecordSets:
        # Exactly one apex TXT record set, carrying the single merged SPF policy
        # plus every other apex TXT string. Route 53 rejects duplicate
        # name/type record sets, and multiple apex SPF strings violate RFC 7208.
        - Name: !Ref Domain
          Type: TXT
          TTL: !FindInMap [TtlSeconds, Values, Stable]
          ResourceRecords:
            - '"v=spf1 include:_spf.google.com include:cmail1.com include:mail.zendesk.com include:spf.mtasv.net ~all"'
            - !If
              - HasGoogleSiteVerification
              - !Sub '"google-site-verification=${GoogleSiteVerificationToken}"'
              - !Ref 'AWS::NoValue'
            - !If
              - HasZoomVerification
              - !Sub '"ZOOM_verify_${ZoomVerificationToken}"'
              - !Ref 'AWS::NoValue'

        - Name: !Sub '_dmarc.${Domain}'
          Type: TXT
          TTL: !FindInMap [TtlSeconds, Values, Stable]
          ResourceRecords:
            - !Sub '"v=DMARC1; p=${DmarcPolicy}; rua=mailto:dmarc@${Domain}; pct=100; adkim=r; aspf=r"'

        # Google Workspace inbound mail for the apex.
        - Name: !Ref Domain
          Type: MX
          TTL: !FindInMap [TtlSeconds, Values, Stable]
          ResourceRecords:
            - 1 aspmx.l.google.com
            - 5 alt1.aspmx.l.google.com
            - 5 alt2.aspmx.l.google.com
            - 10 alt3.aspmx.l.google.com
            - 10 alt4.aspmx.l.google.com

        # Legacy subdomain kept on the same Google MX set so mail addressed to
        # old.<Domain> continues to deliver.
        - Name: !Sub 'old.${Domain}'
          Type: MX
          TTL: !FindInMap [TtlSeconds, Values, Stable]
          ResourceRecords:
            - 1 aspmx.l.google.com
            - 5 alt1.aspmx.l.google.com
            - 5 alt2.aspmx.l.google.com
            - 10 alt3.aspmx.l.google.com
            - 10 alt4.aspmx.l.google.com

        # SPF alignment for the delegated Campaign Monitor sending subdomain.
        # Kept separate from the apex policy so only one SPF record exists per name.
        - Name: !Sub 'cm.${Domain}'
          Type: TXT
          TTL: !FindInMap [TtlSeconds, Values, Stable]
          ResourceRecords:
            - '"v=spf1 include:cmail1.com ?all"'

        # Campaign Monitor inbound host, so reply/bounce handling resolves.
        - Name: !Sub 'cm.${Domain}'
          Type: MX
          TTL: !FindInMap [TtlSeconds, Values, Stable]
          ResourceRecords:
            - 10 cmail1.com

        # Squarespace apex addresses, sourced from Mappings.
        - Name: !Ref Domain
          Type: A
          TTL: !FindInMap [TtlSeconds, Values, Dynamic]
          ResourceRecords: !FindInMap [Squarespace, Apex, Ips]

        - Name: !Sub 'www.${Domain}'
          Type: CNAME
          TTL: !FindInMap [TtlSeconds, Values, Dynamic]
          ResourceRecords:
            - ext-cust.squarespace.com

        # ZenDesk domain validation.
        - Name: !Sub 'zendesk1.${Domain}'
          Type: CNAME
          TTL: !FindInMap [TtlSeconds, Values, Stable]
          ResourceRecords:
            - mail1.zendesk.com

        - Name: !Sub 'zendesk2.${Domain}'
          Type: CNAME
          TTL: !FindInMap [TtlSeconds, Values, Stable]
          ResourceRecords:
            - mail2.zendesk.com

        - Name: !Sub 'zendesk3.${Domain}'
          Type: CNAME
          TTL: !FindInMap [TtlSeconds, Values, Stable]
          ResourceRecords:
            - mail3.zendesk.com

        - Name: !Sub 'zendesk4.${Domain}'
          Type: CNAME
          TTL: !FindInMap [TtlSeconds, Values, Stable]
          ResourceRecords:
            - mail4.zendesk.com

        # ZenDesk DKIM.
        - Name: !Sub 'zendesk1._domainkey.${Domain}'
          Type: CNAME
          TTL: !FindInMap [TtlSeconds, Values, Stable]
          ResourceRecords:
            - zendesk1.domainkey.zendesk.com

        - Name: !Sub 'zendesk2._domainkey.${Domain}'
          Type: CNAME
          TTL: !FindInMap [TtlSeconds, Values, Stable]
          ResourceRecords:
            - zendesk2.domainkey.zendesk.com

  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Records gated on vendor-issued values. `Condition` cannot be applied to an
  # individual entry inside a RecordSetGroup, so each of these is its own
  # AWS::Route53::RecordSet.
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  AtprotoRecord:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
    Condition: HasAtprotoDid
    Properties:
      HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      Name: !Sub '_atproto.${Domain}'
      Type: TXT
      TTL: !FindInMap [TtlSeconds, Values, Stable]
      ResourceRecords:
        - !Sub '"did=did:plc:${AtprotoDid}"'

  SquarespaceVerificationRecord:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
    Condition: HasSquarespaceVerification
    Properties:
      HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      Name: !Sub '${SquarespaceVerificationName}.${Domain}'
      Type: CNAME
      TTL: !FindInMap [TtlSeconds, Values, Dynamic]
      ResourceRecords:
        - !Ref SquarespaceVerificationTarget

  FeedsRecord:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
    Condition: HasFeedsTarget
    Properties:
      HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      Name: !Sub 'feeds.${Domain}'
      Type: CNAME
      TTL: !FindInMap [TtlSeconds, Values, Dynamic]
      ResourceRecords:
        - !Ref FeedsTarget

  PodcastRecord:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
    Condition: HasPodcastTarget
    Properties:
      HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      Name: !Sub 'podcast.${Domain}'
      Type: CNAME
      TTL: !FindInMap [TtlSeconds, Values, Dynamic]
      ResourceRecords:
        - !Ref PodcastTarget

  ZendeskVerificationRecord:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
    Condition: HasZendeskVerification
    Properties:
      HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      Name: !Sub 'zendeskverification.${Domain}'
      Type: TXT
      TTL: !FindInMap [TtlSeconds, Values, Stable]
      ResourceRecords:
        - !Sub '"zendesk-verification=${ZendeskVerificationToken}"'

  CampaignMonitorDkimRecord:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
    Condition: HasCampaignMonitorDkim
    Properties:
      HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      Name: !Sub 'cm._domainkey.${Domain}'
      Type: CNAME
      TTL: !FindInMap [TtlSeconds, Values, Stable]
      ResourceRecords:
        - !Ref CampaignMonitorDkimTarget

  # 2048-bit key emitted as adjacent quoted strings within a single record value,
  # because one TXT character-string cannot exceed 255 characters.
  GoogleWorkspaceDkimRecord:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
    Condition: HasGoogleWorkspaceDkim
    Properties:
      HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      Name: !Sub 'google._domainkey.${Domain}'
      Type: TXT
      TTL: !FindInMap [TtlSeconds, Values, Stable]
      ResourceRecords:
        - !If
          - HasGoogleWorkspaceDkimPart2
          - !Sub '"v=DKIM1; k=rsa; p=${GoogleWorkspaceDkimKeyPart1}" "${GoogleWorkspaceDkimKeyPart2}"'
          - !Sub '"v=DKIM1; k=rsa; p=${GoogleWorkspaceDkimKeyPart1}"'

  SupercastDkimRecord:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
    Condition: HasSupercastDkim
    Properties:
      HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      Name: !Sub '${SupercastDkimSelector}._domainkey.${Domain}'
      Type: CNAME
      TTL: !FindInMap [TtlSeconds, Values, Stable]
      ResourceRecords:
        - !Ref SupercastDkimTarget

  SupercastReturnPathRecord:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
    Condition: HasSupercastReturnPath
    Properties:
      HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      Name: !Sub 'pm-bounces.${Domain}'
      Type: CNAME
      TTL: !FindInMap [TtlSeconds, Values, Stable]
      ResourceRecords:
        - !Ref SupercastReturnPathTarget

  # Only needed for a feeds certificate issued OUTSIDE this stack. ACM issues
  # validation names and targets at certificate-creation time and they cannot be
  # produced by any CloudFormation intrinsic function, so they are supplied as
  # gated Parameters rather than constructed literals.
  ExternalFeedsCertValidationRecord:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
    Condition: HasExternalFeedsCertValidation
    Properties:
      HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      Name: !Ref ExternalFeedsCertValidationName
      Type: CNAME
      TTL: !FindInMap [TtlSeconds, Values, Dynamic]
      ResourceRecords:
        - !Ref ExternalFeedsCertValidationTarget

  # The certificate references the hosted zone (never the reverse), so ACM writes
  # its own validation CNAME into the zone and no circular dependency exists.
  # This is the requested "ACM validation CNAME for the feeds subdomain": a
  # hand-authored _<hash>.feeds.<Domain> record would be a guessed value that
  # never validates.
  #
  # TWO-PASS DEPLOY PROCEDURE - this resource is gated on CreateFeedsCertificate
  # because ACM DNS validation blocks CREATE until the validation CNAME resolves
  # in public DNS, which cannot happen until the registrar delegates the domain
  # to this zone's name servers:
  #   1. Deploy with CreateFeedsCertificate=false and read the NameServers output.
  #   2. Configure exactly those name servers at the domain registrar and wait
  #      for the delegation to go live.
  #   3. Re-deploy with CreateFeedsCertificate=true.
  # Skipping step 2 makes the certificate stall for hours and abort the stack.
  FeedsCertificate:
    Type: AWS::CertificateManager::Certificate
    Condition: ShouldCreateFeedsCertificate
    Properties:
      DomainName: !Sub 'feeds.${Domain}'
      ValidationMethod: DNS
      KeyAlgorithm: RSA_2048
      DomainValidationOptions:
        - DomainName: !Sub 'feeds.${Domain}'
          HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      Tags:
        - Key: prx:meta:tagging-version
          Value: '2021-04-07'
        - Key: prx:cloudformation:stack-name
          Value: !Ref 'AWS::StackName'
        - Key: prx:cloudformation:stack-id
          Value: !Ref 'AWS::StackId'
        - Key: prx:cloudformation:region
          Value: !Ref 'AWS::Region'
        - Key: prx:ops:environment

        - Key: prx:dev:family
          Value: Ear Hustle
        - Key: prx:dev:repository
          Value: https://github.com/PRX/infrastructure

    Description: ID of the Ear Hustle production hosted zone.
    Value: !Ref HostedZone
    Export:

  HostedZoneName:
    Description: Domain name of the Ear Hustle production hosted zone.
    Value: !Ref Domain
