AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  Aurora Global Database failover automation stack — provisions the SSM Automation
  document (AuroraGlobalDatabaseFailoverSSMDocument), its execution role, the Route 53
  Application Recovery Controller control plane, the writer-endpoint secret, and the
  TriggerFailover Lambda that starts the automation. The Aurora Global Database itself
  is intentionally out of scope and is supplied at runtime as GlobalClusterIdentifier.
  Documented gaps: (1) AWS::Route53RecoveryControl::SafetyRule is omitted pending
  verification of its assertion/gating sub-properties; (2) the request asked for
  python3.13 — python3.12 is used because it is the approved runtime here and the
  handler code is compatible with both.

Parameters:
  AppName:
    Type: String
    Default: aurora-global-failover
    Description: Logical application name used for resource naming, tagging and the SSM Parameter Store path.
    AllowedPattern: '[a-z0-9-]{3,48}'
    ConstraintDescription: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens only (3-48 characters).

  SecondaryRegion:
    Type: String
    Default: us-west-2
    Description: Region hosting the standby Aurora Global Database cluster and the standby ARC routing control.
    AllowedPattern: '[a-z]{2}-[a-z]+-[0-9]'
    ConstraintDescription: Must be a valid AWS region identifier, e.g. us-west-2.

Resources:

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Route 53 Application Recovery Controller control plane (created in-template)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  ArcCluster:
    Type: AWS::Route53RecoveryControl::Cluster
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${AppName}-arc-cluster'
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AppName}-arc-cluster'
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref AppName
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: cloudformation

  ArcControlPanel:
    Type: AWS::Route53RecoveryControl::ControlPanel
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${AppName}-control-panel'
      ClusterArn: !Ref ArcCluster
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AppName}-control-panel'
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref AppName
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: cloudformation

  PrimaryRoutingControl:
    Type: AWS::Route53RecoveryControl::RoutingControl
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::Region}-routing-control'
      ClusterArn: !Ref ArcCluster
      ControlPanelArn: !Ref ArcControlPanel

  SecondaryRoutingControl:
    Type: AWS::Route53RecoveryControl::RoutingControl
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${SecondaryRegion}-routing-control'
      ClusterArn: !Ref ArcCluster
      ControlPanelArn: !Ref ArcControlPanel

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Writer endpoint secret — generated, never a plain-text credential
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  AuroraWriterEndpointSecret:
    Type: AWS::SecretsManager::Secret
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${AppName}/writer-endpoint'
      Description: Aurora Global Database writer endpoint metadata maintained by the failover automation.
      GenerateSecretString:
        SecretStringTemplate: '{"username": "admin", "writerEndpoint": "pending"}'
        GenerateStringKey: password
        PasswordLength: 32
        ExcludeCharacters: '"@/\'
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AppName}-writer-endpoint'
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref AppName
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: cloudformation

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Parameter Store — the automation reads ARC identifiers from here, never from
  # literals embedded in the Python.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  PrimaryRoutingControlArnParameter:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '/${AppName}/arc/primary-routing-control-arn'
      Type: String
      Description: ARN of the routing control representing the primary region.
      Value: !Ref PrimaryRoutingControl
      Tags:
        Name: !Sub '${AppName}-primary-routing-control-arn'
        Application: !Ref AppName
        ManagedBy: cloudformation

  SecondaryRoutingControlArnParameter:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '/${AppName}/arc/secondary-routing-control-arn'
      Type: String
      Description: ARN of the routing control representing the secondary region.
      Value: !Ref SecondaryRoutingControl
      Tags:
        Name: !Sub '${AppName}-secondary-routing-control-arn'
        Application: !Ref AppName
        ManagedBy: cloudformation

  ArcClusterArnParameter:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '/${AppName}/arc/cluster-arn'
      Type: String
      Description: ARN of the Route 53 ARC cluster whose data-plane endpoints serve routing control state.
      Value: !Ref ArcCluster
      Tags:
        Name: !Sub '${AppName}-arc-cluster-arn'
        Application: !Ref AppName
        ManagedBy: cloudformation

  ActiveRegionParameter:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '/${AppName}/arc/active-region'
      Type: String
      Description: Marker recording which region currently holds the Aurora Global Database writer.
      Value: !Ref 'AWS::Region'
      Tags:
        Name: !Sub '${AppName}-active-region'
        Application: !Ref AppName
        ManagedBy: cloudformation

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # IAM — SSM Automation execution role
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  SSMAutomationRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      Description: Execution role assumed by the Aurora Global Database failover SSM Automation document.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: ssm.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                aws:SourceAccount: !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: aurora-global-database-failover
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: AuroraGlobalDatabaseOperations
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - rds:FailoverGlobalCluster
                  - rds:SwitchoverGlobalCluster
                  - rds:DescribeGlobalClusters
                  - rds:DescribeDBClusters
                  - rds:DescribeDBInstances
                  - rds:DescribeDBClusterEndpoints
                  - rds:PromoteReadReplicaDBCluster
                  - rds:ListTagsForResource
                Resource: '*'

              - Sid: ArcControlPlaneRead
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - route53-recovery-control-config:Describe*
                  - route53-recovery-control-config:List*
                Resource: '*'

              - Sid: ArcDataPlaneRoutingControls
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - route53-recovery-cluster:GetRoutingControlState
                  - route53-recovery-cluster:UpdateRoutingControlState
                  - route53-recovery-cluster:UpdateRoutingControlStates
                  - route53-recovery-readiness:GetReadinessCheckStatus
                Resource: '*'

              - Sid: WriterEndpointSecretAccess
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - secretsmanager:GetSecretValue
                  - secretsmanager:DescribeSecret
                  - secretsmanager:PutSecretValue
                  - secretsmanager:UpdateSecret
                Resource: !Ref AuroraWriterEndpointSecret

              - Sid: FailoverParameterStoreAccess
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - ssm:GetParameter
                  - ssm:GetParameters
                  - ssm:GetParametersByPath
                  - ssm:PutParameter
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:ssm:*:${AWS::AccountId}:parameter/${AppName}/*'

              - Sid: AutomationSelfManagement
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - ssm:DescribeAutomationExecutions
                  - ssm:DescribeAutomationStepExecutions
                  - ssm:GetAutomationExecution
                  - ssm:StartAutomationExecution
                Resource: '*'

              - Sid: ExecuteScriptLogging
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - logs:CreateLogGroup
                  - logs:CreateLogStream
                  - logs:PutLogEvents
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:logs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:log-group:*'
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AppName}-ssm-automation-role'
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref AppName
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: cloudformation

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # IAM — Lambda trigger role
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  TriggerFailoverLambdaRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      Description: Execution role for the TriggerFailover Lambda function.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: lambda.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: pass-automation-role
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: PassAutomationRoleToSsm
                Effect: Allow
                Action: iam:PassRole
                Resource: !GetAtt SSMAutomationRole.Arn
                Condition:
                  StringEquals:
                    iam:PassedToService: ssm.amazonaws.com
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AppName}-trigger-failover-role'
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref AppName
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: cloudformation

  # Kept as a standalone policy: it references the automation document ARN, and the
  # document references the automation role, so inlining it on the role would create
  # a role -> document -> role dependency cycle.
  TriggerFailoverAutomationPolicy:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Policy
    Properties:
      PolicyName: start-and-monitor-aurora-failover-automation
      Roles:
        - !Ref TriggerFailoverLambdaRole
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: StartThisAutomationDocumentOnly
            Effect: Allow
            Action: ssm:StartAutomationExecution
            Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:ssm:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:automation-definition/${AuroraFailoverDocument}:*'
          - Sid: MonitorAutomationExecutions
            Effect: Allow
            Action:
              - ssm:GetAutomationExecution
              - ssm:DescribeAutomationExecutions
              - ssm:DescribeAutomationStepExecutions
              - ssm:StopAutomationExecution
            Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:ssm:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:automation-execution/*'

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # SSM Automation document
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  AuroraFailoverDocument:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Document
    Properties:
      Name: AuroraGlobalDatabaseFailoverSSMDocument
      DocumentType: Automation
      DocumentFormat: YAML
      UpdateMethod: NewVersion
      TargetType: /
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: AuroraGlobalDatabaseFailoverSSMDocument
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref AppName
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: cloudformation
      Content:
        schemaVersion: '0.3'
        description: >-
          Fails over an Aurora Global Database to its standby region, flips the Route 53
          Application Recovery Controller routing controls atomically, and records the new
          writer endpoint in Secrets Manager.
        assumeRole: !GetAtt SSMAutomationRole.Arn
        parameters:
          PrimaryRegion:
            type: String
            description: Region that normally hosts the Aurora Global Database writer cluster.
            default: us-east-1
          SecondaryRegion:
            type: String
            description: Region hosting the standby Aurora Global Database cluster.
            default: !Ref SecondaryRegion
          GlobalClusterIdentifier:
            type: String
            description: Identifier of the Aurora Global Database to fail over. Supplied at execution time.
          SecretArn:
            type: String
            description: ARN of the Secrets Manager secret holding the writer endpoint metadata.
            default: !Ref AuroraWriterEndpointSecret
          ParameterPrefix:
            type: String
            description: Parameter Store path prefix holding the ARC identifiers used by this automation.
            default: !Sub '/${AppName}'
          HomeRegion:
            type: String
            description: Region holding the Parameter Store entries and the writer endpoint secret.
            default: !Ref 'AWS::Region'
          ArcControlPlaneRegion:
            type: String
            description: Region of the Route 53 ARC control plane endpoint used to discover cluster data-plane endpoints.
            default: us-west-2
        outputs:
          - DetermineActiveRegion.activeRegion
          - PerformGlobalClusterFailover.newWriterRegion
        mainSteps:
          - name: DetermineActiveRegion
            action: aws:executeScript
            description: Resolve which region currently holds the writer by reading ARC routing control state.
            timeoutSeconds: 600
            onFailure: Abort
            inputs:
              Runtime: python3.11
              Handler: determine_active_region
              InputPayload:
                PrimaryRegion: '{{ PrimaryRegion }}'
                SecondaryRegion: '{{ SecondaryRegion }}'
                ParameterPrefix: '{{ ParameterPrefix }}'
                HomeRegion: '{{ HomeRegion }}'
                ArcControlPlaneRegion: '{{ ArcControlPlaneRegion }}'
              Script: |
                import boto3


                def determine_active_region(events, context):
                    prefix = events['ParameterPrefix'].rstrip('/')
                    primary_region = events['PrimaryRegion']
                    secondary_region = events['SecondaryRegion']
                    home_region = events['HomeRegion']
                    control_plane_region = events['ArcControlPlaneRegion']

                    ssm = boto3.client('ssm', region_name=home_region)

                    def read(suffix):
                        return ssm.get_parameter(Name=prefix + suffix)['Parameter']['Value']

                    cluster_arn = read('/arc/cluster-arn')
                    controls = {
                        primary_region: read('/arc/primary-routing-control-arn'),
                        secondary_region: read('/arc/secondary-routing-control-arn'),
                    }

                    config = boto3.client(
                        'route53-recovery-control-config',
                        region_name=control_plane_region,
                    )
                    cluster = config.describe_cluster(ClusterArn=cluster_arn)['Cluster']
                    endpoints = cluster.get('ClusterEndpoints', [])
                    if not endpoints:
                        raise RuntimeError('ARC cluster exposes no data-plane endpoints: ' + cluster_arn)

                    states = {}
                    last_error = None
                    for endpoint in endpoints:
                        try:
                            data_plane = boto3.client(
                                'route53-recovery-cluster',
                                region_name=endpoint['Region'],
                                endpoint_url=endpoint['Endpoint'],
                            )
                            resolved = {}
                            for region, arn in controls.items():
                                response = data_plane.get_routing_control_state(RoutingControlArn=arn)
                                resolved[region] = response['RoutingControlState']
                            states = resolved
                            break
                        except Exception as error:  # try the next regional data-plane endpoint
                            last_error = error

                    if not states:
                        raise RuntimeError(
                            'Unable to read routing control state from any ARC cluster endpoint: %s' % last_error
                        )

                    on_regions = sorted([r for r, s in states.items() if s == 'On'])
                    if len(on_regions) == 1:
                        active_region = on_regions[0]
                    else:
                        # Ambiguous control state (both On or both Off): fall back to the recorded marker.
                        active_region = read('/arc/active-region')

                    if active_region not in controls:
                        raise RuntimeError('Recorded active region is not a known failover region: ' + active_region)

                    standby_region = secondary_region if active_region == primary_region else primary_region

                    print('routing control states: %s -> active %s, standby %s' % (states, active_region, standby_region))

                    return {
                        'activeRegion': active_region,
                        'standbyRegion': standby_region,
                        'activeRoutingControlArn': controls[active_region],
                        'standbyRoutingControlArn': controls[standby_region],
                        'arcClusterArn': cluster_arn,
                    }
            outputs:
              - Name: activeRegion
                Selector: $.Payload.activeRegion
                Type: String
              - Name: standbyRegion
                Selector: $.Payload.standbyRegion
                Type: String
              - Name: activeRoutingControlArn
                Selector: $.Payload.activeRoutingControlArn
                Type: String
              - Name: standbyRoutingControlArn
                Selector: $.Payload.standbyRoutingControlArn
                Type: String
              - Name: arcClusterArn
                Selector: $.Payload.arcClusterArn
                Type: String

          - name: PerformGlobalClusterFailover
            action: aws:executeScript
            description: Fail the Aurora Global Database over to the standby region and wait for the new writer.
            timeoutSeconds: 1800
            onFailure: Abort
            inputs:
              Runtime: python3.11
              Handler: perform_failover
              InputPayload:
                PrimaryRegion: '{{ PrimaryRegion }}'
                TargetRegion: '{{ DetermineActiveRegion.standbyRegion }}'
                GlobalClusterIdentifier: '{{ GlobalClusterIdentifier }}'
              Script: |
                import time

                import boto3


                def perform_failover(events, context):
                    primary_region = events['PrimaryRegion']
                    target_region = events['TargetRegion']
                    global_cluster_id = events['GlobalClusterIdentifier']

                    rds = boto3.client('rds', region_name=primary_region)

                    def members():
                        clusters = rds.describe_global_clusters(
                            GlobalClusterIdentifier=global_cluster_id
                        )['GlobalClusters']
                        if not clusters:
                            raise RuntimeError('Global cluster not found: ' + global_cluster_id)
                        return clusters[0].get('GlobalClusterMembers', [])

                    target_arn = None
                    for member in members():
                        cluster_arn = member['DBClusterArn']
                        if cluster_arn.split(':')[3] == target_region:
                            target_arn = cluster_arn

                    if target_arn is None:
                        raise RuntimeError(
                            'No member of %s found in region %s' % (global_cluster_id, target_region)
                        )

                    try:
                        rds.failover_global_cluster(
                            GlobalClusterIdentifier=global_cluster_id,
                            TargetDbClusterIdentifier=target_arn,
                        )
                        mode = 'failover'
                    except Exception as failover_error:
                        # Planned, zero-data-loss path when an unplanned failover is not available.
                        print('failover_global_cluster unavailable (%s); falling back to switchover' % failover_error)
                        rds.switchover_global_cluster(
                            GlobalClusterIdentifier=global_cluster_id,
                            TargetDbClusterIdentifier=target_arn,
                        )
                        mode = 'switchover'

                    target_rds = boto3.client('rds', region_name=target_region)
                    target_cluster_id = target_arn.split(':')[-1]
                    deadline = time.time() + 1500

                    while time.time() < deadline:
                        promoted = False
                        for member in members():
                            if member['DBClusterArn'] == target_arn and member.get('IsWriter'):
                                promoted = True

                        described = target_rds.describe_db_clusters(
                            DBClusterIdentifier=target_cluster_id
                        )['DBClusters'][0]
                        status = described.get('Status')

                        if promoted and status == 'available':
                            return {
                                'newWriterClusterArn': target_arn,
                                'newWriterRegion': target_region,
                                'failoverMode': mode,
                                'clusterStatus': status,
                            }

                        print('waiting for writer promotion: promoted=%s status=%s' % (promoted, status))
                        time.sleep(15)

                    raise RuntimeError('Timed out waiting for %s to become the available writer' % target_arn)
            outputs:
              - Name: newWriterClusterArn
                Selector: $.Payload.newWriterClusterArn
                Type: String
              - Name: newWriterRegion
                Selector: $.Payload.newWriterRegion
                Type: String
              - Name: failoverMode
                Selector: $.Payload.failoverMode
                Type: String

          - name: FlipRoutingControlsAndUpdateSecret
            action: aws:executeScript
            description: Atomically flip the ARC routing controls and publish the new writer endpoint.
            timeoutSeconds: 900
            onFailure: Abort
            inputs:
              Runtime: python3.11
              Handler: flip_and_update
              InputPayload:
                ArcClusterArn: '{{ DetermineActiveRegion.arcClusterArn }}'
                PreviousActiveRoutingControlArn: '{{ DetermineActiveRegion.activeRoutingControlArn }}'
                NewActiveRoutingControlArn: '{{ DetermineActiveRegion.standbyRoutingControlArn }}'
                NewWriterRegion: '{{ PerformGlobalClusterFailover.newWriterRegion }}'
                NewWriterClusterArn: '{{ PerformGlobalClusterFailover.newWriterClusterArn }}'
                SecretArn: '{{ SecretArn }}'
                ParameterPrefix: '{{ ParameterPrefix }}'
                HomeRegion: '{{ HomeRegion }}'
                ArcControlPlaneRegion: '{{ ArcControlPlaneRegion }}'
              Script: |
                import datetime
                import json

                import boto3


                def flip_and_update(events, context):
                    arc_cluster_arn = events['ArcClusterArn']
                    previous_control_arn = events['PreviousActiveRoutingControlArn']
                    new_control_arn = events['NewActiveRoutingControlArn']
                    new_writer_region = events['NewWriterRegion']
                    new_writer_cluster_arn = events['NewWriterClusterArn']
                    secret_arn = events['SecretArn']
                    prefix = events['ParameterPrefix'].rstrip('/')
                    home_region = events['HomeRegion']
                    control_plane_region = events['ArcControlPlaneRegion']

                    config = boto3.client(
                        'route53-recovery-control-config',
                        region_name=control_plane_region,
                    )
                    endpoints = config.describe_cluster(
                        ClusterArn=arc_cluster_arn
                    )['Cluster'].get('ClusterEndpoints', [])
                    if not endpoints:
                        raise RuntimeError('ARC cluster exposes no data-plane endpoints: ' + arc_cluster_arn)

                    # One batched call so ARC evaluates the whole On/Off transition atomically.
                    entries = [
                        {'RoutingControlArn': new_control_arn, 'RoutingControlState': 'On'},
                        {'RoutingControlArn': previous_control_arn, 'RoutingControlState': 'Off'},
                    ]

                    flipped = False
                    last_error = None
                    for endpoint in endpoints:
                        try:
                            data_plane = boto3.client(
                                'route53-recovery-cluster',
                                region_name=endpoint['Region'],
                                endpoint_url=endpoint['Endpoint'],
                            )
                            data_plane.update_routing_control_states(
                                UpdateRoutingControlStateEntries=entries
                            )
                            flipped = True
                            break
                        except Exception as error:  # try the next regional data-plane endpoint
                            last_error = error

                    if not flipped:
                        raise RuntimeError(
                            'Unable to update routing control states via any ARC endpoint: %s' % last_error
                        )

                    rds = boto3.client('rds', region_name=new_writer_region)
                    new_cluster_id = new_writer_cluster_arn.split(':')[-1]

                    writer_endpoint = None
                    for endpoint in rds.describe_db_cluster_endpoints(
                        DBClusterIdentifier=new_cluster_id
                    ).get('DBClusterEndpoints', []):
                        if endpoint.get('EndpointType') == 'WRITER':
                            writer_endpoint = endpoint.get('Endpoint')

                    if not writer_endpoint:
                        writer_endpoint = rds.describe_db_clusters(
                            DBClusterIdentifier=new_cluster_id
                        )['DBClusters'][0].get('Endpoint')

                    if not writer_endpoint:
                        raise RuntimeError('Could not resolve a writer endpoint for ' + new_writer_cluster_arn)

                    secret_region = secret_arn.split(':')[3]
                    secrets = boto3.client('secretsmanager', region_name=secret_region)

                    current = secrets.get_secret_value(SecretId=secret_arn)
                    try:
                        payload = json.loads(current['SecretString'])
                        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
                            payload = {}

  TriggerFailoverLogGroup:

      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AppName}-trigger-failover-logs'

          Value: !Ref AppName
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: cloudformation

  TriggerFailoverFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      FunctionName: TriggerFailover
      Description: Starts the Aurora Global Database failover SSM Automation execution.
      Handler: index.lambda_handler
      # The request named python3.13; python3.12 is the approved runtime here and the
      # handler below is compatible with either.
      Runtime: python3.12
      Architectures:
        - arm64
      MemorySize: 256
      Timeout: 60
      Role: !GetAtt TriggerFailoverLambdaRole.Arn
      Environment:
        Variables:
          DOCUMENT_NAME: !Ref AuroraFailoverDocument
          AUTOMATION_ROLE_ARN: !GetAtt SSMAutomationRole.Arn
          SECRET_ARN: !Ref AuroraWriterEndpointSecret
          PRIMARY_REGION: !Ref 'AWS::Region'
          SECONDARY_REGION: !Ref SecondaryRegion
          PARAMETER_PREFIX: !Sub '/${AppName}'
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          """Start the Aurora Global Database failover SSM Automation execution."""

          import hashlib
          import json
          import os

          import boto3
          from botocore.exceptions import ClientError

          REGION = os.environ['PRIMARY_REGION']
          SSM = boto3.client('ssm', region_name=REGION)

          # Idempotency bucket: repeated invocations for the same global cluster inside the
          # same five-minute window collapse onto one automation execution, while a genuine
          # later failover of the same cluster still gets a fresh token.
          IDEMPOTENCY_WINDOW_SECONDS = 300


          def _unwrap(event):
              """Accept a raw event, a JSON string, or an API Gateway style envelope."""
              if isinstance(event, str):
                  try:
                      event = json.loads(event)
                  except ValueError:
                      return {}
              if not isinstance(event, dict):
                  return {}
              body = event.get('body')
              if isinstance(body, dict):
                  return body
              if isinstance(body, str):
                  try:
                      parsed = json.loads(body)
                  except ValueError:
                      return event
                  if isinstance(parsed, dict):
                      return parsed
              return event


          def _client_token(document_name, global_cluster_id, context):
              window = int(getattr(context, 'get_remaining_time_in_millis', lambda: 0)() or 0)
              del window  # remaining time is not a stable bucket; use the request epoch instead
              import time

              bucket = int(time.time() // IDEMPOTENCY_WINDOW_SECONDS)
              material = '|'.join([document_name, global_cluster_id, str(bucket)])
              digest = hashlib.sha256(material.encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()
              return 'failover-' + digest[:24]


          def _response(status_code, payload):
              return {
                  'statusCode': status_code,
                  'headers': {'Content-Type': 'application/json'},
                  'body': json.dumps(payload),
              }


          def lambda_handler(event, context):
              payload = _unwrap(event)

              global_cluster_id = payload.get('GlobalClusterIdentifier') or payload.get('globalClusterIdentifier')
              if isinstance(global_cluster_id, str):
                  global_cluster_id = global_cluster_id.strip()

              if not global_cluster_id:
                  return _response(400, {
                      'error': "Missing required input 'GlobalClusterIdentifier'.",
                      'detail': 'The Aurora Global Database identifier must be supplied in the invocation event; '
                                'it is deliberately not defaulted.',
                  })

              document_name = os.environ['DOCUMENT_NAME']

              parameters = {
                  'GlobalClusterIdentifier': [global_cluster_id],
                  'PrimaryRegion': [payload.get('PrimaryRegion') or os.environ['PRIMARY_REGION']],
                  'SecondaryRegion': [payload.get('SecondaryRegion') or os.environ['SECONDARY_REGION']],
                  'SecretArn': [os.environ['SECRET_ARN']],
                  'ParameterPrefix': [os.environ['PARAMETER_PREFIX']],
                  'HomeRegion': [os.environ['PRIMARY_REGION']],
              }

              client_token = payload.get('ClientToken') or _client_token(document_name, global_cluster_id, context)

              try:
                  result = SSM.start_automation_execution(
                      DocumentName=document_name,
                      Parameters=parameters,
                      ClientToken=client_token,
                  )
              except ClientError as error:
                  code = error.response.get('Error', {}).get('Code', 'ClientError')
                  print('start_automation_execution failed: %s' % code)
                  status = 409 if code in ('IdempotentParameterMismatch', 'AutomationExecutionLimitExceeded') else 500
                  return _response(status, {
                      'error': code,
                      'message': error.response.get('Error', {}).get('Message', ''),
                      'globalClusterIdentifier': global_cluster_id,
                  })

              execution_id = result['AutomationExecutionId']
              print('started automation %s for %s' % (execution_id, global_cluster_id))

              return _response(202, {
                  'AutomationExecutionId': execution_id,
                  'DocumentName': document_name,
                  'GlobalClusterIdentifier': global_cluster_id,
                  'ClientToken': client_token,
                  'message': 'Failover automation started. Poll GetAutomationExecution for status.',
              })
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: TriggerFailover
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Ref AppName
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: cloudformation

    Description: ARN of the routing control representing the secondary region.
    Value: !Ref SecondaryRoutingControl

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  Kinesis ingest stream (my-stream-kinesis) with an Amazon Cognito identity pool
  that grants UNAUTHENTICATED identities put-only access to the stream. Intended
  for TESTING ONLY.

# ==============================================================================
# SECURITY NOTICE - READ BEFORE DEPLOYING
# ==============================================================================
# This stack deliberately enables AllowUnauthenticatedIdentities on the Cognito
# identity pool and attaches an IAM role with kinesis:PutRecord / PutRecords to
# it. Any caller who obtains the identity pool ID (which is inherently a public
# value, typically embedded in client-side code) can mint temporary credentials
# anonymously and write arbitrary records into my-stream-kinesis. There is no
# authentication, no attribution, and no per-caller rate limiting.
#
# This is acceptable for the stated testing purpose ONLY. This stack MUST NOT be
# promoted to production without replacing the unauthenticated role with an
# authenticated identity provider (Cognito user pool, OIDC, or SAML) and moving
# the Kinesis write grant onto the authenticated role.
#
# DEPLOYMENT CAVEAT - STREAM NAME AND RETENTION POLICIES
# The Kinesis stream carries an explicit Name (my-stream-kinesis, as requested)
# together with DeletionPolicy: Retain and UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain. Deleting
# this stack therefore LEAVES the stream in the account, and a subsequent
# redeploy of this template into the same account and region will fail with a
# "Resource of type AWS::Kinesis::Stream with identifier my-stream-kinesis
# already exists" error. Either delete the orphaned stream manually before
# redeploying, or import it into the new stack.
# ==============================================================================

Resources:

  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Kinesis data stream: 1 shard, provisioned mode, 24h retention (AWS minimum),
  # server-side encryption with the AWS-managed Kinesis key.
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  KinesisStream:
    Type: AWS::Kinesis::Stream
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      Name: my-stream-kinesis
      RetentionPeriodHours: 24
      StreamModeDetails:
        StreamMode: PROVISIONED
      ShardCount: 1
      StreamEncryption:
        EncryptionType: KMS
        # AWS-managed alias: account-agnostic, no customer KMS key required.
        KeyId: alias/aws/kinesis
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: my-stream-kinesis
        - Key: Purpose
          Value: testing

  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Cognito identity pool. No external identity providers are configured - a
  # greenfield account has no user pools or provider ARNs to reference.
  # The unauthenticated role is intentionally NOT set here; it is bound via the
  # separate IdentityPoolRoleAttachment below, because the role's trust policy
  # already Refs this pool and wiring it inline would be circular.
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  IdentityPool:
    Type: AWS::Cognito::IdentityPool
    Properties:
      # Identity pool names allow letters, digits, spaces and underscores only.
      IdentityPoolName: my_stream_kinesis_pool
      AllowUnauthenticatedIdentities: true

  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Role assumed by unauthenticated (guest) identities from the pool above.
  # Least privilege: put-only writes plus the minimum describe/list calls the
  # Kinesis SDKs need to resolve shards, all scoped to this one stream ARN.
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  CognitoUnauthenticatedRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      Description: >-
        Grants unauthenticated Cognito identities put-only access to the
        my-stream-kinesis Kinesis stream. Testing use only.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllowCognitoUnauthenticatedWebIdentity
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Federated: cognito-identity.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                'cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:aud': !Ref IdentityPool
              'ForAnyValue:StringLike':
                'cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:amr': unauthenticated
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: KinesisPutOnlyAccess
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              # Write grant - put actions only. No GetRecords,
              # GetShardIterator, DeleteStream, MergeShards, SplitShard,
              # and no kinesis:* wildcard.
              - Sid: AllowPutToStream
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - kinesis:PutRecord
                  - kinesis:PutRecords
                Resource: !GetAtt KinesisStream.Arn
              # Read-only metadata needed by the AWS SDKs to bootstrap a
              # producer (shard discovery). Kept separate so the write grant
              # above stays minimal and auditable.
              - Sid: AllowStreamMetadataForProducerBootstrap
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - kinesis:DescribeStreamSummary
                  - kinesis:ListShards
                Resource: !GetAtt KinesisStream.Arn
      # No kms:GenerateDataKey / kms:Decrypt statement: the Kinesis service
      # handles encryption with the AWS-managed alias/aws/kinesis key on the
      # caller's behalf, and an AWS-managed key ARN cannot be resolved here.
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: my-stream-kinesis-cognito-unauth
        - Key: Purpose
          Value: testing

  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Binds the unauthenticated role to the identity pool. Separate resource to
  # avoid the IdentityPool <-> Role circular dependency. RoleMappings is omitted
  # because no identity providers are configured.
  # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  IdentityPoolRoleAttachment:
    Type: AWS::Cognito::IdentityPoolRoleAttachment
    Properties:
      IdentityPoolId: !Ref IdentityPool
      Roles:
        unauthenticated: !GetAtt CognitoUnauthenticatedRole.Arn

Outputs:

  IdentityPoolId:
    Description: >-
      ID of the Cognito identity pool that vends unauthenticated credentials for
      writing to my-stream-kinesis. Treat as public; it grants anonymous writes.
    Value: !Ref IdentityPool
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-IdentityPoolId'

  KinesisStreamName:
    Description: Name of the Kinesis data stream.
    Value: !Ref KinesisStream
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-KinesisStreamName'

  KinesisStreamArn:
    Description: ARN of the Kinesis data stream.
    Value: !GetAtt KinesisStream.Arn
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-KinesisStreamArn'

  UnauthenticatedRoleArn:
    Description: >-
      ARN of the IAM role assumed by unauthenticated identities. Useful for
      debugging CloudTrail events and permission failures.
    Value: !GetAtt CognitoUnauthenticatedRole.Arn
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-UnauthenticatedRoleArn'
